allCourses.description: Directed study with Anthropology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Independent research with Anthropology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Proseminar in Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Year-long intensive introduction to the history of anthropological thought and reading in classical and contemporary ethnography for first-year graduate students.

allCourses.title: Proseminar in Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Year-long intensive introduction to the history of anthropological thought and reading in classical and contemporary ethnography for first-year graduate students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ANTHRO 202A. ANTHRO 202A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Proseminar in Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Year-long intensive introduction to the history of anthropological thought and reading in classical and contemporary ethnography for first-year graduate students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ANTHRO 202B. ANTHRO 202B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Proseminar in Medicine, Science, and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Students pursuing a Graduate Certification in Anthropoligies of Medicine, Science, and Technology have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the phenomena studied by "medical anthropology" and "science and technology studies" are inextricably linked, and how understanding formations requires moving between disparate fields of inquiry.  Required for students pursuing a Graduate Certificate in Anthropoligies of Medicine, Science, and Technology.

allCourses.title: Anthropological Fieldwork Methodology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A survey of anthropological fieldwork methodology techniques, including attention to contemporary analysis of fieldwork.

allCourses.title: People, Cultures, and Environmental Sustainability
allCourses.description: Anthropological consideration of global environmental sustainability from the perspective of human cultures and communities. Causes and consequences of population growth, natural resource management, environmental law, environmental ethics. Case studies emphasize tropical rain forests, arid lands of Africa and North America.

allCourses.title: Anthropology of Food
allCourses.description: Examines how food communicates ideas about ethnocentrism, disgust, privilege, gender, race, labor, social identities and hierarchies, globalization, power, and the "Western diet" and its health consequences.

allCourses.title: Statistics and Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces basic concepts of research design for anthropology in conjunction with relevant concepts from the field of statistics, which will be learned in conjunction with the research designs that require use of those methods.

allCourses.title: Research Design and Data Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces advanced concepts of research design for anthropology, presents statistical models for multivariate analysis and for analysis of systems of relationships, and includes practice in sampling and data analysis.

allCourses.title: Grant and Proposal Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on production, critique, and revision of student research proposals. A practical seminar designed to improve student proposals, help students through the application processes, and increase students' chances of obtaining support for their research.

allCourses.title: Ethnographic Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exposes students to diverse methods, both traditional and experimental, used in anthropological ethnographic research. Students gain experience practicing diverse methods, and learn to select methods appropriate to particular study designs and contexts.

allCourses.title: Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces research design for anthropology, including concept work and mapping, research topic and aims development, research question construction, and fieldwork planning.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ANTHRO 215A. ANTHRO 215A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Grant and Proposal Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on production, critique, and revision of student research proposals. A practical seminar designed to improve student proposals, help students through the application processes, and increase students' chances of obtaining support for their research.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ANTHRO 215B. ANTHRO 215B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Pedagogy and Professionalization in Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Anthropology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to pedagogical approaches in anthropology, fostering professional development in and beyond academia, and providing general advice about teaching and mentorship. Periodically invites authors of the reviewed texts to participate in classroom conversation.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Oral History, Life History
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Interdisciplinary and comparative work in oral and life history; methods of interviewing.

allCourses.title: Grant and Proposal Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on production, critique, and revision of student research proposals. A practical seminar designed to improve student proposals, help students through the application processes, and increase students' chances of obtaining support for their research.

allCourses.title: Anthropology Encounters
allCourses.description: Cultural encounters have long provided the ground for ethnographic research. This seminar refocuses on "encounter" not only as the material condition but also as a productive heuristic device in anthropological inquiry. Examines the reorientation of anthropology as a "global discipline.".

allCourses.title: Anthropology of Knowledge
allCourses.description: Examines the politics of knowledge. Considers the long history of anthropological studies concerning a wide variety of knowledge forms and practices, including more recent feminist and postcolonial studies. Aims to investigate and enlarge normative definitions of knowledge and science.

allCourses.title: Anthropology and History
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An examination of the complex, long-standing relationship between anthropology and history. Themes include: history, culture, and colonialism; history and the power to represent; nostalgia and the uses of the past in struggles over "national history.".

allCourses.title: Ethnography and its Collaborative Futures
allCourses.description: Structured readings of selected career-making ethnographic works, past and present, with an emphasis on how ethnographic projects evolve into diverse, collaborative projects.

allCourses.title: Ethnography
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the theory and practice of ethnography with a focus on anthropology, the discipline most associated with ethnography. Students are exposed to the theoretical underpinnings of ethnographic work, traditional and innovative practices, and sample ethnographies.

allCourses.title: Technomethods for Sociocultural Research
allCourses.description: An introduction to using particular technologies for conducting contemporary ethnographic fieldwork. Focuses both on the practical use of these tools and the conceptual work that is necessary for successfully integrating them into specific research projects.

allCourses.title: Medical Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Students pursuing a Graduate Certification in Anthropoligies of Medicine, Science, and Technology have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores historical and contemporary theoretical positions and debates in medical anthropology. Topics may include subjectivity, theories of the body, biopolitics, biomedical technologies, sexuality, pharmaceuticals, political economy and health, infectious disease and epidemics, health disparities, and humanitarianism.

allCourses.title: Ethnographies of Science and Medicine
allCourses.description: Surveys current ethnographic research pertaining to medical anthropology and science and technology studies.

allCourses.title: Anthropology of Food
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Course examines the role of food in culture history and in anthropological thinking about ethnocentrism, disgust, privilege, gender, race, identities, social relationships, kinship, social hierarchies, globalization, production, consumption, food scarcities, body image, health, and power.

allCourses.title: Transnational Migration
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

allCourses.title: Borders and Bodies:  Places, Processes, and Transgressions
allCourses.description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

allCourses.title: Economic Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Classic and contemporary theory in economic anthropology. Case studies: Latin America (primarily Mexico and the Andes), Africa, and the Pacific. Substantive topics: non-market exchange, markets and marketplaces, households, gender, management of common property (fisheries, pastoral lands, forests), labor, and development.

allCourses.title: Language and the Social World
allCourses.description: An introduction to the study of language in culture. Topics include theories of the sign; the relation of language structure to linguistic practice; language and group formation; linguistic ideologies; conversation analysis; and language and embodiment.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Political Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores anthropological approaches to politics. Covers a range of issues and topics, including: theories of culture, power, and hegemony; approaches to colonial and post-colonial relations of global inequality; and ethnographic approaches to the modern state.

allCourses.title: Feminist Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines feminist anthropology’s rise as an interdisciplinary field. Paying special attention to issues of power, subjectivity, and authority in the research encounter, feminist anthropologists’ major contributions to ethnography, gender studies, queer studies, and cultural anthropology are surveyed.

allCourses.title: Law, Colonialism, & Nationalism
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Origins and spread of law in colonial and nationalist contexts: law's role in constituting and policing difference. Recent theoretical approaches; property in things and people; human and indigenous rights; "customary" law; legal foundations of nationalism; resistance to/through law; globalization.

allCourses.title: Nations, States, and Gender
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the ways in which nations, nationalism, states, and citizenship are gendered relations and processes.  Questions include: How do women construct themselves as political subjects and how are constructions of citizenship and discourses of rights gendered.

allCourses.title: Capital and Empire
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines theories of capital and empire via anthropological theory, post/colonial critique, feminist theory, and Black political thought. Moreover, it examines social movements, geo/political trajectories and formations, and political economic trends that have emerged after the 2008 financial crisis.

allCourses.title: Structuralism and Post-Structuralism
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Traces recent theoretical discussions and arguments over the philosophical and historical "subject" from structuralist decenterings toward the characteristically "post-structuralist" contemporary concern with the historical and political constitution of subjectivities and subject positions.

allCourses.title: Approaches to Globalization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Historical and contemporary approaches to the world economy, emphasizing anthropological questions of culture, power, identity, inequality. Examines "neo-imperialism," "late capitalism," accumulation, global markets, urban space, the state, business and policy globalization discourse, "local" responses to and instantiations of the "global.".

allCourses.title: Globalizing Social Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Developing critical, interdisciplinary, feminist, and postcolonial approaches to global issues. Review of European modern and postmodern schools of thought, and theories of globalization. Incorporating theories from the global south to develop a more global and inclusive system of knowledge production.

allCourses.title: Humanism and Posthumanism
allCourses.description: Examines alternative forms of human, humanisms, and posthumanisms to explore the inherent ambiguities and shifting boundaries of knowing and being human, and to venture into modes of analysis that problematize the universality and globality of liberal humanism.

allCourses.title: Multispecies Anthropology
allCourses.description: Examines how the co-constituting categories of animal and human in tandem with investigating how engagements with human/animal relations continue to define and alter anthropology. Subthemes: meaning, nature/culture, non-humanism, ontologies, relations, matter, evolutions, ecologies, and futures.

allCourses.title: The Cultural Politics of Visual Representation
allCourses.description: Develops a theoretical framework for analyzing and reading visual images. Images, as cultural productions, are steeped in the values, ideologies, and taken-for-granted beliefs of the culture which produced them and a political economy that is class, race, and gender inflected.

allCourses.title: Digital Technologies, Culture, and Media
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores questions of sociality in cyberspace, including what social theories and ethnographic methods are effective in studying online cultures. Topics include general issues like indexicality, reference, temporality, spatiality, and embodiment, and topics such as language, gender, ethnicity, property, and inequality.

allCourses.title: Queer Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores historical and contemporary scholarship that employs ethnographic approaches to address the discursive construction of sexuality. Also examines how the discipline of anthropology has been shaped by the study of sexuality.

allCourses.title: Design, Aesthetics, and Social Life
allCourses.description: Anthropology has only recently recognized that design demands consideration as a cultural form linked to, yet nonetheless distinct from, other aesthetic endeavors. Course is largely oriented toward collaboratively working out a conceptual basis for a distinctly anthropological approach to design.

allCourses.title: Digital Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines “the digital” from an anthropological perspective by exploring ethnographic research on digital culture and using anthropological frameworks to approach the digital and the human. Readings are interdisciplinary, including work from history and communications.

allCourses.title: Postcoloniality and the Subject
allCourses.description: Examines key issues regarding postcoloniality and conceptions of selfhood in the context of varied forms of colonial and state power. In particular, explores how technology and desire intersect with these questions of subjectification.

allCourses.title: Disability Worlds
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores disability from a range of methodological and theoretical perspectives. Examines the genealogy of disability in anthropology and related disciplines, with an emphasis on ethnographic work. Topics addressed include access, embodiment, politics, selfhood, and sexuality.

allCourses.title: Ethnographies of Technology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Surveys current ethnographic research pertaining to technologies, technical systems, and infrastructures.

allCourses.title: Secrecy, Security, and Surveillance
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores secrecy and security as fundamental to constructions of public and private domains, relations of citizenship and sovereignty, the militarization of everyday life, and the ways that the fabrics of societies are woven of both trust and deceit.

allCourses.title: Natures and Environments
allCourses.description: Examines social scientific understandings of natural contexts and human milieus via a survey of key analytic categories. Begins by examining historical and ongoing definitions and problems organized around “nature” and “environment” as separate but imbricated concepts.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Writing Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for advanced, post-fieldwork Anthropology graduate students. Emphasis on the presentation of research design and results, problems of ethnographic writing, and qualitative and quantitative data and analysis. Prerequisites: post-fieldwork; graduate standing in Anthropology or consent of instructor.

allCourses.title: Environmental Injustice
allCourses.description: Explores how pollution, climate change, and other environmental problems impact people around the world, often worsening social inequality. Students use social science frameworks to understand environmental problems, different interpretations of these problems, and how people have organized for political change.

allCourses.title: Critical Medical Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reading-intensive graduate seminar offers an overview of theoretical and ethnographic approaches to illness and healing in different settings, while also studying the political economic distribution of risks that contribute to disease. Students develop their own research papers integrating course readings.

allCourses.title: Anthropology of the Mind
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reading-intensive graduate seminar looks at emergence of mind/soul in modern age and similar concepts across cultural and historical contexts; studies psychiatric anthropological approaches to trauma, the subconscious, dreaming, madness. Students develop their own research papers integrating course readings.

allCourses.title: Literary Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Looks at genre-blending between creative nonfiction, ethnography, fiction,.

allCourses.title: Transformative Teaching in Higher Education
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces graduate students to the theoretical and practical aspects of teaching and learning in higher education. Topics include critical and liberatory pedagogies; theories of learning; course design and instructional strategies; inclusive teaching; and teaching in academic careers.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Anthropology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Anthropology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Anthropology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Sociocultural Anthropology
allCourses.description: Introduction to cultural diversity and the methods used by anthropologists to account for it. Family relations, economic activities, politics, gender, and religion in a wide range of societies. Stresses the application of anthropological methods to research problems.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
allCourses.description: Evolutionary theory and processes, comparative primate fossil record, human variation, and the adequacy of theory, and empirical data.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Archaeology
allCourses.description: Archaeological theory and cultural processes with emphasis on the American Southwest, Mesoamerica, and Mesopotamia.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Language and Culture
allCourses.description: Explores what the study of language can reveal about ourselves as bearers of culture. After introducing some basic concepts, examines how cultural knowledge is linguistically organized and how language might shape our perception of the world.

allCourses.title: Global Issues in Anthropological Perspective
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores anthropological perspectives on issues of importance in an increasingly global society. Topics include emphases on ethnic conflict; identity; immigration and citizenship; religion and religious diversity; medical anthropology; legal anthropology; development and economic change; gender.

allCourses.title: Ethnography and Anthropological Methods
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores ethnography, anthropology's classic method. Students obtain hands-on training in participant observation, interviewing, and other methods, in local communities, and the preparation of research reports. Also provides theoretical and reflexive readings on ethnography.

allCourses.title: Visual Anthropology
allCourses.description: Focusing on the construction of culture through visuality, this course engages traditional ethnographic films, popular media and anthropological texts to analyze ethics, “reality” and fiction; propaganda and documentary, construction of a frame, the responsibility of the filmmaker, photographer, and anthropologist.

allCourses.title: Global Cultures and Society
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Offers a general overview of the rise of global interdependence in political, economic, demographic, and cultural terms. Considers what drove people from relative isolation into intensified intercourse with one another, and investigates the consequences of this shift.

allCourses.title: Science, Culture, Power
allCourses.description: Examines science in historical and cultural context (Scientific and Darwinian Revolutions, Manhattan Project, contemporary biosciences) to understand scientific truths and their limits, scientists as social actors, and vital intersections of sciences with religion, politics, gender, and other forms of culture.

allCourses.title: Archaeology or Aliens?: Conspiracy, Pseudoscience, and the Emergence of Civilizations
allCourses.description: Archaeology has inspired (and sometimes actively encouraged) various theories about aliens, lost civilizations, dark conspiracies, and mysterious technologies. Does such an intimate relationship with these fantastic notions undermine archaeology and its claims of authoritative knowledge about past cultures.

allCourses.title: Gender and Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the social forces, life circumstances, and political and economic processes that influence gendered health outcomes. Focuses especially on women located at the economic and political margins of societies throughout the world.

allCourses.title: Global Themes in Sikh Studies
allCourses.description: Serves as an introduction to Sikhism and the field of Sikh Studies. Examines the development of the religious tradition and the formation of the scholarly field of Sikh Studies in the contemporary Western university.

allCourses.title: Cultures in Collision: Indian-White Relations Since Columbus
allCourses.description: An introduction to theories, terms, concepts, and methods used by anthropologists and sociologists to understand Native American cultures. How racial construction of an Indian "other" emerged, how anthropology contributed to Indian invisibility, and the persistence of Indian identity are examined.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Anthropology
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Anthropology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Honors Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Students design a research project and articulate its goals and significance. Written work consists of a research proposal describing the research questions, the relevant literature, methods of data collection and analysis, and ethical considerations.

allCourses.title: Honors Field Research
allCourses.restriction: Anthropology Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Students begin or continue ethnographic field research and gain experience with a variety of data collection methods, including participant-observation, interviews, surveys, and the study of archival and documentary materials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ANTHRO 199 and ANTHRO H190A

allCourses.title: Honors Research Analysis
allCourses.description: Students apply qualitative data analysis techniques to ethnographic data collected as part of their Honors research.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ANTHRO H190B and ANTHRO 199. Anthropology Honors ONLY.

allCourses.title: Honors Thesis Writing
allCourses.description: Students draft a senior honors thesis (typically) with the following sections: problem statement, literature review, ethnographic background, and descriptions of the methods, results, and conclusions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ANTHRO H190C and ANTHRO 199. Anthropology Honors ONLY. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Honors Senior Thesis
allCourses.description: Student drafts a senior honor thesis (typically) with the following sections: problem statement, literature review, ethnographic background, description of the methods, results, and conclusions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ANTHRO H190A and ANTHRO H190B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Arabic Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
allCourses.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. ARABIC 10A is for language mentors.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Arabic Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program
allCourses.description: Peer-to-Peer Language Mentor Program in which student mentors work with student mentees to increase the language skills of both participants. One hour weekly meetings. ARABIC 10B is for language mentees.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Modern Arabic Literature in Translation
allCourses.description: In English. Major works in Arabic literature and culture in context.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Research paper required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Arabic
allCourses.restriction: ARABIC 1A and ARABIC S1AB may not be taken for full credit.
allCourses.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Arabic. Using real world texts, provides a firm foundation in the orthography, grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of Modern Standard Arabic. Introduces students to Arab world cultures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Placement into ARABIC 1A.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Arabic
allCourses.restriction: ARABIC 1B and ARABIC S1AB and ARABIC S1BC may not be taken for full credit.
allCourses.description: Designed for students with little or no exposure to Arabic. Using real world texts, provides a firm foundation in the orthography, grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of Modern Standard Arabic. Introduces students to Arab world cultures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARABIC 1A. ARABIC 1A with a grade of C or better. Placement into ARABIC 1B is also accepted.

Students will develop their understanding of grammar and syntax to a more sophisticated level. Facilitates intermediate-level reading, writing, and speaking skills. Fosters college-level cultural literacy.

allCourses.title: Introduction to the Koran
allCourses.description: An introduction to understanding the Koran and its significance to Muslim life, culture, and history. An overview of scholarly traditions related to the Koran, and its critics. Close readings of the Koran in English translation.

allCourses.title: Introductory Arabic
allCourses.restriction: ARABIC S1AB and ARABIC 1A and ARABIC 1B may not be taken for full credit.
allCourses.description: First half of first-year Arabic. Designed for students with little or no exposure to Arabic. Provides students with firm foundation in orthography, grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of written and spoken Modern Standard Arabic.  Course may be offered online.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Placement in ARABIC 1A or ARABIC S1AB.

allCourses.restriction: ARABIC S1BC and ARABIC 1B and ARABIC 1C may not be taken for full credit.
allCourses.description: Second half of first-year Arabic. Continuation of S1AB, or for students with limited exposure to Arabic. Provide firm foundation in orthography, grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of written and spoken Modern Standard Arabic.  Course may be offered online.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARABIC 1B or ARABIC S1AB or placement into ARABIC 1B or ARABIC 1C. ARABIC 1B with a grade of C or better. ARABIC S1AB with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARABIC 1B or ARABIC S2AB. ARABIC 1B with a grade of B or better. ARABIC S2AB with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.title: Elementary Armenian
allCourses.description: Written and conversational Armenian for students with no knowledge of the language. Students learn the Armenian alphabet, read and comprehend simple texts, and carry basic conversation. Emphasis on reading and comprehension, grammar rules, and basic composition.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Placement into ARMN 1A.

allCourses.title: Elementary Armenian
allCourses.description: Continues development of the fundamentals of Armenian, including comprehension, reading of simple texts, basic conversation, and writing with a fair degree of grammatical correctness. Students learn basic reading, writing, and sentence structure through lectures, games, and assignments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARMN 1A. ARMN 1A with a grade of C or better. Placement into ARMN 1B is also accepted.

allCourses.title: Elementary Armenian
allCourses.description: Focus on building grammatical knowledge of the Armenian language and developing skills in reading, writing, listening, and speaking. Includes a strong emphasis on expanding vocabulary and developing oral proficiency in higher/formal registers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARMN 1B. ARMN 1B with a grade of C or better. Placement into ARMN 1C is also accepted.

allCourses.description: Designed to develop students’ ability to communicate further orally and in writing in Armenian (Western or Eastern) by consolidating knowledge of grammar, increasing vocabulary, and developing reading, comprehension, and writing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARMN 1C. ARMN 1C with a grade of C or better. Placement into ARMN 2A is also accepted.

allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Materials fee, topic dependent.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Lower-division writing strongly recommended.

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 6 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Artists as Writers
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Contemporary art practice involves text, as final form or an integral element. Many contemporary artists consider writing as essential to their practice. Covers historical and contemporary uses of text and image as well as artists' writing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A and ART 11A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology
Topics in History of Contemporary Art

allCourses.title: Intermediate Painting
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Continuation of the investigation initiated in basic painting, with an emphasis on experimentation, personal investigation, development of conceptual working premises, as well as the acquisition of necessary skills. Group discussion and critique are emphasized.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C and ART 30A and ART 30B
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Intermediate Sculpture
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Investigation of three-dimensional space, including the construction of objects and the manipulation of the environment. Students define personal projects and translate personal, social, and political experience into visual meaning. Range of artists' works introduced. Group discussion and critiques. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C and ART 40
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Intermediate Ceramic Sculpture
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Further investigation of the use of clay as a medium, with an emphasis on experimental practice and the relationship to contemporary visual art. Emphasizes discussion of ideas, and provides information on clay body, fabrication, glazing, and firing.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C and ART 51
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Programming for Artists
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Programming as a means to create interactive artworks with an emphasis on the integration of video, sound, text, and stills. Topics include basic concepts in programming, understanding the limits of code, working with video and audio files, and interface design. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 65A. Recommended: ART 11B.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Game Studies
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: Critical analysis of various genres of computer games and gaming theory and practice through playing, writing, and discussion. The focus is on creating a Design Document for the student's own gaming environment using gaming metaphors, design principles, and technologies. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 65A. Recommended: ART 11B.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Design for Print
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Investigates the use of print for communication as an artist. Covers the fundamentals of print design and output using digital media.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 65A. Recommended: ART 11B.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Intermediate Projects in Photography
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students begin learning how to develop photographic projects of their own making. Focuses on employing and expanding upon previously learned technical and critical skills specific to students' individual interests and ideas. Critiques, readings, lectures, labs. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C and ART 71A and ART 71B
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Filmmaking Project I
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students learn to conceive, develop, and produce original video works building directly upon previously learned skills. Use of video stage and post-production editing facilities. Lectures on video/film subjects, production strategies, readings, screening, field trips, and group critiques. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 81A and ART 81B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Performance and the Camera
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Surveys the development of contemporary artists who use performance strategies in the making of videos and films. Students analyze the artist's conceptual approach to performative gestures, actions, and landscapes created for their video or film art.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1B or ART 81A or ART 91 or ART 128

prerequisite_list.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Mechatronic Art I
allCourses.description: Introduces the practice and theory of analog electronics, emphasizing the design and development of simple interactive systems and the integration of such systems into real-world contexts of performance, installation, sculpture, and automated artifacts. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Mechatronic Art II
allCourses.description: Introduces the practice and theory of embedded microcontrollers, digital electronics, coding, sensor interfacing, motor control, and output stages along with mechanical and electromechanical design and construction, emphasizing the integration of such systems into real-world contexts of performance, installation, and art-making.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 110A

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Mechatronic Art III
allCourses.description: As the capstone to the Mechatronic Art series, students develop major projects utilizing electronics, microcontrollers, sensors, and electromechanical devices, in a methodical and supervised context, with technical, design, and aesthetic advice and critique. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 110A

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: 3D Methods and Materials
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Presents a wide variety of concepts, materials, tools, and fabrication techniques vital to art production.  Wood tools, clay, castable rubber, urethane foam, fiberglass, plaster, steel, and welding are introduced. Projects are based on conceptual problems incorporating these materials. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: How to be Clever with Stuff
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: How to Be Clever with Stuff is an introduction to the skilled embodied practices of arts and crafts, working with hand tools, wood, and steel. Class includes technical lecture/demos, short technical assignments, a self-initiated final project, and design drawing. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Writing Nearby
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Art writing is increasingly an area of scholarship unto itself as well as a discursive arm of contemporary art practice. Investigates the politics of art writing as well as training students in its various writing practices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A and ART 11A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology
Topics in History of Contemporary Art

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Feminist Issues in Art
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: Feminist perspectives and topics in relation to cultural production. Feminist debates on sexuality, perspectives on women of color, on race and gender, feminist film criticism, histories of the first and second waves of feminism, histories of feminist art.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Recommended: Satisfactory completion of the Upper-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Popular Culture
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: In-depth investigation of the relationship between visual art practices and popular culture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Recommended: satisfactory completion of the upper-division writing requirement strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Contemporary Painting
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Investigation of issues in modern and contemporary art work and criticism, wherein an assessment of Modernist influences is followed by the examination of contemporary painting as a cross-disciplinary practice employing popular culture, "high art," theory, and new technology.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Recommended: Satisfactory completion of the upper-division writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Contemporary Drawing
allCourses.description: Investigation of drawing as a primary practice rather than a developmental tool. Explores the relationship between Conceptualism, process and content, and considers the historical changes in method, presentation, and theory, from past to present.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Topics in History of Contemporary Art
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Surveys mid-19th and 20th-century art production, from modernity through post-modernity, in a historical and cultural context.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Media Art and Design History
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: Survey of the roots of modern techno-media arts in both the history of visual arts and the history of devices such as automata, animatronics, robots, miniature theatres, optical machines, communications technologies, calculators, and computers.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Narrative
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes the construction of narratives in different media--painting, photography, sculpture, video.  Particular attention paid to the development of personal and community histories as a working base.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Recommended: satisfactory completion of the upper-division writing requirement strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Race and Representation
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes the construction of racial difference and stereotyping in the visual and performing arts, and on the histories of cultures and artists who functioned outside the contemporary mainstream. Readings assigned.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Recommended: satisfactory completion of the upper-division writing requirement strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Afro-Futurism I
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: First of a two-part course on the futuristic artistic vision of Black film, video, and cyberspace. Deals with critical analyses of the Black image in Western Art history, and its association to contemporary Hip Hop culture, art, and music.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Satisfactory completion of upper-division writing strongly recommended.

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Afro-Futurism II
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Second of a two-part course on the futuristic artistic visions of Black film, video, and cyberspace. Deals with modern techno-culture, digital activism, and designing technology based on African aesthetic principles of contemporary Hip Hop International Culture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Satisfactory completion of upper-division writing strongly recommended.

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in the New Culture Wars
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: "Culture wars" originally described Reagan/Bush era political efforts launched over matters like abortion, religion, gay rights, school curricula. Such controversies provided motivation and content for many artists. Addresses new culture wars emerging since 9/11 over privacy, technology globalization, terrorism.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Recommended: satisfactory completion of the upper-division writing requirement strongly recommended.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Media, Violence, and Fear
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Violence has been instrumental in story-telling throughout history in art, literature, religion, and entertainment. Continuing presence of media violence provoked debates among parents, politicians, media producers, and academics. Examines history, theory, aesthetics, economics, and politics of violent representation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Satisfactory completion of the Upper-Division Writing requirement is recommended.

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Photography
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Rigorous investigation of photographic practices and critical writings, the relationship of photography to the construction and maintenance of cultural institutions, the circulation of photographic ideas in society, and photography and technology.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 1A"}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 71A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 71B"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 152A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 152B"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 152C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 152D"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 152E"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 190B"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A or ART 71A or ART 71B or ART 152A or ART 152B or ART 152C or ART 152D or ART 152E or ART 190B. Recommended: Satisfactory completion of the Upper-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_list.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
Senior Projects and Critique in Photography

allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Media and Migration: Asia
allCourses.description: Media and migration are profound, twinned influences on contemporary globalized experience. A discourse on Asian cultural production and of its transnational dimensions. Students will explore migration in its multiple facets to include migrations of people, ideas, and technologies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Tactical Media and the Politics of Information
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: Overview of tactical media as a practice and its theoretical influences. Emerged in post-Cold War Europe in early 1990s. Tactical use of media and activism are point of reference for tactical media groups worldwide.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Techno-Arts
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Addresses issues related to artmaking practices that emerge in tandem with new technologies. Topics include sociopolitical contexts of techno-art; utopic/dystopic framings; key moments in the history of techno-arts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Recommended: ART 11B.

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Video History and Criticism
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: Investigation of historical development of video as artistic practice. Topics include relationships between art and video technology, critiques of television, experimentation with image processing/synthesis, performances designed for video, experiments in documentary representation, video installation. Readings and screenings assigned. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in Experimental Film History
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: A critical study of experimental film/video art genres and production techniques considering their narrative, structural, iconographic, and cultural aspects. Hollywood narrative, Nouvelle Vague, American Independent, and Video Art compared in terms of production innovation, design, and conceptual content.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Issues in New Genres
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Investigates issues in post-studio practices, including concepts of time, relational aesthetics, site-specificity, institutional critique, and the post-medium condition.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 9A. Recommended: Satisfactory completion of the Upper-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Art, Design, and Electronic Culture
allCourses.description: Introduction to historical and theoretical foundations of digital media art, tracing how information technologies seeded growth of new expressive medium. Considers how today's pervasive digital culture evolved through interdisciplinary collaborations between artists, engineers, scientists, scholars.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Cultural History of the Anthropocene
allCourses.description: A survey of the ongoing interactions between technological and social change through the 19th century and 20th century, with special attention to the history of computing, changing arts and cultural practices, and the idea of the Anthropocene.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Intelligences of Arts
allCourses.description: Introduces contemporary neuroscience and new approaches to cognition – embodied, enactive, extended, situated, distributed. Reviews the history of related  ethological, biological, psychological, technological, and philosophical traditions. Considers arts and cultural practices from these and other perspectives, and considers case studies.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Projects in New Technologies
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Working with media such as electronic still cameras, desktop publishing, faxes, satellites, virtual reality, digitized imaging. Cultural issues pertinent to the emergence of new technology (e.g., ethical concerns, social impact, copyright laws, nontraditional approaches to distribution, cyberpunk, global markets).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 65A. Recommended: ART 11B and ART 106A.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Topics in Game Design
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Investigates interaction paradigms, game mechanics, game development processes, and methods for analysis and critique of games; and provides opportunities for experimental game design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 106B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: World Building
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: Interdisciplinary approaches to working across the digital/nondigital boundary to create an alternate universe. Emphasis is on critical thinking, comprehensive planning, integration of multiple media, and narrative development.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 65A. Recommended: ART 11B. Recommended: ART 106A strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Projects in Installation
allCourses.description: Investigates interior installation in particular spaces. Working in teams, students install, discuss, and remove projects. Technical information and hands-on experience with various media is provided. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 40
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Filmmaking Pre-Production
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines the preparatory and planning stages of video production, including script writing, story boarding, location scouting, script breakdown, and budgeting. Projects may encompass one or more of these stages which will be explored through readings, discussions, and demonstrations. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 81A and ART 81B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Filmmaking Post-Production
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines procedures and techniques utilized in video production after principal shooting is completed, including effects processing, composting, sound design, and DVD authoring. Projects focus on these processes, and are explored through readings, discussions, and demonstrations. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 81A and ART 81B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Graphic Novel
allCourses.description: An intensive workshop during which students will create a short graphic novel, taking the process all the way from concept to publication. Course work will focus on understanding how narrative emerges from a combination of visual and textual elements.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 65A. Strongly recommended: ART 106C.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Place Making and Public Art
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: How do art interventions in public spaces inform our definition of "place" and develop culturally informed audiences? Students will engage in class projects and group investigations that question the traditional and institutional conceptual boundaries of exhibition/distribution.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 40 and ART 9A

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Filmmaking Advanced Project I
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Incorporating narrative structures in a multi-screen context. Students design and produce an active space in which activities will move from one screen to another. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 81A and ART 81B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Projects in Computer Painting
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Study and utilization of the computer as a digital sketchbook and design tool for the creation of paintings.  Discussion of the issues related to benefits and limitations of new technology in the art-making process.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C and ART 30A and ART 30B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Artist Books as Objects
allCourses.description: Are artist books still relevant in the contemporary creative community? Focusing on intellectual content and raw physicality, students will explore this question and image/text relationships by creating handmade one-of-a-kind or edition book projects utilizing various mechanical reproduction techniques.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 20A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 30A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 40"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 51"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 65A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 71A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 81A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 91"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "ART 9A"}]}

prerequisite_list.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Artist Archives
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Addresses ways in which artistic production and archival practice intermingle and overlap. Examines critical works on the nature of knowledge and the archive, and uncovers methodologies of knowledge production and how these inform what we think of as art.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C and ART 9A and ART 11A

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Studio Topics--Painting
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides an intensive and specialized working environment. Thematic issues and material strategies will be explored. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 30B
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Drawing
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Advanced studio problems in visual exploration. Students pursue individual solutions to self-defined and presubscribed projects. Techniques/materials are individual choice. Continual analysis of the personal process.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 20A
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Figure Drawing
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students develop technical skills in rendering the figure. Live model sessions and an introduction to anatomy. Investigates use of the figure in contemporary art. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 20A
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Figure Painting
allCourses.description: Students develop technical skills in painting the figure. Live model sessions and projects that investigate the use of the figure in contemporary art.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 150F

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Studio Topics--Sculpture
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides an intensive and specialized working environment. Thematic issues and material strategies will be explored.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 40
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Studio Topics: Photography
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focused investigation of a range of issues in photographic practice, with an emphasis on developing individual student projects, refining critical thinking, and conceptual framing. Technical topics covered as required. Readings, lectures, critiques, labs. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 71B
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Documentary Photography
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Documentary practice is examined through the realization of photo-based projects. Thematic focus of student's choosing will be refined through lectures, discussion, technical demonstrations, field trips, labs, and individual meetings.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 71B
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Public Image
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Strategies for artistic intervention in the public circulation of images are examined alongside the role images play in constructing public identity. Individual or collaborative student projects will be directed around course themes. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 71B
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Photographic Tableau
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines and develops photographic projects intended for traditional artistic venues (i.e., galleries and museums). In addition to exploring appropriate techniques and presentation strategies, students consider the interdependency between construction of images and semantic shaping of traditional art venues. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 71B
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Constructed Image
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: A studio investigation of theoretical ideas, critical possibilities, historical precedents, and various techniques involving the production of fabricated images. Techniques may include montage, digital, chemical and in-camera manipulations, studio constructions, appropriations, performance, and projected images. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 71B
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Seminar Production Component
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Photographic and/or inter-media production course tied to a specific Issues course (for example, Issues in Photography, Issues in Feminism, Issues in New Genres). Critiques, labs, field trips, discussion, demonstrations. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 71B
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Filmmaking Advanced Project II
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Directed to the production of individual or collaborative videotapes, using studio, portable camera, editing facilities, and sound and computer elements. Emphasis will be on individually initiated projects. Readings and screenings are assigned. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 81A and ART 81B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Studio Topics: Performance
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: An intensive investigation of the practice of performance art, with an emphasis on the development of individual projects, and the refinement of various technical skills, as well as audiences, spaces, and cultural connections.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 91 or ART 109 or ART 128
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Studio Topics: Ceramic Sculpture
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of ideas, techniques, and personal control of form. Clay body, fabrication, glazing, and firing.  Emphasis on development of personal direction. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 51
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Filmmaking Web Series
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Original video projects produced in collaborative teams combining advanced video students with students from other areas, including Dance, Drama, and Music. Shoots may be carried out on the video stage as well as field locations. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 81A and ART 81B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Advanced Projects
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students working in different mediums focus on ambitious research, planning, development, and experimentation, leading to a single work or focused series that is large in scope. The project is exhibited and documented at the end of the quarter.  Materials fee.

prerequisite_list.title: Senior Projects and Critique in Photography
Senior Projects and Critique in Video

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Critical Aesthetics
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Surveys critical thought that has influenced twentieth-century art production, preparing the student to engage contemporary art with a critical eye, specifically addressing aesthetic and political debates of the historical avant-garde, the neo-avant garde, and postmodern culture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C

prerequisite_list.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Senior Project and Critique
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Directed-study critique class in preparation for final project and life after graduation; documentation and portfolio preparation for graduate school. Investigation of exhibition spaces and funding opportunities, participation in artists' communities outside the university, and artists' rights issues.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Senior Projects and Critique in Photography
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Directed group study focused on production of photographic projects of significant scope and ambition. Emphasis on preparation for continued study and/or practice in photography in advanced settings beyond the undergraduate university experience. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 1A and ART 1B and ART 1C and ART 71A and ART 71B

prerequisite_list.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice

allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Senior Projects and Critique in Video
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Art Majors only.
allCourses.description: Directed group study focused on production and exhibition of individual video projects of significant scope and ambition. Emphasis is placed on critical evaluation.  Assignments include work documentation, graduate school preparation, and investigation for future opportunities outside the University.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 81A and ART 81B
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Studio Problems: Methods and Materials
allCourses.restriction: Art majors only.
allCourses.description: An open media discussion and critique course emphasizing the development of working ideas and the execution of projects in all media. Readings assigned as required; field trips, slide and film/video presentations are integral.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Two intermediate ART courses.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Art Internship
allCourses.restriction: Juniors only.
allCourses.description: Under faculty supervision, students participate directly in a variety of art institution settings, including museums, galleries, and nonprofit organizations.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Honors Exhibition
allCourses.restriction: School of Arts Honors students only. Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Preparation, installation, and participation in the annual honors exhibition. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Individual study or directed creative projects as arranged with faculty member. Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: First in a three-quarter foundation sequence introducing students to a broad range of contemporary art, media, and practices in relation to their 20th-century cultural and historical antecedents. ART 1A deals specifically with contemporary painting and photography.

prerequisite_for.title: Senior Projects and Critique in Photography

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Deals with film/video/performance. Concerned with the development of modern/contemporary film, video, and performance, with a focus on experimental and avant-garde production from the early 20th century to today.

prerequisite_for.title: Senior Projects and Critique in Photography

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Art in Context: History, Theory, and Practice
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Third in a three-quarter foundation sequence introducing students to a broad range of contemporary art, media, and practice in relation to their 20th-century cultural and historical antecedents. Deals specifically with space and cyberspace.

prerequisite_for.title: Senior Projects and Critique in Photography

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Basic Drawing I
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Encourages an investigation of the premises and limits of drawing, primarily, but not inevitably, as a two-dimensional medium. Includes slide presentations and discussions of the historical uses of a wide range of drawing. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Basic Drawing II
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Continuation of the investigation initiated in ART 20A, with an emphasis on experimentation, personal investigation, and development of conceptual working premises, as well as the acquisition of necessary skills. Group discussion and critique are emphasized. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 20A

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: First-Year Graduate Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introductory theory class to contemporary art: intellectual history, theoretical antecedents, and current critical concerns.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Methods and Materials Workshop
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Comprised of a series of workshops introducing graduates to production and facilities in photography, video, digital media, and sculpture.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Graduate Seminar Topics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: In-depth discussion of contemporary art production in relation to a variety of theoretical, cultural, and historical topics. Material is determined by the given instructor's current research interest. Topics vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Graduate Seminar: Issues in Contemporary Art
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Classroom interaction with artists, curators, critics, lecturers from fields outside of the arts or from cross-disciplines. Includes recommended readings, discussions, panel participation, writing assignments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 210. ART 210 with a grade of B- or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Graduate Group Critique
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focus on studio production. Students are expected to help foster and develop an environment in which serious and sophisticated peer critique can take place.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 9 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Graduate Topics in Studio Production
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Graduate group study of a specific medium or art practice (e.g., painting; video, installation, photography, sculpture/3D, performance, digital media, public art, sound art; film). Includes consideration of technical, theoretical, historical, and/or formal issues.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Interdisciplinary Projects
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intensive faculty-led discussion of in-progress graduate studio projects--can be discipline driven or working across fields in a rigorous interdisciplinary studio environment where students meet with the professor both individually and in small groups.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Directed Reading and Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent study with a supervising faculty member to direct academic research, develop bibliographies, and discuss assigned readings.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Special Topics Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed reading and/or study group on a given research topic. Agreed-upon meeting structure may be flexible in order to accommodate off-campus field trips and travel.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Graduate Interdisciplinary and Collaborative Projects
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: For graduate students working collaboratively across the School of the Arts or cross-university. May be team taught with one of the faculty members based in the Department of Art.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Curatorial Projects
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
