allCourses.description: Independent or group study for graduates working on or developing curatorial projects.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Graduate Thesis Writing Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminar for writing as a component of the thesis. Different models of writing, text, and spoken word will be discussed. Required second year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 210 and ART 215 and ART 220. ART 210 with a grade of B- or better. ART 215 with a grade of B- or better. ART 220 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Graduate Thesis Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Tutorials and directed study in thesis writing, research and/or studio production with thesis committee chair and/or thesis committee members to be taken during final quarters of study.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 210 and ART 215 and ART 220. ART 210 with a grade of B- or better. ART 215 with a grade of B- or better. ART 220 with a grade of B- or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Graduate Thesis, Exhibition Critique
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Group critique required for matriculating M.F.A. students during the quarter in which their thesis exhibitions are scheduled. Public presentation/lecture on student's work required.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 210 and ART 215 and ART 220 and ART 230 and ART 240 and ART 261 and ART 262. ART 210 with a grade of B- or better. ART 215 with a grade of B- or better. ART 220 with a grade of B- or better. ART 230 with a grade of B- or better. ART 240 with a grade of B- or better. ART 261 with a grade of B- or better. ART 262 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Critical and Curatorial Thesis Exhibition
allCourses.description: Intensive tutorial geared toward execution of professional gallery exhibition, which is one half of the degree requirement for the M.F.A. concentration in Critical and Curatorial Studies. Must be taken under direction of Committee Chair.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Contemporary Exhibition Systems
allCourses.description: Investigates contemporary case studies of curatorial practice. Sometimes taught in collaboration with a host institution. The history, theory and criticism or curatorial practice are tested through the explication of real exhibitions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 280A
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introduction to Exhibition Systems
allCourses.restriction: M.F.A. students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the basics of curating, covering the fundamentals of collection, research, fundraising, publicity, and installation. Also introduces the related categories of public programming and art criticism.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Basic Painting I
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examination of the fundamental components of painting: color, form, space, surface, scale, and content. Studio work, slide presentations, and critiques of student work. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Basic Painting II
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Further examinations of the essential qualities of painting: color, form, space, surface, scale, and content. Studio work, slide presentations, and critiques of student work. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 30A

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Associates working under the active guidance and supervision of a regular rank faculty member responsible for curriculum and instruction at the University.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Beginning Sculpture
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The practice of sculpture in the contemporary arts; inclusion of spatial interventions, site-specific and environmental design, appropriation of found materials; techniques in cutting joining, and assembly of wood, metals, and plastics. May include casting, welding, and ceramics. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Matter and Media
allCourses.description: A project-based introduction to tools and approaches for creating and sharing digital media content within internet-mediated social environments, with a particular emphasis on art-making and personal expression. Includes an overview of basic user experience and interaction design principles.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Interaction and Experience
allCourses.description: An overview of digital video and audio production for the Web, emphasizing art-making and personal expression. Includes digital media aesthetics and conceptual design, basic audio and video recording, and fundamentals of desktop video, audio, and Web authoring software applications.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Media: Interaction Design
allCourses.description: Principles and practices of interaction design for interactive digital media systems that provide for active involvement of the participant. Students gain experience with interaction design issues through a series of media art projects, emphasizing art-making and personal expression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 12A and ART 12B and ART 50A and ART 50B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Basic Ceramic Sculpture
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Exploration of use of clay as sculptural basis with an emphasis on development of an idea and its relation to contemporary and experimental art practice. Hand-building, glazing, finishing processes, and use of other structural materials. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Foundations in Media Design
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of media design in the digital age, covering principles of design for different media (2D, time-based, interactive); history of relationship between art and design; and practice in working with different design approaches. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Foundations in Internet Art and Design
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to creating art for the Internet, covering history and structure of networks; key types of net-based interactivity; basics of Web design and scripting.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Gizmology and Kinetics
allCourses.description: Provides students with basic skills in materials, construction and design applicable to making machines, musical instruments and things with moving parts enabling work in kinetic sculpture, custom interactive systems, Mechatronics, Robotics, and Maker/DIY culture. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Mechatronic Art I
allCourses.description: Introduces the practice and theory of analog electronics, emphasizing the design and development of simple interactive systems and the integration of such systems into real-world contexts of performance, installation, sculpture, and automated artifacts. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introduction to Photography I
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to technical underpinnings emphasizing photography as a contemporary art practice. Topics include 35mm non-automatic camera operation, exposure and lighting, black and white printing, introduction to digital photography, discussion of critical and historical issues. Materials fee.

prerequisite_for.title: Senior Projects and Critique in Photography

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introduction to Photography II
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Techniques covered include medium and large format cameras, digital photography, studio lighting, digital and analog color printing, mural room. Conceptual direction is developed through critiques, critical readings, discussions, slide lectures.  Materials fee.

prerequisite_for.title: Senior Projects and Critique in Photography

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Changing Creativity
allCourses.description: Explores creativity as a changing concept in historical and contemporary terms from the perspectives of producers, consumers, and institutions. Encompasses international perspectives and the role of new technologies in considering creativity as a resource for innovation and social change.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Filmmaking Production I
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to three production stages of video making.  Study of the narrative structure of cinema and acquisition of video production skills in camera, lighting, sound, and editing. Production work, readings, and screenings outside of class are assigned. Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Filmmaking Production II
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on video stage production, technical skills including camera operation, stage lighting, sound recording, and construction of basic scenic elements.  Emphasis is placed on the function and responsibilities of the production crew and proper working and safety procedures. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ART 81A

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Basic Performance Art
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Exploration of objects, gesture, action, text, image, and media to create narrative or non-narrative works. Elements of theory and history of performance art are discussed to illustrate techniques and styles to understand, identify, and articulate artistic vision and voice.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Basic Media
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic instruction in media or disciplines not otherwise represented in the regular curriculum. Topics vary according to the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Visual Culture: Media, Art, and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines creative activities in all spheres of life, including the "artistic" impulses that dwell in the individual. Culture is addressed in broad terms of the many institutions and cultural forces that shape everyday activities of listening, seeing, doing.

prerequisite_for.title: Topics in History of Contemporary Art
Issues in Media, Violence, and Fear

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Visual Culture: A Culture Divided
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, controversies flourished in the mainstream media over purportedly obscene art, anti-American writing, and moral decay, among other issues. Examines these new conflicts as they manifest themselves in public life and everyday experience.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Visual Culture: Thematic Investigations
allCourses.restriction: Art Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Considers a broad range of concerns and questions raised by various acts of appropriation in contemporary art and visual culture, such as originality, authenticity, authorship, translation, audience and aesthetics, temporal dimensions of a work, and context.

allCourses.title: Studies in Ancient Art
allCourses.description: Topics in Egyptian, Prehistoric, and Etruscan art of the Mediterranean area treated with specific reference to relevant cultural and historical settings.  Specialized courses in Greek and Roman art are also taught.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Ancient Egyptian Art and Archaeology
allCourses.description: Varying topics in ancient Egyptian art and archaeology, from the Predynastic Period through the Late Period. Developments in art and archaeology are analyzed through their sociopolitical and historical contexts.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Greek Art
allCourses.description: Topics in Greek art, architecture, and topography from the Prehistoric period through the end of the fourth century B.C.E.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Roman Art
allCourses.description: Topics in Hellenistic and Roman art and architecture; stresses historical and political background.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Medieval Art
allCourses.description: Specialized topics in Medieval art and architecture in Europe, the Mediterranean area, and the Near East between the fourth and fifteenth centuries.  Examples:  the Art of the Migration Period, Medieval City.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Later Roman and Byzantine Art: ca. 300-650
allCourses.description: Studies in the development of the art and architecture of the Late Roman and Byzantine Empires between ca. 300 and 650.

allCourses.title: Byzantine Art: 650-1450
allCourses.description: Studies in the development of the art and architecture of the Byzantine Empire between ca. 650 and 1450.

allCourses.title: Studies in Early Christian and Byzantine Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics on the development of the art and architecture of the Later Roman and Byzantine Empires between ca. 300 and 1453. Examples: Early Christian architecture, Byzantine painting.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Western Medieval Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics on the development of art and architecture in Western Europe between ca. 700 and 1400. Examples: Romanesque painting, Gothic architecture.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Renaissance and Baroque Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics on the art and architecture of Europe between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries. Examples: Renaissance and Baroque prints, Bruegel to Rubens.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Southern Renaissance Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics determined by individual faculty members exploring historical developments and individual artists of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries in Italy and Spain. Examples: Renaissance Venice, Age of Michelangelo.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Northern Renaissance Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics determined by individual faculty members exploring historical developments and individual artists of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries in Northern Europe. Examples: Late Medieval art, painting from Van Eyck to Bosch.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Southern Baroque Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics determined by individual faculty members exploring historical developments and individual artists of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries in Italy and Spain. Example: Rome in the seventeenth century.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Northern Baroque Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics determined by individual faculty members exploring historical developments and individual artists of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries in Northern Europe. Example: the Age of Rembrandt.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Early Modern European Art: Age of Absolutism
allCourses.description: History of European painting, sculpture, and architecture from 1643 to 1789, during the emergence of nation states dominated by kings and court.

allCourses.title: Modern European Art: From Revolution to Realism
allCourses.description: History of European painting and other arts from 1789 to 1851, as the continent lurched through revolution, reaction, and the birth of modern societies and sensibilities.

allCourses.title: Modern European Art: From Impressionism to the Fauves
allCourses.description: History of European painting and urban transformation from 1851 to 1907, when Paris stood strong as the unquestioned cultural capital of the nineteenth century.

allCourses.title: Modern European Art: From Cubism to Surrealism
allCourses.description: History of European painting, sculpture, and design from 1907 to 1940, when Paris and painting lost their dominance as other cultural centers and other media claimed renewed importance.

allCourses.title: Topics in Modern European Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics within the period 1643 to 1940.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Contemporary Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics exploring historical developments of contemporary art from 1945 to the present. Examples: American Art 1945-1989, European Art 1945-1989, Art After 1989. Works of art are studied as cultural, social, and political practices.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Contemporary Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics exploring artistic movements, artists, and/or issues in contemporary art from 1945 to the present. Examples include Junk Art, Countercultures, Art and Politics Now. Works of art are studied as cultural, social, and political practices.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Modern Architecture
allCourses.description: Architecture and related design practices from the late eighteenth century through 1945 are studied in relation to social, aesthetic, technological, and political questions.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Architecture after 1945
allCourses.description: Architecture and related design practices from 1945 through present are studied in relation to social, aesthetic, technological, and political questions.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Modern and Contemporary Architecture
allCourses.description: Varying topics from the late eighteenth century to the present. Architecture and related design practices are studied in relation to social, aesthetic, technological, and political questions.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Asian Art
allCourses.description: Topics include visual studies in China, Japan, Korea and India.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Ancient China
allCourses.description: Examines the early history of Chinese art, focusing on the development and uses of art and material culture to express political, social, and religious beliefs, particularly in art made for the court, tomb, and temple.

allCourses.title: Later Imperial China
allCourses.description: Investigates the uses, subjects, styles, and social contexts of art made in the later Imperial dynasties, whether court art, religious art, women's painting, scholar painting, or art for the market.

allCourses.title: Modern China
allCourses.description: Examines the evolution and media of Chinese art and visual culture in the context of modern China's sweeping historical, social, and political changes.

allCourses.title: Ancient India
allCourses.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan.  Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

allCourses.title: Medieval India
allCourses.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

allCourses.title: Modern India
allCourses.description: Examines the imperial patronage of the Mughal emperors, covering their territorial holdings extending from Afghanistan through western Bangladesh.  Continues with the "aftermath" of the Mughal empire and the rise of British commercialism and colonialism.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Art and Architecture of India
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Art and Architecture of India. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Art and Globalization, Modern
allCourses.description: Study of modern art as a cause and expression of increasing contacts between cultures. Focusing on regions in Asia and the Americas, adoption of European oil painting, indigenous art movements, and national capital architecture are explored.

allCourses.title: Early Modern Japan
allCourses.description: Focuses on the Edo Period (1615-1868), an enormously productive time in the early modern development of Japanese art in woodblock prints, painting, and crafts. Topics include the image of the beautiful woman, kabuki actor prints, and intoxicated ink painting.

allCourses.title: Modern Japan
allCourses.description: Explores artistic developments during the tumultuous modernization of Japan from 1868-1945, with a focus on painting, commercial art, and architecture. Topics include arts of the Japanese Empire, neo-traditional arts, responses to European modernism, and war propaganda.

allCourses.title: Contemporary Japan
allCourses.description: Study of various media of Japanese art from the time of war defeat in 1945 until the present. Topics include artists' responses to the nuclear bomb, the aesthetics of the "economic miracle," avant-garde groups, manga, and innovations in architecture.

allCourses.title: Asian American Art, Contemporary
allCourses.description: Study of the Asian American experience in contemporary art and visual culture. Art by Asian Americans of diverse backgrounds as well as the history of visualization of Asian identities in American art/visual culture.

allCourses.title: Modern African American Art
allCourses.description: Investigates the history of modern African American art; emphasis on the politics of representation. Examines art in a variety of media from material culture and textiles to painting and photography. Issues of migration, nationalism, gender, sexuality, and hybridity are discussed.

allCourses.title: Contemporary African American Art
allCourses.description: Investigates the history of contemporary African American art; emphasis on the politics of representation. Explores art in a variety of media: painting, sculpture, photography, installation, and new media. Cultural politics, appropriation, identity, gender, sexuality, hybridity and civil rights issues discussed.

allCourses.title: Topics in African American Art
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of African American Art. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: African American Women in Art
allCourses.description: Examines depictions of and by African American women in art and popular culture through a variety of media including textiles, painting, sculpture, photography, and installation. Focuses on African American women's experiences, perspectives, and strategies for contemporary representation.

allCourses.title: African Americans and Photography
allCourses.description: Explores depictions of and by African Americans through photography. Examines the history of photography in relationship to African American culture through a variety of media from early daguerreotype processes to digital imagery.

allCourses.title: Early American Art
allCourses.description: An examination of American visual culture from 1620 to 1860 from the era of European exploration and colonization of the New World to the beginning of the Civil War.

allCourses.title: Nineteenth Century American Art
allCourses.description: An exploration of American visual culture from 1860 to 1900, including paintings, sculpture, and photographs produced during the Civil War and during the decades of prosperity that followed.

allCourses.title: Modern American Art
allCourses.description: Focusing on the period from 1900 until 1965, this course considers the emergence and institutionalization of modern art in the United States.

allCourses.title: Topics in American Art
allCourses.description: Varying topics within the period 1620 to 1970. Works of art are studied in their cultural, social, and political contexts.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Modern Latin American and Latinx Art
allCourses.description: Varying topics exploring the history of modernism in Latin American and Latinx visual art. Art movements and artworks are analyzed through their socio-political and historical contexts with a special attention to race, ethnicity, gender, and migration.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Studies in Native and Tribal Art
allCourses.description: Varying topics on the art and culture of native and tribal societies. For example, North American Indians.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Criticism of Art
allCourses.description: Selected topics discussed on the theoretical and/or practical dimensions of art historical criticism.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Museum Studies
allCourses.description: Addresses the historical and contemporary function of the museum as an instructional device.  The function of exhibitions in the public sphere, and the roles of curators, educators, and the public are analyzed.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Nineteenth-Century Photographic History
allCourses.description: Varying topics within the history of photography in the nineteenth century. Photographic practice studied in relation to art history, cultural history, and social history.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: 20th Century Photographic History
allCourses.description: Varying topics within the history of photography in the 20th century. Photographic practice studied in relation to art history, cultural history, and social history.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Selected Topics in Photographic History
allCourses.description: Varying topics within the history of photography from the early 19th century to the present. Photographic practice studied in relation to art history, cultural history, and social history. Examples include documentary; pictorialism and art photography; photomontage, photographic books.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Visual Studies
allCourses.description: Interdisciplinary topics on the cultural analysis of visual artifacts and practices.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Art History Methods
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Art History Majors only.
allCourses.description: Theory and practice of art history, with an emphasis on formal and social models of analyzing and writing about art.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_for.title: Senior Seminar in Gender and Sexuality Studies

allCourses.title: Ethics, Law, and Art
allCourses.description: Addresses a broad range of ethical and legal issues pertaining to art, ownership, looting and theft, museum policies, and cultural heritage.

allCourses.title: Art History Social Hour
allCourses.description: Students meet members of the faculty and Art History Undergraduate Association, and explore the exceptional opportunities available for internships, independent research, and field trips through the Art History Department’s Steckler Family endowment.

allCourses.title: Advanced Seminar: Topics in Art History
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Art History Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Discussion and report-oriented seminar with emphasis on reading, writing, and thinking about problems in art history. Examples: Gothic Cathedral, Portraiture East and West.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: ART HIS 190W.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study in Art History
allCourses.restriction: Art History Majors only.
allCourses.description: Supervised, but independent reading or research on art historical topics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Ancient India
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan. Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

allCourses.title: Medieval India
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

allCourses.title: Ethics, Law, and Art
allCourses.description: Addresses a broad range of ethical and legal issues pertaining to art, ownership, looting and theft, museum policies, and cultural heritage.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Background in Art History or Legal Studies.

allCourses.title: Master's Seminar: Topics in Art History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Art History. Examples include Gothic Cathedral, Portraiture East and West.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Master's Thesis Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Research and writing of the Master's thesis.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Latin American Art and Architecture: 1492 to the Present
allCourses.description: Charts the history of Latin American art and architecture from the invasion of the Americas in 1492 to the present. It examines the production of visual art in relation to colonization, imperialism, migration, international exchange, and racial formation.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to teaching assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Ancient Greek and Roman Art, and Architecture
allCourses.description: An overview of Greek and Roman art, and related ancient visual cultures. Considers how and why the peoples of antiquity created art and architecture, as well as the significance of these works within their social, religious, and historical contexts.

allCourses.title: Arts of Europe: Medieval and Renaissance
allCourses.description: Focuses on the art of the Mediterranean area and Europe between ca. A.D. 350 and 1600. By means of movements and artists, examines the cultural identities of the Christian, Islamic, and Early Modern worlds.

allCourses.title: Early Modern and Modern Art in Europe and America
allCourses.description: The visual arts from the 17th to the 21st centuries. Explores the purposes and meaning of painting, sculpture, and architecture in relation to artists, viewers, and historical events.

allCourses.title: History of Asian Art: Arts of India
allCourses.description: Emphasizing Hindu, Buddhist, and Islamic art of greater India (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka) from proto-historic to modern times. Themes include art as a source of history, commercial and religious pan-Asian connections, nationalism, and modern versus historical identities.

allCourses.title: History of Asian Art: Arts of China
allCourses.description: An introduction to the arts and visual culture of China from Neolithic to modern times. Themes includes the representation of power, death and the afterlife, popular culture and elite arts, landscape and women's painting, and concludes with contemporary China.

allCourses.title: History of Asian Art: Arts of Japan
allCourses.description: Examines compelling images and objects of spirit and power created in Japan over many centuries. Themes include Buddhist icons, narrative illustration, popular prints, architecture, manga, and the avant-garde. Japanese interactions with Korean, Chinese, and European culture are emphasized.

allCourses.title: History of Asian Art: Arts of Islam
allCourses.description: Examines past and present Islamic art, spanning 1,500 years and extending from the Americas through Indonesia. Themes include Islam as a globalizing force, the definition of "Islamic," and the competing roles of religion and politics in making art.

allCourses.title: Art and Archaeology of Ancient Persia, Egypt, and Mesopotamia
allCourses.description: An introduction to the art and archaeology of ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia, Anatolia, Persia, and the wider Iranian world from the Neolithic to the coming of Islam. Considers wider impact on the ancient and early medieval worlds and their present legacy.

allCourses.title: Arts of Korea
allCourses.description: Introduction to the arts and visual culture of Korea from the Neolithic period to the Joseon Dynasty. Themes include the conceptions of life, death, and afterlife, expressions of power and privilege, leisure, knowledge, and trade.

allCourses.title: Image Collision: A Multicultural Approach to Images and Their Users
allCourses.description: Comparisons between present-day visual culture and pre-modern art to re-evaluate the ways in which one understands the contemporary histories of underrepresented groups in the United States.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Ancient Egyptian Archaeology and Art
allCourses.description: Introduction to the art and archaeology of ancient Egypt from prehistory through the Late Period. Themes covered include kingship and monumentality, the materialization of religious beliefs and practices, and non-royal and non-elite cultural expression.

allCourses.title: Disneyland
allCourses.description: From Dole Whips to roller coasters, the focus is on the innovations in industrial automation and manufacturing that made Disneyland’s attractions possible. Discusses fandom, guest experiences, operating procedures, technical and design patents, and how rides work.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: ArtsCore
allCourses.description: An introduction to the arts in general, and to the arts at UCI. Concentration on (1) the interdisciplinary nature of the arts, and (2) the content of particular arts disciplines.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Senior Thesis
allCourses.restriction: School of the Arts majors only.
allCourses.description: Planning, drafting, writing, and presentation of an academic thesis.  Open to students who will interrelate two or more artistic disciplines, and to Campuswide Honors Program students who will focus their thesis on one or more major areas in the Arts.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Senior Thesis
allCourses.restriction: School of the Arts majors only.
allCourses.description: Planning, drafting, writing, and presentation of an academic thesis.  Open to students who will interrelate two or more artistic disciplines, and to Campuswide Honors Program students who will focus their thesis on one or more major areas in the Arts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARTS 100A.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Senior Thesis
allCourses.restriction: School of the Arts majors only.
allCourses.description: Planning, drafting, writing, and presentation of an academic thesis.  Open to students who will interrelate two or more artistic disciplines, and to Campuswide Honors Program students who will focus their thesis on one or more major areas in the Arts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARTS 100B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Media: History and Foundations
allCourses.description: Introduction to historical and theoretical foundations of digital media art, tracing how information technologies seeded growth of new expressive medium. Considers how today's pervasive digital culture evolved through interdisciplinary collaborations between artists, engineers, scientists, scholars.  Course may be offered online.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Media: Current Directions
allCourses.description: An overview of current practice and research in digital media art. Examines the effects of recent technological, scientific, cultural, and political developments. Addresses the increasing overlap of artistic and scientific practices and issues related to new and emerging technologies.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Athletics Bands
allCourses.description: Bands support athletics events. Includes Pep Band: Rehearsal and performance of band standards; Marching Band: Exercises and performance involving marching fundamentals, formations, and half-time pageantry; and, Drumline: Study and rehearsal of rudiments, cadences, and arrangements.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Individual study or directed projects as arranged with faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Media:  Experience and Content
allCourses.description: A project-based introduction to tools and approaches for creating and sharing digital media content within Internet-mediated social environments, with a particular emphasis on art-making and personal expression.  Includes an overview of basic user experience and interaction design principles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARTS 11 and ARTS 12.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Media: Video and Audio for the Web
allCourses.description: An overview of digital video and audio production for the Web, emphasizing art-making and personal expression.  Includes digital media aesthetics and conceptual design, basic audio and video recording, and fundamentals of desktop video, audio, and Web authoring software applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARTS 11 and ARTS 12 and ARTS 50.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Media: Interaction Design
allCourses.description: Principles and practices of interaction design for interactive digital media systems that provide for active involvement of the participant.  Students gain experience with interaction design issues through a series of media art projects, emphasizing art-making and personal expression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ARTS 11 and ARTS 12 and ARTS 50 and ARTS 60.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Digital Media: Exhibition
allCourses.description: A discussion and critique course in all media arts. Includes a review of key media arts concepts and the preparation of an end-of-quarter exhibition.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Proposal submission required.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Art, Technology, and Science
allCourses.description: Explores development and impact of art and computer technology on society and culture from nineteenth century to present. Covers history of moving images, time-based and experimental media arts viewed in conjunction with progression of science and digital technologies.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Improvisation and Modes of Research / Creative Expression
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only. Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Through immersion, readings, analysis, and observation, students are trained to recognize, build, and engage a set of “improvisatory” cognitive skills in order to enhance artistic creation, the generation of language, data analysis, and the application of the scientific method.

allCourses.title: Research Methodologies for Asian American Studies
allCourses.description: Explores various research methodologies for Asian American Studies combining theoretical knowledge with field research. Goals: conduct field research about immigrants and refugees from Asia. Topics vary: migration and labor, assimilation and cultural preservation, cultural expressions in the diaspora.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_for.title: Senior Seminar in Gender and Sexuality Studies

allCourses.title: Asian American Writers
allCourses.description: Literary analysis of Asian American writers' representations of issues of identity, class, history among others. Variety of literary forms—novel, poem, drama, essay—included in a study of a variety of Asian American ethnic groups.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian American History
allCourses.description: Introduction to important themes in the history of people of Asian ancestry in the United States from the nineteenth century to the present.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian American Art History
allCourses.description: Investigation of Asian American experience expressed by art and visual culture throughout the twentieth century. Art by Asian Americans of diverse backgrounds as well as the history of cultural visualization of Asian identities in American art/visual culture.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Asian American Film and Video
allCourses.description: Topics include histories of Asian American film and video, including documentaries, experimental, short subjects, feature-length independent film, and other forms of cinematic expression. Explores issues of identity (national, racial, gendered, among others).
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian American Media and Arts
allCourses.description: Includes the study of Asian American history and society through the analysis of a variety of media forms such as painting, music, cinema, video, and other artistic representations.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian Americans and Popular Culture
allCourses.description: Focuses on Asian Americans' relationship to popular culture as both producers and consumers. Topics include consumer cultures and subcultures, cyberspace and public space, popular music, indy comics and other print media.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Sexuality in Asian and Asian American Film and Video
allCourses.description: Analyzes sexuality and gender roles in specific social, historical, and political contexts represented in selected Asian and Asian American films and videos, in terms of feminine/masculine constructions, the body, family roles.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Race and Performance
allCourses.description: Focuses on new ways of understanding race, ethnicity, class, and gender issues through performance.

allCourses.title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
allCourses.description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

allCourses.title: Asian American Politics
allCourses.description: Provides various overviews of politics within Asian American communities. May compare with African American and/or Latino politics.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Comparative Minority Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the political experiences of Blacks, Latinos, and Asian Americans in the United States from roughly 1950 to the present. Focuses on how each group has pursued political empowerment via both conventional political channels and social movements.

allCourses.title: Asian American Community Public Health
allCourses.description: Focuses on major issues and concepts of community health and their application to public health programs for Asian American populations. Analyzes individual, institutional, community, and policy factors that influence a person's health status within a larger environmental context.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Asian American Social Sciences and Social Ecology
allCourses.description: Explores a broad range of issues in Asian American social sciences and social ecology.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian American Labor
allCourses.description: Explores history of Asian Americans and work from the nineteenth century to the present. Areas of study include migration, colonialism, family, social organization, and work culture.

allCourses.title: Race and Urban Space
allCourses.description: Examines how ethnic and racial processes shape and structure interactions in urban settings, such as schools, housing, employment, and public spaces, with attention to the international impact of globalization and postcolonial forces.

allCourses.title: Asian Americans and Education
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the major issues facing Asian Americans in K-16 education and schooling experiences through scientific, historical, and interdisciplinary approaches, in both mainstream and minority education.

allCourses.title: Asian American Psychology
allCourses.description: Examines the social and psychological concerns of Asian Americans; e.g., coping with racial prejudice, maintaining bicultural identities, dealing with cross-cultural conflicts in interracial relationships, and trying to reconcile generational differences between immigrant parents and their American-born children.

allCourses.title: Arabs and Muslims in the US
allCourses.description: Offers a critical academic study of Islam in America, focusing on the core tenets of belief, the diversity of practices, and historical transformations that have taken place since the arrival of Muslims in the United States.

allCourses.title: Religious Traditions of Asian Americans
allCourses.description: Studies the religious traditions of Asian Americans, focusing on the transplantation of religious institutions, establishment of sacred spaces, celebration of religious holidays, socialization of children, as well as birth, marriage, gender relations, death, family.

allCourses.title: The Politics of Protest
allCourses.description: Examines the Civil Rights, Black Power, and women’s movements in relationship to the Asian American movement. Uses social movement theories to illuminate the cases, and the cases to critique and revise the theories.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Asian American Studies
allCourses.description: Analyzes a variety of themes in Asian American Studies—identity, history, culture—from various interdisciplinary perspectives in humanities, arts, social sciences.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian American Ethnic Groups
allCourses.description: Topics include study of the history, culture, and social formations of diverse Asian American subgroups such as Pacific Islanders, Hmong, Thai, Indonesian, Indian subcontinental, among others.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Korean American Studies
allCourses.description: Explores the factors that have distinctly shaped the Korean American experience, including patterns of racial domination, the profile of immigrant flow, immigrant roles in the urban political economy, politics in Korea, and the role of the church.

allCourses.title: Vietnamese American Studies
allCourses.description: Studies the resettlement of Vietnamese in the United States following their exodus from Southeast Asia. Topics include the Vietnam War, the 1975 evacuation, boat and land refugees, the shaping of Vietnamese communities, and Vietnamese American literature.

allCourses.title: Japanese American Studies
allCourses.description: Studies the settlement of Japanese in Hawaii and the continental United States since the late 19th century. Topics include sugar plantations, development of rural Japanese America, World War II internment, post-War community development, and persistence of Japanese American identity.

allCourses.title: South Asian American Studies
allCourses.restriction: Asian American Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines and compares the experiences of South Asian immigrants in the U.S. over time. Looks at the economic, political, and social positions of the immigrants, with special emphasis on religious changes and the changes in the second and later generations.

allCourses.title: Southeast Asian American Studies
allCourses.description: Analyzes experiences of refugees and immigrants from Southeast Asia, which may include those from Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, and the Philippines. Examines political and economic factors for their exodus and how they reconstruct their identities, histories, and communities.

allCourses.title: Chinese American Studies
allCourses.description: Analyzes the experiences of Chinese in the United States. Immigration, Chinese exclusion, racial and gender identity. Historical overview and contemporary issues covered.

allCourses.title: Filipina/Filipino American Studies
allCourses.description: Explores the experience of Filipina/Filipino Americans from the era of Spanish colonization of the Philippines to present-day community formations in the United States, with special emphasis on the 20th century. Topics include colonialism, nation, migration, gender, and culture.

allCourses.title: Ethnic and Racial Communities
allCourses.description: Examines various theoretical analyses of race and ethnicity, particularly as they apply to Asian Americans. Also explores the relationship of Asian Americans to other racialized minorities in the U.S.

allCourses.title: Asian American Women
allCourses.description: Examines the representations and experiences of Asian American women from diverse perspectives. Explores the commonalities and differences among various groups of Asian American women, with particular focus on history, culture, values, and family roles.

allCourses.title: Asian American Women's Film
allCourses.description: Explores the significance of film and video made by Asian American women in relation to race, representation, and social change. These film and video makers use media to raise complex issues of class, politics, and race interacting with gender.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Intersectionality
allCourses.description: Topics include intersectional analysis of various themes related to ethnicity, gender, sexuality, and race within Asian American communities.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Race and Citizenship
allCourses.description: Explores historical and contemporary patterns of racialization in relation to citizenship. Topics may include racial categorization, immigration, and comparative racialization.

allCourses.title: Asian American and African American Relations
allCourses.description: Addresses relationships of Asian American and African American communities in the United States. Topics include race, class, gender, labor, economic systems, political mobilization, community, civil rights, activism, cultural expression.

allCourses.title: Politics of Animal Rights
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Asian American Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines animal rights/welfare movement’s efforts to transform moral, practical, and legal standing of nonhuman animals in contemporary U.S. Explores intersection of racism, sexism, and speciesism informed by theories of race and ethnicity, including Asian American Studies.

allCourses.title: Migration Destinations
allCourses.description: Examines the migration patterns to the three largest nations that receive immigrants (i.e., permanent settlers): Australia, Canada, and the United States.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty member. Substantial written work required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Theory and Methods in Asian American Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the intersection of the social sciences, humanities, and other fields that constitute the theory and methodology of Asian American Studies. Focuses on the interventions and contestations within Asian American Studies that have transformed the discipline in recent years.

allCourses.title: Contemporary Issues in Asian American Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the interrelations between history, theory, and race in the aftermath of the twentieth-century decolonial movements, offering an account of race through postcolonial and postnationalist approaches in comparative contexts. Considers the interventions made by transnational feminist and racialized queer critiques.

allCourses.title: Leadership and Social Change in Asian American Communities
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to models of community-engaged learning and leadership that are central to the field of Asian American studies. Designed to expose students to histories and models of organizing in Asian American communities and forms of community-based research.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Asian American Studies Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to research topics and methods within the field of Asian American studies. Aims to expose students to core and affiliated faculty to help them identify possible advisors for master's research projects or members of doctoral committees.

allCourses.title: Graduate Topics in Asian American Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminars on various topics in Asian American Studies.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Globalization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines immigration to three leading immigrant-receiving nations: the United States, Canada, and Australia, as both cause and consequence of globalization. Specific attention to Asian migration, as well as assimilation and its relationship to multiculturalism.

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Asian American Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminar covering various areas of research within Asian American Studies as an interdisciplinary field. Recommended for advanced graduate students.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Directed Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed graduate study/research in Asian American Studies.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 24 units.

allCourses.title: Directed Reading
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Readings focused on specialized topics in consultation with, and with the consent of, a faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Emphasis in Asian American Studies graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to teaching assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Asian American Histories
allCourses.description: Examines and compares diverse experiences of major Asian American groups since the mid-nineteenth century. Topics include origins of emigration; the formation and transformation of community; gender and family life; changing roles of Asian Americans in American society. Formerly ASIANAM 60A.

allCourses.title: The U.S. and Asia
allCourses.description: Explores the historical and contemporary transnational linkages between the U.S. and regions in Asia and their resultant flows of people, goods, and ideas. Attention given to the role of militarism and processes of globalization, and the histories of cultural contact/conflict.

allCourses.title: Asian American Communities
allCourses.description: Examines the renewal of Asian immigration following World War II. Explores contemporary Asian American populations and communities in the U.S., and the impact of contemporary Asian immigration on the U.S. political economy and social order.

allCourses.title: Asian Americans and Race
allCourses.description: Analyzes the Asian American experience in comparative perspective, which includes comparisons of different ethnic and racial groups, and across gender and class. Possible topics include labor, economy, politics, migration, nation, popular culture, gender, family, sexuality, and multiraciality.

allCourses.title: Asian American Stories
allCourses.description: Examines stories from Asian American communities through literary texts and other media. Selected themes may include the following: dislocation/relocation, finding/inventing a usable past, poetics/politics in language, identities/ethnicities.

allCourses.title: Asian Americans and the Media
allCourses.description: Investigates popular representations of and cultural productions by Asian Pacific Americans and Asians in the Americas from the late-19th century to the present. Cultural media may include political cartoons, film/television, popular music, visual art, blogs/Web sites, and performance.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Business Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides overview of the field of business analytics, and the theory and practice underpinnings of the three MSBA curricular tracks: Data Analytics, Marketing Analytics, and Operations Analytics. Provides students with a working knowledge of the R programming language.

allCourses.title: Statistics for Data Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Methods of statistical inference, emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Topics include classical estimation and hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, decision analysis, and forecasting.

allCourses.title: Management Science for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to computer-based models for decision making. Topics include optimization (linear programming, integer programming, network flow models) and computer simulation. Uses spreadsheets extensively, including Excel built-in and add-in packages.

allCourses.title: Microeconomics for Business Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides basic tools for analyzing economic decisions of consumers and firms. Topics include demand and supply analysis, production and cost theory, perfect competition, monopoly, market failures, and introductory game theory.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Marketing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the field of marketing. Objectives include developing familiarity with fundamental concepts, theories, and techniques in marketing, and acquainting students with the type of decisions made by marketing managers, including customer targeting, product, pricing, distribution, promotion, and research.

allCourses.title: Operations Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to strategic and tactical issues in production and operations management. A blend of quantitative and qualitative considerations. Topics include product planning, process design, capacity management, production planning, inventory control, distribution management, just-in-time manufacturing, quality management.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students in the Merage School Master of Science in Business Analytics program with information and practical skills for success in the MSBA program and for business career planning.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Data and Programming for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Challenges and teaches students how to handle data, from initial data acquisition to final data analysis. Provides students with a working knowledge of the Python programming language.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Basic familiarity with programming is recommended.

allCourses.title: Business Analytics Internship
allCourses.restriction: Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students apply analytics and big data knowledge obtained from classroom theory through work experiences. Provides knowledge of career opportunities, an understanding of the role analytics plays in business environments, and preparation for the business analytics profession.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Marketing on the Internet for Business Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the impact of the Internet on traditional methods of doing marketing, and explores its existing and future uses. Discusses how to capitalize on and increase the Internet's utility as a tool that can increase marketing effectiveness, efficiency, and competitiveness.

allCourses.title: Marketing Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to quantitative marketing analytics methods and teaches them how to apply the methods to business problems of interest. Topics include: resource allocation and ROI, marketing mix analytics, customer analytics, market segmentation and targeting, advertising, promotions, and digital marketing.

allCourses.title: Machine Learning for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces methods to mine data repositories for business intelligence to facilitate analytical decision-making. Topics include clustering for market segmentation, association rules to discover relationships between different purchase decisions, and  Naive-Bayes classification techniques for decision making using decision-trees.

allCourses.title: Deep Learning and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with an understanding of specific topics in machine learning including networks and deep learning, improving neural networks, structuring deep learning projects, and convolutional neural networks.

allCourses.title: Natural Language Processing and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on providing students knowledge of advanced techniques for data analytics. Students deepen their understanding of topics including: dimension reduction, text mining and topic modeling, sentiment analysis, collaborative filtering, and causal estimation.

allCourses.title: Customer and Social Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how business managers can leverage Web 2.0 and social media analytics to create value for their organizations and customers. Topics include digital and social strategies; Web and search analytics; display and mobile advertising; social networks and influence; social media.

allCourses.title: Business Data Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides essential knowledge for business managers to store and utilize data effectively. Aims to introduce the core concepts in databases, data warehouses, and big data on cloud. Offers an in-depth understanding of each technology’s core concepts with hands-on programming.

allCourses.title: Supply Chain Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the tools and strategies to effectively match supply and demand. Focuses on the coordination of material and information flows in supply chains. Recent innovations are also discussed, including globalization, the impact of electronic commerce, and sustainability issues.

allCourses.title: The Art and Science of Applied Forecast Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Covers core and advanced techniques of forecasting. Emphasizes the innovation required to develop accurate models, inspires the need to break rules, leverages ideation needed to discover data sources and engineer variables, and seeks ways to build new models.

allCourses.title: Predictive Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Deals with predicting entities (forecasting) and predicting membership of known groups (classification). Blends methodologies of forecasting and data mining, focusing on multiple regression, logistic regression, neural nets, ARIMA, discriminate analysis, and k-nearest neighbors, and applying these methods to managerial problems/decision-making.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Business Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of business analytics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Big Data Analytics with Hadoop
allCourses.restriction: Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: In-depth hands-on exploration of various cutting-edge information technologies used for big data analytics. Focuses on using Hadoop, Sqoop, Pig, and Hive for ETL operations and on understanding the MapReduce algorithm using Apache Mahout for data mining algorithms.

allCourses.title: Big Data Management Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introductory-level overview to the emerging technologies in database systems. Students gain critical insight into big data challenges, the choices of different systems and technologies available, relative advantages/disadvantages, and unique aspects of different systems.

allCourses.title: Business Analytics Capstone Prep
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Prep course for the required capstone project. Students apply the knowledge and methods acquired through the program’s coursework to an applied business analytics problem. Requirements include project selection, submission of project plan, and data collection/analysis.

allCourses.title: Business Analytics Capstone Project
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Analytics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Continuation of the capstone project. Students apply the knowledge and methods acquired through the coursework in the program to an applied business analytics problem. Work includes data analysis, completed research paper, and final presentation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BANA 298A. BANA 298A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Pathways in Biomedical and Translational Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides fundamental knowledge to promote understanding of the process of bringing discoveries to the bedside and then to the population, providing a fundamental basis for clinical and translational science.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Medical Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides understanding of medical statistics for clinicians; clinical and biomedical researchers to read and interpret literature.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Medical Statistics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides sufficient understanding of medical statistics to read and interpret medical literature critically, identify appropriate statistics for basic research designs used in medicine, and discriminate between appropriate and inappropriate statistical applications for common research designs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BATS 209A. BATS 209A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Clinical Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces principles and practice of clinical epidemiology and the population-based approach to health and disease.

allCourses.title: Design and Analysis of Clinical Trials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents history, organization and planning, rationale for methods, limits, and ethics in conducting clinical trials.

allCourses.title: Science Communication Skills for Clinical and Translational Scientists
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to train clinical and translational researchers to communicate their research effectively to expert audiences and community members, and creates opportunities for training in scientific writing, presenting scientific talks, or doing job interviews. Recommended elective for all MS-BATS students.

allCourses.title: Understanding the Pathobiology and Clinical Treatment of Skin Diseases
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides participants with the clinical presentation, biology, and treatment of skin disease. At the completion of the course, attendees are able to identify gaps in research and clinical care of skin diseases.

allCourses.title: Basic Science of the Skin
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides participants with a basic understanding of the structure and function of skin and the latest advances in skin biology.

allCourses.title: Comparative Effectiveness Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of comparative effectiveness research (CER) with in-depth methodologic clinical practice and policy/dissemination issues related to the conduct, interpretation, and clinical applications of CER.

allCourses.title: Comparative Effectiveness Research II
allCourses.description: Two-part course designed to provide a comprehensive overview of comparative effectiveness research (CER) with in-depth methodologic clinical practice and policy/dissemination issues related to the conduct, interpretation, and clinical applications of CER.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BATS 245A

allCourses.title: Measurement Science, Outcomes Research, and Advanced Applied Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Furthers the understanding of methodologic issues involved in the conducting of comparative effectiveness research (CER). Topics include risk adjustment, balancing observational study designs, use of outcomes from multiple data sources, innovations clinical trial designs, the conduct of meta-analysis, psychometric methods.

allCourses.title: Quality Efficiency and Cost Effectiveness
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the principles and practice of quality of care, patient safety, and patient experience research, along with major national and statewide policy and legislative initiatives related to quality of care and patient safety.

allCourses.title: Disparities in Health and Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews all aspects of culture that influence health status, development of public health policy, and management and practice of health care. Explores how race and ethnicity affect health and health care, including health care services and policies governing these services.

allCourses.title: Health Politics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Offers political and analytical insights into understanding U.S. health policymaking and developing strategies that influence health policy outcomes.

allCourses.title: Laboratory in Big Data Analysis for Health Services and Clinical Researchers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biomedical/Translational Sci Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces quantitative research methods, with an emphasis on large surveys and administrative health data sets. Presents the advantages and disadvantages of these data sources and the iterative process of formulating research questions and identifying data sources to answer these questions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BATS 209A

allCourses.title: Biomedical and Translational Science Seminar
allCourses.description: Students present their current research or a topic of interest and are exposed to diverse projects in the biomedical and translational science arena.

allCourses.title: Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the following topics from a biomedical perspective: protein and nucleic acid biochemistry, carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids, purines and pyrimidines, genome structure, molecular mechanisms of development, and signal transduction.

allCourses.title: Signal Transduction and Growth Control
allCourses.description: Covers various eukaryotic signaling pathways (tyrosine kinase, ras-raf-MAPK, TGF-ß, wnt, JAK-STAT, and FAS) with an emphasis on the experimental underpinnings. The material is covered in lectures and discussions of pertinent papers.

allCourses.title: Mouse Developmental Genetics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to using the mouse in contemporary biomedical research. The biology and development of the laboratory mouse, methods for manipulation of the mouse genome and embryos, and examples of application of these methods to understand mammalian development and homeostasis.

allCourses.title: Human Evolution and Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers theories and empirical research concerning the evolutionary origins of human behaviors and their variations. An interdisciplinary course emphasizing both evolutionary psychology (e.g., mating strategies, kinship, and parenting) and molecular evolution (i.e., evolution of genes for various behaviors).

allCourses.title: Epigenetics in Health and Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the role of chromatin/nuclear structure organization (histone and DNA modification, chromatin remodeling, higher order chromatin structure and nuclear organization) on gene regulation, DNA replication and repair, relevant to development, metabolism, learning and memory, and human disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 203 or MOL BIO 204 or NEURBIO 206. MOL BIO 203 with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 204 with a grade of B- or better. NEURBIO 206 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: New Breakthroughs in Basic and Translational Cancer Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Highlights breakthroughs in molecular and cellular aspects of cancer biology and emerging therapeutic approaches. Emphasis on new discoveries of critical pathways/processes in cancer etiology, progression, and metastasis. Introduces strategies used in the discovery, design of biological and small molecules-based therapies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 204 or PHYSIO 252. A gene regulation course is also required.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Informatics for Biologists
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students learn the fundamentals of bioinformatics and the unix operating system.

allCourses.title: Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Student research-based colloquium covering current topics in gene organization and expression, cell cycle and differentiation, DNA repair, checkpoint control, and the physical, chemical, and biological properties of macromolecules. Students are encouraged to read critically and analyze recent literature.
