allCourses.description: Students study sustainability concepts and theories and how they apply to our most pressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. Concurrently, they work on hands-on projects to improve the sustainability of campus operations and systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 193A

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Campus as a Living Lab III
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Students study sustainability concepts and theories and how they apply to our most pressing environmental, social, and economic challenges. Concurrently, they work on hands-on projects to improve the sustainability of campus operations and systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 193B

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Current Topics in Biology
allCourses.description: A seminar designed to discuss recent research findings and experimental issues in biology.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Safety and Ethics for Research
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the concepts, techniques, and ethics involved in biological sciences laboratory work.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Study in Biological Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Maximum of 5 units (per quarter) between BIO SCI 197, BIO SCI 198, and BIO SCI 199.
allCourses.description: Individualized instruction dealing with conceptual or theoretical problems in the biological sciences, rather than technical problems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Directed Group Studies
allCourses.description: Small group experimental laboratory or field work performed under the direction of a faculty member.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Independent Study in Biological Sciences Research
allCourses.description: Individual experimental laboratory or field research under a professor's direction. Required for participation in the Excellence in Research Program.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Writing
allCourses.description: Development of research skills such as learning how to plan and conduct research experiments, read and analyze scientific journal articles, and practice presenting the data experiments and journal articles with an emphasis on scientific writing.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Life Sciences
allCourses.description: Designed to introduce nonmajors to the basic concepts of modern biology. Discussion of evolutionary biology, ecology, molecular biology, and genetics.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: California Natural History
allCourses.description: Introduction to ecological relationships within a variety of California habitats. Explores aspects of the physical environments and the adaptations of organisms to their physical and biological surroundings in habitats such as the coastal zone, mountains, and deserts.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Sustainable Landscaping: Design and Practices
allCourses.description: Through lectures and hands-on work, students learn how to design habitats around dwellings, within cities, and in rural environments. These include traditional/sustainable landscaping, restoration, stormwater/wastewater treatment, xeriscaping, and low impact development design. Sustainable landscape plant materials emphasized.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biology of Cancer
allCourses.restriction: BIO SCI 25 may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI M125.
allCourses.description: Biological, clinical, and psychosocial nature of cancer through the perspectives of medical researchers, biologists, physicians, and health educators. For students of all majors, designed so that each can increase personal awareness of the biology of cancer.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Allied Health Microbiology
allCourses.restriction: Program in Nursing Science students only. Master of Nursing Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Basic microbiology with emphasis for allied health professions such as nursing. Emphasis is on micro-organisms involved in human health, disease and food safety.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 4 units as topics vary.
allCourses.overlap: BIO SCI M122, BIO SCI M118L.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Freshman Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Freshmen only. School of Biological Sciences students only.
allCourses.description: Weekly meetings consisting of presentations by faculty, professional staff, and Peer Academic Advisors provide information about the School of Biological Sciences, campus resources, learning skills, and special programs/opportunities.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Freshman Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Freshmen only. School of Biological Sciences students only.
allCourses.description: Faculty presentations and readings focused on the structure, function, opportunities, and current issues in the biological sciences.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Solutions in Science
allCourses.description: Students will be introduced to approaches that can be used to solve scientific problems. These methods can be utilized in introductory to advanced classes and will allow students to become independent thinkers.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: EASE Seminar
allCourses.description: Seminars designed to help students achieve success in STEM courses. Provides collaborative learning environment facilitated by undergraduate mentor. Students develop critical thinking and study skills. Also receive guidance to campus resources that assist acclimation to University.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics and Careers in Ecology and Evolution
allCourses.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to topics, research opportunities, and career options in ecology and evolutionary biology.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Academic Success
allCourses.description: There is an increasing awareness of the importance of non-academic factors (like belongingness) for student success. Provides students with peer mentoring and tools specific to different career stages that have been shown to improve student outcomes.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 1 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biomedical Ethics
allCourses.description: Ethical issues inherent in twenty-first-century biological and medical advances. Introduction to the basic biology underlying these issues and an analysis of the ethical implications to society. Topics such as cloning, stem cell research, genetic engineering are discussed by guest speakers.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: The Brain and Behavior
allCourses.description: Introduction to how the brain works. Biological processes underlying perception, movement, sleep-wake cycles, motivation, language, learning, and memory. Changes in the brain associated with sex differences, drug use, aging, seasons, and time of day. Fundamental properties of the nervous system.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Drugs and the Brain
allCourses.description: Introduction to the actions of drugs on the brain. How studying drug action helps reveal normal functions of neurons. How drugs can correct neural disorders or disrupt neural function. Biological issues related to drug abuse, drug addiction, and drug seeking.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Brain Dysfunction and Repair
allCourses.description: Introduction to the disruptions in brain function that underlie disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinsonism, schizophrenia, and depression, and the basis for drug therapies. The brain's ability to repair itself after damage and the pros and cons of that repair.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Mind and Memory
allCourses.description: Introduction to neural mechanisms underlying learning and memory. Emphasis on molecular changes that mediate memory as well as structures involved in different forms of memory. Additionally, examines the biology of memory phenomena, from extraordinary memory to false memory to amnesia.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Career Decision-Making
allCourses.description: An introductory course designed to facilitate the career decision-making process. Decision-making processes, values, and standardized tests of aptitudes, interests, and values are utilized with non-test data in appraising biological sciences career options.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Non-Health Sciences Career Exploration
allCourses.description: A survey course designed to assist students in exploring non-health science career options. Lectures by professionals in various fields.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neurobiology of Communication
allCourses.restriction: Non-school majors only
allCourses.description: Explores various modes of communication focusing on neurobiological and sensory bases that support these modes. Topics include:  communication codes for a specific signal, such as alarm, social heirarchy, mating readiness, emotions, and the purpose, accuracy, and honesty of these signals.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Mood Disorders
allCourses.description: There are significant differences in response to psychiatric illness across cultures. Delves into the neuroscience underlying mood disorder, investigating current pharmacological treatments and sociocultural influences on treatment outcomes.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Origin of Life
allCourses.description: Biochemical explanations for the origin of life are presented. Topics include definitions of life, the first replicating molecules, the first catalyzed biosynthesis and metabolism, the origin of cells (compartmentalization) and the origins of information and the genetic code.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Media on the Mind
allCourses.description: Surveys an ever-increasing collection of research, suggesting modern technology and social media are changing in the way our brains function.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Stem Cells and Brain Repair
allCourses.description: Students introduced to the field of regenerative neurobiology. Both basic stem cell discoveries and their potential clinical application to brain disorders examined. Discussion of opportunities, challenges, and implications of this research.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: AIDS Fundamentals
allCourses.description: Considers the biological and sociological bases of the AIDS epidemic. Topics include the history of AIDS, current medical knowledge, transmission, risk reduction, and how the community can respond.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Discussion and Literature Research in AIDS
allCourses.description: Students carry out two activities: (1) leading discussions about HIV/AIDS (predominantly regarding sociological and personal reactions) among students taking the AIDS Fundamentals course and (2) literature research about biomedical aspects of AIDS.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 45 or PUBHLTH 80

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Stress
allCourses.description: Investigates stress at a psychological, physiological, and molecular level, and provides a current overview of the field of stress research.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: The Mind-Body Connection in the Neuroscience of Well-Being
allCourses.description: Explores research that provides insight into how exercise, diet, sleep, contemplative practices such as mindfulness and meditation, and contemporary psychological therapeutic approaches alter brain function in beneficial ways to promote positive mental health well-being.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Field Biology
allCourses.restriction: Ecology and Evolutionary Biol Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Field excursions to introduce students to local field sites and resources.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Molecular Biology
allCourses.restriction: Non-Biological Sciences majors only. BIO SCI 5 may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 99.
allCourses.description: Molecules of life, with emphasis on medical applications.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Ecology
allCourses.restriction: No Biological Sciences Majors. BIO SCI 55 may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 96 or BIO SCI E106.
allCourses.description: Principles of ecology; application to populations, communities, ecosystems, and humans.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Life Sciencing from Aristotle to Venter
allCourses.description: History of biology from Aristotle through to the scientific revolutions precipitated by Darwin, geneticists, molecular biologists, and now genomics. Introduces the practices and achievements of biological research to both beginning biology students and non-majors.
allCourses.overlap: BIO SCI H90, BIO SCI H90B.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Tropical Biology: Race to Save the Tropics
allCourses.description: Population growth combines with tropical resource consumption by industrialized nations to cause high rates of deforestation, pollution, habitat fragmentation, and extinction of species. Discusses tropical biomes, their population, community,  ecosystem processes, and possible means of conservation of biodiversity.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biodiversity & Conservation
allCourses.description: A biological perspective on the current environmental crisis. The origin, evolution, and value of biological diversity. Extinction and depletion caused by overexploitation, habitat loss, and pollution. Conservation through habitat preservation and restoration, captive breeding, cryopreservation.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Vaccines
allCourses.description: Focus on introducing vaccines, covering how vaccines work, as well as how they are tested. Introduction to the immune system, to facilitate understanding how vaccines function. Also covers types of vaccines, clinical trials, and vaccine hesitancy.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Development
allCourses.description: Processes leading to the birth of a healthy child and the avoidance of birth defects. Male and female reproductive systems, hormonal control of egg-sperm formations, sexual intercourse, contraception, venereal diseases, fertilization, cell division, embryonic development, fetal physiology.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Evolution and the Modern World
allCourses.description: Pandemics, disease, antibiotic resistance, your pets, the food you eat: evolution has shaped our world. Discusses the intellectual development of evolution and illustrates, with current events, that evolution is happening all around us, all the time.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Curriculum
allCourses.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students only.
allCourses.description: Initiation, planning, and coordination of student-run courses.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 12 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: From DNA to Organisms
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Unaffiliated Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. BIO SCI 93 may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI 98.
allCourses.description: Cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, and the biology of organ systems. Covers concepts of building blocks (nucleotides, amino acids, and cells) and of information flow (DNA to proteins, receptors to nuclei, the blood to distant organs, and DNA to offspring).

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: DNA to Organisms - Introduction to Biology Research
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Unaffiliated Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development of quantitative reasoning and science inquiry skills.  Helps students learn how to use the scientific method, ask questions, and develop professional skills applicable to any major or career. Materials fee.

prerequisite_for.title: Organisms to Ecosystems - Introduction to Biology Research Analysis

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: From Organisms to Ecosystems
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Unaffiliated Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. BIO SCI 1A may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 94.
allCourses.description: Patterns of diversity, ecology, and evolutionary biology. Emphasis is on the Tree of Life and how its members are distributed and interact.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Organisms to Ecosystems - Introduction to Biology Research Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Unaffiliated Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Helps students learn how to use the scientific method, ask and answer questions about environmental DNA, and develop professional skills. Students learn how to design and conduct experiments, analyze data, interpret graphs, and communicate their findings. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93L

prerequisite_list.title: DNA to Organisms - Introduction to Biology Research

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Genetics
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engr: Premedical Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Nursing Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to genetics. Basic features of replication and expression of DNA, cell division, and gene transmission. Recombination and mutation in diploid organisms.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94

prerequisite_for.title: Cell, Developmental, and Molecular Biology of Plants

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engr: Premedical Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Nursing Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Structure and properties of proteins; major biochemical pathways and mechanisms for their control.

prerequisite_for.title: Biochemistry of Animals in their Environments
Biotechnological Applications of  Energy and Environmental Research
Topics in Molecular Biology and Biochemistry

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Biology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Nursing Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biomedical Engr: Premedical Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Biochemistry and replication of nucleic acids; molecular genetics; protein biosynthesis; genetic code; regulation of expression of genetic information; biochemical evolution.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98

prerequisite_for.title: The Biology and Genetics of Cancer
Topics in Developmental and Cell Biology
Biochemistry of Animals in their Environments
Learning to Read Primary Literature in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Nutrition Science
allCourses.description: An introduction to nutrition science, integrating concepts from biology, biochemistry, microbiology, physiology, and psychology to explain the interaction between nutrients and the human body. Biological basis of nutrient standards is analyzed. Effects of nutrition, behavior, exercises on health/disease.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biology and Chemistry of Food and Cooking
allCourses.description: The kitchen is used as a laboratory to introduce fundamental principles of biology, chemistry, and physics. A molecular/cellular analysis of cooking, including concepts such as protein structure, browning reactions, colloids, emulsions, carbohydrate metabolism, and development of flavor/texture through biochemical transformations.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biotech Basics
allCourses.description: An overview of current biotechnology. Discusses the biological/molecular basis of novel therapies for diseases, modification of human genes, human genome project, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, and genetically modified food. Targeted for students interested in modern breakthroughs in biology.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Diseases of the Twenty-First Century
allCourses.description: Why do we get sick? An introduction to the biological basis of human disease, including diseases of the cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, and reproductive systems. Case studies present diagnosis, treatment, and prevention protocols. Inheritable and infectious diseases also discussed.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Horticulture Science
allCourses.description: Scientific principles of horticulture at the UCI Arboretum. Taxonomy, plant life history strategies; experiments with seed dormancy; morphological adaptations for specialized sexual and clonal reproduction; basics of plant propagation and ecological restoration.  Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Physiology of Fitness
allCourses.description: An introduction to the organ systems of the human body, including muscle, cardiovascular, immune, and reproductive systems, with an emphasis on how the body responds to exercise, diet, and disease.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biology of Oriental Medicine
allCourses.description: With lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on learning, the theory and practice of herbal medicine, acupuncture, qigong, and manipulative therapies are explained in Western biomedical terms. The latest basic and clinical research advances in each area are also described.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Global Change Biology
allCourses.description: Field trips and lectures that address ways in which humans are altering the global environment, with consequences for the ecology of animals, plants, and microbes.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Complementary and Alternative Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Non-Biological Science majors only.
allCourses.description: Basic and clinical research on complementary and alternative therapies (e.g., herbal medicine, mind-body practices, energy medicine, acupuncture, homeopathy, chiropractic, Ayurveda), and how such practices are integrated into Western medicine are discussed. Includes lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on learning.
allCourses.overlap: BIO SCI 9J, BIO SCI 9D, BIO SCI 10, BIO SCI D124.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cell Biology
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of the basic structure and function of animal cells, with an emphasis on the regulation of cellular processes. The basic features of membranes, cellular compartmentalization, protein trafficking, vesicular transport, cytoskeleton, adhesion, signal transduction, and cell cycle are covered.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Developmental Biology
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Cellular and molecular analysis of how a fertilized egg develops into an organism consisting of complex structures such as the eye, arms, and brain. Emphasis is on the key concepts of developmental processes underlying pattern formation, growth, and regeneration.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cell, Developmental, and Molecular Biology of Plants
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes the special features of plant cells and plant development as compared to animals. Two central topics: plants' ability to fuel our planet through photosynthesis, and the interactions of plants with microorganisms in making nitrogen available to other life forms.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Developmental and Cell Biology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers the division of cells, isolate cellular organelles (chloroplasts, mitochondria, nuclei), and follows changes in cells undergoing programmed cell death. Development is demonstrated in experiments showing cooperation of individual cells in forming a multicellular organism.  Materials fee.
