allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Genetics Majors Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Genetics Majors only.
allCourses.description: Genetics majors attend a weekly seminar to discuss current research techniques and career opportunities in the field. Students have the opportunity to present their own independent research.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Developmental and Cell Biology Majors Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Developmental and Cell Biology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Developmental and Cell Biology majors attend a weekly seminar to discuss current research techniques and career opportunities in the field. Students have the opportunity to present their own independent research.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Reproduction and Development PBL Course
allCourses.description: Focuses on human reproductive biology and in utero human development. Taught in a problem-based learning (PBL) format focused on the biological, social, economic, and ethical implications of specific clinical cases.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93 and BIO SCI 94 and BIO SCI 97 and BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Movement and Health
allCourses.description: Mechanisms of movements of molecules within and across cell membranes, cytoskeleton and cell motility, muscle contraction, and physical exercises and mind-body practices. Chemical, electromagnetic, and vital energy, and regulatory pathways in such processes. Relevance to health, diseases, and integrative medicine.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Stem Cell Biology
allCourses.description: Introduces upper-level undergraduate students to stem cell biology. Include the basic biology of stem cells, potential applications of stem cells, and the ethical, legal, and moral issues associated with human stem cell research.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D103"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D104"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103 and BIO SCI D104.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biology of Integrative Medecine
allCourses.description: Presentation of biological principles and the latest clinical and basic research on complementary and alternative therapies (e.g., mind-body medicine, energy medicine, herbal medicine, acupuncture, manipulative therapies) and their integration with Western medicine. Lectures supplemented by demonstrations and hands-on learning sessions.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: The Biology and Genetics of Cancer
allCourses.description: Cancer is a major field in modern biology. Topics discussed include genetics, cellular oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, and molecular targets for diagnosis and therapy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biotechnology and Plant Breeding
allCourses.description: Conventional plant breeding techniques, their limitations, and supplementations through modern biotechnology. Includes cloning, cell transformation (genetic engineering), and cell fusion. Crop improvement, state of the art in animal and human systems, and the impact of gene technology of society.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Photomedicine
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies the use of optical and engineering-based systems (laser-based) for diagnosis, treating diseases, manipulation of cells and cell function. Physical, optical, and electro-optical principles are explored regarding molecular, cellular, organ, and organism applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 3C or PHYSICS 7D

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Precision Medicine
allCourses.description: Introduction to the use of genomic techniques for the study of individual genomes and transcriptomes in healthy and diseased samples. Covers GWAS, current sequencing techniques, cancer genomics, and biomarker discovery.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advances in Regenerative Medicine
allCourses.description: Introduces the rapidly growing field of regenerative medicine. New developments in stem cell research are discussed. Cellular, molecular, and engineering aspects of stem cell-based organ replacement strategies are examined, with emphasis on specific regenerative therapies.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D103"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D104"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cell Biology of Human Disease
allCourses.description: Builds on prior biology courses about the underlying cell biological mechanisms and recent treatment advances of several model diseases. Emphasizes literature searches, reading primary literature, and student group work.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Anatomy
allCourses.description: Presents a systems approach to the analysis of human structure. Molecular, cellular, tissue, organ, and organ system levels of structure and organization are integrated throughout.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Eukaryotic and Human Genetics
allCourses.description: Structure and function of genes in eukaryotes with emphasis on special problems of genetic studies in humans. Molecular methods of genetic analysis and gene transfer are discussed. Practical applications and ethical and social issues raised by genetic studies are addressed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Critical Thinking in Cell Biology
allCourses.description: Builds on prior biology courses about cell biology, and works to develop a deeper understanding of experimental techniques and interpretation of experiments. A key focus will be the question of how one moves from specific examples to general.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Intercellular Signaling and Disease
allCourses.description: Introduces cell-to-cell communication mechanisms, which are fundamentally essential but still not well understood. From well-established to cutting-edge, researches of intercellular communication and how its malfunction leads to diseases are discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D103"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D104"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: How to Read a Science Paper
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides junior and senior undergraduates currently involved or interested in pursuing research exposure to current scientific literature and training on how to read and critically evaluate primary research articles in preparation for research-oriented.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Genomics, Development, and Medicine
allCourses.description: Focuses on the applications of genomics and proteomics to problems in genetics, cell, and developmental biology.  Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the techniques currently used for genomics analysis and how best to apply these tools to solve problems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Development and Disease
allCourses.description: Development of animal embryos from a fertilized egg to a functioning organism. Topics include reproduction, body-axis formation, growth and differentiation of embryonic cells, and organogenesis, with an emphasis on congenital birth defects and diseases that disrupt these processes.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D103"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D104"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular and Cellular Basis of Disease
allCourses.description: Provides students with examples of how human disease is usually manifested at the cellular level. The roles of specific molecules and organelles are discussed where their roles in the disease process are understood.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cell Biology
allCourses.description: An advanced, integrated view of cell biology. Topics include the cell cycle, the cytoskeleton, the extracellular matrix, signal transduction, the cellular basis of development, and the cell biology of cancer.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D103"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 103"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 107"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI 107.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Human Anatomy
allCourses.description: Systems approach to analyze the form and function of the human body with an emphasis on applying anatomical concepts to evaluate clinical cases. The laboratory uses human models and a simulated cadaver dissection for structure. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109", "minGrade": "C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PHRMSCI 120", "minGrade": "C"}]}, {"NOT": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D136"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120. BIO SCI E109 with a grade of C or better. PHRMSCI 120 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Developmental and Cell Biology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Biological Sciences students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of developmental and cell biology.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Processes in Ecology and Evolution
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An in-depth study of the mechanisms that drive evolution and ecology including: natural selection, mutation, genetic drift, speciation, extinction, life history patterns, population dynamics, ecosystem and community structure, predator-prey and host pathogen interactions, and social behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94

prerequisite_for.title: Plant Diversity in a Changing World
Topics in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Habitats and Organisms
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. BIO SCI E106L may not be taken for credit concurrently with or after taking BIO SCI E166. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to local habitats and organisms through required field trips and applies ecological and evolutionary principles from BIO SCI E106. Students also explore related literature.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}, {"NOT": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E166"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Ecology and Evolutionary Biol Majors only.
allCourses.description: Invited speakers, graduate students, and faculty present current research in ecology and evolutionary biology.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this class for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Functional features of the major organ systems in the human body. Emphasis on homeostasis and the interactions of organ systems in health and disease. (Discussion of behavior and brain function deferred to BIO SCI N110.).
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 93"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI H93"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "CHEM 1C"}, {"NOT": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PHRMSCI 120"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93) and (CHEM 1C or CHEM M2C)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Physiology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory with a focus on the whole organism and its organ systems. Examples of structure-function relationships are drawn from both animal and human physiology. Cellular and molecular aspects are introduced as required.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BME 120"}]}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BME 121"}]}, {"NOT": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PHRMSCI 120L"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and (BIO SCI E109 or (BME 120 and BME 121)).

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Evolution Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students perform experiments which illustrate important concepts in evolutionary biology such as natural selection, random genetic drift, inbreeding, age-specific selection, sexual selection, and phylogenetic reconstruction. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
allCourses.description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E112L"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E183"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120) and BIO SCI E112L and BIO SCI E183

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Exercise Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E117A

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Exercise Sciences Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Exercise Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students are introduced to fundamental concepts and topics in exercise sciences with an emphasis on developing innovative approaches for exploring the biological response to physical activity/inactivity. Interactive course with robust discussion amongst faculty and students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E117B

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Ecosystem Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Ecology and Evolutionary Biol Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A mechanistic perspective on ecosystem processes. Covers ecosystem development, element cycling, and interactions with plants and microbes. The role of ecosystems in environmental change is also addressed.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "EARTHSS 51"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "EARTHSS 60A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "CHEM 51C"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106 or EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 60A or CHEM 51C

prerequisite_list.title: Fundamental Processes in Earth and Environmental Studies

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Selfish DNA
allCourses.description: Focuses on the genetics and evolution of selfish DNA, and introduces necessary background knowledge from molecular biology, cytogenetics, and bioinformatics.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 94"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 97"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI H97"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI H94"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H94 or BIO SCI H97

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Marine Biology
allCourses.description: Examines the biotic and abiotic factors influencing the physiology, distribution, abundances, interactions, and evolution of marine organisms and the roles of those organisms in mediating ecosystem services and functions. A field trip is required. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Physiology and Pathology of the Kidney
allCourses.description: Examines the structure, function, and pathology of the kidney. Topics include anatomy of the kidney, cellular function, urine formation, and disease states of the kidney.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Infectious Disease Dynamics
allCourses.description: Learn how the immune system interacts with infectious diseases, in particular with viral infections. An introduction to basic virology and immunology, it concentrates on the way in which the immune system is critical to the prevention of infections.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Parasitology
allCourses.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Parasitism is the most common animal lifestyle. Yet, because parasites are invisible, they are often overlooked. Explore parasite diversity, disease dynamics, and more with an emphasis on the influential roles that parasites play on ecosystem structure and function.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Physiological Plant Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An examination of the interactions between plants and their environment. Emphasis on the underlying physiological mechanisms of plant function, adaptations and responses to stress, and the basis of the distribution of plants and plant assemblages across the landscape.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EARTHSS 51 or BIO SCI 94 or (EARTHSS 60A and EARTHSS 60C)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Chemical Ecology
allCourses.description: An introduction to the unspoken chemical language of nature. Emphasis on interactions between insects, plants, and microbes including plant defense, pollination, and microbial warfare.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94) and CHEM 51A. CHEM 51A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Forensic Genetics
allCourses.description: Covers techniques currently used for forensic identification and paternity testing. Topics include STR, Y-STR and mitochondrial DNA tests, database searches, mixtures, allelic drop out, likelihood ratios, laboratory errors and the interaction of science and the legal system.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93 and BIO SCI 94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Image Analysis in Biological Research
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to scientific image analysis including techniques such as high-speed, time-lapse, thermal imaging, and flow visualization. Students make movies using cameras, edit and analyze images using computers, and do a writing project.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109"}]}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI E106 or PHRMSCI 120 or BIO SCI E109) and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Diversity of Fishes
allCourses.description: A survey of the many dimensions of diversity existing across fishes, the largest group of vertebrate organisms (over 30,000 species). Covers systematics, functional anatomy, development, physiology, biogeography, behavior, and more.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Environmental Microbiology
allCourses.description: Focuses on non-pathogenic microbes within all habitats (soils, oceans, associated with animals and plants) and their essential functions for ecosystems. Their applied importance for agriculture, bioremediation, energy and food production are also discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Microbiomes
allCourses.description: Students develop an understanding of microbiomes in the context of both their environment and their impact on host physiology. Discussions on how microbiomes interact with the human body.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI M122

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Evolution
allCourses.description: Introduction to the study of evolutionary change in genes and DNA sequences. Combines study of molecular biology with the study of evolution. Molecular evolution has application to many disciplines, including molecular biology, virology, systematics, and the origin of life.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: The Physiology of Human Nutrition
allCourses.description: Examines the biochemical basis of energy metabolism, physiological processes in digestion and uptake, and the biochemical transformation of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins in the human body. The emphasis is on expanding the students' understanding of physiology.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 98"}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PHRMSCI 120"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and (BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Genetics of Complex Traits
allCourses.description: Many ecologically important traits (e.g., size, age at sexual maturity) and clinical.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Comparative Animal Physiology
allCourses.description: Maintenance aspects of physiology: water balance; feeding and digestion; metabolism; respiration and circulation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Animal Locomotion
allCourses.description: The physiology, biomechanics, and neuroscience that determines how animals propel themselves and navigate through the world. Considers the principles that govern the walking, running, flying, and swimming of animals, including exercising humans.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Evolution and the Environment
allCourses.description: Explores basic topics in ecology and evolutionary biology and applications to agriculture, conservation, environmental issues, and public health. Format involves discussion of scientific journal articles and other readings, with focus on learning to evaluate scientific evidence.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI E106.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Evolution and the Environment Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores basic topics in ecology and evolutionary biology and applications to agriculture, conservation, environmental issues, and public health. Format involves lab activities and discussion of scientific journal articles, with focus on learning to evaluate scientific evidence.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": true, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Writing/Philosophy of Biology
allCourses.restriction: Juniors only.
allCourses.description: Philosophy of biology, e.g., scientific method in biology, the structure of evolutionary theory, teleology, ethics, and evolution. Course work includes one 4,000-word and four 1,000-word papers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Animal Coloration and Vision
allCourses.description: Physiological and behavioral mechanisms of color production and vision including crypsis, mimicry, aposematism, masquerade, sexual dimorphism, and predator-prey interactions through the lens of signals, receivers, and receptors; color and polarization vision in mate choice and visual adaptations to aquatic environments.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Ecosystem Services
allCourses.description: Covers what ecosystem services are, how to classify them, what the impacts of land degradation are on ecosystem services, how to quantify and value them, and the importance of mainstreaming ecosystem services in decision-making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 70A and EARTHSS 70B) or (EARTHSS 51 and EARTHSS 53 and EARTHSS 55)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Behavioral Endocrinology
allCourses.description: Comparative examination of the major hormone systems that regulate behavior across animals. Emphasizes the reciprocating nature of hormone-behavior interactions and seeks to understand how natural selection drives the evolution of hormone structure and function.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Conservation Biology
allCourses.description: Genetic and ecological issues in conservation biology, including effects of human population growth, the value of biodiversity, conservation genetics, demography, metapopulation dynamics, community and ecosystem processes, species invasions, global climate change, and reserve design and management.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Evolutionary and Ecological Principles in Medicine
allCourses.description: Explore the dynamics of populations on an ecological, epidemiological, and medical level. Considers the dynamics of competition, predation, and parasitism; the spread and control of infectious diseases; and the in vivo dynamics of viral infections and the immune system.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biochemistry of Animals in their Environments
allCourses.description: Interactions between organisms and their environments. Topics include the effects of environmental variables on biochemical functions: membrane stability, protein kinetics, energy metabolism, heat-shock-responses, energetics, gene-expression, and circadian rhythms. These topics are integrated with physiological-ecology in context of global climate change.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Functional and Structural Evolutionary Genomics
allCourses.description: Function and organization of genomes analyzed from an evolutionary perspective. Review of some of the most recent experimental approaches in genome analysis and comparative genomics. Relevant software to analyze DNA and expression data is used.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 97 or BIO SCI H97

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Genetics and Human History
allCourses.description: Explores topics in human health/history from an evolutionary perspective, with emphasis on genetics. Topics include the relationship between genetics and human disease as an evolutionary question, and how modern genetic techniques are used to study the history of human populations.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": true, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}]}]}

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Physiology in Extreme Environments
allCourses.description: An in-depth look at the physiological mechanisms that allow animals, including humans, to be physically active and survive in extreme environments. Physiological responses to high altitude, diving, microgravity, deserts, and extreme cold are examined.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy
allCourses.description: Structure and evolution of the major organ systems in vertebrates, from fish to mammals.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biology of Birds
allCourses.description: A thorough introduction to the biology of birds, covering topics ranging from avian anatomy and physiology to behavior, natural history, ecology, genetics, evolution, systematics, and conservation. Examples from both local and global avifauna.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biology of Birds Lab
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The companion to Biology of Birds (E160). Consists primarily of field trips to identify local birds and study avian natural history. Students must provide their own transportation to field sites, some with entrance fees. Students must have field binoculars.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108", "minGrade": "D-"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 194S", "minGrade": "D-"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biology of Birds Lab
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The companion to Biology of Birds (E160). Consists primarily of field trips to identify local birds and study avian natural history. Students must provide their own transportation to field sites, some with entrance fees. Students must have field binoculars.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 100 and BIO SCI 194S

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Environmental Microbiology
allCourses.description: Establishes a fundamental understanding of microbes living in the environment, including their distribution, diversity, and biochemistry, and discusses how they attribute to global biogeochemical cycles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 53) or (EARTHSS 60A and EARTHSS 60C) or (BIO SCI E106 and BIO SCI M122)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Field Biology
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Conducting group and independent studies in Southern California ecosystems, this course covers the fundamentals of experimental design, statistical analysis, communicating scientific findings (orally, visually, in writing), and other skills necessary for the scientific investigation of biological processes in the field.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E106. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Field Methods in Ecology
allCourses.description: Field studies of major concepts in plant and animal ecology, with emphasis on experimental design, field sampling methods, statistical analysis, and scientific writing. An independent project and two field trips are required.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 194S and BIO SCI E106. Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI 100. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Evolution
allCourses.description: An integrative treatment of evolutionary biology that covers evolutionary processes, basic research methods, and the history of life.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Mechanical Physiology
allCourses.description: Explores the mechanics of animal physiology. Basic biomechanical principles are introduced and illustrated in a variety of physiological systems. Topics include the fluid and structural mechanics of muscles, skeletons, circulation, insect flight, biomaterials, and fish swimming.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Plant Diversity in a Changing World
allCourses.description: Investigation of planet diversity in California and throughout the world, including basic systematic concepts, an introduction to major groups of flowering plants, and the effects of global biological change on plant diversity.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Plant Systematics Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Diversity of flowering plants is investigated in the laboratory and field. Familiarity with flowering plant families, particularly those prominent in the California flora, is emphasized.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": true, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": true, "courseId": "BIO SCI E172"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 194S"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106 and BIO SCI 100 and BIO SCI 194S. Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI E172.

prerequisite_list.title: Plant Diversity in a Changing World

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Behavioral Ecology
allCourses.description: Animal behavior as an evolutionary solution to problems encountered during an animal's life cycle. Includes a broad comparative approach to communication, social behavior, habitat selection, and food finding.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Restoration Ecology
allCourses.description: Theoretical and practical aspects of habitat restoration and mitigation. Design, implementation, and monitoring of restoration projects in local habitats. Collection of seed and cuttings, planting and maintenance presented. Control of exotics in natural areas discussed. Environmental ethics of restoration emphasized.   Materials fee.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Evolution of Infectious Disease
allCourses.description: Introduction to the major human pathogens, and the ecological and evolutionary processes affecting their impact on public health. Topics include the evolution of drug resistance, problems in vaccine development, diseases emerging from animals, and bioterrorism.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Ocean Ecology
allCourses.description: Examines the relationships between physical processes in the ocean, biological productivity, and the exploitation of ocean resources by high-trophic-level predators, including humans. Discusses open ocean ecosystems, intertidal and benthic regions of the world ocean.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Limnology and Freshwater Biology
allCourses.description: Biology of freshwater environments: lakes, ponds, rivers, their biota, and the factors which influence distribution of organisms.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94 or BIO SCI H94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Field Freshwater Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analytical techniques for common water-quality variables of lakes, streams, and rivers. Benthic fauna, vertebrates and invertebrates, algae, and aquatic plants. Emphasis on field methods with an experimental approach; laboratory exercises. Field trips to marshes, vernal pools, rivers, and streams. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": true, "courseId": "BIO SCI E179"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E179"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI E179

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Conservation in the American West
allCourses.description: Critical examination of contemporary conservation issues in the American West, with particular attention to water in California, grazing on public lands, and species decline and extinctions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Mediterranean Ecosystems: Biodiversity and Conservation
allCourses.description: Biodiversity, history of human impacts, and conservation efforts are examined in the five Mediterranean-type ecosystems. Remaining natural habitat, approaches to ecological habitat restoration, control of exotic species, and predicted consequences of global climate change are described. Field trip required.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 94

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Exercise Physiology
allCourses.description: Focus upon critical topics in the area of exercise biology using the comparative physiological approach. Specifically examine the physiological factors that limit the capacity of an organism to sustain high levels of aerobic metabolism.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Ecology and Diversity of Insects
allCourses.description: Insects—representing two-thirds of all species—play fundamental roles in human health, agriculture, and natural ecosystems. Topics include insect morphology, development, physiology, taxonomy, ecology, and insects in human affairs. Lecture includes interactive demonstrations and an optional weekend trip.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Population and Community Ecology
allCourses.description: Population structure, function, development, and evolution. Topics include population structure, population growth and regulation, metapopulations, predation, competition, species diversity, ecosystem function, macroecology, and island biogeography. Offered every other Winter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Population and Community Ecology Lab
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Covers processes specific to groups of the same species (populations) and multiple species (communities). Includes growth, regulation, dynamics, and persistence of populations and community interactions, development, diversity, and macroecology. Lab activities focus on application of population prediction and biodiversity assessment.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E106"}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Exercise as Medicine
allCourses.description: Explores the link between regular physical activity and health, focusing on mechanistic insights into how regular exercise improves overall health and alters disease trajectories of cancer, type-II diabetes, depression, and other chronic  illnesses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Insect Physiology
allCourses.description: Physiology of insects. Insect respiration, digestion, excretion, and neurobiology, including sensory systems and effectors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109 or PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Environmental Ethics
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: History of evolution of environmental ethics in America. Management problems in national parks, wilderness areas, wild and scenic rivers, national forests. Contemporary and historical aspects/contributors to the field. Mitigation, endangered species, habitat restoration, biodiversity, and environmental activism. Field trips required.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of ecology and evolutionary biology.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E106
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Topics in Biological Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Biological Sciences Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Varied course topics in Biological Sciences designed for students in Honors in Biological Sciences.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Writing for Biological Research
allCourses.restriction: Excellence in Research Program students only.
allCourses.description: Science writing and critical reasoning. Work, research, and writing exercises are conducted in a computer laboratory. Preliminary writing exercises and further development of Excellence in Research to a full scientific senior thesis. This forms the basis for an oral defense.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 199. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Biological Sciences Honors Program students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Contemporary research problems in physiology using insects as model systems. Topics include digestion, osmoregulation, development, and neurobiology, including sensory systems and behavior. Participating students present papers in a journal club-style format and write short essays summarizing research findings.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Virus Evolution
allCourses.description: Viruses infect all domains of life and have had profound consequences on the development and survival of life. Examines virus emergence and evolution in a broad context. Weekly overview is followed by student presentations and essays based on contemporary literature.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI M124A.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: The Idiom and Practice of Science
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: The importance of biological sciences in our world is discussed. Topics may include brain and behavior, health and disease, genetics and society, and conservation biology. Primary goal is to encourage students to understand better the world in which they live.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors From DNA to Organisms
allCourses.restriction: BIO SCI H93 may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 97, BIO SCI H97, or BIO SCI 98.
allCourses.description: Cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, and the biology or organ systems. Covers concepts of building blocks (nucleotides, amino acids, and cells) and of information flow (DNA to proteins, receptors to nuclei, the blood to distant organs, and DNA to offspring).

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors From Organisms to Ecosystems
allCourses.restriction: BIO SCI 1A may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI H94.
allCourses.description: Patterns of diversity, ecology, and evolutionary biology. Emphasis is on the Tree of Life and how its members are distributed and interact.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Genetics
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only. BIO SCI H97 may not be taken for credit if taken after BIO SCI 97.
allCourses.description: Introduction to genetics. Basic features of replication and expression of DNA, cell division, and gene transmission. Recombination and mutation in diploid organisms.

prerequisite_for.title: Cell, Developmental, and Molecular Biology of Plants

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Biochemistry
allCourses.description: Physical-chemical properties of macromolecules. Structure-function relationships in nucleic acids, protein, carbohydrates, and lipids. Integration and regulation of metabolism. Biochemistry of organs and biochemistry of diseases.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biochemistry Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Properties of enzymes and the culture and isolation of mutants of microorganisms. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 99"}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Allied Health Microbiology
allCourses.restriction: Program in Nursing Science students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introductory microbiology lecture and laboratory with an emphasis on microbial growth control and the relationship between microbes and human health.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 93"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI H93"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "CHEM 1C"}, {"NOT": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M122"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M118L"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93) and CHEM 1C. CHEM 1C with a grade of C- or better
allCourses.overlap: BIO SCI M122, BIO SCI M118L.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Molecular Biology
allCourses.description: Mechanisms of gene expression; special emphasis on regulatory events that occur in Eukaryotic organisms other than initiation of transcription. Chromatin structure and rearrangement, RNA polymerases, cis- and trans-acting elements, RNA processing, transport and stability, protein synthesis, trafficking, and turnover.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Biology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students perform experiments which illustrate the chemical and biological properties of nucleic acids. Emphasis is placed on recent techniques in recombinant DNA technology including gene isolation and characterization.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 99"}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Microbiology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introductory general microbiology designed for preprofessional biology majors. Includes microscopy, cultivation of bacteria, morphological and biochemical characterization of bacteria, microbial metabolism, growth and genetics, microorganisms and human disease, and interactions of microorganisms with the environment.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 99"}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108)

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Microbiology and Immunology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Literature-based, interactive discussions focused on review of seminal historic and recent immunology literature. Student responsibilities include reading, critical evaluation, and discussion of manuscripts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI M121

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Signal Transduction in Mammalian Cells
allCourses.description: Introduction to major biochemical pathways that transmit information from extracellular cues into changes in cell behavior. Focuses on kinases, phosphateses, G proteins, second messengers, and protein-protein interactions. Includes discussion of primary research articles and experimental techniques.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Immunology with Hematology
allCourses.description: Antibodies, antigens, antigen-antibody reactions, cells and tissues of lymphoreticular and hematopoietic systems, and individual and collective components of cell-mediated and humoral immune response.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Immunology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Emphasis is placed on learning modern techniques in immunology such as ELISAs, western blotting, and immunofluorescent staining assays.   Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 108"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M121"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (BIO SCI 100 or BIO SCI 108) and BIO SCI M121

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: General Microbiology
allCourses.description: Comparative metabolism of small molecules and cell structure and relationship to microbial classification. Macromolecule synthesis and regulation, sporulation, cell division, growth, and effect of antibiotics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Microbiology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Advanced course featuring selective isolation of a wide variety of microbial types. Identification and characterization of organisms by morphological, nutritional, and biochemical approaches. Medical, industrial, and research applications.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 194S"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M122"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M132"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 194S. Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI 100 and (BIO SCI M122 or BIO SCI M132).

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
allCourses.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MATH 2D"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MATH 2J"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MATH 7"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 7"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "STATS 7"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "STATS 8"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D or MATH 3A or STATS 7 or STATS 8

prerequisite_list.title: Infinite Series and Basic Linear Algebra

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Virology
allCourses.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students only.
allCourses.description: Replication of viruses in populations, animals, and the host cell. The effects of viral infection on populations, individuals, and specific molecular effects on the target cell. Role of viral infections in cancer and degenerative diseases.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Viral Pathogenesis and Immunity
allCourses.description: The mechanisms of viral pathogenesis and of host resistance to viruses are explored in detail. HIV-1 and Influenza-A are used as examples. In each case, viral replication, cytopathic effects, immune response, and viral evasion are discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M121"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M124A"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M124A. Recommended: BIO SCI M122.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Virus Engineering Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An advanced laboratory for undergraduates who have completed a virology lecture class. Students learn to engineer recombinant viruses and express genes in mouse tissue.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M124A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M124B"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M116L"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 194S and BIO SCI M116L and (BIO SCI M124A or BIO SCI M124B). Prerequisite or corequisite: BIO SCI 100.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Biology of Cancer
allCourses.description: Molecular mechanisms of carcinogenesis. Consideration of transformation by DNA tumor viruses, RNA tumor viruses, and chemical carcinogens.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Learning to Read Primary Literature in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
allCourses.description: An introduction to primary literature focusing on methods to approach, understand, and analyze scientific papers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Virology and Immunology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introductory laboratory course in virology and immunology designed for biology majors. Curriculum includes plasmid preparation, plasmid characterization, microscopy, cell culture, transfection and infection of cells, cell counting, plaque assays, ELISA, Western blot, mixed lymphocyte reactions.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and BIO SCI 194S and BIO SCI 100 and BIO SCI M116L
allCourses.corequisite: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M124A.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Discovery of the New RNA World
allCourses.description: Focus is on RNAs role in catalysis and regulation. Topics include non-coding RNAs function in normal cells (regulation of cell homeostasis, development, and differentiation) and in disease (cancer, viral infection).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and (BIO SCI D103 or BIO SCI D104).

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Molecular Lab Techniques
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Discovery-driven experimentation in the fields of molecular biology, biochemistry, and cell biology. Also involves other aspects of the lab experience including group discussion of results, scientific paper analysis, and student presentations.   Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 100"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 194S"}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI D111L"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M114L"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M116L"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M118L"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 100 and (BIO SCI D111L or BIO SCI M114L or BIO SCI M116L or BIO SCI M118L)
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Innate Immunity, Infection, and Pathogenesis
allCourses.description: Role of the innate immune system in health and disease. Molecular pathways of innate immune recognition, expression, and regulation of immune receptors, signal transduction, pathogen sensors, and detection of microbial ligands. Lecture and discussion of primary research articles.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M121"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M122"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M124A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M124B"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI M143"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI M121 or BIO SCI M122 or BIO SCI M124A or BIO SCI M124B or BIO SCI M143

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Structural Biology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of magnetic resonance, X-ray crystallography, and CryoEM toward the determination of high-resolution biomolecular structures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B or MATH 5B

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Microbial Genetics
allCourses.description: Basic principles of microbial genetics are presented as lectures for the first half of the course. The second half is devoted to applications of these principles and requires reading review and original research papers and interactions with guest lecturers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Parasitology
allCourses.description: Introduction to human animal-parasitic diseases including worms and protozoan infections.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cell Organelles and Membranes
allCourses.description: Structure, function, and biogenesis of biological membranes and membrane-bound organelles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 51A

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Nutritional Biochemistry
allCourses.description: Metabolic processes of sugar and fat that lead to an understanding of diabetes, cancer, obesity and other disease states will be the focus of this course.  Nutritional supplements, analysis of metabolites and mechanisms of metabolic enzymes will be covered.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Vascular Biology: Blood Vessels in Health and Disease
allCourses.description: Every cell in the body is within a half hair’s width of a blood vessel. As such, we cannot understand the body, in health or disease, without understanding the vasculature. Mixes lectures and primary literature reviews.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Structure-Function Relationships of Integral Membrane Proteins

allCourses.description: Covers microbiological and biochemical background related to current biotechnological applications, case studies of biotech-companies, and basic information related to patents and start-up companies. Topics include biofuel, bioremediation, agricultural, and environmental applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98

allCourses.title: Clinical Psychophysiology
allCourses.description: Psychophysiology investigates the relationships between physiological processes and psychological phenomena. Technologies examined include reaction times, heart rate variability, EEGs, ERPs, magnetoencephalography, and eye tracking. Applications include diagnosis, the longitudinal assessment, and the identification of individuals at risk of disease onset.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A

allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: An overview of the conceptual and technical foundations of contemporary neuroscience from ancient times to the present. The subjects include synapses, neurons, brain organization, sensory, motor and regulatory systems, learning and memory, human brain function and dysfunction.

allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of topics in the addiction field, including drug pharmacology, models/approaches to investigate addiction, brain circuits, genetics, epigenetics, and the cellular and molecular biology of drug addiction.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Scientific Argumentation and Critical Thinking
allCourses.description: Explicitly teaches argument structure, deductive logic, inductive logic, and common fallacies in the biology context. Students identify assumptions and fallacies in faulty arguments and data figures and learn to compose sound arguments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Human Neuroimaging Lab
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Students who require this lab for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Hands-on laboratory course in human neuroimaging, with particular emphasis on using MRI to understand brain function and how it changes over the course of the lifespan and with disease.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Model Systems in Biology
allCourses.description: On the use of animal and in vitro models in biomedical research, focusing on assumptions, promises, limitations, and compromises.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Foundations in Neuroimmunology
allCourses.description: The immune system supports normal brain development as well as controls central nervous system (CNS) infections and augments neurodegenerative and neurological diseases. Assesses how the immune system contributes to both host defense and disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI M121

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Into the Human Brain
allCourses.description: Explores different methods for studying the human brain in vivo (EEG, MRI, TMS, and others). Discusses ways to measure and manipulate brain activity directly and indirectly and how these different approaches complement each other.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: The Transparent Brain
allCourses.restriction: Students who require this course for completion of their degree have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Teaches students how to perform new 3-D histology techniques that reveal the complex circuitry of the brain in unprecedented detail. Students work with real brain samples as part of ongoing neuroscience research projects. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Neurodegenerative Diseases
allCourses.description: Clinical and epidemiological aspects of neurodegenerative diseases causing dementia are reviewed, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, and Frontotemporal Dementia. Seminar format includes student presentation and group discussion.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cognitive Neuroepigenetics
allCourses.description: Current topics in the emerging field of cognitive neuroepigenetics focusing on understanding the underlying epigenetic mechanisms of memory formation and persistence. Primary literature is used to explore these processes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Sex Differences in the Brain
allCourses.description: Explores the neural bases of sex influences on brain function.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences

allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An overview of brain mechanisms of hearing, including perception of simple sounds, speech, and music. Begins with sound itself, and looks at processing by the ear, auditory pathways, auditory cortex, and beyond. Also auditory development, learning, and clinical issues.

allCourses.title: Brain Dysfunction and Repair
allCourses.restriction: Neurobiology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the disruptions in brain function that underlie disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinsonism, schizophrenia, and depression, and the basis for drug therapies. The brain's ability to repair itself after damage and the pros and cons of that repair.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neurobiology of Aging
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary overview of the functional capacity of the aging brain, its structural changes and the mechanisms underlying function and structure. Emphasis is on successful brain aging and those mechanisms which lead to the development of Alzheimer's disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI N110"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI N115A"}]}]}

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Developmental Neurobiology
allCourses.description: The development of the nervous system is discussed with emphasis on the processes that underlie the appearance of complex and highly ordered neural circuits. Topics include neural induction, specification, migration and death; axon growth, and neural circuit formation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 93 or BIO SCI H93

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropharmacology
allCourses.description: Survey of neurotransmitter systems, focusing on how transmitters are made, how they interact with their receptors, and how drugs can influence these processes to alter neural function and behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI N110"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI N115A"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Neurobiology
allCourses.description: Provides a fundamental understanding of how the brain works at the molecular level. Topics include nature and actions of molecules that regulate the functioning of the brain and cellular mechanisms underlying learning and memory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Wiring the Developing Brain
allCourses.description: The development of the nervous system is discussed with particular emphasis on the processes that underlie the appearance of complex and highly ordered neural circuits. Basic neurodevelopmental processes are discussed and correlated with normal brain function/dysfunction.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI N110"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI N115A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI N152"}]}]}

allCourses.description: Current topics focused on understanding the molecular mechanisms that contribute to synaptic plasticity, learning, and memory. Primary literature is used to explore the variety of molecular mechanisms underlying these processes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neurobiology of Learning and Memory
allCourses.description: How the brain and behavior change as a result of experience, with an emphasis on identifying the neurochemical processes through which memory is stored and the parts of the brain that are involved.

allCourses.description: Explores why animals behave the way they do from evolutionary/mechanistic perspectives. Considers selective pressures and evolutionary constraints that shape animal behavior and the underlying neural and hormonal mechanisms by using examples such as why dogs bark, why some birds migrate.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Language and the Brain
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Research analysis on biological bases of human linguistic capacity. Development, focusing on hemispheric specialization, plasticity; localization of specific linguistic functions in adults, with emphasis on study of aphasias; relation of linguistic capacity to general cognitive capacity, considering research on retardation.

allCourses.description: How neuroscience uses tools of many disciplines, from imaging to behavior, to develop and test hypotheses about functions of specific parts of the brain. Basic organization of nerve cells/vertebrate nervous system; methods of visualizing nerve cells; neural connections/activity patterns.
