allCourses.description: Introduction to the neural basis of human perceptual, motor, and cognitive abilities. Topics include sensory perception, motor control, memory, language, attention, emotion, frontal lobe function, functional brain imaging, and neuropsychological disorders.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 7A or (PSYCH 9A and PSYCH 9B) or PSY BEH 9 or (PSY BEH 11A and PSY BEH 11B) or BIO SCI 35 or BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A

allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSYCH 7A or PSCI 11A or PSYCH 9A or BIO SCI 99.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Regenerative Neurobiology
allCourses.description: Explores the field of regenerative neurobiology. Both basic stem cell discoveries and their potential clinical application to brain disorders examined. Opportunities, challenges, and implications of this research also discussed.

allCourses.description: Introduction to the theoretical principles and biological mechanisms underlying how brains acquire, assimilate, store, and retrieve information, and how they compute adaptive responses to external inputs.

allCourses.description: Visual perception and the anatomy and physiology of the visual system. Topics include the retina and the visual pathway; visual sensitivity; color vision; spatial vision; motion perception; and the development of the visual system.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Neurobiology and Behavior
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of neurobiology and behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biomedical Engr: Premedical Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the central topics of biomedical engineering. Offers a perspective on bioengineering as a discipline in a seminar format. Principles of problem solving, design, engineering inventiveness, entrepreneurship, information access, communication, ethics, teamwork, and social responsibility are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Biomechanics I

allCourses.description: Introduction to statics and dynamics. Topics include rigid bodies, analysis of structures, forces in beams, moments of inertia, friction, kinetics, work, and energy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7C and MATH 3A and MATH 3D and BME 60B

allCourses.title: Biomechanics II
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biomedical Engr: Premedical Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to biomechanics from subcellular to tissue levels. Introduction to stress, strain, and constitutive laws of cells and tissues. Emphasis is placed on biosolids. Introduction to elastic and viscoelastic behaviors with emphasis on the standard linear model of viscoelasticity.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BME 110A

allCourses.title: Photomedicine
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies the use of optical and engineering-based systems (laser-based) for diagnosis, treating diseases, manipulation of cells and cell function. Physical, optical, and electro-optical principles are explored regarding molecular, cellular, organ, and organism applications.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7E or PHYSICS 3C

allCourses.title: Introduction to Biomedical Imaging
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to imaging modalities widely used in medicine and biology, including X-ray, computed tomography (CT), nuclear medicine (PET and SPET), ultrasonic imaging, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), optical tomography, imaging contrast, imaging processing, and complementary nature of the imaging modalities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BME 130 or EECS 50 or EECS 150

allCourses.title: Spectroscopy and Imaging of Biological Systems
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biomedical Engr: Premedical Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of spectroscopy; absorption; molecular orbitals; multiphoton transitions; Jablonski diagram; fluorescence anisotropy; fluorescence decay; quenching; FRET; excited state reactions; solvent relaxations; instruments; microscopy: wide field, LSM, TPE; fluorescent probes, fluctuations spectroscopy; optical resolution and super-resolution; CARS and SHG microscopy.

allCourses.title: Design of Biomedical Electronics
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analog and digital circuits in bioinstrumentation. AC and DC circuit analysis, design and construction of filter and amplifiers using operational amplifier, digitization of signals and data acquisition, bioelectrical signals, design and construction of ECG instrument, bioelectrical signal measurement and analysis.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BME 60A and BME 130

allCourses.title: Microfabrication
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Essentials of photolithography, soft-lithography, microfabrication, Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS), BioMEMS; applications in biomedical engineering.

allCourses.title: Microfluidics and Lab-on-a-Chip
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of microfluidics and state-of-the-art micro Total Analysis Systems (uTAS). Lab-on-a-Chip for bimolecular assays with device design principles for microscale sample preparation, flow transport, bimolecular manipulation, separation and detection, and the technologies for integrating these devices into microsystems.

allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: BME 111

allCourses.title: Biomedical Microdevices
allCourses.description: In-depth review of microfabricated devices designed for biological and medical applications. Studies of the design, implementation, manufacturing, and marketing of commercial and research bio-medical devices.

allCourses.description: Fundamentals of heat and mass transfer, similarities in the respective rate equations. Emphasis on practical application of fundamental principles.

allCourses.title: Biomedical Engineering Internship
allCourses.description: Students majoring in BME may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Independent research conducted in the lab of a biomedical engineering core faculty member. A formal written report of the research conducted is required at the conclusion of the quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Biomedical Big Data
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis and visualization of large biomedical datasets. Topics covered include cloud computing, learning Structured Query Language (SQL), database normalization and joins, using Google’s BigQuery, using the statistical analysis package R, machine learning algorithms, application of machine learning for classification problems.

allCourses.title: Biomedical Imaging and Biophotonics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed as a subfield of optical imaging and biophotonics as it applies to their applications to basic lifesciences and in vivo imaging to diagnose disease. Topics span all of of the areas of biophotonics and techniques.

allCourses.title: Digital Health
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Digital health is the convergence of genomics and technology to radically change the way health and medicine is practiced. Explores the history of healthcare in the U.S., its current status, and the future of digital health.

allCourses.title: Personalized Medical Devices
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to fundamental aspects of medical devices and discusses therapeutic as well as diagnostic devices. Basic aspects of microfluidics and biology critical to personalized medical systems are studied. Typical FDA approval pathways for medical devices are presented.

allCourses.title: Molecular and Cellular Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engineering of physiological function at the genetic, cellular, and tissue scales. Topics include cloning and genetic engineering, extracellular matrix biomaterials, principles of regenerative medicine and tissue engineering, and experimental design.

allCourses.title: Molecular and Cellular Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engineering of physiological function at the genetic, cellular, and tissue scales. Topics include cloning and genetic engineering, extracellular matrix biomaterials, principles of regenerative medicine and tissue engineering, and experimental design.

allCourses.title: Microscale Tissue Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engineering of physiological function at the scale of individual cells. Topics include cell micropatterning, microfluidic tissue culture, engineering the cellular microenvironment, and microphysiological systems.

allCourses.title: Microscale Tissue Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engineering of physiological function at the scale of individual cells. Topics include cell micropatterning, microfluidic tissue culture, engineering the cellular microenvironment, and microphysiological systems.

allCourses.title: Cardiovascular Mechanobiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in cellular engineering and mechanobiology, with focus on the cardiovascular system.  Tools and techniques used to manipulate and measure mechanical forces at the molecular, cellular, tissue, and organ levels, and their applications in cardiovascular devices and tissue engineering.

allCourses.title: Cardiovascular Mechanobiology
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in cellular engineering and mechanobiology, with focus on the cardiovascular system. Tools and techniques used to manipulate and measure mechanical forces at the molecular, cellular, tissue, and organ levels, and their applications in cardiovascular devices and tissue engineering.

allCourses.title: Systems Cell and Developmental Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces concepts needed to understand cell and developmental biology at the systems level, i.e., how the parts (molecules) work together to create a complex output. Emphasis on using mathematical/computational modeling to expand/modify insights provided by intuition.

allCourses.title: Linking Modeling and Experiments in Bioengineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of modeling based on experimental techniques in bioengineering. Construct and evaluate models of varying complexity and to relate them to experimental data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BME 220 and BME 221. BME 220 with a grade of B- or better. BME 221 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Stem Cell Therapy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate student only.
allCourses.description: Introduces new paradigms in regenerative medicine particularly those that involve stem cells, and emerging molecular, nano- and micro-engineered tools for in vivo imaging that is critical for studying and monitoring regeneration.

allCourses.title: Directed Evolution
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed evolution harnesses the processes of Darwinian evolution for biomolecular engineering goals. This class will begin with fundamental principles in evolutionary biology and move on to the experimental evolution techniques and their applications.

allCourses.title: Sensory Motor Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A quantitative and systems approach to understanding physiological systems. Systems covered include the nervous and musculoskeletal systems.

allCourses.title: Sensory Motor Systems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A quantitative and systems approach to understanding physiological systems. Systems covered include the nervous and musculoskeletal systems.

allCourses.title: Organ Transport Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A quantitative and systems approach to understanding physiological systems. Systems covered include the cardiopulmonary, circulatory, and renal systems.

allCourses.title: Organ Transport Systems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Applies engineering models and mathematics to understand human physiology in order to understand the physiology. Covers the pulmonary, cardiac, and cardiovascular systems focusing on transport phenomena.

allCourses.title: Biofluid Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces principles of biofluid mechanics in a research oriented scheme and approaches a wide spectrum of biofluid related problems in human body and solutions that involves engineering concepts.

allCourses.title: Critical Thinking in Cardiovascular Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Interpretation and critical assessment of current cardiovascular research in basic science, application of engineering tools, and clinical cardiology and cardiovascular surgery. Open only to graduate students engaged in research.

allCourses.title: Molecular and Cellular Biophotonics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles underlying the application of photonic technologies to biomolecular and cellular systems. Sample technologies Optical Tweezers, Linear and Nonlinear Optical Microscopy and Fluorescence Lifetime and Correlation Methods, and their use to investigate emergent problems in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology.

allCourses.title: Tissue and Organ Biophotonics
allCourses.description: Principles underlying the application of photonic technologies to tissues, organs, organisms. Sample technologies include Optical Coherence Tomography, Optical Speckle Imaging, Optoacoustic Imaging, Wide-Field Spectroscopic Imaging, Diffuse Optical Spectroscopy. Addressing the use of these technologies to detect/monitor disease and physiological processes.

allCourses.title: Applied Engineering Mathematics I
allCourses.description: Analytical techniques applied to engineering problems in transport phenomena, process dynamics and control, and thermodynamics.

allCourses.title: Applied Engineering Mathematics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on biomedical system identification. Includes fundamental techniques of model building and testing such as formulation, solution of governing equations, sensitivity theory, identifiability theory, and uncertainty analysis.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts in programming and machine learning. The goal is to provide an accessible introduction to the field of machine learning and related techniques for students with a wide variety of engineering degrees.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Clinical Medicine for Biomedical Engineering

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of microfluidics; LOC (Lab-on-a-Chip) device design, fabrication, operation principles for microscale flow transport, biomolecular manipulation/separation/detection, sample preparation; integrated microfluidic technologies for micro total analysis systems (microTAS) and bioassays.
