allCourses.title: Chemical Processes and Material Balances
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to chemical engineering and the industries where chemical engineers play vital roles. Problem-solving skills and techniques. Quantitative calculations and applications using mass and energy balances. Stoichiometric equations, multiple bypasses, and others in process industries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B and PHYSICS 7C and (CHEM 1B or CHEM H2B)

allCourses.title: Process Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of thermodynamics: definitions, basic concepts, and laws; property relationships; construction of thermodynamic charts and tables; energy balances; phase and chemical equilibria; combined mass and energy balances.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBE 40A and (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N). CBE 40A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Elements of chemical engineering thermodynamics, including equilibrium and stability; equations of state; generalized correlations of properties of materials; properties of ideal and non-ideal mixtures; thermodynamics of real solutions; ideal and non-ideal phase equilibria; chemical equilibria for ideal and non-ideal solutions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 10 and MATH 2D and CBE 40B. CBE 40B with a grade of C- or better

prerequisite_for.title: Introduction to Numerical Methods in Engineering

allCourses.title: Biopharmaceutics & Nanomedicine
allCourses.restriction: Prerequisite required
allCourses.description: Introduces theories and tools of new drug formulations. Particularly new novel therapeutics based on biological materials, pathological characteristics utilized to achieve the maximum efficacy and specificity, and drug delivery systems based on emerging nanotechnology are extensively discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHRMSCI 170B

allCourses.title: Reaction Kinetics and Reactor Design
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to quantitative analysis of chemical reactions and chemical reactor design. Reactor operations including batch, continuous stirred tank, and tubular reactor. Homogeneous and heterogeneous reactions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 1C and MATH 3D and CBEMS 45B and CBEMS 45C. CBEMS 45B with a grade of C- or better. CBEMS 45C with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Biochemical Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of engineering principles to biochemical processes. Topics include microbial pathways, energetics and control systems, enzyme and microbial kinetics and the design and analysis of biological reactors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 110 and CHEM 1C and MATH 3D

allCourses.title: Kinetics of Biochemical Networks
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Principles from statistical mechanics, thermodynamics, and chemical kinetics applied to biochemical systems, from fundamental processes such as receptor-ligand binding and enzyme catalysis, to complex cellular functions including signal transduction and gene regulation.

allCourses.title: Field Practicum in Environmental Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of concepts from engineering and microbiology to the characterization and analysis of microbial pollution in coastal waters. Topics include public health microbiology, microbial diversity and ecology, and molecular diagnostics of waterborne pathogens. Laboratory exercises and a field-scale experiment.

allCourses.title: Biomaterials: Structural Biology and Assembly
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of fundamental concepts in structural biology (proteins, DNA/RNA, carbohydrates, lipids), biomolecular thermodynamics, and molecular interactions to the design of novel biomaterials via self-assembly.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 45C and CBEMS 110

allCourses.title: Transport Phenomena in Living Systems
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering and Chemical Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to transport phenomena in cellular and whole organ systems. Application of transport theory including advection and diffusion to the movement of molecules in biological systems, including the cardiovascular system (heart and microcirculation), and the lung.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 125A.

allCourses.title: Momentum Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fluid statics, surface tension, Newton's law of viscosity, non-Newtonian and complex flows, momentum equations, laminar and turbulent flow, velocity profiles, flow in pipes and around objects, piping systems design, pumps and mixing, and other applications to chemical and related industries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CBEMS 45C or CBEMS 65B) and MATH 3D. CBEMS 45C with a grade of C- or better. CBEMS 65B with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Heat Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of conduction, radiation, and convection of heat; phenomenological rate laws, differential and macroscopic energy balances; heat transfer rates, steady state and unsteady state conduction, convection; applications to chemical and related industries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 125A. CBEMS 125A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Mass Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Molecular and continuum approaches to diffusion and convection in multi-component mixtures; steady state, quasi-steady state and transient mass transfer; effect of reactions on mass transfer; convective mass transfer; simultaneous mass, heat and momentum transfer; applications to chemical and related industries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 125B

allCourses.title: Introduction to Numerical Methods in Engineering
allCourses.description: An introduction to the fundamentals of numerical analysis and the computer algorithms in MATLAB for the solution of engineering problems, with emphasis on problems arising in chemical engineering thermodynamics, transport phenomena, and reaction engineering.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 45C

allCourses.title: Separation Processes
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of equilibria and mass and energy balances for design of separation processes. Use of equilibrium laws for design of distillation, absorption, stripping, and extraction equipment. Design of multicomponent separators.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CBEMS 45B or CBEMS 65A or ENGRMAE 91) and (CBEMS 45C or CBEMS 65B or ENGRMAE 115). CBEMS 45B with a grade of C- or better. CBEMS 65A with a grade of C- or better. ENGRMAE 91 with a grade of C- or better. CBEMS 45C with a grade of C- or better. CBEMS 65B with a grade of C- or better. ENGRMAE 115 with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Bioseparation Processes
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Recovery and purification of biologically produced proteins and chemicals. Basic principles and engineering design of various separation processes including chromatography, electrophoresis, extraction, crystallization, and membrane separation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 45A and CBEMS 45B and CBEMS 45C and CBEMS 125A.

allCourses.title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Chemistry Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. CHEM 133 and CHEM 170 cannot both be taken for credit.
allCourses.description: Advanced treatment of nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, and radioactive-decay processes. Introduction to nuclear activation analysis, isotope effects, radiation chemistry, hot-atom chemistry, nuclear age-dating methods, nuclear reactors, and nuclear power.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CHEM M3C or CHEM 1C or CHEM H2C) and MATH 2D

allCourses.title: Introduction to Bioreactor Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Unique features of bioreactors. Analyses and design of bioreactors of batch, fed-batch, and continuous flow types. Microbial reactors with and without cell recycles.  Bioreactor operations for industrial-important biological products and for biological treatment of wastewater.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 110.

allCourses.title: Chemical Process Control
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Dynamic responses and control of chemical process equipment, dynamic modeling of chemical processes, linear system analysis, analyses and design of feedback loops and advanced control systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 110 and CBEMS 125B and CBEMS 125C

allCourses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory I
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Experimental study of thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat and mass transfer. Operation and evaluation of process equipment, data analysis.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 110 and (CBEMS 125C or BME 150)

allCourses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory II
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Continuation of the CBEMS 140A covering mass transfer operations such as distillation, absorption, extraction, etc. Rate and equilibria studies in simple chemical systems with and without reaction. Study of chemical process. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 130 and CBEMS 135 and CBEMS 140A

allCourses.title: Nano-Scale Materials and Applications
allCourses.description: Overview of the chemistry, physics, and applications of nanometer-scale materials. Explore the effects of composition, bonding, and confinement on physical properties of nanomaterials, their chemical syntheses, and their device physics in electronic, optoelectronic, and energy technologies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A) and MATH 2B and PHYSICS 7D

allCourses.title: Chemistry and Technology for the Nuclear Fuel Cycle
allCourses.description: Introduces basic concepts of nuclear chemistry and focuses on chemical engineering aspects of the nuclear power industry. A broad survey of the nuclear fuel cycle (uranium processing, reactor concepts, spent fuel treatment and repositories) will be given.

allCourses.title: Chemical Engineering Design I
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to process design; flow sheets for chemical processes; synthesis of multicomponent separation sequences and reaction paths; synthesis of heat exchange networks; computer-aided design and simulation of processes and components pacts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 110 and CBEMS 125C and CBEMS 130

allCourses.title: Chemical Engineering Design II
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Application of chemical engineering basics to practical design problems; process economics; process safety; environmental impacts; a major team design project with progress reports, oral presentation, and technical report with engineering drawings and economics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 149A

allCourses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to physical aspects of polymers, including configuration and conformation of polymer chains and characterization techniques; crystallinity, viscoelasticity, mechanical properties, polymer alloys, processing, and application.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and (CBEMS 110 or CBEMS 165)

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior and Design Principles
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles governing structure and mechanical behavior of materials, relationship relating microstructure and mechanical response with application to elasticity, plasticity, yielding, necking, creep, and fracture of materials. Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize the properties of materials. Design parameters.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

prerequisite_list.title: Principles of Materials Science and Engineering

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize mechanical properties of materials. Emphasis on correlations between property and microstructure. Experiments include: plastic stability in tension, effect of grain size on flow stress, microstructural engineering.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Composite Materials Design
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering and Materials Science Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fiber-reinforced composites for mechanical applications. Properties of reinforcing fibers. Manufacture of fibers and composites. Micromechanics of fiber composites. Strength criteria and failure modes. Macromechanics in design of laminated composite structures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and ENGR 150.

allCourses.title: Ceramic Materials
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A technical elective for students interested in the materials area. Topics covered include structure and properties of ceramics, and design with ceramics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Advanced Lab in Synthesis of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Synthesis and characterization of organic and inorganic materials including polymers and oxides. Techniques include electron and scanning probe microscopy, gel permeation chromatography, X-ray diffraction, porosimetry, and thermal analysis. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 or (CHEM 131A and CHEM 131B)

allCourses.title: Computer Techniques in Experimental Research
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles and practical guidelines of automated materials testing. Computer fundamentals, programming languages, data acquisition and control hardware, interfacint techniques, programming strategies, data analysis, data storage, safeguard procedures.

allCourses.title: X-ray Diffraction, Electron Microscopy, and Microanalysis
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Material characterization using X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Topics include X-ray diffraction and analysis; SEM imaging and microanalysis. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: X-ray Diffraction, Electron Microscopy, and Microanalysis Lab
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Material characterization using X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Topics include X-ray diffraction and analysis; SEM imaging and microanalysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Materials Kinetics and Phase Transformations
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Treatment of the kinetics of solid-state reactions and reactions at interfaces. Thermodynamics and kinetics of phase transformations, including solidification processes, diffusional and diffusionless phase transformations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and (ENGRMAE 91 or CBEMS 45C or CBEMS 65B). ENGRMAE 91 with a grade of C- or better. CBEMS 45C with a grade of C- or better. CBEMS 65B with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Electronic and Optical Properties in Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers the electronic, optical, and dielectric properties of crystalline and amorphous materials to provide a foundation of the underlying physical principles governing the properties of existing and emerging electronic and photonic materials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7D and PHYSICS 7E and MATH 3A and MATH 3D

allCourses.title: Semiconductor Device Packaging
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the semiconductor device packaging and assembly process. Electrical, thermal, optical, and mechanical aspects of package design and reliability. Special topics on optoelectronics packaging will be covered.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 45B

allCourses.title: Design Failure Investigation
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Survey of mechanisms by which devices fail, including overload, fatigue, corrosion, and wear. Use of fractography and other evidence to interpret failure modes and specify design/manufacturing changes. Students redesign failed parts or structures based on actual parts and/or case histories.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Surface and Adhesion Science
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Structure, thermodynamics of, kinetics, and reactions on surfaces. Surface electronic and mechanical properties and characterization of all classes of materials including metals, semiconductors, ceramics, polymers, and soft materials. Adhesion between different materials is also addressed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CBEMS 110 or CBEMS 165) and (CBEMS 141 or CBEMS 169)

allCourses.title: Senior Design Project I
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Materials Science Engineering Majors only. CBEMS 189A-CBEMS 189B-CBEMS 189C must be taken in the same academic year.
allCourses.description: Group supervised senior design projects that deal with materials selection in engineering design and that involve case studies in ethics, safety, design, failure modes, new products, and patents. Activities conclude with a presentation of the projects. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Senior Design Project II
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Materials Science Engineering Majors only. CBEMS 189A-CBEMS 189B-CBEMS 189C must be taken in the same academic year.
allCourses.description: Group supervised senior design projects that deal with materials selection in engineering design and that involve case studies in ethics, safety, design, failure modes, new products, and patents. Activities conclude with a presentation of the projects. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 189A

allCourses.title: Senior Design Project III
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Materials Science Engineering Majors only. CBEMS 189A-CBEMS 189B-CBEMS 189C must be taken in the same academic year.
allCourses.description: Group supervised senior design projects that deal with materials selection in engineering design and that involve case studies in ethics, safety, design, failure modes, new products, and patents. Activities conclude with a presentation of the projects. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 189B

allCourses.title: Materials Selection and Design
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Meaning and phases of design. Design considerations. Safety issues and engineering ethics. Codes and standards. Materials selection in design. Materials selection to meet specific requirements. Statistical considerations. Engineering economics. Seminars on materials selection and design by industry leaders and faculty.

allCourses.title: Materials Outreach
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Demonstrates major concepts in Materials Science and Engineering. Concepts of materials engineering covered include deformation in crystalline solids, effects of heat treatment on mechanical properties, thermal barrier materials, composites design, mechanical behavior of polymers, superconductivity in ceramics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Chemical Engineering and Materials Science
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chemical Engineering and Materials Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Group Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Group study of selected topics in engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: For undergraduate engineering majors in supervised but independent readings, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in The School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Reaction Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in reaction engineering, reactor stability analysis, diffusional effect in heterogeneous catalysis, energy balance, optimization of reactor operation, dispersed in phase reactors.

allCourses.title: Kinetics of Biochemical Networks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles from statistical mechanics, thermodynamics, and chemical kinetics applied to biochemical systems, from fundamental processes such as receptor-ligand binding and enzyme catalysis, to complex cellular functions including signal transduction and gene regulation.

allCourses.title: Bioengineering with Recombinant Microorganisms
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engineering and biological principles important in recombinant cell technology. Host/vector selection; plasmid propagation; optimization of cloned gene expression; metabolic engineering; protein secretion; experimental techniques; modeling of recombinant cell systems.

allCourses.title: Biomaterials: Structural Biology and Assembly
allCourses.description: Application of fundamental concepts in structural biology (proteins, DNA/RNA, carbohydrates, lipids), biomolecular thermodynamics, and molecular interactions to the design of novel biomaterials via self-assembly.

allCourses.title: Transport Phenomena
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Heat, mass, and momentum transfer theory from the viewpoint of the basic transport equations. Steady and unsteady state; laminar and turbulent flow; boundary layer theory, mechanics of turbulent transport with specific application to complex chemical engineering situations.

allCourses.title: Drug Delivery
allCourses.description: Introduction to design of drug delivery systems. Includes physicochemical and pharmacokinetic considerations in drug formulations, types of therapeutics, routes of administration, biomaterials, and novel drug delivery systems.

allCourses.title: Molecular and Cellular Biophotonics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles underlying the application of photonic technologies to biomolecular and cellular systems. Sample technologies Optical Tweezers, Linear and Nonlinear Optical Microscopy and Fluorescence Lifetime and Correlation Methods and their use to investigate emergent problems in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology.

allCourses.title: Tissue and Organ Biophotonics
allCourses.description: Principles underlying the application of photonic technologies to tissues, organs, organisms. Sample technologies include Optical Coherence Tomography, Optical Speckle Imaging, Optoacoustic Imaging, Wide-Field Spectroscopic Imaging, Diffuse Optical Spectroscopy. Addressing the use of these technologies to detect/monitor disease and physiological processes.

allCourses.title: Colloid Science and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the basic foundations of colloid science, interfacial phenomena, suspensions and complex fluids, and engineering and assembly of colloidal materials.

allCourses.title: Applied Engineering Mathematics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analytical techniques applied to engineering problems in transport phenomena, process dynamics and control, and thermodynamics.

allCourses.title: Bioseparation Processes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Recovery and purification of biologically produced proteins and chemicals. Basic principles and engineering design of various separation processes including chromatography, electrophoresis, extraction, crystallization, and membrane separation.

allCourses.title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced treatment of nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, and radioactive-decay processes. Introduction to nuclear activation analysis, isotope effects, radiation chemistry, hot-atom chemistry, nuclear age-dating methods, nuclear reactors, and nuclear power.

allCourses.title: Advanced Engineering Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to modern thermodynamics and applications, with a focus on aspects relevant to chemical and materials engineering. Mathematical tools; equilibrium and stability; microscope rigorous equations of state; molecular-level thermodynamics of real mixtures; and phase and chemical equilibrium.

allCourses.title: Nano-Scale Materials and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of the chemistry, physics, and applications of nanometer-scale materials. Explore the effects of composition, bonding, and confinement on physical properties of nanomaterials, their chemical syntheses, and their device physics in electronic, optoelectronic, and energy technologies.

allCourses.title: Physical and Geometrical Optics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the practical aspects of optics and optical engineering, starting at the fundamentals. Topics include geometrical optics, ray tracing, polarization optics, interferometers, and diffractive optics.

allCourses.title: Applied Optics
allCourses.description: Focuses on the treatment of a wide variety of tools and techniques used in optics, particularly in research. Subjects include an introduction to lasers, optical detection, coherent optics, spectroscopic techniques, and selected topics corresponding to the interest of the students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 242A

allCourses.title: Chemistry and Technology for the Nuclear Fuel Cycle
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces basic concepts of nuclear chemistry and focuses on chemical engineering aspects of the nuclear power industry. A broad survey of the nuclear fuel cycle (uranium processing, reactor concepts, spent fuel treatment and repositories) will be given.

allCourses.title: Detection and Measurement of Radiation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of detection and measurement of ionizing radiation; both theory and practical aspects of measurement techniques for alpha, beta, gamma, and neutron radiation, properties of different detector materials, electronics and data treatments, and analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 233 or CBEMS 233

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Chemical Engineering and Materials Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chemical Engineering and Materials Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Systems Microbiology Research
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A research and journal club seminar that covers topics on bacteria and phage using approaches and principles from biology, engineering, and physics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Optoelectronics Packaging
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic and current issues in the packaging of integrated circuits (IC) and fiber-optic devices are discussed.

allCourses.title: Seminars in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminars scheduled each year by individual faculty in major field of interest.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Master of Science Thesis Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the thesis required for the M.S. degree.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Seminars in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presentation of advanced topics and reports of current research efforts in chemical engineering and materials science.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Individual Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Chemical Processing and Materials Balances
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to chemical engineering and the industries where chemical engineers play vital roles. Problem-solving skills and techniques. Quantitative calculations and applications using mass and energy balances. Stoichiometric equations, multiple bypasses, and others in process industries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B and CHEM 1B and PHYSICS 7C

allCourses.title: Chemical Processing and Energy Balances
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of thermodynamics: definitions, basic concepts, and laws; property relationships; construction of thermodynamic charts and tables; energy balances; phase and chemical equilibria; combined mass and energy balances.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CBEMS 45A or PHYSICS 7E) and MATH 3A. CBEMS 45A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Elements of chemical engineering thermodynamics, including equilibrium and stability; equations of state; generalized correlations of properties of materials; properties of ideal and non-ideal mixtures; thermodynamics of real solutions; ideal and non-ideal phase equilibria; chemical equilibria for ideal and non-ideal solutions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EECS 10 or ENGRMAE 10) and MATH 2D and CBEMS 45B. CBEMS 45B with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Principles of Materials Science and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the experimental techniques to characterize the properties of engineering materials. Emphasis on understanding the influence of microstructure on elastic, plastic, and fracture behavior. Topics include microstructure characterization, heat treatment, grain size effect, precipitation hardening, and impact loading. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Treatment of the laws of thermodynamics and their application in understanding properties and equilibrium states of engineering materials. Develops relationships pertaining to multiphase equilibrium and presents graphical constructions for interpretation of phase diagrams. Statistical thermodynamics in relation to materials phenomena.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A) and PHYSICS 7C

allCourses.title: Diffusion in Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Mass transfer in solids. Models of diffusion and the treatment of steady-state and non-steady state diffusion phenomena and ion-migration. Mechanisms controlling kinetics of diffusion and the role of material structure and point defects. Diffusion in binary systems and Kirkendall effect.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CBEMS 65A. CBEMS 65A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Research in the Latino Community
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students engage in firsthand research in the local Orange County environment. Students identify a research problem, conduct a literature review, develop questions and/or hypotheses, appropriate methods, and write a proposal.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Two courses from CHC/LAT 61 or CHC/LAT 62 or CHC/LAT 63 and two courses from CHC/LAT 110-189.

allCourses.title: Supervised Research for Chicano/Latino Studies Majors
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies majors only.
allCourses.description: Students who have designed a research project & begun collecting data in CHC/LAT 101 will continue to collect/analyze data for their research projects. By end of the course, students will be prepared to write up their findings in CHC/LAT 102W.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHC/LAT 101.

allCourses.title: Chicano/Latino Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: Taught as a writing and research seminar in Chicano/Latino Studies.  Student develops own project; engages in peer editing; drafts, writes, and presents paper at Spring research conference.  Prior course work in Chicano/Latino Studies helpful, i.e., CHC/LAT 61, 62, 63.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHC/LAT 101. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Topics in Chicano Literature and Culture
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter. Taught in English.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Film Media and the Latino Community
allCourses.description: Uses film as a resource for understanding contemporary issues and problems facing the Chicano/Latino community.  (Does not study cinema as a genre.).

allCourses.title: Latino Music:  A View of Its Diversity and Strength
allCourses.description: A survey of the music of the many Latin cultures of the Americas including Mexico, Central and South America, as well as the Caribbean and of those many Latin cultures which thrive and survive in the United States.

allCourses.title: Afro-Latin American Music
allCourses.description: Musical culture of Afro-Latin American peoples, emphasizing Spanish-speaking Caribbean.  Topics include:  background in West Africa, the persistence of traditions in the Caribbean, the commercial music of the twentieth century, the connections between musical culture, religion and the economy.

allCourses.title: Reading Images Culturally
allCourses.description: Provides analytical tools necessary to undertake research on visual representations. Images, as cultural productions, are steeped in the values, ideologies, and taken-for-granted beliefs of the culture which produced them. Of concern are representations of race, identity, gender, and the "Other.".

allCourses.title: Anthropology of Food
allCourses.description: Examines how food communicates ideas about ethnocentrism, disgust, privilege, gender, race, labor, social identities and hierarchies, globalization, power, and the "Western diet" and its health consequences.

allCourses.title: Peoples and Cultures of Latin America
allCourses.description: Surveys the prehistory of Latin America and its indigenous cultures, emphasizing the impact of colonial rule, capitalism, and 20th-century transformations.  Emphasis on communities from several countries. In some years, emphasis on comparisons between the Latin American and Caribbean experiences.

allCourses.title: Latina/Latino Pop:  Latina/Latino Popular Culture
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. History Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: With a focus on the politics of language and space/place, prepares students to critically analyze sites of Latina/Latino popular culture including: music, film, performance, sports, media, and varied subcultures.

allCourses.title: Engaging Latino Issues in Media
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to address contemporary issues related to Latinidad and Latinos according to a variety of media forms including commercial and independent news sources, talk shows, and Internet sites.  Issues range from immigration to electoral politics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Engaging Latino Issues in Media
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to address contemporary issues related to Latinidad and Latinos according to a variety of media forms including commercial and independent news sources, talk shows, and Internet sites. Issues range from immigration to electoral politics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Immigration, Nation, and Media
allCourses.description: Examines media shapes and reflects public opinion on immigration and its representation of immigrants, citizens, and ideas about the nation, and who belongs and who is a potential threat; as well as the relationship between scholars and journalists.

allCourses.title: Immigrant Emotionality
allCourses.description: Explores the emotional universe created by the Latin American immigrant experience, and guides students in the creation of a literary work based on an investigation into, or reflection on that experience.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Latinx Performance
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores Latinx cultural history from the 19th century to the present through the lens of theater and performance. Analyzes the Latinx experience as seen in plays, films, social media, visual culture, music, and archival sources.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Literature, Arts, Media, Culture
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Cuba: History, Culture, and Society
allCourses.description: Introduction to Cuban history, culture, and society using social science texts, visual and musical materials. Examines major historical moments including the historical relationship between the United States and explores evolution of Cuban music from the earliest times to present.

allCourses.title: Histories of Chicana/o/x and Latina/o/x Struggles for Civil Rights, 1960-1980
allCourses.description: Provides students with an opportunity to learn more about the historical, political, and social underpinnings that oriented the civil rights struggles of mid-to-late 20th-century Chicana/o/x and Latina/o/x activists.

allCourses.title: Chicana/Chicano History: Pre-Colonial to 1900
allCourses.description: Examines social history of the southwest region from antiquity to 1900. Discusses major questions, theory and research methods pertinent to Chicanas/Chicanos. Themes include: indigenous empires, conquest, colonialism, social stratification, ideology, marriage, sexuality, industrial capitalism, accommodation and resistance.

allCourses.title: Chicana/Chicano History: Twentieth Century
allCourses.description: Examines social history of the Southwest with emphasis on Mexican-origin people. Discusses major questions, theory and research methods pertinent to Chicana/Chicano history. Themes explored include: immigration, xenophobia, class struggle, leadership, generational cohorts, unionization, education, barrioization, ethnicity, patriarchy, sexuality.

allCourses.title: Interdisciplinary Legacies
allCourses.description: Students learn from the institutional histories and scholarship of the Chicano/Latino Studies faculty emeriti who founded the Department and contributed to its scholarly presence and impact.

allCourses.title: Twentieth-Century Mexico
allCourses.description: Examines the history of contemporary Mexico beginning with the Mexican Revolution and concluding with the present administration. Social, economic, and political effects of the Revolution; formation of a "one-party democracy"; economic transformation of the nation; the present crisis.

allCourses.title: U.S. Latino Literature and Cultures
allCourses.description: Focuses on aspects of literature, art, cultural production, and history of the multifaceted Latino cultures that have developed within the United States.  Focuses on one group, such as Caribbean Americans, Chicanos, Central Americans, or a comparative perspective of several groups.

allCourses.title: Latinas in the Twentieth Century U.S.
allCourses.description: Latinas in the U.S. from 1900 to present, offering a diversity of their cultures, regional histories, sexualities, generations, and classes.

allCourses.title: Comparative Latino Populations
allCourses.description: Provides foundation for understanding of Chicano/Latino Studies as an interdisciplinary field of inquiry. Focus on the history, arts, cultures of distinct (Mexican, Cuban, Puerto Rican, Central American) Latino communities. Topics include: precolonial history and culture, conquest, mestizaje, colonialism/neocolonialism, resistance.

allCourses.title: Chicano/Chicana Labor History
allCourses.description: Examines origins of Latino/ Latina labor from colonial period to present. Emphasis on the issues of race, culture, class, and gender. Focus on processes and institutions including: encomienda, migration, unions, informal economies, Bracero program, domestic work.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Chicano/Latino History
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino History. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Latina/Latino Queer Sexualities
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the notion of "queer" in relation to Chicanas/Chicanos and Latinas/Latinos and provides students with theoretical frameworks to explore the shifting categories of sexuality, gender, Chicano, Latino within the scholarship areas of Chicana/Chicano and Latina/Latino Studies.

allCourses.title: Latinos and the Law
allCourses.description: Examines a range of theoretical, empirical, and policy approaches to legal issues affecting the Latino population, with emphasis on California. Discusses topics concerning the purpose of law, the creation of law, and the enforcement of law.

allCourses.title: Latinx Racial Formations
allCourses.description: Students explore the meanings attributed to Latina/o/x racial identities over time; the political, economic, and social structures that have shaped those identities; and their impact on Latinx self-concepts, interpersonal/intra-community relations, and life chances.

allCourses.title: Comparative Minority Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the political experiences of Blacks, Latinos, and Asian Americans in the United States from roughly 1950 to the present. Focuses on how each group has pursued political empowerment via both conventional political channels and social movements.

allCourses.title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.

allCourses.title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

allCourses.title: Sex and Conquest in Latin America
allCourses.description: Competing ideas of masculinity and femininity, sexual violence, sexual identities, and gendered hierarchies informed how the Spanish engaged in military and religious domination of Mexican and Andean communities, as well as the forms of native resistance throughout colonial Latin America.

allCourses.title: Latinos in U.S. Politics
allCourses.description: Comparing the political issues facing Latino groups by examining their migration histories, voting behavior, nonelectoral participation, and policy issues.  Latino issues are examined on the national, state, and local levels, including formal representation, immigration, affirmative action, and language policy.

allCourses.title: Latin American Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the main concepts and theoretical approaches underlying the study of Latin American politics, examines recent political dynamics, and explores the challenges the region faces in the twenty-first century and how countries will attempt to address them.

allCourses.title: Revolution in Latin America
allCourses.description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada.  Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

allCourses.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Social Control
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides a historical and sociological survey of racial and ethnic group relations in contexts of crime control, emphasizing the roles of racial ideology, structural racism, and social movements in shaping these dynamic relations, and their significance to American liberal democracy.

allCourses.title: Community, Social Justice, and Health Equity Research for Action
allCourses.description: Focuses on community as a unit of identity, community, well-being, and social justice perspectives and initiatives to promote community health. Addresses community change and improvements in community well-being, with a focus on health equity research for action.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 or PUBHLTH 2 or CHC/LAT 61 or CHC/LAT 62 or CHC/LAT 63

prerequisite_list.title: Case Studies in Public Health Practice

allCourses.title: Cross-Cultural Research on Urban Gangs
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SocEcol-Urban & Regional Plan Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Taking an urban policy approach, examines the background and contemporary traditions of gangs in several ethnic groups including African-, Asian-, and Mexican-Americans. Cross-cultural exploration of the varied facets of gang life. The major social-control institutions affecting them.

allCourses.title: Latino Metropolis
allCourses.description: Explores the processes of Latino urbanization in the United States and the spatialization of Latino identities, particularly in the context of Southern California with selected comparisons drawing from other cities.

allCourses.title: Culture Change and the Mexican People
allCourses.description: Reviews culture contact and colonization, innovation diffusion, acculturation, assimilation, culture conflict and marginality, modernization, urbanization, legal transformations. Mexico and the Southwestern U.S. are reviewed through several centuries to better appreciate the indigenous base of the Mexican people.

allCourses.title: Chicano/Latinos and Labor
allCourses.description: Explores theories that explain the occupational pathways and workplace experiences of Latinos in various work sectors. Investigates jobs such as migrant labor, child street vendors, Latina/Latino professionals, and Latinos migrating to the U.S. South that work in poultry processing plants.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
allCourses.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

allCourses.title: Feminisms of Color
allCourses.description: Surveys the development of Chicana feminist thought and practice.  Focuses on historical contemporary writings by and about Chicana feminists.  Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship in order to survey the diversity of Chicana feminisms.

allCourses.title: Gender and Ethnicity: Chicana/Latina Feminisms in the US
allCourses.description: Focuses on the Latina Feminist Group and testimonios to examine the historical development of Chicana/Latinx feminist thought and practice. Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship to survey the diversity of contemporary Chicana/Latinx feminisms through an intersectionality lens.

allCourses.title: Feminisms of Color
allCourses.description: Surveys the development of Chicana feminist thought and practice.  Focuses on historical contemporary writings by and about Chicana feminists.  Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship in order to survey the diversity of Chicana feminisms.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Society, Labor, Politics, Law, Gender, Race, Ethnicity
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Perspectives on the U.S. - Mexican Border
allCourses.description: Economic aspects of the historical development of the United States-Mexican border.  The current economic situation in the Southwest and border areas as it affects both Mexico and the Latino/Chicano population is also examined.

allCourses.title: Transnational Migration
allCourses.description: Examines the movement of people across national borders, governmentality and the role of state practices to control populations, and issues of citizenship, belonging, and identity. Examples are drawn from the United States, Europe, Latin America, Asia, and Africa.

allCourses.title: Transnational Central America
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Offers an overview of the history of Central America and its diasporas, as well as the struggles, accomplishments, and activism, art and cultural expressions of Central Americans in the United States.

allCourses.title: Urban America
allCourses.description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.

allCourses.title: U.S. Immigration Policy
allCourses.description: Examines selected immigration policy debates since the nineteenth century, rationale and consequences of immigration law since 1965, problems of administration, implementation and enforcement, impact of immigration policy on foreign relations, and contemporary debate regarding the future of U.S. policy.

allCourses.title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
allCourses.description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

allCourses.title: Chicano Movement
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the history of Mexicans in the U.S. with particular attention paid to their integration into the U.S. capitalist economy. Examines this economic history and the Chicano movement, "El Movimiento," within the wide context of socio-economic change.

allCourses.title: Latinos in a Global Society
allCourses.description: Examines interconnections between diverse Latino groups in the U.S. and the effects of globalization on their social, cultural, and political realities. Topics include immigration, demographics, socioeconomic differentiation, familial relations, political protest/resistance, law and policy, and links to "homeland" issues.

allCourses.title: Chicano/Latino Social Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines theories, research, and major issues of relevance to understanding social psychological processes in Chicano/Latino populations. Topics include social development, cultural orientations, gender and sexuality, close relationships, happiness and well-being, stereotyping, prejudice and discrimination, and mental and physical health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Globalization, Transnationalism, Immigration, U.S.-Mexico Border
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Chicano/Latino Families
allCourses.description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

allCourses.title: Chicano/Latino Psychology
allCourses.description: Examines research and literature investigating Chicano/Latino ethnicity as a variable influencing behavior.  Explores mental health needs and issues of Chicano/Latinos and discusses competent, sensitive methods of mental health service delivery.

allCourses.title: Race, Gender, and Science
allCourses.description: Perfect for pre-health, science, and social science majors wanting to appreciate how science and society interact. Race and gender as biological and socio-cultural constructs are examined. Questions explored: What is disease? What is science? What are social and biological differences.

allCourses.title: Culture and Close Relationships
allCourses.restriction: Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines cultural influences on close relationship processes including attraction, love, friendship, family, social support, and significance of close relationships for health and well-being. National and ethnic sources of cultural variation examined include Latin America, Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.

allCourses.title: Culture and Close Relationships
allCourses.restriction: Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines cultural influences on close relationship processes including attraction, love, friendship, family, social support, and significance of close relationships for health and well-being. National and ethnic sources of cultural variation examined include Latin America, Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Health and the Latino Paradox
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines research and theories concerning the physical and mental health of U.S. Latino populations. Contemporary accounts, health care implications, and new directions for understanding sources of risks and resilience for health in Latino populations are evaluated and discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Medical Anthropology
allCourses.description: Introduces students to cross-cultural perspectives and critical theories in anthropological studies of medicine. Special attention is given to diverse ways of understanding bodies, illnesses, and therapeutic practices in our changing world.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Health, Medicine, and Psychosocial Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Chicanx/Latinx Education
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latinx low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

allCourses.title: Latina/Latino Access and Persistence in Higher Education
allCourses.description: Introduction to how social, political, and economic forces impact on Latina/Latino racial/ethnic minorities with regard to their access and persistence in the U.S. higher education system. Investigates historical perspectives and theoretical underpinnings of college access and retention research.

allCourses.title: Multicultural Education in K-12 Schools
allCourses.description: Provides a theoretical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting low-income immigrant and U.S. born minority student populations in an increasingly diverse and changing society.

allCourses.title: College Advising for High School Students
allCourses.description: Provides a brief introduction to college-access issues and in-depth understanding in the field of college advising. Students learn how to help high school students develop higher education plans and guide them through the college application process.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Educational Policy and Issues
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: HABLA: Language Intervention for Disadvantaged Children
allCourses.restriction: Psychology, Chicano/Latino Studies, and Social Policy and Public Service majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Train students for home visits promoting school readiness among two-four year-olds from low SES and educational backgrounds. Covers fundamentals of child language, literacy, cognitive development; procedures, ethics of home visitation. Work with families to create better literacy and language environment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Must pass an interview conducted by instructor, be fluent in English and one other language (Spanish most typically), must have experience with preschool children, and be culturally sensitive.

allCourses.title: HABLA: Language Intervention for Disadvantaged Children
allCourses.restriction: Psychology, Chicano/Latino Studies, and Social Policy and Public Service majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Train students for home visits promoting school readiness among two-four year-olds from low SES and educational backgrounds. Covers fundamentals of child language, literacy, cognitive development; procedures, ethics of home visitation. Work with families to create better literacy and language environment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 144A or SOC SCI 186A or CHC/LAT 191A. Must pass an interview conducted by instructor, be fluent in English and one other language (Spanish most typically), must have experience with preschool children and be culturally sensitive.

allCourses.title: HABLA: Language Intervention for Disadvantaged Children
allCourses.restriction: Psychology, Chicano/Latino Studies, and Social Policy and Public Service majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Train students for home visits promoting school readiness among two-four year-olds from low SES and educational backgrounds. Covers fundamentals of child language, literacy, cognitive development; procedures, ethics of home visitation. Work with families to create better literacy and language environment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 144B or SOC SCI 186B or CHC/LAT 191B. Must pass an interview conducted by instructor, be fluent in English and one other language (Spanish most typically), must have experience with preschool children, and be culturally sensitive.

allCourses.title: Directed Group Study
allCourses.description: Directed study with Chicano/Latino faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Independent research with Chicano/Latino faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Theoretical Issues in Chicano/Latino Research
allCourses.description: Introduction to theoretical issues in the scholarship in Chicano/Latino Studies. Theories from social sciences, humanities, critical theory. Topics: immigration, identity, gender and sexuality, globalization, transnationalism, social, political, and economic integration, race theory, labor market participation, social history, cultural productions.

prerequisite_for.title: Models of Practice and Intervention at the Community Level

allCourses.title: Cultural and Historial Precedents for Latinos and Medical Care
allCourses.description: Introduction to the history of Latinos, focusing on relevant pre-Columbian, colonial, and modern social and cultural developments, including issues of race, gender, sexuality, religious beliefs, and health beliefs and practices.

allCourses.title: Cultural and Historical Precedents for Latinos and Medical Care
allCourses.description: Introduction to the history of Latinos, focusing on relevant pre-Columbian, colonial, and modern social and cultural developments, including issues of race, gender, sexuality, religious beliefs, and health beliefs and practices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHC/LAT 210A. CHC/LAT 210A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Latinos/Latinas and Medical Care: Contemporary Issues
allCourses.description: Introduction to medical anthropological and social science perspectives on Latinos/Latinas in relation to a number of health and medically-related issues, i.e., immigration, gender, reproduction, culture, social structure, political economy, sexuality, utilization of medical services, and health beliefs.

allCourses.title: Latinos/Latinas and Medical Care: Contemporary Issues
allCourses.description: Introduction to medical anthropological and social science perspectives on Latinos/Latinas in relation to a number of health and medically-related issues, i.e., immigration, gender, reproduction, culture, social structure, political economy, sexuality, utilization of medical services, and health beliefs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHC/LAT 211A. CHC/LAT 211A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Borders and Bodies:  Places, Processes, and Transgressions
allCourses.description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

allCourses.title: Transnational Migration
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

allCourses.title: Ethnography
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the theory and practice of ethnography with a focus on anthropology, the discipline most associated with ethnography. Students are exposed to the theoretical underpinnings of ethnographic work, traditional and innovative practices, and sample ethnographies.

allCourses.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Social Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Origins and organization of racialized social control, with emphasis on criminal justice. Racial politics of criminal/juvenile justice considered in comparative (historical and international) perspective. Exploration of theoretical and methodological issues for research on race, ethnicity, and social control.

allCourses.title: Theorizing Illegality and the Experiences of Undocumented Immigrants

allCourses.title: Chemistry Outreach Program
allCourses.description: Involves intensive participation in the UCI Chemistry Outreach Program, which performs Chemistry demonstrations at local high schools.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 6 times.

allCourses.title: Tutoring in Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: The first eight may be taken for a letter grade. The remaining ten units must be taken Pass/Not Pass only. NOTE: No more than eight units may be counted toward the 180 units required for graduation. Satisfies no degree requirement other than contribution to the 180-unit total.
allCourses.description: Enrollment limited to participants in the Chemistry Peer Tutoring Program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 9 times.

allCourses.title: Research Methods
allCourses.description: Explores tools of inquiry for developing and implementing science research projects.  Students undertake independent projects requiring data collection, analysis, and modeling, and the organization and presentation of results.  Additional topics include ethical issues and role of scientific literature.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 14 or PHY SCI 5

allCourses.title: Professional Internship
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Chemistry Majors only.
allCourses.description: Internship program that provides students with opportunity to develop professional skills necessary for competitive placement in their chosen chemical-inspired industry. Students gain new and field-specific skills outside the classroom while participating in a supervised internship.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Enrollment requires completion of an application form. Student selection is made by a selection committee.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 13 units.

allCourses.title: Independent Study in Chemistry
allCourses.description: Independent research with Chemistry faculty.  Student time commitment of three to four hours per week per unit is expected, and a written report on the independent study is required at the end of each quarter of enrollment.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.
