allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Lecture and experiments covering chemical concepts for accelerated students who do not plan to take organic chemistry. Properties of gases, liquids, solutions, and solids; chemical  equilibrium and chemical thermodynamics; atomic and molecular  structure; chemical kinetics; electrochemistry. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 1A or ENGR 1A or AP Chemistry. CHEM 1A with a grade of C- or better. ENGR 1A with a grade of C- or better. AP Chemistry with a minimum score of 3

allCourses.title: Preparation for General Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Undeclared Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Physical Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment. Program in Nursing Science students have first consideration for enrollment. Dept Pharmaceutical Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. Program in Public Health students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Units of measurement, dimensional analysis, significant figures; elementary concepts of volume, mass, force, pressure, energy, density, temperature, heat, work; fundamentals of atomic and molecular structure; the mole concept, stoichiometry; properties of the states of matter; gas laws; solutions concentrations.

allCourses.title: General Chemistry Plus
allCourses.description: Units of chemical measurements, dimensional analysis, significant figures; elementary physicochemical concepts; fundamentals of atomic and molecular structure; molar amounts and stoichiometry; properties of the states of matter; solutions concentrations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Students who meet the requirements for taking Chem 1A through their SAT, ACT, or AP test scores are not eligible for enrollment in Chem 1X. Specifically, the students must have ALL of the following advisory prerequisites (the inverse of the Chem 1A prerequisites): S02<600 (score below 600 on the SAT Mathematics Reasoning test) A02<27 (score below 27 on the ACT Mathematics test) Z43<700 (score below 700 on the SAT Chemistry subject exam) AP25<3 (score below 3 on the AP Chemistry exam) AP66<3 (score below 3 on the AP Calculus AB Exam) AP68<3 (score below 3 on the AP Calculus BC Exam) Students who meet Chem 1A eligibility through ALEKS-based training are permitted to enroll in Chem 1X. Chem 1X is open to interested BioEASE students.

allCourses.title: Conduct of Research
allCourses.description: Introduces new graduate students to ethical conduct of scientific research, mentoring, and current research in the Department of Chemistry.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms I
allCourses.description: Advanced treatment of basic mechanistic principles of modern organic chemistry. Topics include molecular orbital theory, orbital symmetry control of organic reactions, aromaticity, carbonium ion chemistry, free radical chemistry, the chemistry of carbenes and carbanions, photochemistry, electrophilic substitutions, aromatic chemistry.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

allCourses.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms II
allCourses.description: Topics include more in-depth treatment of mechanistic concepts, kinetics, conformational analysis, computational methods, stereoelectronics, and both solution and enzymatic catalysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 201. CHEM 201 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Organic Spectroscopy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Modern methods used in structure determination of organic molecules. Topics include mass spectrometry; ultraviolet, chiroptical, infrared, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C) or (CHEM H52A and CHEM H52B and CHEM H52C)

allCourses.title: Organic Synthesis I
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of modern synthetic organic chemistry is developed. Major emphasis is on carbon-carbon bond forming methodology. Topics include carbonyl annelations, cycloadditions, sigmatropic rearrangements, and organometallic methods.

allCourses.title: Organic Synthesis II
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of modern synthetic organic chemistry will be developed. Major emphasis this quarter is on natural product total synthesis and retrosynthetic (antithetic) analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 204. CHEM 204 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Advanced Data Acquisition and Analysis
allCourses.description: Introduces students to a variety of practical laboratory techniques, including lock-in, boxcar, coincidence counting, noise filtering, PID control, properties of common transducers, computer interfacing to instruments, vacuum technology, laboratory safety, basic mechanical design, and shop skills. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Applied Physical Chemistry
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts in molecular structure and reactivity: theory of bonding, valence and molecular orbitals; structure and reactivity in inorganic chemistry; elements in molecular group theory; nomenclature in organic chemistry; and survey of macromolecules.

allCourses.title: Math Methods
allCourses.description: Applications of mathematics to physical and chemical problems. Calculus of special functions, complex variables and vectors; linear vector spaces and eigenvalue problems. Differential equations.

allCourses.title: Physics for Chemists
allCourses.description: An introduction to concepts of electrodynamics with special emphasis on applications to chemistry: vector analysis, electrostatics, magnetostatics, electrodynamics, electromagnetic waves, classical radiation theory, special relativity.

allCourses.title: Chemical Kinetics
allCourses.description: Surveys gas phase and organic reaction mechanisms and their relationship to kinetic rate laws; treats the basic theory of elementary reaction rates.  A brief presentation of modern cross-sectional kinetics is included.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

allCourses.title: Inorganic Chemistry I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles of modern inorganic chemistry with applications to chemical systems of current interest. Inorganic phenomena are organized into general patterns which rationalize observed structures, stabilities, and physical properties.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 107 and CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

allCourses.title: Organometallic Chemistry
allCourses.description: Synthesis and reactivity of organometallic complexes with an emphasis on mechanisms. Topics include bonding and fluxional properties; metal-carbon single and multiple bonds; metal š-complexes. Applications to homogenous catalysis and organic synthesis are incorporated throughout the course.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 107 or CHEM 215. CHEM 215 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Physical Inorganic Chemistry
allCourses.description: General principles of the spectroscopy and magnetism of inorganic compounds. Characterization of inorganic complexes by infrared, near-infrared, visible, ultraviolet, NMR, EPR, EXAFS, and Mossbauer spectroscopies. Some necessary group theory developed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 215. CHEM 215 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Metallobiochemistry
allCourses.description: A review of the biochemistry of metallic elements emphasizing: methods for studying metals in biological systems; the chemical basis for nature's exploitation of specific elements; structures of active sites; mechanisms; solid-state structures and devices; metals in medicine.

allCourses.title: Chemical and Structural Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A survey of the organic chemistry underlying biological function. Introduction to chemical genetics, receptor-ligand interactions, small molecule agonists and antagonists, combinatorial synthesis, high throughput assays, molecular evolution, protein and small molecule design.

allCourses.title: Advanced Chemical Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Modern topics in chemical biology, with an emphasis on application of principles from organic chemistry to biological research and biotechnology. Topics include methods to generate, identify, and manipulate major classes of biomolecules including nucleic acids, carbohydrates, lipids, and secondary metabolites.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 219. CHEM 219 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Molecular Biophysics
allCourses.description: An overview of the principles and concepts in molecular biophysics.  Topics covered include energy and entropy in biology, non-equilibrium reaction kinetics, random walks and molecular diffusion, molecular forces in biology.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate courses in physical chemistry and biochemistry.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Biological Macromolecules
allCourses.description: Introduction to nucleic acid and protein structure, dynamics, and function. Topics include analytical methods, molecular evolution, folding, and catalysis.

allCourses.title: Molecular and Cellular Biophotonics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles underlying the application of photonic technologies to biomolecular and cellular systems. Sample technologies Optical Tweezers, Linear and Nonlinear Optical Microscopy and Fluorescence Lifetime and Correlation Methods, and their use to investigate emergent problems in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology.

allCourses.title: Polymer Chemistry:  Synthesis and Characterization of Polymers
allCourses.description: Structure of synthetic and natural polymers.  Survey of modern polymer synthetic methods.  Molecular weight and molecular weight distribution.  Chain conformation and stereochemistry. Introduction to polymer characterization, chain models, and solution behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate courses in organic and physical chemistry.

allCourses.title: Electromagnetism
allCourses.description: Maxwell’s equations, electrodynamics, electromagnetic waves and radiation, wave propagation in media, interference and quantum optics, coherent and incoherent radiation, with practical applications in interferometry, lasers, waveguides, and optical instrumentation.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences
allCourses.description: Mathematical and numerical analysis using Mathematica and C programming, as applied to problems in physical science.

allCourses.title: Computational Methods
allCourses.description: Mathematical and numerical analysis using Mathematica and C programming, as applied to problems in physical science.

allCourses.title: Classical Mechanics and Electromagnetic Theory
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of classical mechanics and electromagnetic theory are developed with specific application to molecular systems. Newtonian, Lagrangian, and Hamiltonian mechanics are developed. Boundary value problems in electrostatics are investigated. Multipole expansion and macroscopic media are discussed from a molecular viewpoint.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: The postulates of quantum mechanics are discussed and applied to a variety of model problems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 131A and CHEM 131B and CHEM 131C

allCourses.title: Applications of Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: Approximate methods for solving atomic and molecular structure problems are developed, and the application of quantum mechanics to spectroscopy is introduced.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 231A. CHEM 231A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Molecular Spectroscopy
allCourses.description: Theory and techniques of spectroscopy as used for the study of molecular and condensed phase properties. Coherent time domain spectroscopies are covered.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 231B. CHEM 231B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Thermodynamics and Introduction to Statistical Mechanics
allCourses.description: A detailed discussion from an advanced point of view of the principles of classical thermodynamics. The fundamentals of statistical mechanics. Topics include an introduction to ensemble theory, Boltzmann statistics, classical statistical mechanics, and the statistical mechanics of ideal gas systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 131A and CHEM 131B and CHEM 131C

prerequisite_list.title: Molecular Structure and Elementary Statistical Mechanics

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Statistical Mechanics
allCourses.description: Continued discussion of the principles of statistical mechanics. Applications to topics of chemical interest including imperfect gases, liquids, solutions, and crystals. Modern techniques such as the use of autocorrelation function methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 232A. CHEM 232A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Non-Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics
allCourses.description: Phenomenology of material processes, including: kinetic theories of transport and continuum, linear response theory, critical phenomena of phase transition, self-assembly, and nucleation.

allCourses.title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced treatment of nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, and radioactive-decay processes. Introduction to nuclear activation analysis, isotope effects, radiation chemistry, hot-atom chemistry, nuclear age-dating methods, nuclear reactors, and nuclear power.

allCourses.title: Advanced Chemical Kinetics
allCourses.description: Topics and format vary.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 213.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Molecular Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: Application of quantum mechanics to calculation of molecular properties. Electronic structure of molecules.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 231A

allCourses.title: Forces Between Molecules
allCourses.description: The nature and effects of non-covalent interactions between molecular systems. The focus is on properties of these interactions in condensed phases: macromolecular systems; particle-surface interactions.

allCourses.title: Mathematical Methods in Chemistry
allCourses.description: Survey of essential math methods in chemistry. Topics may include series and limits, complex analysis, Fourier and Laplace transforms, linear algebra and operators (theory and algorithms), differential equations, and probability concepts for stochastic processes.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Density Functional Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in density functional theory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: One year of graduate quantum mechanics, or the equivalent.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Machine Learning in Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introductory course in machine learning, accessible to any graduate student in chemistry. Covers the basics of theory and practice of machine learning in modern chemistry. No coding or previous experience required.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Must be familiar with standard computer operation.

allCourses.title: Current Issues Related to Air Quality, Climate, and Energy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current issues related to the atmosphere, climate, and air quality in the context of energy conversion and sustainability. Topics include transportation systems; building design; impacts on humans and ecosystems; modeling and meteorology; economics; and application to public policies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 261 or CHEM 245 or EARTHSS 240. ENGRMAE 261 with a grade of B- or better. CHEM 245 with a grade of B- or better. EARTHSS 240 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Physical and Geometrical Optics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the practical aspects of optics and optical engineering, starting at the fundamentals. Topics include geometrical optics, ray tracing, polarization optics, interferometers, and diffractive optics.

allCourses.title: Applied Optics
allCourses.description: Focuses on the treatment of a wide variety of tools and techniques used in optics, particularly in research. Subjects include an introduction to lasers, optical detection, coherent optics, spectroscopic techniques, and selected topics corresponding to the interest of the students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 242A

allCourses.title: Advanced Instrumental Analysis
allCourses.description: Theory and applications of modern advanced instrumental methods of analysis. Includes data acquisition, storage, retrieval, and analysis; Fourier transform methods; vacuum technologies; magnetic sector; quadrupole and ion trap mass spectrometry; surface science spectroscopic methods; lasers and optics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 152 and CHEM 132C. CHEM 152 with a grade of B or better. CHEM 132C with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Detection and Measurement of Radiation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of detection and measurement of ionizing radiation; both theory and practical aspects of measurement techniques for alpha, beta, gamma, and neutron radiation, properties of different detector materials, electronics and data treatments, and analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 233 or CBE 276. CHEM 233 with a grade of B- or better. CBE 276 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Atmospheric Chemistry of the Natural and Polluted Troposphere
allCourses.description: Kinetics, mechanisms and photochemistry of tropospheric reactions in the gas, liquid, and solid phases, and methods of analysis. Chemistry of photochemical oxidant formation and acid deposition, and applications to control strategies. Chemistry of toxic chemicals and indoor air pollution.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 131A and CHEM 131B and CHEM 131C.

allCourses.title: Gas-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
allCourses.description: Sources, chemistry, sinks, and measurements of key atmospheric gaseous species. Chemistry of photochemical oxidant formation, transformation of key inorganic and organic trace gases, and stratospheric ozone cycling. Applications of atmospheric chemistry models to control strategies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 132A and CHEM 132B and CHEM 132C

allCourses.title: Multi-Phase Atmospheric Chemistry
allCourses.description: Chemical and physical processes leading to the production, aging, and removal of atmospheric particles. Multi-phase processes involving gases, particles, water droplets, and environmental surfaces. Approaches for modeling these processes with applications to control strategies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 245A. CHEM 245A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Atmospheric Chemistry
allCourses.description: The subjects covered vary from year to year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 245B. CHEM 245B with a grade of B- or better
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Separations and Chromatography
allCourses.description: Introduction to modern separation techniques such as gas chromatography, high-performance liquid chromatography, supercritical fluid chromatography, capillary electrophoresis, and field flow fractionation. Applications of these separation strategies are discussed.

allCourses.title: Current Problems in Analytical Chemistry
allCourses.description: Surveys current research challenges in analytical chemistry. Topics include electrochemistry, chromatography, spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry.

allCourses.title: Electrochemistry
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of electrochemistry including thermodynamics and the electrochemical potential, charge transfer kinetics, and mass transfer. Methods based on controlled potential and controlled current are described; the effects of slow heterogeneous kinetics and the perturbation caused by homogeneous chemistry are discussed.

allCourses.title: Analytical Spectroscopy
allCourses.description: Advanced treatment of spectroscopic techniques and instrumentation. Atomic and molecular absorption, emission, and scattering processes and their application to quantitative chemical analysis are outlined. Puts different spectroscopic techniques in perspective and demonstrates most appropriate applications to analytical problems.

allCourses.title: Computational Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic concepts, methods, and techniques in computational chemistry: density functional and wavefunction theory, molecular property calculations, analysis tools, potential energy surfaces, vibrational effects, molecular dynamics simulations.

allCourses.title: Computational Chemistry Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the practice of modern computational chemistry through a series of advanced computational experiments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 250. CHEM 250 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Organic Chemistry
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in organic chemistry.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Physical Chemistry
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in physical chemistry. Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Inorganic Chemistry
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in inorganic chemistry.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 215
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Computational and Theoretical Chemistry
allCourses.description: Subjects covered vary from year to year.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Quantum Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in quantum science.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Materials Chemistry
allCourses.description: An introduction to crystalline solids, descriptive crystal chemistry, solid-state synthesis and characterization techniques, x-ray and electron diffraction, phase diagrams, electronic band structure of extended solids, semi conductors, and nanoscale inorganic materials.

allCourses.title: Analytical Methods for Organic Nanomaterials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of analytical techniques related to measuring the structure and dynamics of organic nanomaterials. Topics include transmission electron microscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, liquid phase electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, light scattering, small angle X-ray, and neutron scattering.

allCourses.title: Current Topics in Chemical, Applied, and Materials Physics
allCourses.description: The subjects covered vary from year to year.  Connection between fundamental principles and implementations in practice in science, industry, and technology.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Photochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Photochemical and photovoltaic processes in molecules and semiconductors; quantum mechanics; statistical thermodynamics; kinetics; and experimental techniques relevant to photon absorption and emission; photochemical charge separation, recombination, and transport of electrons and ions; and interfacial redox chemistry.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Early Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from its origins in the Bronze Age to the mid-Archaic period. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, religion, and archaeological remains.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society:  Late Archaic and Classical Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the Late Archaic period to the Classical period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Greek Society: Fourth-Century and Hellenistic Greece
allCourses.description: A survey of ancient Greek civilization from the fourth century BCE through to the Hellenistic period. Focuses on major institutions and cultural phenomena as seen through the study of ancient Greek literature, history, archaeology, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Origins to Roman Republic
allCourses.description: A survey of the development of Roman civilization from its eighth century BCE beginnings to the civil wars of the first century BCE. Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: Roman Empire
allCourses.description: A survey of Roman civilization from Augustus’s consolidation of power following the civil wars of the first century BCE to the crisis of the third century CE. Includes social history, literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: The Formation of Ancient Roman Society: The Fall of Rome
allCourses.description: A survey of Roman civilization from the crisis of the third century CE to the so-called “fall of Rome” in 476 CE.  Examines political and social history, as well as literature, art, architecture, and religion.

allCourses.title: Classical Mythology: The Gods
allCourses.description: An overview of the main myths of the gods of the ancient Greeks and Romans and their influence in contemporary and later literature and art. Includes readings from both ancient and modern sources.

allCourses.title: Classical Mythology: The Heroes
allCourses.description: An overview of the main myths of the heroes of the ancient Greeks and Romans and their influence in contemporary and later literature and art. Includes readings from both ancient and modern sources.

allCourses.title: Classical Mythology: Ancient and Modern Perspectives of Classical Mythology
allCourses.description: Detailed examination of key Greek and Roman myths, their interpretations, and the influence they have exerted on literature, art, and popular culture in subsequent periods.

allCourses.title: Building English Vocabulary through Greek and Latin Roots
allCourses.description: Formation and use of English words from Greek and Latin derivatives. Particularly useful for first-year students who wish to augment their vocabulary systematically.

allCourses.title: Political Economy: Methods and Critique
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to canonical texts in Marxism coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken after CLT&THY 200B.

allCourses.title: Libidinal Economy: Methods and Critique
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to canonical texts in psychoanalysis coupled with an examination of the questions of race, gender, ethnicity, and sexuality that distend the calculus of the canon’s assumptive logic. May be taken before CLT&THY 200A.

allCourses.title: Theory from Below
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to systems of thought understudied or undervalued in academic canons; for instance, systems constituted in communities' practices or theories that do not seek permanence or generality.

allCourses.title: A Critical Theory of Subalternity
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the importance of subaltern studies for the study of modern history, postcolonial studies, social theory, and cultural studies. Also considers subaltern studies within a larger set of debates in structuralism, post-structuralism, Marxism, and post-Marxism.

allCourses.title: Crossing Borders: Empire and Im/migration
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Utilizes historically-based intersectional analysis to explore the connections between U.S. empire and migration; border formation and incarceration; as well as identity and structural forms of hierarchy.

allCourses.title: Freedom Dreams: Subaltern Forms of Resistance
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores how subjugated peoples have creatively and collectively resisted oppression. Explores how individuals and communities envision a more just society, experiment with political strategies, and create meaningful legacies.

allCourses.title: Resistance Spaces
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between the production of space and the operation of power in cultural studies and critical social theory.

allCourses.title: Ethics, Erotics, and Will: Gendered Black Politics, Sexualized Racisms, and the Humanities
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces doctoral students to an interdisciplinary conversation about black queer sexuality and black heteropatriarchy. Uses disciplinary formations as a tool for understanding knowledge formations about the shifting relations that constitute sexuality, gender, and racial blackness.

allCourses.title: Afro-Pessimism and the Status of the Subject
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Afro-Pessimism theorizes the Black as a being against which all other beings become legible as human subjects. Focuses on either the subject of psychoanalysis or the subject of capital accumulation in their explorations of the antagonism between Blackness.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Performance Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to key issues and critical methods within the field of performance studies. These include performance/performativity, liveness, everyday life, auto-ethnography, archive/repertoire, affect and performance, and disidentificatory practices.

allCourses.title: Perception and Sensory Processes
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A general introduction to the scientific study of sensory processes and perceptual phonomena, with special emphasis in the visual systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9) or (PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A)

allCourses.title: Neuroscience of Perception
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the principles that human perception is determined by the properties of brain circuitry and that these brain circuits evolved to interpret the properties of the physical environment to explore human perception from peripheral sensory organs to cortical processing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9 or PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A

allCourses.title: Vision
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Visual perception and the anatomy and physiology of the visual system. Topics include the retina and the visual pathway; visual sensitivity; color vision; spatial vision; motion perception; and the development of the visual system.

allCourses.title: Hearing
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Auditory perception, the anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, and the physics of sound. Topics include neural transduction of sound, sensitivity, sound localization, complex sound perception, and hearing loss.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A) and (PSYCH 9B or PSCI 11B)

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Perception and Sensory Processes
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of perception and sensory processes. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Judgment and Decision Making
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The psychology of human decision making. Theories, models, experiments, and data that inform how people make choices, judgments, and other decisions. Topics include optimality and bias, mental simulation, learning and feedback, expertise, emotional effects, and group decision making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSYCH 9A and PSYCH 9B

allCourses.title: Learning and Decision Making
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The psychological and neural bases of learning about and interacting with the world. Topics include shaping of behavior by rewards and punishments, abstraction of relational information, goal-directed versus habitual decision strategies, social knowledge transmission, and behavioral and substance addictions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9) or (PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A)

allCourses.title: Human Memory
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Developments in the area of memory; history of memory research; theories of the nature of memory. Visual memory, recognition memory, high-speed scanning, free recall, short-term memory, mnemonics, retrieval, relationship of memory to thinking. Selected theoretical formulations for memory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSYCH 7A or PSCI 9) or (PSYCH 9B or PSCI 11B)

allCourses.title: MATLAB Programming
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: MATLAB is a mathematical software package for solving quantitative problems often encountered in experimental psychology. Topics include rudiments of programming, statistical analysis of data, matrix algebra, signal processing, graphic visualization, and simulated models of cognitive and perceptual processes.

allCourses.title: Scientific Python for Research
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces Python for data analysis and modeling encountered in cognitive science and neuroscience. Topics include data structures, execution control, graphic visualization, and interaction with sound and display interfaces. Application in statistical analysis, model simulation, and stimulus presentation and experimental control.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Cognitive Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the neural basis of human perceptual, motor, and cognitive abilities. Topics include sensory perception, motor control, memory, language, attention, emotion, frontal lobe function, functional brain imaging, and neuropsychological disorders.

allCourses.restriction: Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the localization of human brain functions and the effects of neurological disorders on psychological functions such as perception, motor control, language, memory, and decision-making.

allCourses.description: Introduction to the conceptual foundations and basic research results in the cognitive sciences for first-year graduate students.

allCourses.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Logic and set theory are covered during the first three weeks, using an interactive computer system. The remaining seven weeks are devoted to probability theory and cover elementary concepts from samples spaces to Chebychev's Inequality and the moment generating function.

allCourses.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to statistical estimation and statistical inference. Topics include sufficiency and the Rao-Blackwell Theorem, completeness and the Lehmann-Scheffe Theorem. The method of maximum likelihood is explored in some detail. Inference in linear models covers regression and analysis of variance.

allCourses.title: Statistical Models for Cognitive Sciences III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of the fundamentals of statistical inference and computational implementations of common statistical models.

allCourses.title: Applied Mathematics for Cognitive Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the basics of linear systems analysis, focusing on linear algebra, Fourier analysis, differential equations, and elementary signal processing. Applications in Cognitive Science and Cognitive Neuroscience research are developed.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Professional Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Development of professional skills. Focuses on grant writing and submission process, responsible conduct of research, and ethics training.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Professional Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Development of professional skills. Focus on scientific presentations and preparation.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Professional Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only. Psychology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Development of professional skills. Focuses on career opportunities, interests and information, and community outreach.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Programming
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces rudiments of programming, statistical analysis and probability theory, graphic visualization, GUI design, spectral analysis, and simulation models using MATLAB, a software package for solving quantitative problems often encountered in experimental psychology.

allCourses.title: Computational Lab Skills for Cognitive Scientists I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an in-depth introduction to writing MATLAB programs to run auditory and visual experiments. Topics covered include program structure, stimulus generation, presentation, and data collection.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Statistical Learning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cognitive Neuroscience Majors only. Cognitive Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to statistical learning for scientific research. Topics include linear regression, logistic regression, model selection, cross-validation, ridge and Lasso regularization, classification trees, ensemble methods, random forests, unsupervised learning, PCA, k-means clustering, Gaussian mixture models, and PLS regression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Knowledge of calculus, computer programming, and undergraduate-level statistics.

allCourses.title: Neural Networks and Machine Learning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction and review of the current state of the art in neural networks and machine learning with specific emphasis of applications to behavioral and neuroscience data analysis and modeling.

allCourses.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences I: Topics in Perception
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses models of cognition and evidence linking cognition and the brain. Focus is on visual, auditory, and somatic perception and bottom-up mechanisms of attention.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences II: Topics in Cognition
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses models of cognition and evidence linking cognition and the brain. Focus is on emotion, top-down attention, goal-directed behavior, categorization, judgment, and decision-making.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Cognitive and Brain Sciences III: Topics in Learning and Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses experimental data, formal models of learning, and evidence linking learning and development to its neural substrates. Topics include Pavlovian and instrumental conditioning, language acquisition, causal reasoning, perceptual learning, category formation, and structure learning.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: The Mind/Body Problem
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary, drawing on information from the fields of quantum physics, computer vision, artificial intelligence, cognition, neurophysiology, philosophy, and psychophysics.

allCourses.title: Bayesian Cognitive Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Considers a range of statistical methods of data analysis and simple cognitive models using the Bayesian graphical modeling framework.

allCourses.title: Hearing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines auditory sensation and perception using psychophysical and neuroscientific perspectives. Covers physical aspects of sound; subcortical auditory processing; aspects of sensation and perception such as sensitivity, sound localization, and complex-sound recognition; neuroscientific studies of cortical function; and abnormal auditory processing.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Human Cognition
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in brain/ behavior relationships, human memory, and learning theory is presented.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Analysis of Neural Time Series
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Hands-on introduction to techniques for the analysis of neural time series data, with a primary focus on the electroencephalogram (EEG). Topics may include the physiological basis of EEG, time-frequency analysis, spatial filtering, and methods of assessing connectivity.

allCourses.title: Advanced Bayesian Cognitive Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Considers a range of advanced cognitive process models including models of signal detection, memory retention, category learning, stimulus representation, and reasoning using the Bayesian graphical modeling framework.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COGS 214. COGS 214 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Methodology and Models
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in cognitive sciences methodologies, concepts, and models is presented.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Cortical Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Physiology of the cerebral cortex, theoretical neuroscience, and the neural basis of perception.

allCourses.title: Functional Neuroanatomy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: It is impossible to truly understand human behavior without some understanding of the physical structure that enables behavior. Examines recent findings in functional neuroantomy through lectures and papers discussing links between particular behaviors and specific brain structures.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Functional MRI
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Describes the fundamentals of imaging the human brain function using functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI). Topics include basic fMRI physics, experimental design, and data acquisition and analysis.

allCourses.title: Computational Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computational neuroscience. Mathematical models of single neurons, neural circuits, thalamocortical systems, and cortical mass action can stimulate single-unit, local field potential, and EEG dynamics. These models are used to investigate mechanisms of sensation, motor control, attention, and consciousness.

allCourses.title: Cognitive Robotics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces concepts for studying cognitive function by embedding brain models on robotic platforms. Topics include robot construction, computer programming, and the notion of embodiment. Students construct simple robots and program these robots to perform different behaviors.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Cognitive Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in cognitive neuroscience.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.description: Discusses the roles of differences such as race, class, gender, and sexuality in society, culture, and literature across the globe, covering topics such as theoretical and literary representations of queer sexuality, gender performance, critical race theory.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Graphical model techniques dealing with probabilistic and deterministic knowledge representations. Focuses on graphical models such as constraint networks, Bayesian networks, and Markov networks that have become a central paradigm for knowledge representation and reasoning in AI and general computer science.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 171

allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.

allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students to solve a substantial real-world problem with knowledge gained from many areas in computer science. Project has a focus on computer science but can overlap with neighbor disciplines.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 180A. In Progress (IP) grade for COMPSCI 180A is also accepted.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
allCourses.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D or MATH 3A or STATS 7 or STATS 8

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biology and Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computational methods in molecular biology, aimed at those interested in learning about this interdisciplinary area. Covers computational approaches to understanding and predicting the structure, function, interactions, and evolution of DNA, RNA, proteins, and related molecules and processes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Probabilistic Modeling of Biological Data
allCourses.description: A unified Bayesian probabilistic framework for modeling and mining biological data. Applications range from sequence (DNA, RNA, proteins) to gene expression data. Graphical models, Markov models, stochastic grammars, structure prediction, gene finding, evolution, DNA arrays, single- and multiple-gene analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 184A

prerequisite_list.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biology and Medicine

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computational Systems Biology
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Computational inference and modeling of gene regulation networks, signal transduction pathways, and the effects of regulatory networks in cellular processes, development, and disease. Introduction of required mathematical, computational, and data handling tools.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 184A

prerequisite_list.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biology and Medicine

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Project in Bioinformatics
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Teaches problem definition and analysis, data representation, algorithm design, component integration, solution validation, and testability with teams specifying, designing, building, and testing a solution to a bioinformatics problem. Lectures include engineering values, discussions, and ethical ramifications of biomedical computing issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 184A. COMPSCI 184A with a grade of C or better

prerequisite_list.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biology and Medicine

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Information and Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Information and Computer Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation with Computer Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Computer Science Research
allCourses.description: Graduate colloquium series. Includes weekly talks by notable computer scientists.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Foundations of Cryptographic Protocols
allCourses.description: Explores fundamental cryptographic tools, including encryption, signatures, and identification schemes. Students are introduced to the provable security paradigm of modern cryptography, focusing on understanding of security properties provided by cryptographic tools, and on proving security (or insecurity) of cryptographic constructions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 260 or COMPSCI 263. COMPSCI 260 with a grade of B- or better. COMPSCI 263 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Fundamentals of the Design and Analysis of Algorithms

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Security
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Master of Data Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computer security, including systems, technology, and management. Topics include authorization, authentication, data integrity, malware, operating systems security, network security, web security, and basic cryptography.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Knowledge of Python or C++ programming is required.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Cryptography
allCourses.description: Design and analysis of algorithms for applied cryptography. Topics include symmetric and asymmetric key encryption, digital signatures, one-way hash functions, digital certificates and credentials, and techniques for authorization, non-repudiation, authentication, identification, data integrity, proofs of knowledge, and access control.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 260 and COMPSCI 263. COMPSCI 260 with a grade of B- or better. COMPSCI 263 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Fundamentals of the Design and Analysis of Algorithms

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Cryptography
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design and analysis of algorithms for applied cryptography. Topics include symmetric and asymmetric key encryption, digital signatures, one-way hash functions, digital certificates and credentials, and techniques for authorization, non-repudiation, authentication, identification, data integrity, proofs of knowledge, and access control.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network and Distributed Systems Security
allCourses.description: Modern computer and networks security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Group communication and multicast security techniques. Covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network Security
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Computer Science Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to network security, including network threats and attacks, as well as defenses against such attacks. Topics include network infrastructure security, mobile and Wi-Fi security, spam, phishing, firewalls, anonymity, secure email, secure and private cloud computing, and web security.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 201P or COMPSCI 202P. COMPSCI 201P with a grade of B- or better. COMPSCI 202P with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Usable Security and Privacy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Undergraduate degree in Computer Science is strongly recommended.
allCourses.description: Examines how to design for security and privacy from a user-centered perspective by combining insights from computer systems and human-centered computing. Explores several challenges in integrating usability into core security and privacy systems design.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer and Systems Security
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Lecture and discuss latest security research in software, OS, protocols, mobile devices, machine learning, sensors, and emerging IoT/CPS systems such as smart home and smart transportation. Students perform research projects and gain hands-on experience evaluating and designing secure systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 134 and COMPSCI 142A and COMPSCI 143A

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Scientific Computing
allCourses.description: Overview of widely used principles and methods of numerical and scientific computing, including basic concepts and computational methods in linear algebra, optimization, and probability.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Basic courses in multivariate calculus, linear algebra, and probability.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Scientific Computing
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of widely used principles and methods of numerical and scientific computing, including basic concepts and computational methods in floating-point, linear algebra, optimization, simulation, modeling, and probability/statistics as it relates to model evaluation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Basic knowledge of multivariate calculus, linear algebra, and familiarity with MATLAB.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Graphics and Visualization
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Interactive 3D graphics rendering pipeline, illumination and shading, ray tracing, texture-, bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface removal, anti-aliasing, multiresolution representations, volume rendering techniques, iso-surface extraction.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Familiarity with linear algebra is required.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Visual Computing
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of image processing (convolution, linear filters, spectral analysis), vision geometry (projective geometry, camera models and calibration, stereo reconstruction), radiometry (color, shading, illumination, BRDF), and visual content synthesis (graphics pipeline, texture- bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface removal, anti-aliasing).

prerequisite_for.title: Light and Geometry in Computer Vision

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Graphics and Visualization
allCourses.description: Interactive 3D graphics rendering pipeline,  illumination and shading, ray tracing,  texture-, bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface removal, anti-aliasing,  multiresolution representations, volume rendering techniques, iso-surface extraction.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 211A. COMPSCI 211A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Realistic Image Synthesis
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an in-depth overview on a core sub-field of computer graphics. Graduate  students who take this course are better prepared for conducting research on the related topics in computer graphics, vision, and scientific computing.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Visual Computing
allCourses.restriction: Master of Computer Science Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Develops a comprehensive understanding of fundamentals of image processing (convolution, linear filters, spectral analysis), vision geometry (projective geometry, camera models and calibration, stereo reconstruction), radiometry (color, shading, illumination, BRDF), visual content synthesis (graphics pipeline, texture- bump-, mip-mapping, hidden surface, anti-aliasing).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate-level familiarity with Linear algebra (matrices and operations), eigenvalue, eigenvectors, linear regression; basic of algorithms; programming in C/C++.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Multimedia Systems and Applications
allCourses.description: Organization and structure of modern multimedia systems; audio and video encoding/compression; quality of service concepts; scheduling algorithms for multimedia; resource management in distributed and multimedia systems; multimedia protocols over high-speed networks; synchronization schemes; multimedia applications; and teleservices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 143A and COMPSCI 161. B.S. degree in Computer Science is also accepted. Recommended: COMPSCI 131 and COMPSCI 132 and COMPSCI 133.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Visual Perception
allCourses.description: Introduction to the process of human visual perception. Offers the physiological and psychophysical approach to understand vision, introducing concepts of perception of color, depth, movement. Examples of quantification and application of these models in computer vision, computer graphics, multimedia, HCI.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 121A

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Image Understanding
allCourses.description: The goal of image understanding is to extract useful semantic information from image data. Course covers low-level image and video processing techniques, feature descriptors, segmentation, objection recognition, and tracking.
