allCourses.description: In-depth examination of social psychology of police interrogation in America, the evolution of American interrogation practices from the nineteenth century to the present, impact of law on police behavior and ideology, causes and consequences of false confessions, possibilities of reform.

allCourses.title: Social Theory and the Law
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society and Social Ecology majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides theoretical tools to understand the relationship between law and society. Focuses on the connections between law and discourse, power, space and geography, economic markets, gender, race, class, democratic legitimacy, and the indeterminacy of language.

allCourses.title: Cross-Cultural Research on Urban Gangs
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SocEcol-Urban & Regional Plan Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Taking an urban policy approach, examines the background and contemporary traditions of gangs in several ethnic groups including African-, Asian-, and Mexican-Americans. Cross-cultural exploration of the varied facets of gang life. The major social-control institutions affecting them.

allCourses.title: Language in Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Considers the role of language in legal practice and power. Particular attention is paid to linguistic and discourse analytic research that covers topics such as: trial talk, language crimes, law talk in cross-cultural perspectives, and linguistic evidence.

allCourses.title: U. S. Law and Native Americans: Colonial Imagery, Native Nationhood
allCourses.description: Considers U.S. laws governing Native Americans and the way these laws shape and reflect popular conceptions of Native identity. Also surveys the legal practices that Native Nations themselves enact to articulate their sovereign status and identities.

allCourses.title: Employment Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society and Social Ecology majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers federal and state laws that govern the employer-employee relationship, including "at will" employment; wrongful discharge; sexual harassment; discrimination; "whistle-blowing." Considers political, economic, ideological, and cultural factors that have shaped these laws and caused their evolution over time.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C7.

allCourses.title: Forensic Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Forensic psychology is the interface between clinical psychology and the law. Emphasizes clinically relevant legal topics (insanity defense; competency to stand trial) and includes critical thinking about issues that arise when psychologists are involved in legal proceedings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSCI 11C.

allCourses.title: Crime Hotspots
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Criminological theories of local public safety hazards or hotspots are introduced. Spatial statistics are developed for different types of hotspots. Hotspot policing theories are introduced and research on the effectiveness of policing strategies is reviewed.

allCourses.title: Ethics and Politics of Justice
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical perspective on how ethics and politics relate to criminal justice through an introduction to moral philosophy; consideration of specific theories of punishment and justice; and consideration of practical and empirical illustrations of the intersection of ethics, politics, and justice.

allCourses.title: Social Control of Delinquency
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Assumes familiarity with theories of delinquency, the juvenile justice system, and elements of juvenile law. Explores socio-historical origins and evolution of juvenile justice, current research and policy on delinquency prevention and treatment, and future directions of law, policy, and practice.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: CRM/LAW C109.

allCourses.title: The Death Penalty
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines why the U.S. continues to have a death penalty when so many other countries have abandoned it. Arguments for and against the death penalty are covered.

allCourses.title: Spatial Criminology
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Scholars have long noted crime events exhibit a spatial patterning. The principal theoretical perspectives that attempt to explain such a spatial patterning, as well as the research methods used to study crime in spatial context are considered.

allCourses.title: Crime Measurement
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The strengths and weaknesses of three crime measures (police reports, victim surveys, and offender self-reports) are illustrated through analyses of research articles. Common measurement problems are analyzed with a focus on reliability and validity.

allCourses.title: Extreme Punishment
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the history and law of America’s Eighth Amendment prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment, examining the death penalty, long prison sentences, harsh confinement conditions, and other punishments. Students debate practical, legal, and moral arguments for and against these punishments.

allCourses.title: Advanced Research Methods
allCourses.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Federal Law Enforcement
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. SocEcol-Urban & Regional Plan Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The peculiar legal, organizational concerns of the federal system of law enforcement and some of the crimes it is uniquely designed to address—white-collar crime, drug trafficking, racketeering, public corruption. Roles, responsibilities of the FBI, DEA, Customs, other policing agencies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C7

allCourses.title: Latinos and the Law
allCourses.description: Examines a range of theoretical, empirical, and policy approaches to legal issues affecting the Latino population, with emphasis on California. Discusses topics concerning the purpose of law, the creation of law, and the enforcement of law.

allCourses.title: Culture Change and the Mexican People
allCourses.description: Reviews culture contact and colonization, innovation diffusion, acculturation, assimilation, culture conflict and marginality, modernization, urbanization, legal transformations. Mexico and the Southwestern U.S. are reviewed through several centuries to better appreciate the indigenous base of the Mexican people.

allCourses.title: Maritime Piracy, Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the historical and contemporary images and reality of pirates and piracy since the 16th century across the globe through an analysis of primary sources, key historiographical and legal debates, and criminological theories.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Crime
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines immigration and crime in the global context, highlighting immigrants as criminals and victims; immigration and crime control; immigrants’ perceptions of the criminal justice system; public discourse and public perception on immigration and crime; and human rights issues.

allCourses.title: Issues in Policing
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Lectures and readings focus on the history and strategies of policing, measuring the quality of policing, and police misconduct. Strategies for enhancing the quality of policing for controlling misconduct are covered.

allCourses.title: Classics in Crime Cinema
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A multidimensional understanding of crime films and how they shape public thinking about crime and criminals.

allCourses.title: Eyewitness Testimony
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Faulty eyewitness testimony is a major cause of wrongful convictions. Covers the fast-growing topic of eyewitness testimony and memory for real-world events, both how psychologists study eyewitness capacity, and how the legal system has dealt with eyewitness issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10

allCourses.title: Critical Race Theory
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. African-American Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to Critical Race Theory and key American cases on racial inequality. Using this literature, examines the possibilities and pitfalls of legal claims of race, gender, and sexuality discrimination in the age of colorblindness.

allCourses.title: Race and Incarceration
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the racial politics of mass incarceration through historical, empirical, theoretical, and legal frameworks. Focuses on race, gender, and sexual differences to develop a critique on policing, incarceration, and other forms of punishment.

allCourses.title: Power, Constructions of Deviance, and Social Control
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the forms and limits of power in the construction of social deviants. Theories of state power are covered to understand the prison system as a contemporary driver of social inequality. The collateral consequences of mass incarceration are discussed.

allCourses.title: Illegal Economics
allCourses.restriction: Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: How illegal firms function in illegal markets, why individuals participate in these groups and markets, and what federal, state, and local governments do to disrupt organized illegal activity.

allCourses.title: Controversies, Courts, Cultures: The Anthropology of Law
allCourses.description: Assesses the contributions anthropology has made to legal scholarship, reviewing historical and contemporary themes. Considers both comparative questions of law’s norms, structures, and practices around the globe, and the specific insights anthropology offers about contemporary U.S. law.

allCourses.title: Economics of Criminal Justice
allCourses.restriction: Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Quantitative Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to the economics of crime literature.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ECON 122A or ECON 123A

allCourses.title: Criminal Justice System Capacity
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society, Social Ecology, and Chicano/Latino Studies majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines "system capacity" in criminological and criminal justice related research and how it is used to explain and describe current problems and practices in the American legal system. Limitations of sanctioning criminals due to political, physical space, and resource constraints.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C7.

allCourses.title: Social Media and The Law
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines legal and policy issues raised by the rise of social media. Surveys how social networking platforms and other emerging technologies impact the right to privacy, public perceptions of judicial systems, and the law generally.

allCourses.title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
allCourses.description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

allCourses.title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 13

allCourses.title: Law and Modernity
allCourses.description: The rise and spread of Enlightenment legal traditions, social contract theory, individual rights, ideologies of "liberty, equality, fraternity"; contradictions of liberal law, its understandings of "primitive" and "civilized"; pervasive myths of property, difference, race, and rights. Reading- and writing-intensive.

allCourses.title: Research Seminar in Criminology, Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Special topics research seminar. Content varies with interest of instructor. Capstone research opportunity with Criminology, Law and Society faculty members.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to techniques of inductive methodologies, including qualitative interviewing and participant observation, and deductive methodologies, including survey research and experimental and quasi-experimental design. Provides a sound overview of research methodology with tools to pursue specific methods in greater depth.

allCourses.title: Research Methods II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers qualitative approaches (interview strategies, varieties of ethnography, archival and historical methods, etc.) and quantitative approaches (survey methods, experimental designs, secondary data sets, comparative and international data, etc.), and concludes with mixed-method approaches.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C201. CRM/LAW C201 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Qualitative Methods Practicum
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to deepen students’ familiarity with qualitative research strategies and to guide them through the initial stages of their Second Year Project requirement, such as the development of an original research proposal and/or a research instrument.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C202. CRM/LAW C202 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Quantitative Methods Practicum
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Deepens familiarity with quantitative research and provides a foundation for the second-year paper, e.g., initial models for data analysis and/or a replication study. Students evaluate what assumptions are necessary for credible inference in different evaluation approaches.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C202. CRM/LAW C202 with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Land-Use Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Investigates legal and institutional frameworks for development control. Review of constitutional issues implicated in land-use regulation. Traces development control historically and analyzes contemporary approaches to land-use control which reflect environmental and economic development concerns.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Criminology, Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Criminology, Law and Society Majors only.
allCourses.description: Familiarizes students with the interrelated fields of criminology, law and society studies, and criminal justice studies. Organized around three well-established interdisciplinary literatures: criminology, sociolegal studies, and criminal justice studies.

allCourses.title: Legal Institutions and Society
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Acquaints students with the institutions of U.S. legal system and its operations, as well as with the constitutional framework undergirding this system, and defines the relationship between U.S. citizens and government at a variety of levels.

allCourses.title: Policing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the subject of policing. Topics include the management of police organizations, the effectiveness of police patrol strategies, the experiences of women in policing, the recruitment and retention of police officers, and other related topics.

allCourses.title: Crime and Social Deviance
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the major social scientific perspectives on criminal and deviant behavior. Specific deviant and criminal activities are described and explained using established theoretical frameworks.

allCourses.title: Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Structures research methodology, the approach to developing and evaluating knowledge of the sciences for use in criminal justice professional activities. Special emphasis on differentiating scientific approaches from pseudo-science.

allCourses.title: Applied Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a basis for the use of fundamental statistical analysis techniques for solving public policy and management problems through a series of assignments, examinations, and online discussions and demonstrations.

allCourses.title: Public Policy, Crime, and Criminal Justice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Increases understanding of crime, violence, and the criminal justice system. Assesses the state of knowledge on key policy issues of our time. Discusses the contribution of communities, schools, employment, drugs, guns, and alcohol to crime and violence.

allCourses.title: Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces concepts, ideas, and theories about leadership and its operation. Explores leadership concepts through interviews with leaders from the community and fellow classmates.

allCourses.title: Social Problems, Law, and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Criminology, Law and Society Majors only.
allCourses.description: Capstone course for M.A.S. program in Criminology, Law and Society. Students choose a social problem related to crime, criminal justice, and law; relate the problem to legal and social issues; and devise a plan of action to research the problem.

allCourses.title: Hate Crime
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the causes, manifestations, and consequences of hate crimes, as well as the larger social context within which they occur, are reacted to, and seem to be proliferating.

allCourses.title: Sentencing and Corrections
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews U.S. attempts to punish and rehabilitate convicted law violators. Conflicts among major purposes of sentencing (rehabilitation, deterrence, incapacitation, and retribution) are discussed, as well as effects of different sanctions on public safety, offender rehabilitation, and justice system costs.

allCourses.title: Ethnography
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the theory and practice of ethnography with a focus on anthropology, the discipline most associated with ethnography. Students are exposed to the theoretical underpinnings of ethnographic work, traditional and innovative practices, and sample ethnographies.

allCourses.title: Organizational Perspectives on the Legal System
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Familiarizes students with organization theory and research as ways to make sense of, navigate, and act on the legal system. Acquaints students with major frameworks in organization theory and their application to the system of legal organizations.

allCourses.title: Consequences of Imprisonment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews imprisonment and its consequences in the United States. Views prison and inmates as part of (rather than separate from) society. Examines the effects of prison on American society, the family, the labor market, and the community.

allCourses.title: Causal Methods for Policy Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with hands-on experience using existing data to estimate the impact of policy and law on individual behavior or aggregate social outcomes. Covers different econometric strategies used to identify causal effects in the absence of an experiment.

allCourses.title: Conflict Resolution: Theory and Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provide an understanding of the major alternatives to the traditional system for the administration of justice, expanding on some of the newer theories and methods in the field. Key research on social conflict and its resolution examined.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Criminology: Micro Approaches
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the dominant theories in modern criminology, their theoretical antecedents and extensions, major empirical tests and implications for programs, policy and practice, and focuses on micro-level, individual theories of crime causation. Formerly Criminology, Law and Society C233A.

allCourses.title: Criminology: Macro Approaches
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the dominant theories in modern criminology, their theoretical antecedents and extensions, major empirical tests and implications for programs, policy and practices, and addresses macro-level theories of crime causation. Formerly Criminology, Law and Society C233B.

allCourses.title: Crime and Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses the measurement of violent crime; violent offenders and their victims; theoretical explanations of violence; the contribution of the media, drugs, guns, and alcohol to violence; and how the justice system treats and punishes violent offenders.

allCourses.title: Crime and Gender
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the legal, political, social, economic, and policy implications of making gender (primarily) and race (secondarily) the focus in the study of crime, criminal law, and the criminal justice system.

allCourses.title: Juvenile Delinquency
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the major theoretical perspectives regarding the onset, persistence, and desistance of juvenile delinquency, and examines empirical evidence for each perspective.

allCourses.title: Anthropology of Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Law has been a key site of anthropological inquiry since the discipline's nineteenth-century origins. Course introduces and critically assesses the contributions anthropology has made to sociolegal lytic trends.

allCourses.title: Theories of Crime
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines classical and contemporary theories of crime and crime control with special emphasis on the implications of theory for public and social action.

allCourses.title: Gender and Power in Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on questions of gender and sexuality in law and society studies. Drawing on a variety of theoretical frameworks, especially feminist legal theory, examines social processes and structures related to legal regulation, inequality, and social change.

allCourses.title: Legal Reasoning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to law and legal process; use of legal source materials; history and assumptions underlying modern legal reasoning. Key jurisprudential perspectives, development and application of constitutional doctrines (focus on equal protection and right of privacy), and procedure and evidence issues.

allCourses.title: White-Collar Crime
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the illegal behavior of individuals who commit crimes in the course of their employment. Special attention will be paid to ways in which power and organizational structure affect the behavior of the white-collar offenders.

allCourses.title: Law and Society I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to the law and society field from its origins in social scientific, legal, and philosophical scholarship during the eighteenth, nineteenth, and early-twentieth centuries. Formerly Criminology, Law, and Society C239.

allCourses.title: Law and Society II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Building on Law and Society I, addresses contemporary issues in the field from mid-twentieth century to the present with emphasis on the degree to which the field's foundational assumptions are being challenged, refined, or confirmed through current research.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C239A. CRM/LAW C239A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to foster intellectual discussion, encourage practice and skill-building in providing feedback, and build substantive knowledge of legal scholarship, this workshop is for both law and doctoral students across campus who are interested in interdisciplinary approaches to studying law.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to foster intellectual discussion, encourage practice and skill-building in providing feedback, and build substantive knowledge of legal scholarship, this workshop is for both law and doctoral students across campus who are interested in interdisciplinary approaches to studying law.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C240A. CRM/LAW C240A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Socio-Legal Workshop
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to foster intellectual discussion, encourage practice and skill-building in providing feedback, and build substantive knowledge of legal scholarship, this workshop is for both law and doctoral students across campus who are interested in interdisciplinary approaches to studying law.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C240B. CRM/LAW C240B with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Social Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Origins and organization of racialized social control, with emphasis on criminal justice. Racial politics of criminal/juvenile justice considered in comparative (historical and international) perspective. Exploration of theoretical and methodological issues for research on race, ethnicity, and social control.

allCourses.title: Crime Hotspots
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the criminological theory of hotspots, beginning with the “when, where, and why” questions and ending with the practical policing strategies that have been developed to mitigate hotspot public safety hazards.

allCourses.title: Social Science and the Legal Process
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the use (and misuse) of social science in the legal process, focusing on role of social science evidence in trial and appellate decision making. Test-case litigation in which social science has been used to challenge laws or support reform.

allCourses.title: Geographic Information Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Prepares students to become proficient in the basic GIS functionality including visualization, data management, and spatial analysis.

allCourses.title: Preventing Errors of Justice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the types of errors that are made in the U.S. criminal justice system and how we might prevent these errors, including failures to convict guilty offenders as well as wrongful convictions of the innocent.

allCourses.title: Issues in Environmental Law and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Treatment of legal and policy strategies for promoting environmental protection and deterring environmental degradation within the context of other societal objectives. Topical approach with a focus on problems of special interest to criminologists and to environmental policy specialists.

allCourses.title: Cybercrime, Cybersecurity, and Society
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Criminology, Law and Society M.A.S. students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the world of cybercrime in the age of globally networked digital, and information and communication technologies (ICT). Presents a socio-legal approach to the study of cybercrime, cybersecurity, and how it relates to society.

allCourses.title: Immigration in the US: Economic, Fiscal, and Social Outcomes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Criminology, Law and Society Majors only.
allCourses.description: The changing patterns of immigration in the U.S. and the role that immigrants play in our society. In particular, the economic and social outcomes of immigration, as well as the relationship between immigration, crime, and criminal justice policy.

allCourses.title: Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst.  Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.

allCourses.title: Juvenile Justice and Gangs
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Criminology, Law and Society M.A.S. students only.
allCourses.description: Aims to understand the history and evolution of the juvenile justice system, and introduces the challenges that street and prison gangs pose to the mission and operations of juvenile justice in America.

allCourses.title: Crimmigration
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the criminalization of immigration, with an emphasis on U.S. enforcement procedures and outcomes. Analyzes the devolution of federal immigration law to local authorities, the rise in immigrant detention and deportation, and the militarization of the U.S.-Mexico border.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A year-long proseminar conducted by a team of instructors specializing in race and justice studies. Conceived as a reading and peer mentor group focusing on intellectual and professional development. Required for students pursuing the Race and Justice Studies emphasis.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A year-long proseminar conducted by a team of instructors specializing in race and justice studies. Conceived as a reading and peer mentor group focusing on intellectual and professional development. Required for students pursuing the Race and Justice Studies emphasis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C260A. CRM/LAW C260A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Race and Justice Studies Proseminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A year-long proseminar conducted by a team of instructors specializing in race and justice studies. Conceived as a reading and peer mentor group focusing on intellectual and professional development. Required for students pursuing the Race and Justice Studies emphasis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C260B. CRM/LAW C260B with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_for.title: Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar
Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar
Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar

allCourses.title: Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A required writing-intensive seminar conducted by an instructor affiliated with the Race and Justice Studies emphasis. Students with manuscripts on relevant topics will read and critique peer manuscripts, and revise manuscripts toward completion of articles, dissertation chapters, and other publications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C260C. CRM/LAW C260C with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Race and Justice Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A seminar focused on special issues in race and justice studies.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Eyewitness Testimony
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the evidence that shows that faulty eyewitness memory is the major cause of wrongful convictions. Explores what the legal system thinks of eyewitness testimony and how the legal system has dealt with eyewitness issues.

allCourses.title: Memory and the Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the controversial topic of repressed memory, or perception and memory of real-world events.

allCourses.title: Psychology and the Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of how psychology is applied to the civil and criminal justice systems, how case law shapes this application, and how legal decisions affect the direction of psychological research. Interdisciplinary approach to research in psychology, law, and/or  criminology.

allCourses.title: Contemporary Issues in Crime and Justice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intensive reading and discussion of several recent works that raise critical issues for criminology and criminal justice policy, with a special emphasis on issues of inequality, diversity, and social justice.

allCourses.title: Economics of Crime
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the economic approach of thinking about criminal activity. Using the Becker model of rational criminal behavior as a starting point, we evaluate how education, employment, social insurance, and local economic development programs can affect criminal behavior.

allCourses.title: Economics of Criminal Justice
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Considers empirical research from the economics literature on various topics related to the criminal justice system, such as policing, bail reform, incarceration, or recidivism.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Criminology, Law and Society
allCourses.description: Topics covered vary with interests of instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on two areas that are key to scholarly and professional success in graduate school but are rarely discussed in a structured setting: 1) publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals; and 2) preparing for the academic job market.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on two areas that are key to scholarly and professional success in graduate school but are rarely discussed in a structured setting: 1) publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals; and 2) preparing for the academic job market.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C280A. CRM/LAW C280A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Professionalization Proseminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on two areas that are key to scholarly and professional success in graduate school but are rarely discussed in a structured setting: 1) publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals; and 2) preparing for the academic job market.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CRM/LAW C280B. CRM/LAW C280B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Criminology, Law and Society faculty.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Advancement to candidacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Directed Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed study with Criminology, Law and Society faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Criminology, Law and Society faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Forms of Criminal Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Undergraduates are introduced to the subjects of crime and criminal behavior. Topics include "street" and "white-collar" crimes. Histories of the offenses, the types of people who commit the crimes, and society's reactions to the offenses are presented.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Criminology, Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces characteristics of the U.S. criminal justice system, including responses to crime, components of the system, and current challenges to the system. Examines structure and function of police and courts, criminal procedure, and sentencing and incarceration policies.

allCourses.title: The Properties of Property
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Develops an understanding and critique of private property. Draws from interdisciplinary sources to explore the foundations of private property, the institutions that support it over time, and possible alternatives to it.

allCourses.title: Principles of Operating Systems
allCourses.description: Principles and concepts of process and resource management, especially as seen in operating systems. Processes, memory management, protection, scheduling, file systems, and I/O systems are covered. Concepts illustrated in the context of several well-known systems.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introduction to Costume Design
allCourses.restriction: Music Theatre Majors only. Drama Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the process and procedures employed by the costume designer for the theatre. The elements of design are discussed in the context of character development, historical period, and style. Exercises extend to drawing, rendering, and investigation of human proportions.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introduction to Scenic Design
allCourses.restriction: Music Theatre Majors only. Drama Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the principles and practice of scenic design. Weekly problems include research into various periods and styles of production with an emphasis on the conceptual idea. Perspective drawing, rendering, and model building are covered in studio exercises and assignments.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introduction to Lighting Design
allCourses.restriction: Music Theatre Majors only. Drama Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the principles, theories, and equipment employed by the lighting designer for the stage.  Areas of investigation include history, technology, and script analysis. Detailed studio attention is given to the theory and practice of design.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introduction to Sound Design
allCourses.restriction: Music Theatre Majors only. Drama Majors only.
allCourses.description: Principles, theories, equipment use, and terminology employed by the sound designer for the stage. Areas of study include history, technology, and script analysis.  Focuses on the theory and practice of design.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introduction to Stage Management
allCourses.restriction: Music Theatre Majors only. Drama Majors only.
allCourses.description: A basic study of theatrical, dance, and opera stage management practices, forms, and methods, from first script reading to closing night.  Opportunity to observe professionals at work in regional and touring situations as available.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: History and Theories of Scenography
allCourses.restriction: Music Theatre Majors only. Drama Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores the aesthetics of the stage and the evolution of scenery and costume in live performance as inspiration for today’s theatre analysts. Topics include shared vocabulary, historical trends, shifts in approaches, and focus briefs on leaders in the field.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Topics in Advanced Stage Management
allCourses.description: Nurtures a greater appreciation for the stage manager and his or her process, and supports students who are interested in pursuing a career in professional stage management.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Music Theatre Workshop I
allCourses.description: Basic vocal technique and characterization of musical theatre repertoire explored.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Audition required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Directing I
allCourses.description: Introduction to comprehensive directing process from pre-production to opening. Focus on fundamental skills: analysis, staging, action, actor coaching, and elements of design. Skills applied to scripted theatrical material. Develop a language for commenting on theatrical production. Attending and critiquing productions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: DRAMA 30A and DRAMA 30B

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Directing I
allCourses.description: Exercises introduce students to standard practices for shaping a play, such as table work, blocking, business, and actor coaching. Students take charge of sample rehearsals, guiding casts through exercises, followed by peer review, and instructor critique.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: DRAMA 30A and DRAMA 30B and DRAMA 30C.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.description: For graduate student actors and undergraduate directors who are candidates for Honors in Directing and involved in the Director Class Projects. The Head of Directing (HoD) supervises these students.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Earth System Science
allCourses.description: Covers the origin and evolution of the Earth, its atmosphere, and oceans, from the perspective of biogeochemical cycles, energy use, and human impacts on the Earth system.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Earth System Science
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Devoted to current topics in the field of Earth System Science. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 51 and EARTHSS 53 and EARTHSS 55) or (EARTHSS 70A and EARTHSS 70B)
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Paleoclimatology
allCourses.restriction: Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores past changes in Earth's climate. Topics include tools and techniques used to reconstruct past climate from natural archives; records and mechanisms of past climate changes throughout Earth history; and lessons learned from the paleo-record for predication of future climate.

allCourses.title: Climate Change and Policy
allCourses.description: Develops an understanding of the physical basis behind global climate change; examines how human activities cause it, looks to future rates and impacts of global warming, and reviews the international conventions, protocols, and scientific assessments of climate change.

allCourses.title: Environmental Controversies
allCourses.restriction: Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the roles and strategies of advocacy groups, scientists, lobbyists, celebrities, pundits, politicians, and other opinion-makers in creating and shaping public opinion on controversial environmental issues. Use and misuse of science to influence public opinion is elicited.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 60A and EARTHSS 60B and EARTHSS 60C) or EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 53 or EARTHSS 55

allCourses.title: Global Climate Change and Impacts
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Observations over the 20th century show extensive changes in atmospheric composition, climate and weather, and biological systems that have paralleled industrial growth. Evidence of globally driven changes in these biogeochemical systems is studied, including projected impacts over the 21st century.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 51 and EARTHSS 53 and EARTHSS 55) or (EARTHSS 70A and EARTHSS 70B)

allCourses.title: Earth System Science Laboratory and Field Methods
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to methods used to measure exchange of gases and energy between the atmosphere and terrestrial ecosystems. Laboratories include data acquisition and isotopic and chromatographic analysis. Field measurements at UCI's Marsh Reserve include microclimate, hydrology, trace-gas exchange, and plant growth. Materials fee.

allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students design sampling plans, conduct field research techniques, and carry out data analyses that are relevant to aquatic field research. Aquatic field sites covered in the course include marine, estuarine, and fluvial systems. Materials fee.

allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis and interpretation of geophysical data, including functional fitting, probability density functions, and multidimensional time-series methods, with applications in atmospheric, oceanic, and biogeochemical sciences.

allCourses.title: Analysis, Modeling, and Visualization of Multidimensionnal Environmental Data
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students learn programming and numerical methods in Python with applications in Earth System Science and ecology. Topics include regression, uncertainty and significance, the development of simple box models, and the visualization of multi-dimensional climate and satellite datasets.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 31 or EARTHSS 116

allCourses.title: Atmospheric Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fluid dynamical processes that determine the large-scale flow of the atmosphere and ocean. Most important are interactions between the density stratification and the Coriolis force associated with Earth's rotation. Topics include circulation, vorticity, planetary waves, and their role in climate.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EARTHSS 55 and (PHYSICS 7C or PHYSICS 3B)

allCourses.title: Weather Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of weather systems in midlatitudes and tropics. The fundamental dynamics possible for these weather systems are described. Elementary weather analysis and forecasting techniques are introduced.

allCourses.title: Global-Change Biology
allCourses.description: Addresses ways in which humans are altering the global environment, with consequences for the ecology of animals, plants, and microbes. Discussion on how these biologically oriented questions relate to human society, politics, and the economy.

allCourses.title: Physical Oceanography
allCourses.restriction: Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Physical processes that determine the distribution of water properties such as salt and temperature. Fluid-dynamical underpinnings of physical oceanography. Wave motions. The wind-driven and thermohaline circulation. Similarities and differences between ocean and atmosphere dynamics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PHYSICS 7C or PHYSICS 3B) and EARTHSS 53

allCourses.title: Terrestrial Hydrology
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Comprehensive treatment of modern conceptual and methodological approaches to hydrological science. Combines qualitative understanding of hydrological processes with quantitative representation, approaches to measurement, and treatment of uncertainty. Components of the hydrological cycle and their linkages within the coupled Earth system.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 51 and EARTHSS 55) or (EARTHSS 40C and EARTHSS 70B)

allCourses.title: Soil: It's the Good Dirt
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors only. Environmental Science Majors only. Earth System Science Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the critical role soils play in sustaining land ecosystems and humans. Covers how soils form and how human actions contribute to the pollution and loss but also the health and productivity of soils.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 51 and EARTHSS 53 and EARTHSS 55) or (EARTHSS 70A and EARTHSS 70B)

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of GIS for Environmental Science
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Topics include fundamentals of cartography, creating/editing GIS data, linking spatial and tabular data, georeferencing, map projections, geospatial analysis, spatial statistics, and the development of GIS models. Examples from hydrology, ecology, and geology.

allCourses.title: Satellite Remote Sensing for Earth System Science
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Satellite remote sensing data are increasingly used to study the Earth system. Provides an overview of the principles behind remote sensing, and the types of satellite data available for study of the oceans, land, and atmosphere.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 51 and EARTHSS 53) or (EARTHSS 70A and EARTHSS 70B)

allCourses.title: Advanced Geology
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the geological processes which have formed and continue to shape the Earth. Topics include geological time, minerals and the rock cycle, plate tectonics and associated geological hazards, earth resources, and earth surface processes. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 70B

allCourses.title: Air Quality Management
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamental science and terminology of regional air quality issues and developing and implementing the strategies used to prevent and mitigate air pollution impacts. Topics include setting regional air quality goals, applying measurements and numerical models, cost/benefits analysis, evaluation and enforcement.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EARTHSS 40A and EARTHSS 40B and EARTHSS 40C

allCourses.title: Atmospheric Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Chemistry of the troposphere and stratosphere. Topics include processes controlling the lifetime and reaction pathways of chemicals in the atmosphere, the role of the atmosphere in biogeochemical cycles, and interactions between atmospheric chemistry and the physical climate system.

allCourses.title: Global Physical Climatology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A descriptive overview of Earth’s climate system and energy budget. Large-scale circulations, key physical processes, and climate sensitivity of the atmosphere, ocean, land surface, and cryosphere.

allCourses.title: Paleoclimatology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores past changes in Earth's climate. Topics include tools and techniques used to reconstruct past climate from natural archives; records and mechanisms of past climate changes throughout Earth history; and lessons learned from the paleo-record for predication of future climate.

allCourses.title: Climate Change
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores past, present, and projected changes in Earth's climate. Topics include paleoclimate records and mechanisms of natural climate variability at a range of timescales (orbital to seasonal); General Circulation Models; and IPCC observations and projections of future climate change.

allCourses.title: Humans in the Earth System
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Earth System Science Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the human systems of energy and food production which have the greatest effects on the Earth system. Assess the physical mechanisms and feedbacks of human-nature interactions and consider approaches of mitigation, interventions, and adaptation.

allCourses.title: Global Biogeochemical Cycles
allCourses.description: Global biogeochemical cycling of the elements. Topics include: global cycling of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and sulfer; impact of human activities on biogeochemical processes.

allCourses.title: On Thin Ice: Climate Change and the Cryosphere
allCourses.description: Introduction of the basic science that governs the cryosphere and its interaction with the climate system. Covers some of the significant economic, sociological, and political consequences of the recent melting of the cryosphere driven by anthropogenic climate change.

allCourses.title: Geoscience Modeling and Data Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Computer-based course. Fundamental statistical techniques needed to analyze Earth system data and models. Basic numerical techniques to solve Earth system models. Focuses on linear and non-linear ordinary differential equations, as well as simple partial differential equations.

allCourses.title: Cryosphere
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A global perspective of the major components of the cryosphere. Includes current extent and trends, mass balance, energetics, and physical processes. Quantitative assessment of current state, in situ and remote observations, and interactions with climate.

allCourses.title: Global Climate Change and Impacts
allCourses.description: Observations over the 20th century show extensive changes in atmospheric composition, climate and weather, and biological systems that have paralleled industrial growth. Evidence of globally driven changes in these biogeochemical systems is studied, including projected impacts over the 21st century.

allCourses.title: Ocean Processes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the physics, chemistry, and biology of the oceans. Offers a mechanistic perspective of the structure and functioning of marine ecosystems, nutrient cycles, and role of ecosystem dynamics in local and global biogeochemistry.

allCourses.title: Marine Biogeochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Philosophy Degree students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview of ocean biology and biogeochemistry, with a focus on lower trophic levels and the roles of biota in the marine biogeochemical cycles of key elements.

allCourses.title: Land Surface Processes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A mechanistic perspective of the structure and functioning of terrestrial ecosystems. Includes processes such as nutrient cycling, biogeochemical cycling, mass balance, energetics, terrestrial hydrology, and water cycle.

allCourses.title: Geophysical Fluid Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces fluid dynamical processes that determine the large-scale flow of the atmosphere and ocean, with particular emphasis on the interactions between the stable density stratification and the Coriolis force associated with Earth's rotation.

allCourses.title: Air Pollution: From Urban Smog to Global Change
allCourses.description: Air pollution occurs on regional to global scales. A wide range of air pollution sources and physical, chemical, and meteorological sciences behind air pollution are introduced. The consequences of air pollution to our society are also discussed.

allCourses.title: Physical Oceanography
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Physical processes that determine the distribution of water properties such as salt and temperature.  Fluid-dynamical underpinnings of physical oceanography.  Wave motions.  The wind-driven and thermohaline circulation.  Similarities and differences between ocean and atmosphere dynamics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D and PHYSICS 7A and PHYSICS 7B and PHYSICS 7E

allCourses.title: Terrestrial Hydrology
allCourses.description: Comprehensive treatment of modern conceptual and methodological approaches to hydrological science. Combines qualitative understanding of hydrological processes with quantitative representation, approaches to measurement, and treatment of uncertainty. Components of the hydrological cycle and their linkages within the coupled Earth system.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EARTHSS 60A or EARTHSS 51

allCourses.title: Radiative Processes and Remote Sensing
allCourses.description: Solar and terrestrial radiation and Earth system interaction. Radiative transfer theory. Principles, applications of remote sensing of environment. Planck's law, radiative transfer equation, radiative properties of trace gasses and aerosols, remote sensing techniques, global trends in radiative forcing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D and PHYSICS 7D.

allCourses.title: Satellite Remote Sensing for Earth System Science
allCourses.description: Satellite remote sensing data are increasingly used to study the Earth system. Provides an overview of the principles behind remote sensing, and the types of satellite data available for study of the oceans, land, and atmosphere.

allCourses.title: Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the physical/chemical processes which determine the structure and composition of Earth's atmosphere and its role in the climate system.

allCourses.title: Advanced Atmospheric Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Chemistry of the troposphere and stratosphere.  Topics include: processes controlling the lifetime and reaction pathways of chemicals in the atmosphere, the role of the atmosphere in biogeochemical cycles, and interactions between atmospheric chemistry and the physical climate system.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Atmospheric Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers fundamentals of atmospheric dynamics including thermodynamics, quasi-geostrophy, the weak-temperature gradient of the tropics, and the turbulent boundary layer.

allCourses.title: Marine Ecosystems and Global Change
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents an overview of marine ecosystem structure, diversity, and processes in the context of global change, including the impacts of climate warming, ocean acidification, marine fisheries, and anthropogenic additions of nutrients and pollutants.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EARTHSS 224. EARTHSS 224 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Laboratory Methods in Earth System Science
allCourses.description: Introduction to analytical methods used in Earth science research. Lectures cover theory and applications of each method. Laboratories cover sample preparation, experimental design, standardization and calibration, operation of analytical instruments (mass spectrometers, gas chromatographs, and spectrophotometers), and analysis of data.

allCourses.title: Environmental Isotope Geochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of stable, radioactive, and radiogenic isotope variability in the Earth System. Focuses on theory, measurement techniques, biogeochemistry, hydrology, ecology, and climate related applications.

allCourses.title: Paleoclimatology and Paleoceanography
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores past changes in Earth's climate. Topics include tools and techniques used to reconstruct past climate from natural archives; records and mechanisms of past climate changes throughout Earth history; and lessons learned from the paleo-record for prediction of future climate.

allCourses.title: Ecosystem Ecology
allCourses.description: A mechanistic perspective on ecosystem processes. Covers ecosystem development, element cycling, and interactions with plants and microbes. The role of ecosystems in environmental change is also addressed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 51C

allCourses.title: Global Biogeochemical Cycles
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Global biogeochemical cycling of the elements. Topics include global cycling of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and sulfur; impact of human activities on biogeochemical processes.

allCourses.title: Physiological Plant Ecology
allCourses.description: An examination of the interactions between plants and their environment. Emphasis on the underlying physiological mechanisms of plant function, adaptations and responses to stress, and the basis of the distribution of plants and plant assemblages across the landscape.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 51 or EARTHSS 60A) and (EARTHSS 60C or BIO SCI E106).

allCourses.title: The Sustainable Ocean
allCourses.description: An introduction to sustainability as it relates to marine resources and conservation. Topics include the scientific basis of our understanding of marine ecosystems, and the political, social, and cultural principles that govern resource protection.

allCourses.title: Environmental Microbiology
allCourses.description: Establishes a fundamental understanding of microbes living in the environment, including their distribution, diversity, and biochemistry, and discusses how they attribute to global biogeochemical cycles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EARTHSS 53 or EARTHSS 60A) and (EARTHSS 60C or BIO SCI E106)

allCourses.title: Science Communication and Outreach
allCourses.description: Students learn and practice effective science communication skills useful in public and educational outreach. Topics include research explication, language scaffolding, educational psychology, oral presentation techniques, K-12 science standards, and effective writing styles for op-eds, blogs, and Web sites.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Ice in the Climate System
allCourses.description: Examines the major components of the Earth’s cryosphere. Characteristics, volume, extent, remote sensing observations, long-term trends, mass balance, key physical processes, relevance and importance to the climate system, responses and feedbacks, future evolution, and key uncertainties will be discussed.

allCourses.title: Oceanography
allCourses.description: Examines circulation of the world oceans and ocean chemistry as it relates to river, hydrothermal vent, and atmospheric inputs. Geological features, the wide variety of biological organisms, and global climate changes, such as greenhouse warming, are also studied.

allCourses.title: Earth System Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: To understand the cycling of matter on Earth, we need to learn about the chemistry of elements and molecules in the environment. Introduces students to the understanding of how chemical principles apply in context to their everyday lives.

allCourses.title: Earth System Biology
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Earth System Science is a highly interdisciplinary field that requires knowledge of various components of the Earth as a system, including the biosphere. Students are introduced to several fundamental principles of biology, from the smallest cells to the largest ecosystems.

allCourses.title: Earth System Physics
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamental physical forces and laws that affect the Earth system, such as electromagnetic radiation and energy transfer, atmospheric and ocean dynamics. Also covers aspects of physics related to environmental issues, such as electricity generation and transmission.

allCourses.title: New Student Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. New students only (freshman, transfer, and change of major).
allCourses.description: Weekly meetings led by faculty, current students, and staff, to provide information on the Department of Earth System Science, campus resources, and special programs and opportunities. Designed for students who recently joined the Earth System Science and Environmental Science majors.

allCourses.title: The Atmosphere
allCourses.description: The composition and circulation of the atmosphere with a focus on explaining the fundamentals of weather and climate. Topics include solar and terrestrial radiation, clouds, and weather patterns.

allCourses.title: Land Interactions
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The role of terrestrial processes in the Earth system. Provides an introduction to ecosystem processes that regulate the cycling of energy, water, carbon, and nutrients. Analysis of the impact of human activities. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Physical and functional principles common to many living forms. Course forms a basis for subsequent specialization in any of the subdisciplines of physiology. Course offered in even years.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Evolutionary Biology

allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Ecological Genetics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Content and instructor will vary from year to year. Possible topics include coevolution, sex-ratio evolution, evolution senescence, plant population biology, and density-dependent selection.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.description: Weekly discussion of current topics in ecology at the graduate level.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Statistical Learning in Ecology and Evolution
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews basic principals of variance/bias trade-offs. Topics include models for prediction and classification, variable selection methods, cross-validation, tree based methods, unsupervised learning. Applications in ecology and evolution using R.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Plant Physiological Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
