allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with conceptual and methodological tools for using video in educational research.  Students work with their own video data or with publicly accessible databases.

allCourses.title: Use of Video in Educational Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with conceptual and methodological tools for using video in educational research. Students work with their own video data or with publicly accessible databases.

allCourses.title: Hierarchical Linear Models for Education Research
allCourses.description: Descriptive and inferential analysis methods for education projects with nested data. Focuses on linear models that account for nesting of children in classrooms or schools or of repeated measures over time on the same individuals.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Planning and Design
allCourses.restriction: Doctoral degree candidates only.
allCourses.description: Prepares the doctoral student to write an outstanding dissertation proposal. In workshop format, students complete a draft dissertation proposal that includes the Introduction, Conceptual Framework, Methodology, and References. Students also develop a timeline for conducting their dissertations.

allCourses.title: Pre-Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Independent study course taken under the direction of a faculty member who guides the student's research. May include guidance on data collection, methodology, human subjects protocol, conference presentation, scholarly publication, program benchmark activities.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Professional Writing in Educational Research I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: First of a two-course series designed to extend students’ knowledge of conducting and publishing educational research. Topics include the logic of research and how to effectively communicate research findings, with particular emphasis on proficient scientific writing.

allCourses.title: Professional Writing in Educational Research II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Second of a two-course series designed to extend students’ knowledge of conducting and publishing educational research. Topics include the logic of research and how to effectively communicate research findings, with particular emphasis on proficient scientific writing.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research on topics related to education.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Reserach
allCourses.restriction: Doctoral students only.
allCourses.description: Specifically designed for students researching and writing their dissertations.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: 21st Century Literacies
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of literacies required for academic and career success in the 21st century. Issues addressed include reading, writing, academic language, research skills, media and technology skills, scientific literacy, critical thinking, communication, collaboration, and creativity.

allCourses.title: Directed Elementary Field Experiences in Diverse Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Fieldwork experiences and seminars to provide introduction to the California Teaching Performance Expectations, including guidelines for professional expectations, observation and participation in classrooms, instructional planning, classroom management, and formative experiences and preparation for the state-mandated Teaching Performance Assessment.

allCourses.title: Directed Secondary Field Experiences
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Field work experiences and seminars to provide introduction to the California Teaching Performance Expectations, including guidelines for professional expectations, observation and participation in classrooms, instructional planning, classroom management, and formative experiences and preparation for the State-mandated Teaching Performance Assessment.

allCourses.title: Learning to Learn from Teaching in Elementary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Teacher Credential Program students only.
allCourses.description: Preparation for elementary school teaching that provides analytic tools for observing and reflecting on instruction, examining how student thinking is demonstrated, understanding components of and relationships between the teaching and learning process and planning effective instruction including innovative teaching practices.

allCourses.title: Student Teaching in the Elementary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Student teaching seminars prepare candidates for assumption of classroom instructional responsibilities in accordance with State credentialing requirements. Four full days a week of student teaching in public school elementary classrooms in winter quarter and five full days in spring quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Learning to Learn from Teaching in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Analytic tools for (1) observing and reflecting on observed instruction; (2) examining student thinking and the relationship between teaching and learning; (3) understanding particular components of the teaching/learning process; and (4) planning effective instruction including innovative teaching practices.

allCourses.title: Supervised Teaching in Bilingual Education, Elementary
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Student teaching experiences in bilingual public school classrooms to include orientation, regular seminars, and preparation for bilingual classroom instructional responsibilities in accordance with State credentialing requirements and in conjunction with the public school calendar.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Student Teaching in Intermediate/Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Student teaching includes orientation, seminars, and preparation for and assumption of secondary school classroom instructional responsibilities in accordance with State credentialing requirements and in conjunction with public school calendar. Five full days a week in both winter and spring quarters.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Performance Assessment for California Teachers, Multiple Subjects
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Preparation and technical support for multiple subjects teacher candidates to complete State-required Teaching Performance Assessment for the California preliminary credential. Includes assistance in planning, teaching/videotaping, assessment and reflection, and document production.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Supervised Teaching in Bilingual Education, Secondary
allCourses.restriction: Teaching Credential Program students only.
allCourses.description: Student teaching experiences in bilingual public school classrooms to include orientation, regular seminars, and preparation for bilingual classroom instructional responsibilities in accordance with State credentialing requirements and in conjunction with the public school calendar.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Performance Assessment for California Teachers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Preparation and technical support for teacher candidates to complete the required Teaching Performance Assessment for California credential licensure. Structured support for planning, videotaping, and document production occurs in meetings scheduled to coincide with the timeline for the project.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Learning to Learn from Teaching Practice
allCourses.restriction: Teacher Credential Program students only.
allCourses.description: Secondary curriculum and methodology, including instructional planning, teaching strategies, classroom management, evaluation, cultural and linguistic considerations and interpersonal skills. Application of these to fieldwork experience in preparation for teaching responsibilities assumed in secondary schools.

allCourses.title: Intern Teaching in the Secondary School: Single Subject Instruction
allCourses.restriction: Teacher Credential Program students only.
allCourses.description: A paid intern practicum (usually one year) cosponsored by an employing school district and the UCI Department of Education.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 36 units.

allCourses.title: Direct Field Experiences
allCourses.restriction: Teacher Credential Program students only.
allCourses.description: Observation, participation, and teaching in diverse public school classrooms. Application of theory and pedagogy in field work classrooms.

allCourses.title: Teaching Physical and Health Education in Elementary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Methods of teaching physical education for the elementary classroom teacher. Through an interactive environment, students experience the California Physical Education and Health content standards with appropriate pedagogy. Concepts address motor skills, physical fitness, and personal responsibility for lifelong health.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Social Studies
allCourses.restriction: Teacher Credential Program Students only.
allCourses.description: Description, scope, sequence, and methods of teaching social studies and inquiry in grades K-8.  Includes utilization of California State Framework for Teaching History/Social Science and addresses current aspects and trends in multicultural education.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Mathematics I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Scope, sequence, and methods of teaching mathematics at all levels of elementary school. Presented through lectures, discussions, demonstrations, and exploration of a variety of materials. Covers how to plan lessons, motivate students, diagnose difficulties, and evaluate learning in mathematics.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Mathematics II
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Part two of a course addressing pedagogical methods for elementary mathematics. Lectures, discussions, and exploration of instructional strategies and materials support preservice teacher development in the critical areas of planning, instruction, and assessment for conceptual understanding in mathematics.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Science
allCourses.description: Prospective elementary teachers learn how to teach science in grades K-8. Covers States science requirements, a variety of teaching methods, criteria for selecting science curriculum materials, and how to plan science lessons, units, experiments, projects, and demonstrations.

allCourses.title: Curriculum Methods in Elementary Science
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prospective elementary teachers learn how to teach science in grades K-8. Covers state science requirements, a variety of teaching methods, and criteria for selecting science curriculum materials.

allCourses.title: Curriculum Methods in Elementary Science
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prospective elementary teachers learn how to teach science in grades K-8. Covers state science requirements, a variety of teaching methods, criteria for selecting science curriculum materials, and how to plan science lessons, units, experiments, projects, and demonstrations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EDUC 323A. EDUC 323A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Language Arts Integrated with Social Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: An integrated approach to language arts and social studies instruction at the K–6 level based on California State English/Language Arts and Social Studies Frameworks and Standards. Focus on teaching content through literature and writing and providing access for all learners.

allCourses.title: Teaching the Visual and Performing Arts in Elementary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the issues and practices — including student diversity, academic literacy, and interdisciplinary content —  involved in integrating the California visual and performing arts curriculum framework and academic content standards with developmentally appropriate teaching strategies for the elementary classroom. Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary School Reading
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Teaching an integrated reading/language arts program in the elementary classroom. Implementing theories, principles, and methods which are research and reality-based. Creating a child-centered, language-rich program to meet needs of children in multicultural/multilingual settings.

allCourses.title: Theories and Methods of English Language Development Applied to Elementary Students
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Theories and methods of English language development and instruction of English language learners, with focus on elementary students. Includes language acquisition theory, language and content, assessment strategies, and preparation of curricula and instruction for grades K–6 English language learners.

allCourses.title: Instructional Technology: Resources for the Multiple Subject Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Teacher Credential Program majors only.
allCourses.description: Issues and techniques in uses of computer-based and media technologies in the multiple subject classroom: social implications and professional responsibilities; productivity tools to enhance student thinking skills; and strategies for instruction and management.

allCourses.title: Health Principles and Practices for the Elementary Teacher
allCourses.description: Methods for creating healthy environments for student learning in elementary schools. Introduction of California content standards and frameworks with appropriate pedagogy. Personal, family, school, community factors, and legal responsibilities of teachers. Academic, physical, emotional, and social well-being.

allCourses.title: Literacy and Technology in the Secondary Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: A view of literacy expanded beyond typological print, students learn: (1) strategies for incorporating, (2) tools for evaluating and selecting, and (3) learning theories for understanding how information and communication technologies and online resources contribute to general and disciplinary literacy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Limited to students accepted into the Teacher Credential Program

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching Languages other than English in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prepares future teachers of foreign language or primary/home language. Emphasizes hands-on, practical strategies for communication-based instruction and authentic assessment in reading, writing, listening, speaking, and culture.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching Social Science in the Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theories, strategies, and methodologies related to the teaching of history and social science in the secondary school. Emphasis on the planning, delivery, and assessment of lessons reflecting an understanding of the History-Social Science Framework for California.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching English in the Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to teaching reading, writing, and speaking skills in secondary school. Emphasis upon integrative approach to teaching literature, composition, and grammar consistent with the California State Framework. Practice in the design of lesson plans that are both integrated and cumulative.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching Visual Arts in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theory, curriculum, and strategies for teaching visual arts in the secondary school. Emphasis on the planning, delivery, and assessment of lessons consistent with California State Framework and content standards.

allCourses.title: Methods of Teaching Mathematics in Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theories, strategies, and methodologies related to the teaching of mathematics in the secondary school. Emphasis on the planning, delivery, and assessment of lessons reflecting an understanding of the Mathematics Framework for California and the recommendations of professional organizations.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 4 units.

allCourses.title: Teaching Science in Secondary School
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Prospective secondary science teachers learn how to teach science in grades 7-12. Covers State science requirements, a variety of teaching methods, criteria for selecting science curricular materials, and how to plan science lessons, units, experiments, projects, and demonstrations.

allCourses.title: Applied Instructional Strategies in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Teaching Credential Degree students only. EDUC 342 and EDUC 342A-B may not both be taken for credit.
allCourses.description: Application of pedagogy and research to practice teaching experiences in the secondary schools. A continuation of the methodology course series with an emphasis on the needs of students with culturally diverse backgrounds.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Applied Instructional Strategies in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only. EDUC 342 and EDUC 342A may not both be taken for credit.
allCourses.description: Application of pedagogy and research to practice teaching experiences in the secondary schools. A continuation of the methodology course series with an emphasis on the needs of students with culturally diverse backgrounds. Conducted in a five-week format.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Applied Instructional Strategies in Secondary Schools
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only. EDUC 342 and EDUC 342B may not both be taken for credit.
allCourses.description: Application of pedagogy and research to practice teaching experiences in the secondary schools. A continuation of the methodology course series with an emphasis on the needs of students with culturally diverse backgrounds. Conducted in a five-week format.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Applied Instructional Strategies in Secondary School Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Teacher Credential Program students only.
allCourses.description: Application of pedagogy and research to practice science teaching experiences in the secondary schools. A continuation of the Education 340 series with an emphasis on the needs of students with culturally diverse backgrounds.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Child Development and Educational Equity
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores theories of child development applied to teaching and learning in elementary schools. Attention is given to role of cultural norms in defining goals for child development and for educational practices and in creating equal learning opportunities for all children.

allCourses.title: Reading and Writing in Middle School and High School Classrooms
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasis is placed upon understanding the literacy processes (listening, speaking, viewing, reading, and writing) as they relate to all Single Subject areas. Teachers are guided to integrate literacy-related strategies with curriculum-based goals supported in the California State Frameworks.

allCourses.title: Culture, Diversity, and Educational Equity
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of and social theories about the origins and consequences of U.S. racial, gender, and social inequality, and the effects of poverty and racism on the educational opportunities and outcomes of minority groups in the United States.

allCourses.title: Culture, Diversity, and Educational Equity
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of and social theories about the origins and consequences of U.S. racial, gender, and social inequality and the effects of poverty and racism on the educational opportunities and outcomes of minority groups in the United States.

allCourses.title: Culture, Diversity, and Educational Equity
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of and social theories about the origins and consequences of U.S. racial, gender, and social inequality and the effects of poverty and racism on the educational opportunities and outcomes of minority groups in the United States.

allCourses.title: Educational Equity and the Exceptional Learner
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Knowledge, skills, and strategies to teach exceptional learners in the general education classroom. Legislation pertaining to the education of exceptional learners. Role of general education teacher in the special education process. Inclusive curriculum to provide equal access to content.

allCourses.title: Educational Equity and the Exceptional Learner I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on knowledge, skills, and strategies needed to teach special populations in general education secondary classrooms. Covers categories and characteristics of disability and exceptionality, state and federal legislation, and the role of general education teachers in the special education process.

allCourses.title: Educational Equity and the Exceptional Learner II
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes the use of differentiated instruction to meet special needs and the creation of a positive, inclusive learning environment that provides access to the core curriculum for special needs students.

allCourses.title: Theories and Methods of English Language Development Applied to Secondary Students
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theories and methods of English language development and instruction of English language learners, with focus on secondary students. Includes language acquisition theory, language and content, assessment strategies, and preparation of curricula and instruction for grades 7–12 English language learners.

allCourses.title: Adolescent Development in Education
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Secondary teachers must understand adolescent physical, cognitive, emotional, and social development, particularly how educators can promote healthy adjustment in their students. Focuses on why and how changes occur in each of these areas as children grow older.

allCourses.title: Instructional Technology: Resources for the Single Subject Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Teacher Credential Program majors only.
allCourses.description: Issues and techniques in uses of computer based and media technologies in the single subject classroom: social implications and professional responsibilities; productivity tools to enhance student thinking skills; and strategies for instruction and management.

allCourses.title: Creating a Supportive & Healthy Environment for Student Learning in Secondary Classrooms
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Creation of healthy environments for student learning in secondary classrooms. Personal, family, school, community, environmental factors. Academic, physical, emotional, social well-being of students. Legal responsibilities of teachers related to student health, safety. Communication with family and use of community resources.

allCourses.title: Foundational Reading
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: To prepare Multiple Subject (MS) candidates to become competent, confident decision-makers who effectively monitor students' instructional progress and support all learners in grades K-8 in achieving reading proficiency, informed by assessment and data.

allCourses.title: Media and Information Literacy in the Secondary Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how teachers can help their students to become critical, ethical, and effective users of technological resources in the secondary classroom. Students learn tools for evaluating, selecting, and incorporating appropriate learning technologies into the secondary classroom.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary Social Science and Information Literacy
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Methods of instruction for Social Science at the K–6 level. Includes integration of the use of technology, development of content literacy, and use of evidence to construct arguments.

allCourses.title: The Adolescent Learner
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Issues of adolescent development and learning in family, school, and community contexts from biological, psychological, cognitive, and social perspectives. Focuses on how adolescents learn, what motivates them to learn, and how schools and teachers contribute to adolescents’ growth.

allCourses.title: Curriculum and Methods for Elementary Language Arts  and English Language Development
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Methods, instructional practices, and assessment strategies for teaching English-Language Arts, with a focus on instructional practices for supporting English Language Learners. Focuses on core language arts topics, including composition of persuasive, expository, and narrative texts; speaking; and listening.

allCourses.title: Methods for Integrating Visual and Performing Arts throughout Elementary School Curriculum
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Methods for using visual and performing arts content and processes across the curriculum with an emphasis on building literacy skills with English Language Learners (ELL). Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Instructional Design and Education Technology for the Elementary Classroom
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how teachers can effectively integrate educational technologies for teaching and learning in the elementary school classroom. Students learn tools for evaluating, selecting, and incorporating appropriate technologies into their classroom activities.

allCourses.title: Cognition and Learning in Educational Settings
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Education Majors only.
allCourses.description: Foundational concepts in cognition and development as applied to student learning. Primary topics include historical behaviorism, basic cognitive structure and processes, complex cognition, cognitive development, and motivation.

allCourses.title: Learning and Child Development
allCourses.restriction: Master of Arts in Teaching Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Issues of child development and learning in family, school, and community contexts from biological, psychological, cognitive, and social perspectives. Focuses on how young children learn and develop, how schools and teachers contribute to children’s growth, and implications for instruction.

allCourses.title: Special Topics
allCourses.restriction: Professional Administrative Services Credential students only.
allCourses.description: Meets induction and program planning requirements for students enrolled in Professional Administrative Services Credential.  Also serves as final course in program, wherein the candidate, the University instructor, and a representative of the involved school district assess and evaluate candidate competency.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.description: Limited to teaching assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Theories of Development and Learning Applied to Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an introductory examination of central theories of human development and learning in their application to contemporary educational settings.

allCourses.title: Origins, Purposes, and Central Issues in K-12 Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the role of education in U.S. society and to central issues in K–12 education. Education is studied from four different perspectives: social, historical, philosophical, and political.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism
allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of current issues in bilingual education and bilingualism. Topics include dimensions of bilingualism, the effects of bilingualism on children's linguistic and cognitive development, bilingual education programs, literacy, special needs, and assessment.

allCourses.title: Knowing and Learning in Mathematics and Science
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary study of knowing and learning in secondary school mathematics and science. Topics include standards for knowing, scientific epistemologies, mental representations, problem solving, expert-novice studies, assessment, and domain-specific thinking, learning, and teaching. Applied analysis of learning through clinical interviews.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHY SCI 5 or BIO SCI 14

prerequisite_list.title: California Teach 1: Introduction to Science and Mathematics Teaching
California Teach 1: Introduction to Science and Mathematics Teaching

prerequisite_for.title: Student Teaching Mathematics and Science in Middle/High School

allCourses.title: Interdisciplinary Topics in Education
allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of issues in education from interdisciplinary perspectives. Topics covered vary with interests of instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the fields of Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering, including possible careers in both traditional and new emerging areas. Background on both the Electrical Engineering and the Computer Engineering majors, curriculum requirements, specializations, and faculty research interests.

allCourses.title: Computational Methods in Electrical and Computer Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to computers and structured programming. Binary Data Representation. Hands-on experience with a high-level structured programming language. Introduction to algorithm efficiency. Applications of structured programming in solving engineering problems. Programming laboratory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB. AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3

prerequisite_for.title: Numerical Analysis in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

allCourses.title: Introduction to Machine Vision
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The use of digital computers for the analysis of visual scenes; image formation and sensing, color, segmentation, shape estimation, motion, stereo, pattern classification, computer architectures, applications. Computer experiments are used to illustrate fundamental principles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 150 or EECS 50

allCourses.title: System Software
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Multiprogramming, interrupt, processes, kernel, parallelism, critical sections, deadlocks, communication, multiprocessing, multilevel memory management, binding, name management, file systems, protection, resource allocation, scheduling. Experience with concurrent programming, synchronization mechanisms, interprocess communication.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 112 and (I&C SCI 46 or EECS 114)

allCourses.title: Organization of Digital Computers
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Building blocks and organization of digital computers, the arithmetic, control, and memory units, and input/out devices and interfaces. Microprogramming and microprocessors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 31L

allCourses.title: Organization of Digital Computers Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Specification and implementation of a processor-based system using a hardware description language such as VHDL. Hands-on experience with design tools including simulation, synthesis, and evaluation using testbenches.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 112

allCourses.title: Processor Hardware/Software Interfaces
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science and Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Hardware/software interfacing, including memory and bus interfaces, devices, I/O, and compiler code generation/instruction scheduling. Experience microcontroller programming and interfacing. Specific compiler code generation techniques including local variable and register allocations, instruction dependence and scheduling, and code optimization.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 112

allCourses.title: Engineering Data Structures and Algorithms
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces abstract behavior of classes data structures, alternative implementations, informal analysis of time and space efficiency. Also introduces classic algorithms and efficient algorithm design techniques (recursion, divide-and-conquer, branch-and-bound, dynamic programming).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 40

prerequisite_for.title: Data and Knowledge Science and Engineering

allCourses.title: Introduction to Data Management
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the design of databases and the use of database management systems (DBMS) for applications. Topics include entity-relationship modeling for design, relational data model, relational algebra, relational design theory, and Structured Query Language (SQL) programming.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 33 or EECS 114. I&C SCI 33 with a grade of C or better

prerequisite_for.title: Project in Databases and Web Applications

allCourses.title: Parallel Computer Systems
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: General introduction to parallel computing focusing on parallel algorithms and architectures. Parallel models: Flynn's taxonomy, dataflow models. Parallel architectures: systolic arrays, hypercube architecture, shared memory machines, dataflow machines, reconfigurable architectures. Parallel algorithms appropriate to each machine type area also discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 20 and EECS 114 and EECS 112

allCourses.title: Data and Knowledge Science and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction of basic concepts in artificial intelligence. Knowledge representation and reasoning, search, planning, declarative programing, problem solving, and data science.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 114

allCourses.title: VLSI
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design techniques for Very Large Scale Integrated (VLSI) systems and chips. Review CMOS and related process technologies; primitives such as logic gates and larger design blocks; layout; floor planning; design hierarchy, component interfaces; use of associated CAD tools for design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 112 and EECS 170B

allCourses.title: Introduction to Programming
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to computers and programming. Python programming syntax/style, types. Numbers and sequences. Control flow. I/O and errors/exceptions. Function calling, parameter passing, formal arguments, return values. Variable scoping. Programming laboratory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB. AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3

prerequisite_for.title: Introduction to Machine Learning for Engineers
Numerical Analysis in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Parallel Computing
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of parallel computing, focusing on parallel algorithms and architectures. Topics include design of parallel and I/O efficient algorithms, basics of parallel machine architectures, and current/emerging programming models (shared memory, distributed memory, and accelerators).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EECS 12 or COMPSCI 152) and EECS 114

allCourses.title: System Security
allCourses.description: Fundamentals and practices of system security. Topics include cryptographic (encryption, decryption, and message authentication), software vulnerabilities (buffer overflow), network security (layer 2-7 attacks and defenses and PKI), web security (XSS and XSRF), and privacy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 22 or I&C SCI 45C

prerequisite_list.title: Programming in C/C++ as a Second Language

allCourses.title: Introduction to Real-Time Distributed Programming
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering and Computer Science and Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the techniques for programming applications involving timing-sensitive actions. Hands-on experiences with object-oriented programming styles. Timing requirements, timing specification, response times, deadlines, application programming interfaces to real-time operating systems and middleware, remote procedure call, and distributed objects.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (COMPSCI 143A or EECS 111) and EECS 112.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning for Engineers
allCourses.description: Introduction to ML with a special focus on engineering applications. Starts with a mathematical background required for ML and covers various models for supervised learning (classification and regression) and unsupervised learning (clustering).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 55 and EECS 145 and EECS 12. Recommended: EECS 114.

allCourses.title: Computer Engineering Senior Design Project
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Computer Engineering majors only.
allCourses.description: Conception, planning, implementation, programming, testing of an approved project. Options include: parallel processing, VLSI design, microprocessor-based design, among others.

allCourses.title: Computer Engineering Senior Design Project
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Computer Engineering majors only.
allCourses.description: Conception, planning, implementation, programming, testing of an approved project. Options include: parallel processing, VLSI design, microprocessor-based design, among others. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 129A.

allCourses.title: Communication Systems I
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to analog communication systems including effects of noise. Modulation-demodulation for AM, DSB-SC, SSB, VSB, QAM, FM, PM, and PCM with application to radio, television, and telephony. Signal processing as applied to communication systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 55 and EECS 150

allCourses.title: Communication Systems II
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Signal space analysis. Optimum receivers for digital communication. Maximum a posteriori and maximum likelihood detection. Matched filter and correlation receiver.  PAM, QAM, PSK, FSK, and MSK and their performance. Introduction to equalization, synchronization, information theory, and error control codes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 141A

allCourses.title: Antenna Design for Wireless Communication Links
allCourses.description: Analysis and synthesis of antennas and antenna arrays.  Adaptive arrays and digital beam forming for advanced wireless links.  Friis transmission formula.  Wireless communication equations for cell-site and mobile antennas, interference, slow and fast fading in mobile communication.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 180A

allCourses.title: Electrical Engineering Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Vector calculus, complex functions, and linear algebra with applications to electrical engineering problems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 3D

prerequisite_for.title: Introduction to Machine Learning for Engineers

allCourses.title: Computer Networks
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Computer network architectures, protocols, and applications.  Internet congestion control, addressing, and routing. Local area networks. Multimedia networking.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 55 or STATS 67

prerequisite_list.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Computer Science

allCourses.title: Continuous-Time Signals and Systems
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Characteristics and properties of continuous-time (analog) signals and systems. Analysis of linear time-invariant continuous-time systems using differential equation convolutional models. Analysis of these systems using Laplace transforms, Fourier series, and Fourier transforms. Examples from applications to telecommunications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 70A and MATH 3D

allCourses.title: Digital Signal Processing
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Nature of sampled data, sampling theorem, difference equations, data holds, z-transform, w-transform, digital filters, Butterworth and Chebychev filters, quantization effects.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 50

prerequisite_for.title: Digital Signal Processing Design and Laboratory

allCourses.title: Digital Signal Processing Design and Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design and implementation of algorithms on a DSP processor and using computer simulation. Applications in signal and image processing, communications, radar, etc.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 152A

allCourses.title: Senior Design Project I
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Computer Science Engineering Majors only. Electrical Engineering Majors only. Computer Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Teaches problem definition, detailed design, integration, and testability with teams of students specifying, designing, building, and testing complex systems. Lectures include engineering values, discussions, and ethical ramifications of engineering decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 113 or EECS 170C or COMPSCI 145

allCourses.title: Senior Design Project II
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors only. Electrical Engineering Majors only. Computer Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Teaches problem definition, detailed design, integration, and testability with teams of students specifying, designing, building, and testing complex systems. Lectures include engineering values, discussions, and ethical ramifications of engineering decisions. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 159A

allCourses.title: Senior Design Project III
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, and Computer Science and Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment. EECS 159A-EECS 159B-EECS 159CW/CSE 181A-CSE 181B-CSE 181CW must be taken in the same academic year.
allCourses.description: Completion, documentation, and presentation of senior design projects. Teaches engineering documentation and presentation skills. Students write comprehensive project reports individually and participate in a presentation of project results.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (EECS 159A and EECS 159B) or (CSE 181A and CSE 181B). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Control Systems
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Modeling, stability, and specifications of feedback control systems. Root locus, Bode plots, Nyquist criteria, and state-space methods for dynamic analysis and design.

allCourses.title: Sampled-Data and Digital Control Systems
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sampled-data and digital control systems. Sampling process and theory of digital signals; z-transform and modeling; stability; z-plane, frequency response, state-space techniques of digital control system synthesis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 31 and EECS 160A and EECS 160LA.

allCourses.title: Control Systems I Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 160A. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Electric Machines and Drives
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Magnetic circuits and transformers. Fundamentals of energy conversion. Application to synchronous, induction, commutator, and special purpose machines. Electric Drives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 70B.

allCourses.title: Electric Machines and Drives Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory exercises supplementing the content of EECS 161.

allCourses.title: Power Systems
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Generation, transmission, and use of electrical energy. Fault calculation, protection, stability, and power flow.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 70B

allCourses.title: Power Systems Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors only. Electrical Engineering Majors only. Computer Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Experiments and field trips relevant to studies in power systems. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Industrial and Power Electronics
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Power switching devices, pulse width modulation (PWM) methods, switching converter topologies, control, and magnetics. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 170C and EECS 160A

prerequisite_for.title: Advanced Topics in Industrial and Power Electronics

allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Industrial and Power Electronics
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Practical design of switching converters, electromagnetic compatibility, thermal management, and/or control methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 166A.

allCourses.title: Electronics I
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The properties of semiconductors, electronic conduction in solids, the physics and operation principles of semiconductor devices such as diodes and transistors, transistor equivalent circuits, and transistor amplifiers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7D and EECS 70B

prerequisite_for.title: Fundamentals of Solid-State Electronics and Materials

allCourses.title: Electronics II
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design and analysis of single-stage amplifiers, biasing circuits, inverters, logic gates, and memory elements based on CMOS transistors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 70B and EECS 170A and EECS 170LA

allCourses.title: Electronics III
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of operation, design, and utilization of integrated circuit modules, including multi-stage amplifiers, operational amplifiers, and logic circuits.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 170B and EECS 170LB

allCourses.title: Integrated Electronic Circuit Design
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design and fabrication of modern digital integrated circuits. Fabrication of CMOS process, transistor-level design simulation, functional characteristics of basic digital integrated circuits, and different logic families including the static and dynamic logic, layout, and extraction of digital circuits.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 170C and EECS 170LC

allCourses.title: Analog and Communications IC Design
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in design of analog and communications integrated circuits. Topics include: implementation of passive components in integrated circuits; overview of frequency response of amplifiers, bandwidth estimation techniques, high-frequency amplifier design; design of radio-frequency oscillators.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 170C

allCourses.title: Electronics I Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 170A to perform experiments on semiconductor material properties, semiconductor device physics and operation principles, and transistor amplifiers to improve experimental skills and to enhance the understanding of lecture materials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7D and EECS 70B

allCourses.title: Electronics II Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 170B.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 170A and EECS 170LA

allCourses.title: Electronics III Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 170C to provide hands-on training in design of digital/analog circuits/subsystems. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 170B and EECS 170LB

allCourses.title: Semiconductor Devices
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Metal-semiconductor junctions, diodes, bipolar junction transistors, MOS structures, MOSFETs, CMOS technology, LEDs, and laser diodes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 170A

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Solid-State Electronics and Materials
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Physical properties of semiconductors and the roles materials play in device operation. Topics include: crystal structure, phonon vibrations, energy band, transport phenomenon, optical properties and quantum confinement effect essential to the understanding of electronic, optoelectronic and nanodevices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 170A

allCourses.title: Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS)
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Small-scale machines, small-scale phenomena, MEMS fabrication, MEMS CAD tools, MEMS devices and packaging, MEMS testing.

allCourses.title: Engineering Electromagnetics I
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, and electromagnetic fields: solutions to problems in engineering applications; transmission lines, Maxwell's equations and phasors, plane wave propagation, reflection, and transmission.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7E and EECS 145

prerequisite_for.title: Antenna Design for Wireless Communication Links
Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Analysis and Design

allCourses.title: Engineering Electromagnetics II
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Time-varying electromagnetic fields, plane waves, polarization, guidance of waves like rectangular waveguides and microstrips, optical fibers resonant cavities, skin effects and losses, spherical waves, radiation and reception of waves, antenna basics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 180A

allCourses.title: Engineering Electromagnetics III
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Propagation in anisotropic media. Propagation in ferrites and non-reciprocal devices. Scattering and dispersion. Electromagnetic properties of materials. Scattering of small nanoparticles. Spherical waves. Cross section of large and small objects. Radar equation. Coherent and incoherent radiation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 180B

allCourses.title: Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Analysis and Design
allCourses.restriction: Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design of microwave amplifiers including low-noise amplifiers, multiple stage amplifiers, power amplifiers, and introduction to broadband amplifiers. The goal is to provide the basic knowledge for the design of microwave amplifiers ranging from wireless system to radar system.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 180A

allCourses.title: Optical Electronics
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Photodiodes and optical detection, photometry and radiometry, geometric optics, lens theory, imaging system, EM wave propagation, optical waveguides and fibers, heterojunction structures, laser theory, semiconductor lasers, and optical transmission system.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 180A

allCourses.title: Electrical Engineering Senior Design Project I
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors only.
allCourses.description: Design projects for seniors in the Electrical Engineering program. Each project is supervised by a faculty member.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 150 and EECS 170C and EECS 180A.

allCourses.title: Electrical Engineering Senior Design Project II
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering majors only.
allCourses.description: Design projects for seniors in the Electrical Engineering program. Each project is supervised by a faculty member.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 189A.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Electrical and Computer Engineering
allCourses.description: Studies special topics in selected areas of Electrical and Computer Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Internship
allCourses.description: Students majoring in EECS may receive credit for an approved internship, working at  a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Group Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Group study of selected topics in Electrical and Computer Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking Individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: A test course
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Advisory restrictions test text.
allCourses.description: Test catalogue description. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 2A and PHYSICS 7A). MATH 2A with a grade of B or better. PHYSICS 7A with a grade of C+ or better. Advisory prereq text.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.
allCourses.corequisite: I&C SCI 192 and M&MG 298 and Advisory coreq text.

allCourses.title: Computer Systems and C Programming
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to computing systems. Data representation and operations. Simple logic design. Basic computer organization. Instruction set architecture and assembly language programming. Introduction to C. Functions and recursion, data structures, pointers. Programming laboratory.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 12

allCourses.title: Principles of Imaging
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Linear systems, probability and random processes, image processing, projecting imaging, tomographic imaging.

allCourses.title: Techniques in Medical Imaging I: X-ray, Nuclear, and NMR Imaging
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Ionizing radiation, planar and tomographic radiographic and nuclear imaging, magnetism, NMR, MRI imaging.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 202A

allCourses.title: Techniques in Medical Imaging: X-ray, Nuclear, and NMR Imaging
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Ionizing radiation, planar and tomographic radiographic and nuclear imaging, magnetism, NMR, MRI imaging.

allCourses.title: Techniques in Medical Imaging II: Ultrasound, Electrophysiological, Optical
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Sound and ultrasound, ultrasonic imaging, physiological electromagnetism, EEG, MEG, ECG, MCG, optical properties of tissues, fluorescence and bioluminescence, MR impedance imaging, MR spectroscopy, electron spin resonance and ESR imaging.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 202B

allCourses.title: Techniques in Medical Imaging: X-ray, Nuclear, and NMR Imaging
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Ionizing radiation, planar and tomographic radiographic and nuclear imaging, magnetism, NMR, MRI imaging.

allCourses.title: Digital Image Processing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Pixel-level digital image representation and elementary operations; Fourier and other unitary transforms; compression, enhancement, filtering, and restoration; laboratory experience is provided.

allCourses.title: Digital Image Processing
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Pixel-level digital image representation and elementary operations; Fourier and other unitary transforms; compression, enhancement, filtering, and restoration; laboratory experience is provided.

allCourses.title: Personalized Medical Devices
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to fundamental aspects of medical devices and discusses therapeutic as well as diagnostic devices. Basic aspects of microfluidics and biology critical to personalized medical systems are studied. Typical FDA approval pathways for medical devices are presented.

allCourses.title: Modeling and Rendering for Image Synthesis
allCourses.description: Provides the fundamental understanding of mathematical and physical models used in image synthesis applications: geometric models, physics of color image formation, polygon approximations, ray tracing, and radiosity.

allCourses.title: Advanced System Software
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of operating systems including interprocess communication, scheduling, resource management, concurrency, reliability, validation, protection and security, and distributed computing support. System software design languages and modeling analysis.

allCourses.title: Advanced System Software
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of operating systems including interprocess communication, scheduling, resource management, concurrency, reliability, validation, protection and security, and distributed computing support. System software design languages and modeling analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of system software (e.g. EECS 111) and organization of digital computers (e.g. UCI EECS 112).

allCourses.title: Computer Architecture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Problems in hardware, firmware (microprogram), and software. Computer architecture for resource sharing, real-time applications, parallelism, microprogramming, and fault tolerance. Various architectures based on cost/performance and current technology.

allCourses.title: Computer Architecture
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Problems in hardware, firmware (microprogram), and software. Computer architecture for resource sharing, real-time applications, parallelism, microprogramming, and fault tolerance. Various architectures based on cost/performance and current technology.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of organization of digital computers (e.g. EECS 112 and EECS 112L).

allCourses.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
allCourses.description: Computer algorithms from a practical standpoint.  Algorithms for symbolic and numeric problems such as sorting, searching, graphs, and network flow.  Analysis includes algorithm time and space complexity.

allCourses.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Computer algorithms from a practical standpoint. Algorithms for symbolic and numeric problems such as sorting, searching, graphs, and network flow. Analysis includes algorithm time and space complexity.

allCourses.title: Advanced Application of Algorithms
allCourses.description: Medium-sized group and individual programming project. Topics include specification requirements documentation, practical implementation of algorithms, and testing/verification of design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Undergraduate course work in engineering data structures and algorithms.

allCourses.title: VLSI System Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of integrated fabrication, circuit simulation, basic device physics, device layout, timing; MOS logic design; layout generation, module generation, techniques for very large scale integrated circuit design.

allCourses.title: VLSI System Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of integrated fabrication, circuit simulation, basic device physics, device layout, timing; MOS logic design; layout generation, module generation, techniques for very large scale integrated circuit design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of organization of digital computers (e.g. EECS 112).

allCourses.title: Distributed Computer Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design and analysis techniques for decentralized computer architectures, communication protocols, and hardware-software interface. Performance and reliability considerations. Design tools.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 211 and EECS 213.

allCourses.title: Distributed Software Architecture and Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Practical issues for reducing the software complexity,  lowering cost, and designing and implementing distributed  software applications. Topics include the distributed object  model distributed environment, platform-independent software  agents and components, the middleware architecture for  distributed real-time and secure services.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 211

allCourses.title: Advanced C Programming
allCourses.restriction: Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: C language programming concepts. Control flow, function calls, recursion. Basic and composite data types, static and dynamic data structures. Program modules and compilation units. Preprocessor macros. C standard libraries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 10 or EECS 20
