allCourses.title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing Architecture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study the latest DSP architectures for applications in communication (wired and wireless) and multimedia processing. Emphasis given to understanding the current design techniques and to evaluate the performance, power, and application domain of the latest DSP processors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 213

allCourses.title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing Architecture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Study the latest DSP architectures for applications in communication (wired and wireless) and multimedia processing. Emphasis given to understanding the current design techniques and to evaluate the performance, power, and application domain of the latest DSP processors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 213P. EECS 213P with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Topics in Computer Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: New research results in computer engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Embedded System Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Computational models for embedded systems. System-level specification and description languages. Concepts, requirements, examples. Embedded system models at different levels of abstraction. Modeling of test benches, design under test, IP components. Discrete event simulation, semantics, and algorithms. Formerly EECS 222A.

allCourses.title: Real-Time Computer Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Time bases, clock synchronization, real-time communication protocols, specification of requirements, task scheduling. Validation of timelines, real-time configuration management.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 211 and EECS 213. EECS 211 with a grade of B- or better. EECS 213 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Real-Time Computer Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Time bases, clock synchronization, real-time communication protocols, specification of requirements, task scheduling. Validation of timelines, real-time configuration management.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 211P and EECS 213P. EECS 211P with a grade of B- or better. EECS 213P with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: High-Performance Computing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of high-performance computing, covering both theory and practice. Topics include performance analysis and tuning, design of parallel and I/O efficient algorithms, basics of parallel machine architectures, and current/emerging programming models (shared memory, distributed memory, and accelerators).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 215 or COMPSCI 260. EECS 215 with a grade of B- or better. COMPSCI 260 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Embedded Systems Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Embedded systems design flow and methodology. Design space exploration. Co-design of hardware and software, embedded architecture and network exploration and synthesis. System software/hardware interface generation. Real-time constraints, specification-to-architecture mapping, design tools and methodologies. Formerly EECS 222B.

allCourses.title: Embedded System Software
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Embedded system software concepts, requirements, examples, for engineering applications such as multi-media and automotive. Software generation methodology. Algorithmic specification, design constraints. Embedded operating systems. Static, dynamic, real-time scheduling. Input/output, interrupt handling. Code generation, compilation, instruction set simulation. Formerly EECS 222C.

allCourses.title: Cyber-Physical System Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Model-based design of cyber-physical systems including, e.g., plant, sensing, control, actuation, embedded hardware/software, communication, real-time analysis, various levels of simulation (MILS, SILS, HILS), tools and methodologies for automatic synthesis, and application from various interdisciplinary domains.

allCourses.title: Program Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advance study of programming languages, compliers, and interpreters. Static and dynamic program analysis and its use in compilation, optimization, garbage collection, bug finding, and parallelization.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 215 or COMPSCI 260

allCourses.title: Low Power SoC Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: From an inverter to server centers, low-power design theory and practice in modern systems-on-chip (SoC), energy efficient design time and runtime methods are surveyed at circuit, RTL, and architecture levels. Lab assignments will help students quantify tradeoffs and design practices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 217

allCourses.title: Software Engineering Project in C Language
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Hands-on experience with the ANSI-C programming language. Medium-sized programming projects, team work. Software specification, documentation, implementation, testing. Definition of data structures and application programming interface. Creation of program modules, linking with external libraries. Rule-based compilation, version control.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 22

allCourses.title: Energy Efficiency
allCourses.description: Green energy sources for production, transmission, storage, and utilization of electricity, with a special focus on solar, wind, and nuclear energy production. Study of newly developed renewable sources of energy including capital cost, product cost, environmental issues, and technical feasibility.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts in programming and machine learning. The goal is to provide an accessible introduction to the field of machine learning and related techniques for students with a wide variety of engineering degrees.

allCourses.title: Advanced System Security
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced study about system security. Topics include software vulnerabilities (buffer overflow), vulnerability discovery (fuzzing),  network security, side-channel analysis (power analysis and micro-architecture attacks), machine-learning security, IoT security, and privacy (differential privacy).

allCourses.title: Data Privacy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents data privacy in the digital age from multiple perspectives, including theoretical frameworks for privacy; tracking practices and privacy-enhancing technologies in various application domains; and data protection laws and policy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Students should have familiarity with networking (web/HTTP, DNS, mobile devices) (EECS 148 or equivalent), probability (EECS 55 or equivalent), and programming in python (EECS 12 or equivalent) at the undergraduate level.

allCourses.title: Random Processes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Extensions of probability theory to random variables varying with time. General properties of stochastic processes. Convergence. Estimation, including nonlinear and linear minimum mean square error and maximum likelihood. Spectral density and linear filters. Poisson processes and discrete-time Markov chains.

allCourses.title: Random Processes
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Extensions of probability theory to random variables varying with time. General properties of stochastic processes. Convergence. Estimation, including nonlinear and linear minimum mean square error and maximum likelihood. Spectral density and linear filters. Poisson processes and discrete-time Markov chains.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Knowledge of engineering probability (e.g. EECS 55).

allCourses.title: Digital Communications I
allCourses.description: Concepts and applications of digital communication systems. Baseband digital transmission of binary, multiamplitude, and multidimensional signals.  Introduction to and performance analysis of different modulation schemes.

allCourses.title: Digital Communications I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concepts and applications of digital communication systems. Baseband digital transmission of binary, multiamplitude, and multidimensional signals. Introduction to and performance analysis of different modulation schemes.

allCourses.title: Digital Communications II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concepts and applications of equalization, multi-carrier modulation, spread spectrum and CDMA. Digital communications through fading memory channels.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 241A. EECS 241A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Digital Communications II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Concepts and applications of equalization, multi-carrier modulation, spread spectrum, and CDMA. Digital communications through fading memory channels.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 241AP. EECS 241AP with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Information Theory
allCourses.description: Fundamental capabilities and limitations of information sources and information transmission systems. Analytical framework for modeling and evaluating communication systems: entropy, mutual information asymptotic equipartition property, entropy rates of a stochastic process, data compression, channel capacity, differential entropy, the Gaussian channel.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 240. EECS 240 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Error Correcting Codes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Different techniques for error correcting codes and analyzing their performance. Linear block codes; cyclic codes; convolutional codes. Minimum distance; optimal decoding; Viterbi decoding; bit error probability. Coding gain; trellis coded modulation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 240. EECS 240 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Wireless Communications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to wireless communications systems. Wireless channel modeling. Single carries, spread spectrum, and multi-carrier wireless modulation schemes. Diversity techniques.  Multiple-access schemes. Transceiver design and system level tradeoffs. Brief overview of GSM, CDMA, (IS-95) and 2.5, 3G cellular schemes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 241B. EECS 241B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Wireless Communications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to wireless communications systems. Wireless channel modeling. Single carries, spread spectrum, and multi-carrier wireless modulation schemes. Diversity techniques. Multiple-access schemes. Transceiver design and system level tradeoffs. Brief overview of GSM, CDMA, (IS-95) and 2.5, 3G cellular schemes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 241BP. EECS 241BP with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Space-Time Coding
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A fundamental study of: Capacity of MIMO Channels, space-time code design criteria, space-time block codes, space-time trellis codes, differential detection for multiple antennas, spatial multiplexing, BLAST.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 242

allCourses.title: Network Coding: Theory and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical frameworks for network coding: linear, algebraic and random network coding; linear programming and combinatorial frameworks. Network code design. Benefits and costs. Practical network coding. Applications to wireless networks, content distribution, security, and other areas.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 248A or NET SYS 201 or COMPSCI 232

allCourses.title: Information Storage
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Storage architecture, storage network and networking algorithms in data centers, principle of storage devices and non-volatile memory, data consistency, data availability and integrity, power management.

allCourses.title: Computer and Communication Networks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

allCourses.title: Digital Signal Processing I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles of digital signal processing, sampling, decimation and interpolation, discrete Fourier transforms and FFT algorithms, transversal and recursive filters, discrete random processes, and finite-word effects in digital filters.

allCourses.title: Digital Signal Processing I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles of digital signal processing, sampling, decimation and interpolation, discrete Fourier transforms and FFT algorithms, transversal and recursive filters, discrete random processes, and finite-word effects in digital filters.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Knowledge of digital signal processing (e.g. EECS 152A).

allCourses.title: Detection, Estimation, and Demodulation Theory
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of hypothesis testing and Bayes and Maximum Likelihood Estimation.  ARMA and state variable models for random time series analysis.  Wiener and Kalman filtering and prediction.  Adaptive algorithms for identification and tracking of parameters of time-varying models.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 240. EECS 240 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Detection, Estimation, and Demodulation Theory
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of hypothesis testing and Bayes and Maximum Likelihood Estimation.  ARMA and state variable models for random time series analysis.  Wiener and Kalman filtering and prediction.  Adaptive algorithms for identification and tracking of parameters of time-varying models.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 240. EECS 240 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Machine Learning for Signal Processing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Machine learning and computational neuroscience methods for signal processing. Theory and applications are described, as well as practical programming methods in Python using  Keras and TensorFlow 2.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: EECS 125 or equivalent undergraduate-level introduction to machine learning and EECS 152A or equivalent undergraduate course in digital signal processing. Knowledge of introductory linear algebra and differential equations, elementary probability theory, and elementary Python programming.

allCourses.title: Theory of Machine Learning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The math background underlying machine learning algorithms and structures, including backpropagation, radial basis functions, deep belief nets, support vector machines, and dynamic programming. The relation of learning algorithms to estimation, recursive filtering, dimensionality reduction, and sequential optimization.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: EECS 125 or equivalent undergraduate-level introduction to machine learning. Knowledge of introductory linear algebra and differential equations, elementary probability theory, and elementary Matlab programming.

allCourses.title: Linear Systems I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: State-space representation of continuous-time and discrete-time linear systems. Controllability, observability, stability. Realization of rational transfer functions.

allCourses.title: Linear Optimization Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Formulation, solution, and analysis of linear programming and linear network flow problems. Simplex methods, dual ascent methods, interior point algorithms, and auction algorithms. Duality theory and sensitivity analysis. Shortest path, max-flow, assignment, and minimum cost flow problems.

allCourses.title: Industrial and Power Electronics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Power switching devices, pulse width modulation (PWM) methods, switching converter topologies, control, and magnetics. Materials fee.

prerequisite_for.title: Topics in Industrial and Power Electronics

allCourses.title: Topics in Industrial and Power Electronics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Practical design of switching converters, electromagnetic compatibility, thermal management, and/or control methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 267A. EECS 267A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic transistor configurations; differential pairs; active load/current sources; supply/temperature-independent biasing; op-amp gain and output stages; amplifier frequency response and stability compensation; nonidealities in op-amps; noise and dynamic range in analog circuits.

prerequisite_for.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design II
Design of Integrated Circuits for Broadband Applications

allCourses.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic transistor configurations; differential pairs; active load/current sources; supply/temperature-independent biasing; op-amp gain and output stages; amplifier frequency response and stability compensation; nonidealities in op-amps; noise and dynamic range in analog circuits.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Introductory knowledge of control systems (e.g. EECS 160A) and electronics (e.g. EECS 170C).

allCourses.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced transistor modeling issues; discrete-time and continuous-time analog Integrated Circuit (IC) filters; phase-locked loops; design of ICs operating at radio frequencies; low-voltage/low-power design techniques; A/D and D/A converters; AGC circuits.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 270A. EECS 270A with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I

allCourses.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced transistor modeling issues; discrete-time and continuous-time analog Integrated Circuit (IC) filters; phase-locked loops; design of ICs operating at radio frequencies; low-voltage/low-power design techniques; A/D and D/A converters; AGC circuits.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 270AP. EECS 270AP with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Design of Integrated Circuits for Broadband Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics include: broadband standards and protocols; high-frequency circuit design techniques; PLL theory and design; design of transceivers; electrical/optical interfaces.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 270A. EECS 270A with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I

allCourses.title: Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuits and Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental topics in radio-frequency (RF) integrated circuits and systems including basic concepts in RF circuits and systems, RF receiver and transmitter architectures, and RF core building blocks such as low-noise amplifiers (LNAs), RF mixers, and power amplifiers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 270A. EECS 270A with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I

allCourses.title: Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuit Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics include RF component modeling; matching network design; transmission line theory/modeling; Smith chart and S-parameters; noise modeling of active and passive components; high-frequency amplifier design; low-noise amplifier (LNA) design; mixer design; RF power amplifier.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 270AP

allCourses.title: MM-Wave and Terahertz Circuits
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of the new methodologies, circuits, and systems developed at mm-wave and terahertz frequency ranges due to the growing interest in high speed communication and high frequency signal generation.

allCourses.title: Topics in Electrical Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: New research results in electronic system design.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuit Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics include RF component modeling; matching network design; transmission line theory/modeling; Smith chart and S-parameters; noise modeling of active and passive components; high-frequency amplifier design; low-noise amplifier (LNA) design; mixer design; RF power amplifier.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 270AP. EECS 270AP with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Electronics Packaging
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Materials, processes, techniques, and principles in interconnect and packaging of electronic products after the device-containing semiconductor wafer is fabricated. The electronic, optical, thermal, mechanical, and reliability properties of the materials are evaluated in the context of modern electronics manufacturing processes.

allCourses.title: Biomedical Microdevices (MEMOS)
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Construction of biomedical microdevices, lithographic patterning and etching of microdevices, sealing and connecting microdevices, molding of microdevices, testing of microdevices.

allCourses.title: Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Project
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students create VLSI design projects from conception through architecture, floor planning, detailed design, simulation, verification, and submission for project fabrication.  Emphasis on practical experience in robust VLSI design techniques. (Successful students are expected to take EECS 275B.).

allCourses.title: Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Project Testing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Test and document student-created Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) projects designed in EECS 275A. Emphasis on practical laboratory experience in VLSI testing techniques. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 275A

allCourses.title: Advanced Semiconductor Devices I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (CMOSFET), device scaling, device modeling and fabrication, equivalent circuits, and their applications for digital, analog, RF.

allCourses.title: Advanced Semiconductor Devices II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Metal-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MESFET), heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT), microwave semiconductor devices, equivalent circuits, device modeling and fabrication, microwave amplifiers, transmitters, and receivers.

allCourses.title: Nanotechnology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fabrication and characterization techniques of electrical circuit elements at the nanometer scale. Quantized conductance, semiconductor quantum dots, single electron transistors, molecular wires, carbon nanotubes, self-assembly of nano-circuit elements, quantum methods of information processing.

allCourses.title: Micro-System Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

allCourses.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale.  Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

allCourses.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.

allCourses.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Knowledge of engineering electromagnetics (e.g. EECS 180A)

allCourses.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Two- and three-dimensional boundary value problems, dielectric waveguides and other special waveguides, microwave networks and antenna arrays, electromagnetic properties of materials, and electromagnetic optics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 280A. EECS 280A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Knowledge of engineering electromagnetics (e.g. EECS 180A).

allCourses.title: Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Analysis and Design II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design of microwave amplifiers using computer-aided design tools. Covers low-noise amplifiers, multiple stage amplifiers, broadband amplifiers, and power amplifiers. Hybrid circuit design techniques including filters and baluns. Theory and design rules for microwave oscillator design.

allCourses.title: Wireless Communication Links and Antenna Design
allCourses.description: Provides the fundamental understanding of the electromagnetic part of wireless communication links and their antennas, i.e., their key components. Contains hands-on component where students learn how to use the best CADs used in industry and academia.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: EECS 180A

allCourses.title: RF Antenna Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced transmission line design, radiation of electromagnetic waves, dipole antennas, antenna arrays, advanced antenna designs, and practical design considerations in communications systems. Course is supplemented by RF design tools and modeling.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 280AP. EECS 280AP with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Optical Communications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.

allCourses.title: Optical Communications
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate-level Engineering Electromagnetics I (e.g. EECS E80A).

allCourses.title: Lasers and Photonics
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of lasers and applications, including Gaussian beam propagation, interaction of optical radiation with matters, and concepts of optical gain and feedback. Applications are drawn from diverse fields of optical communication, signal processing, and material diagnosis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate course work in electromagnetic theory and atomic physics.

allCourses.title: Nano Imaging
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theory and practice of modern nanoscale imaging techniques and applications. Traces the development of microscopy from ancient times to modern day techniques used for visualizing the nano-world from atoms to molecules including hands-on experience in the laboratory.

allCourses.title: Optical Communications
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate-level Engineering Electromagnetics I (e.g. EECS E80A).

allCourses.title: Fabrication of Biomedical and Wearable Microdevices
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers preliminary details on prototyping and fabrication techniques for biomedical and wearable microdevices. Fabrication and behavior of modern biomed device materials such as hydrogel, PDMS, biopolymer, smart materials, and their uses are introduced.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Knowledge of undergraduate-level basic physics.

allCourses.title: Micro/Nano Biotechnology and Biosensing: Fundamentals, Designs, and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides insight into the current topics in Micro/Nanoscience, Micro/Nanotechnology fundamentals, and their modern-day applications in life sciences. Focus is on Micro/Nanodevices; Sensors’ fundamentals; NanoBioSensors; Microfluidics; Micro/Nanofabrication, detection system-level characterization; performance determination; solid-state materials; and more.

allCourses.title: Bioinstrumentation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces instrumentation used in biomedical research, clinical medicine, and health monitoring. Interfacing of bioelectronics and biomedical sensing are taught with the most updated methods. The integration of bioinstrumentation with data science and cloud computing are introduced.

allCourses.title: Curricular Practical Training
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Curricular practical training. Students will go through practical training under an industry mentor in a technical field corresponding to their concentration area.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Preparation for M.S. Comprehensive Examination
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual reading and preparation for the M.S. comprehensive examination.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Preparation for Ph.D. Preliminary Examination
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual reading and preparation for the Ph.D. preliminary examination.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Colloquium
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Invited speakers discuss their latest research results in electrical engineering and computer science.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Seminars in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Scheduled each year by individual faculty in major field of interest.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Electrical Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Master of Science Thesis Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the thesis required for the M.S. degree in Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparing and completing the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree in Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of Electrical and Computer Engineering concepts.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Individual Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Digital Systems
allCourses.restriction: Computer Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Electrical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Digital representation of information. Specification, analysis, design and optimization or combinational and sequential logic, register-transfer components and register-transfer systems with datapaths and controllers. Introduction to high-level and algorithmic state-machines and custom processors.

allCourses.title: Individual Study for Honors Students
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Program students only.
allCourses.description: Independent reading, research, or design under the direction of faculty in Electrical and Computer Engineering. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Case Studies in Environmental Toxicology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores toxicology principles through case-based discussions. Topics include exposure routes, absorption, metabolism, and mechanisms of toxicity. Lectures with discussions are delivered by invited faculty experts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EHS 206B. EHS 206B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Principles of Environmental Toxicology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores molecular, biological, and structure-based toxicity of environmental toxicants. Topics include dose-response relationship, ADME, mechanisms of action, and its impact on the environment, wildlife, and human health. Covered through lectures, research papers, and discussion.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Occupational Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The importance of work environment for workers’ health and productivity has increased with changing technology, work organization, demographics, and occupation/industry structures. This advanced occupational epidemiology course focuses on work environment as exposures, and workers’ health and productivity as outcomes.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Neurotoxicology
allCourses.description: The effects of various harmful chemicals upon nervous system function. Emphasis given to the molecular events underlying neurological damage and to the relation of such processes to basic mechanisms of neurobiology.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Target Organ Toxicology I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Outlines vulnerability of selected organ systems to environmental and occupational chemicals. Reviews molecular aspects of toxicological damage. Topics include molecular toxicology and the following organ systems: nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, dermal, and skeletal embryology.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Target Organ Toxicology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes mechanistic responses in animals and humans to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation, focusing on organ system physiology. Topics specifically covered include reproductive, endocrine, developmental, kidney, liver, pancreas, vascular, immune toxicology, radiation, and chemical carcinogenesis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 277A or EHS 206A. PUBHLTH 277A with a grade of B- or better. EHS 206A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Experimental Design and Interpretation of Toxicology Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to methods of structuring toxicology experiments and analyzing data, including experimental design, data distributions, sample sizes, hypothesis testing, linear regression, analysis of variance, multiple comparison testing, and non-parametric tests.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Inhalation Toxicology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores laboratory inhalation toxicology principles and practices. Covers aerosols, gases, respiratory tract structure/function, lung defenses, exposure techniques, experimental designs, animal models, and regulations/guidelines.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Industrial Toxicology
allCourses.description: Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 277B or EHS 206B. PUBHLTH 277B with a grade of B- or better. EHS 206B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environ Health Sci and Policy Majors only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. Studies human-environment interaction, focusing on chemical, physical, and biological agents in community and occupational settings. Covers climate change, environmental justice, children’s health, exposure assessment, and policy for public health improvement.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
allCourses.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Learn general principles and basic mathematical methods for environmental modeling and human health risk assessment, including compartmental and advection-dispersion models for contaminants in air and water, uptake by plants and animals, exposure, assessment, dose-response modeling, risk management, and risk perception.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2A and STATS 7

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Independent Study in Environmental Toxicology
allCourses.description: With consent from a faculty member who will supervise the program, a student may receive credit for individual study in some area of toxicology, culminating in the completion of a scholarly paper on the subject.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focus on theory and research in health psychology as applied to major acute, chronic, and occupational health problems. Adopting the biopsychosocial model of health, emphasis is on understanding and influencing how biology, behavior, and the environment influence health and illness.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Occupational Toxicology
allCourses.description: Discussions with clinical and research faculty in environmental toxicology and occupational medicine on current toxicology problems in the workplace and critical review of current publications in the field.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Seminar in Environmental Health Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presentation and discussion of current research problems and issues by students, postdoctoral fellows, faculty, and guests, covering the broad research and policy areas of environmental health sciences.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Research Problems
allCourses.description: Research work for the M.S. thesis or Ph.D. dissertation.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in English and American Literature
allCourses.description: Explores the diversity of human expression manifested in selected works of literature. By engaging with substantial literary texts, students will think critically about how meaning is created and how experience is interpreted in literary language.

allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Principles and significance of the practice of legal sanctuary in medieval English history, literature, and religion. Development of modern use of churches and other safe spaces in the American Civil Rights movement, immigrant sanctuary movements, and international asylum.

allCourses.title: What is a Person?
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Contemporary debates about personhood in law, culture, and society. Beginning with the emergence of ideas of personhood in philosophy and theology, and culminating in the study of highly contested cases: slavery, abortion law, animal rights, corporate personhood, and artificial intelligence.

allCourses.title: What is a University?
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: The history and present of the modern university, with special attention to the history of the UC system. Problems of social justice, racial equality, class mobility in the university as well as student life and universities in popular culture.

allCourses.title: Freshman Seminar In Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Freshmen only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the engineering profession. Weekly seminars by both faculty and representatives from industry present an overview of each engineering discipline. Students learn about current trends and issues in engineering, and career and academic options.

allCourses.title: Computational Methods in Engineering
allCourses.description: Procedures and procedure followers, algorithms and flow charts, computer languages, subprograms. Computer macro- and microelements, number systems. Methods of differentiation, integration, curve fitting, list processing. Error analysis. Must qualify in BASIC and FORTRAN at end of course through computer use.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisite or corequisite: MATH 2A.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Fabrication Safety
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Hands on training in the safe use of item fabrication: metalworking, woodworking, electronics fabrication, composites, welding, adhesives, water disposal, and others. Safety certification will be granted from this course and is required for access to Engineering School fabrication facilities.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Developing Teaching Excellence

allCourses.restriction: Freshmen only.

allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Superconductors to biodegradable polymers. Structure and properties of materials, including metal, ceramics, polymers, semiconductors, composites, traditional materials. Atomic structure, bonding, defects, phase equilibria, mechanical properties, electrical, optical and magnetic properties. Introduction to materials processing and synthesis. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A or CHEM H2A) and PHYSICS 7C

Electronic and Optical Properties in Materials

allCourses.description: Inspection of power-generating stations of various types, oil and gas processing facilities, and end-use facilities.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.description: Introduction to engineering disciplines and the design process. Students enrolled in the online lecture also attend a three-hour lab on campus. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Engineering II
allCourses.restriction: Lower-division students only. School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to engineering disciplines and the design process. Students enrolled in the online lecture also attend a three-hour lab on campus. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 7A

allCourses.title: Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D and PHYSICS 7C

allCourses.title: Engineering and Computer Educational Laboratory
allCourses.description: Comprehensive academic support designed primarily for underrepresented or underprepared students in Engineering, ICS, or selected areas of the physical sciences. Typical program activities: tutoring, study skills, career planning, self-esteem enhancement, library research techniques.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: Public and Professional Service in Engineering
allCourses.description: Student participation in public and professional service activities related to engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Group Study
allCourses.description: Group study of selected topics in engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Modeling and analysis of engineering problems under uncertainty. Engineering applications of probability and statistical concepts and methods.

allCourses.title: Methods III:  Modeling, Economics, and Management
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis, modeling, and management of civil engineering systems. Statistics and system performance studies, probabilistic models and simulation, basic economics and capital investments, project elements and organization, managerial concepts and network technique, project scheduling. Emphasis on real-world examples. Laboratory sessions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 11

prerequisite_for.title: Transportation Systems III: Planning and Forecasting

allCourses.title: Methods IV: Systems Analysis and Decision-Making
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis and optimization for decision-making in civil and infrastructural systems. Topics include linear programming formulations and solution algorithms, network models, and logistical models. Emphasis is on project-level and managerial decision-making and selection from alternative designs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N) and MATH 3D

allCourses.title: GIS for Civil and Environmental Engineering
allCourses.description: GIS for CEE provides an introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and their various applications in civil and environmental engineering. Topics include GIS data formats, data queries, spatial and attribute data, spatial data analysis, coordinate systems, and raster data analysis.

allCourses.title: Transportation Systems I: Analysis and Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to analysis and design of fundamental transportation system components, basic elements of geometric and pavement design, vehicle flow and elementary traffic, basic foundations of transportation planning and forecasting. Laboratory sessions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 11 and ENGRCEE 81A

prerequisite_for.title: Transportation Systems II: Operations and Control
Transportation Systems III: Planning and Forecasting
Transportation Systems IV: Freeway Operations and Control

allCourses.title: Transportation Systems II: Operations and Control
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of urban traffic engineering, including data collection, analysis, and design. Traffic engineering studies, traffic flow theory, traffic control devices, traffic signals, capacity and level of service analysis of freeways and urban streets. Laboratory sessions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 11 and ENGRCEE 121

prerequisite_list.title: Transportation Systems I: Analysis and Design

allCourses.title: Transportation Systems III: Planning and Forecasting
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical foundations of transportation planning, design, and analysis methods. Theory and application of aggregate and disaggregate models for land use development, trip generation, destination, mode, and route choice. Transportation network analysis. Planning, design, and evaluation of system alternatives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 121

prerequisite_list.title: Methods III:  Modeling, Economics, and Management
Transportation Systems I: Analysis and Design

allCourses.title: Transportation Systems IV: Freeway Operations and Control
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of traffic on urban freeways, including data collection analysis, and design. Traffic engineering studies, traffic flow theory, freeway traffic control devices, capacity, and level of service analysis of freeways and highways. Laboratory sessions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 121

prerequisite_list.title: Transportation Systems I: Analysis and Design

allCourses.title: Transportation and the Environment
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of the impacts of motor vehicle transportation on the environment. Introduction to life cycle analysis applied to transportation. Basic economic tools for transportation externalities. Transportation planning, urban form, health, and the environment. Transportation sustainability.

allCourses.title: Soil Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Mechanics of soils, composition and classification of soils, compaction, compressibility and consolidation, shear strength, seepage, bearing capacity, lateral earth pressure, retaining walls, piles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 150 and ENGRCEE 170

allCourses.title: Soil Mechanics Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory procedures of soil testing for engineering problems.  Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Earthquake Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Nature of earthquakes, hazard analyses, structural dynamics for earthquake engineering, seismic design force determination methods: ELF, modal response spectrum, nonlinear time history analyses. Diaphragm analyses, redundancy, nonlinear response, ductile systems, hysteretic behavior. Basics of seismic design for steel, timber, concrete.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 11 and (ENGRCEE 20 or BME 60B) and ENGRCEE 151A

allCourses.title: Mechanics of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Stresses and strains, strain-stress diagrams, axial deformations, torsion, bending and shear stresses in beams, shear force and bending moment diagrams, combined stresses, principal stresses, Mohr's circle, deflection of beams, columns.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 30 or ENGRMAE 30 or ENGR 30. ENGRCEE 30 with a grade of C- or better. ENGRMAE 30 with a grade of C- or better. ENGR 30 with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Mechanics of Materials Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Experimental methods and fundamentals for mechanics of materials analysis.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ENGRCEE 30 or ENGRMAE 30 or ENGR 30) and ENGRCEE 150. ENGRCEE 30 with a grade of C- or better. ENGRMAE 30 with a grade of C- or better. ENGR 30 with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Structural Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of structural analysis and loading. Deformation of statically determinate and indeterminate structures. Influence lines. Structural systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 150 or ENGRMAE 150

allCourses.title: Structural Timber Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design of timber structures. Beams, columns, beam-columns, roof, and connections.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 151A

allCourses.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Ultimate strength design. Design of reinforced concrete beam sections. Design for shear and deflection. Design of columns. Design of isolated and combined footings. Laboratory sessions.   Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 151A

prerequisite_for.title: Computer Methods in Structural Analysis and Design

allCourses.title: Computer Methods in Structural Analysis and Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Matrix techniques for indeterminate framed structures. Computer implementation using the stiffness method. Software packages for design of reinforced concrete, steel, and/or timber structures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 151C

allCourses.title: Statically Indeterminate Structures
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of statically indeterminate structures; strain energy and virtual work; energy theorems; method of virtual work, Castigliano theorem; method of consistent deformations; slope-deflection method; approximate methods; stiffness method for trusses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 151A.

allCourses.title: Structural Steel Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design in steel of tension members, beams, columns, welded and bolted connections; eccentrically loaded and moment resistant joints; plate girders. Plastic design; load and resistance factor design. Composite construction; introduction to computer-aided design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 151A

allCourses.title: Foundation Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Applications of soil mechanics principles to the analysis and design of shallow foundations, retaining walls, pile foundations, and braced cuts. Design criteria: bearing capacity, working loads and tolerable settlements, structural integrity of the foundation element. Damage from construction operations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 130 and ENGRCEE 151C

allCourses.title: Environmental Processes
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to environmental processes in air and water, mass balances, and transport phenomena. Fundamentals of water-quality engineering including water and wastewater treatment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CHEM 1B or CHEM H2B) and ENGRCEE 170

allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic concepts from general, physical, and analytical chemistry as they relate to environmental engineering. Particular emphasis on the fundamentals of equilibrium and kinetics as they apply to acid-base chemistry, gas solubility, and redox reactions. Laboratory sessions.  Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Wastewater Treatment Process Design
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design of biological treatment processes. Topics include attached and suspended growth, aeration, anaerobic systems, process control, and economics. Design projects included.   Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 160

allCourses.title: Carbon and Energy Footprint Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Process design for wastewater treatment. Mass- and energy-balance analysis applied to water and wastewater treatment systems. Case studies include analysis of water supply, treatment, reclamation, and reuse.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 163 or ENGRCEE 165

allCourses.title: Physical-Chemical Treatment Processes
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theory and dynamics of physical and chemical separation processes in water and wastewater treatment. Topics include coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, gas-transfer, membrane separations, and adsorption.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 160 and (ENGRMAE 91 or CBE 40C)

allCourses.title: Microbial Processes for Bioremediation
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamental knowledge on microbiology, organic chemistry, biodegradability and persistence, reaction kinetics, and contaminant transport of water and soil remediation of organic contaminants under aerobic and anaerobic conditions. Overview of Environmental Law and Superfund. Design project of bioremediation for contaminated site.

allCourses.title: Ecology of Coastal Waters
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Engineering majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the ecological processes of the coastal environment. Investigates the causes of coastal ecosystem degradation and strategies to restore the ecosystem balance or prevent further coastal ecosystem health degradation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 1A and CHEM 1B and (SOCECOL E8 or ENGRCEE 60).

allCourses.title: Microorganisms and Climate Change
allCourses.description: Climate change and impacts on microbial processes: greenhouse gas generation, biogeochemical cycles, permafrost thawing, ocean acidification, eutrophication, pathogen proliferation. Microorganism-based solutions that can mitigate climate change impacts (microbial greenhouse control, production of lower carbon and energy footprint goods, carbon sequestration).

allCourses.title: Environmental Microbiology for Engineers
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamental and applied principles of microbiology. Structures and functions of microorganisms, the microbiology of water, wastewater and soil used in environmental engineering, and the impact of microorganisms on human and environmental health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 160

allCourses.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Thermodynamic and mechanical fluid properties; fluid statics; control volume and differential approaches for mass, momentum, and energy; dimensional analysis and similarity.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7C

allCourses.title: Water Resources Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles governing the analysis and design of water resource systems including pressurized pipelines, pipe networks, channels, and ground water. Coverage of fluid mass, momentum and energy conservation, flow resistance, and related laboratory measurements in different systems. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 170

allCourses.title: Groundwater Hydrology
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Topics include conservation of fluid mass, storage properties of porous media, matrix compressibility, boundary conditions, flow nets, well hydraulics, groundwater chemistry, and solute transport. Design projects and computer applications included.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 170 or ENGRMAE 130A or CBE 120A

allCourses.title: Watershed Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of hydrologic modeling are practiced. Concepts of watershed delineation, land use change impact, design studies, and GIS tools are discussed. Focus on the USACE (HEC) software tools (HEC-HMS, and HEC-RAS) along with their associated GIS interfaces.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 170 and ENGRCEE 176

allCourses.title: Hydrology
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Elements of the hydrologic cycle including precipitation, infiltration, evapotranspiration, ground water, and runoff. Unit Hydrograph theory and routing methods. Introduction to precipitation/runoff relationship and watershed modeling. Statistical methods and flood frequency analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRCEE 170 or ENGRMAE 130A

allCourses.title: Fluid Mechanics of Open Channels
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of fluid motion in open channels. Navier-Stokes equations and one-dimensional momentum and energy principles. Topics include rapidly varied flow, flow resistance and turbulence, gradually varied flow, unsteady flow, and computational methods for channel flow modeling.

allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to sustainability and its connection to environmental engineering infrastructure: economic/social sustainability, lifecycle assessment/cost, water and waste management, empathy in engineering, quantitative approaches for social sustainability, and decision-making across sustainability metrics. Includes guest lectures and field trips.

allCourses.title: Wastewater Treatment Process Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Process design for wastewater treatment. Topics include solids separation, biological treatment, aeration, sludge stabilization, process control, and economics. Design projects included.

allCourses.title: Biological Processes for Bioremediation
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental knowledge on microbiology, organic chemistry, biodegradability and persistence, reaction kinetics, and for development of water and soil.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Data Science Programming and Optimization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Basics of object-oriented programming; data analysis using scientific programming packages; best programming practices; civil and environmental engineering analysis and design of linear systems; introduction to the analysis and design of non-linear systems in civil engineering.

allCourses.title: Data Analytics for Civil Engineers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Quantitative research methods and statistical techniques for analyzing and viewing civil and environmental engineering data. Descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing, linear and logical regression, clustering and introduction to machine learning.

allCourses.title: Computational Problem Solving
allCourses.restriction: Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Engineering analysis and problem solving using MATLAB (or similar), including matrix algebra, solving systems of linear and nonlinear equations, numerical integration of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and coupled ODEs, and analysis of numerical errors.
