prerequisite_list.title: Computational Methods in Electrical and Computer Engineering

allCourses.title: Engineering Design in Industry
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of engineering design in the context of an industrial application. Local manufacturing firms define an engineering design project to be completed in 10 weeks. Projects include initial brainstorming to final design, with a formal presentation.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Senior Project - Special Topics
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Mechanical Engineering Majors only.
allCourses.description: Group or individual senior project of theoretical or applied nature involving design.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in MAE Design
allCourses.restriction: Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides early-stage design/hands-on experience for upper-division students, and allows them to participate in senior design projects course ENGRMAE 189.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Seminars in Engineering
allCourses.description: Seminars by individual faculty in major fields of interest. Materials fee.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering Internship
allCourses.description: Students majoring in MAE may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Group Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Group study of selected topics in Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Engineering Analysis I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Linear algebra, including vector spaces, matrices, linear systems of equations, least squares, and the eigenvalue problem. Ordinary differential equations, including analytical and numerical solution methods, stability, and phase portraits.

allCourses.title: Engineering Analysis II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Review of ordinary differential equations, including Bessel and Legendre functions. Partial differential equations, including the diffusion equation, Laplace's equation, and the wave equation. Fourier series, Fourier and Laplace transforms and their applications.

allCourses.title: Integrated Thermal-Fluid Science Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The fundamentals of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer are first.

allCourses.title: Engineering Design and Simulation: Tools and Process
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Practical techniques and use of industry tools that improve the engineering design process by simulating the performance of design options prior to the costly steps of prototyping and manufacturing are covered. Applicable to a wide variety of engineering disciplines.

allCourses.title: Professional Engineering Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: The fundamentals of the core topics in mechanical and aerospace engineering are first reviewed and then integrated and applied in the context of engineered systems.

allCourses.title: Personalized Medical Devices
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to fundamental aspects of medical devices and discusses therapeutic as well as diagnostic devices. Basic aspects of microfluidics and biology critical to personalized medical systems are studied. Typical FDA approval pathways for medical devices are presented.

allCourses.title: Perturbation Methods in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Asymptotic Expansions of integrals. Regular and singular perturbations. Perturbation methods for ordinary and partial differential equations. Matched asymptotic expansions. Multiple-scale asymptotic expansion schemes. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 200A and ENGRMAE 200B. ENGRMAE 200A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 200B with a grade of B- or better. Knowledge of linear differential equations.

allCourses.title: Model-Based Engineering: Systems and Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Engineering design, systems engineering, and product lifecycle management. Model-based approaches and modeling for the digital twin. Software tools and application to the design of a complete product from problem definition to production.

allCourses.title: Nonlinear Optimization Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Numerical methods for constrained and unconstrained optimization. Necessary and sufficient conditions for optimimality. Conjugate gradient, variable metric algorithms. Gradient projection, penalty functions, and Lagrange methods. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 200A. ENGRMAE 200A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Methods of Computer Modeling in Engineering and the Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Unified introduction to finite volume, finite element, field-boundary element, meshless, primal, dual, and mixed methods. Nonlinear problems posed by ordinary as well as partial differential equations. Computer implementations and comparisons of accuracy and convergence.

allCourses.title: Energy Efficiency in the Built Environment
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Energy and power for the built environment; building energy modeling; heat transfer and losses; heating and cooling cycles; control hardware and software; carbon neutrality, optimization.

allCourses.title: Advanced Fundamentals of Combustion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Premixed, nonpremixed, and heterogenous reactions, with emphasis on kinetics, thermal ignition, turbulent flame propogation, detonations, explosions, flammability limits, diffusion flame, quenching, flame stabilization, and particle and spray combustion. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 224 or ENGRMAE 230B

allCourses.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Combustion
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Premixed, nonpremixed, and heterogenous reactions, with emphasis on kinetics, thermal ignition, turbulent flame propogation, detonations, explosions, flammability limits, diffusion flame, quenching, flame stabilization, and particle and spray combustion.

allCourses.title: Energy Storage Systems and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of energy storage systems and technology including lithium ion battery systems for transportation and stationary applications, for flow batteries (e.g., vanadium redox, sodium sulfur), and for reversible fuel cell electrolyzer systems and hydrogen energy storage.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Undergraduate-level knowledge of applied engineering thermodynamics.

allCourses.title: Engineering Electrochemistry: Fundamentals and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to engineering electrochemistry fundamentals and applications. Examine thermodynamics and transport principles in typical electrochemical systems. Electrochemical sensors, batteries, fuel cells, and supercapacitors. Manufacturing aspects will also be covered.

allCourses.title: Engineering Electrochemistry: Fundamentals and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to engineering electrochemistry fundamentals and applications. Examine thermodynamics and transport principles in typical electrochemical systems. Electrochemical sensors, batteries, fuel cells, and supercapacitors. Manufacturing aspects are also covered.

allCourses.title: Electric Propulsion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Space propulsion requirements and maneuvers, stressing those best suited to electric propulsion. An introduction to plasma physics. Electrothermal, electromagnetic and electrostatic accelerators, with emphasis in technologies (ion engines, Hall thrusters and colloidal thrusters) belonging to the latter family.

allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fuel-cell systems design, operation, and materials. Electrochemistry and electrocatalysis, cell degradation, nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes, fuels, and fuel processing. Provides broad insight into fuel-cell science, technology, system design, and operation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 110.

allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions and other characteristics.

allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions, and other characteristics.

allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Systems and Degradation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fuel cell systems design; impacts of operating conditions; experimental and theoretical analysis methods for fuel cells systems; introduction to degradation mechanisms and mitigation techniques; provides broad insight into fuel-cell science, technology, system design and operation.  Offered every other year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 214A. ENGRMAE 214A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: PEM Fuel Cells
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: In-depth introduction to the fundamental principles of PEM fuel cells, including thermodynamics, kinetics, transport, cold start, manufacturing, and experiment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 214A. ENGRMAE 214A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Fuel Cell Fundamentals and Technology
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis; nature of fuel-cell electrodes and electrolytes; charge transfer reactions at interfaces; charge transport and mass transport processes; fuel processing reactions; determination of fuel cell efficiency, fuel flexibility, emissions, and other characteristics.

allCourses.title: Advanced Combustion Technology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Recap of combustion thermodynamics, equilibrium, chemistry concepts in the context of practical systems. Overview of renewable and non-renewable fuels and their implications for practical devices. Concepts associated with computation and experimental methods. Emphasis on pollutant formation and emissions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 200A and (ENGRMAE 230A or ENGRMAE 270A)

allCourses.title: Statistical Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Statistics of independent particles, development of quantum mechanical description of atoms and molecules, application of quantum mechanics, evaluation of thermodynamics properties for solids, liquids, and gases, statistical mechanics of dependent particles (ensembles).

allCourses.title: Generalized Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Generalized thermodynamics develops the laws of continuum thermodynamics from a set of plausible and intuitive postulates. The postulates are motivated qualitatively by a statistical description of matter and are justified by a posterior success for the resulting theory.

allCourses.title: Generalized Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Generalized thermodynamics develops the laws of continuum thermodynamics from a set of plausible and intuitive postulates. The postulates are motivated qualitatively by a statistical description of matter and are justified by a posterior success for the resulting theory.

allCourses.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design and operation of sustainable energy systems including wind, solar photo-voltaic and thermal, hydroelectric, geothermal, oceanic, biomass combustion, advanced coal and next generation nuclear.  Includes power generation, storage, and transmission for stationary power generation.

allCourses.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of sustainable energy systems including wind, solar photo-voltaic and thermal, hydroelectric, geothermal, oceanic, biomass combustion, advanced coal, and next generation nuclear. Includes power generation, storage, and transmission for stationary power generation.

allCourses.title: Solar and Renewable Energy Systems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles, design, and operation of solar and other renewable energy systems including solar photo-voltaic, solar thermal, wind, and PEM fuel cell. Includes power generation and storage, and renewable fuels for transportation and stationary power generation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Knowledge of applied engineering thermodynamics.

allCourses.title: Conduction Heat Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Steady state and transient conduction heat transfer in one- and multi-dimensional geometries. Analytical methods, exact and approximate. Numerical techniques are also included.

allCourses.title: Convective Heat and Mass Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental convective heat transfer for various cases, including flow conditions, flow phases, and boundary conditions. Analysis of heat convection by exact, approximate solutions, and similarity solutions. Boundary layer theory and equations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230B. ENGRMAE 230B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Radiative Heat Transfer
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Black body radiation.  Radiative transport equations for surfaces separated by non-participating media.  Radiant energy transfer through absorbing, emitting, and scattering media. Radiation-conduction interaction.  Radiation-convection interaction.  Introduction to finite-difference solutions.

allCourses.title: Numerical Methods in Heat, Mass, and Momentum Transport (Laminar Flows) I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the discretization of various types of partial differential equations (parabolic, elliptic, hyperbolic). Finite-volume discretization for one- and two-dimensional flows. Use of a two-dimensional elliptic procedure to predict sample laminar flows.

allCourses.title: Numerical Methods in Heat, Mass, and Momentum II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to turbulence. Reynolds-averaging of Navier-Stokes equations. Second-order closure of the average equations. Use of two-dimensional elliptic procedure to predict confined turbulent flows. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 223A

allCourses.title: Advanced Transport Phenomena
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of transport phenomena. Covers the subjects of conservation equations, dimensionless numbers, fundamentals of diffusion, perturbation methods, ion transport, two-phase transport, and interfacial phenomena.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Fluid and Thermal Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Special topics of current interest in fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, multiphase flows, or combustion. Emphasis could be placed on theory, computational methods, or experimental techniques.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Thermal Resistance Analysis in Microdevices and Nanomaterials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Heat transfer and thermal resistance analysis relevant for microdevices and nanomaterials. Overview of recent progress in nanotechnology and materials science. Thermal modeling strategies for novel electronic devices and energy conversion systems.

allCourses.title: Nanoscale Phase Change Transport Physics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses a wide range of phase change processes (i.e., evaporation, boiling, condensation, and freezing) through the use of novel thermal metamaterials with the aim of enhancing phase change performances.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate-level heat transfer is recommended.

allCourses.title: Nanoscale Materials for Modern Electronics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to design and synthesis of nanomaterials. Topics include thermal and liquid transport in materials systems, phase change heat transfer physics, and mechanical properties in materials systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Required: Undergraduate-level knowledge of heat transfer.

allCourses.title: Inviscid Incompressible Fluid Mechanics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Equations of motion. Vector notation. Flow kinematics. Potential flow and complex potential. Vorticity and circulation. Bernoulli's theorem. Crocco's theorem. Conformal, Joukowski, and Schwarz-Christoffel transformations.

prerequisite_for.title: Numerical Methods in Heat, Mass, and Momentum Transport (Laminar Flows) I

allCourses.title: Viscous Incompressible Fluid Mechanics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Review of mass, momentum, energy equations. Stress tensor, constitutive relations. Laminar flows. Stokes and Oseen flows. Self-similarity. Boundary layer theory: thin-layer approximation, Falkner-Skan, Blasius solutions, integral methods. Jet, wake, cavity flows. Introduction to turbulence: instability, Reynolds averaging, mixing length.

allCourses.title: Compressible Fluid Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: One-dimensional unsteady flow; Riemann invariants, acoustics, shock tube. Two-dimensional flow: shock polars, linear theory, similarity rules, method of characteristics. Three dimensional flow: slender-body theory.  Effects of viscosity and conductivity:  laminar boundary layer, Crocco-Busemann relations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230A or ENGRMAE 230B. ENGRMAE 230A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 230B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Theoretical Foundations of Fluid Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Well-posed problems and boundary, initial, and interface conditions; strong and weak solutions. Similarity, perturbation theory and limit behavior, bifurcations. Dispersive and nondispersive wave propagation, acoustics, ship waves, internal gravity waves, water waves. Vortices: mutual interactions and stability. Jets, wakes, cavities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230A and ENGRMAE 230B. ENGRMAE 230A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 230B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts in programming and machine learning. The goal is to provide an accessible introduction to the field of machine learning and related techniques for students with a wide variety of engineering degrees.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Turbulence
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Phenomenon of turbulence. Reynolds equations. Dynamics of turbulence. Free turbulent shear flows. Wall-bounded turbulent shear flows. Turbulent transport of scalar quantities. Spectral dynamics. Mathematical models of turbulence.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230A and ENGRMAE 230B. ENGRMAE 230A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 230B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Robotics and Controls
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Covers basic aspects of robotic and mechatronic design, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, finite state machines, and implementation of advanced feedback control laws.

allCourses.title: Turbulent Free Shear Flows
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Practical and theoretical aspects of turbulent free shear flows. Instability, global scaling laws, mixing, and noise generation in incompressible and compressible shear layers, jets, and wakes. Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, near- and far-field growth rates, effect of compressibility, aeroacoustics of jets.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 200B and ENGRMAE 230A and ENGRMAE 230B. ENGRMAE 200B with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 230A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 230B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Engineering Design and Simulation: Tools and Process
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Practical techniques and use of industry tools that improve the engineering design process by simulating the performance of design options prior to the costly steps of prototyping and manufacturing are covered. Applicable to a wide variety of engineering disciplines.

allCourses.title: Nonequilibrium Gas Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Molecular description of fluid flow. Boltzmann equation. Chapman-Enskog expansion for flows with translational nonequilibrium. Shock structure. Inviscid flows with chemical and vibrational nonequilibrium. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230C. ENGRMAE 230C with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mathematical, physical, and computational fundamentals of computational fluid dynamics, numerical methods for solving the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. Topics include: finite-difference and finite-volume discretization, time marching methods, von Neumann analysis, upwinding, flux splitting, TVD, and other high-resolution shock-capturing schemes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230C. ENGRMAE 230C with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Experimental Fluid Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concepts and techniques for measurement of fluid motion. Quantitative and qualitative flow visualization. Flow facilities, shadowgraph, schlieren, interferometer, thermal anemometer. Laser diagnostics, fluorescence, Rayleigh, Raman, Mie scattering. Laser-Doppler, particle-image, and image- correlation velocimetry. Three- and four-dimensional digital imaging.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230A and ENGRMAE 230B

allCourses.title: Dynamics of Unsteady Flows
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Unsteady potential flow modeling (Kelvin's circulation theorem, unsteady Bernoulli's equation). Theodorsen's frequency response, Wagner's step response, and the Kussner sharp-edged gust. State Space approximations for Unsteady Loads. Vortex Lattice. Flutter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230A is recommended.

allCourses.title: Inertial Navigation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a basic understanding of 1) theory, operation, and performance characteristics of a strapdown inertial navigation system  (INS), (2) distinction between strap down and gimbaled INS, (3) Kalman filtering theory and its application to strap down INS aiding.

allCourses.title: Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Kinematics and dynamics of three-dimensional motions. Lagrange's equations, Newton-Euler equations. Applications include robot systems and spinning satellites.

allCourses.title: Robotics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Spatial rigid-body transformations.  Forward and inverse kinematics. Jacobian of serial and parallel chains.  Screw coordinates and transformations. Rate and static analyses using screw theory. Singularity analysis. Trajectory generation. Not offered every year.

allCourses.title: Spaceflight Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Accurate force modeling; spacecraft trajectory design problem; two-body dynamics; Lambert problem; orbit perturbations and maintenance; applications to Earth and Moon missions; gravity assists and three-body dynamics; applications to Moon, Mars, interplanetary missions; libration point missions and dynamical system theory methods.

allCourses.title: Theoretical Kinematics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Spatial rigid body kinematics is presented with applications to robotics. Orthogonal Matrices, Rodrigues' formula, Quaternions, Plucker coordinates, screw theory, and dual numbers are studied using modern projective geometry and multi-linear algebra. Applications include trajectory planning, inverse kinematics, and workspace analysis.

allCourses.title: Spatial Mechanism Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental kinematic theory required for planar, spherical, and spatial mechanism design. The focus is on algebraic methods for the exact solution of constraint equations. Not offered every year.

allCourses.title: Micro-System Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

allCourses.title: Micro-System Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

allCourses.title: Mechanics of Smart Structures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Modeling, numerical simulation, design, and control of axial, torsional, and bending actuators. Structural analysis of shape-changing trusses, frames, and panels. Behavior and modeling of smart materials such as shape memory alloys/polymers.

allCourses.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale.  Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

allCourses.title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale. Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

allCourses.title: Biorobotics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Sensors, actuators, and neural circuits for biological movement control from an engineering perspective.  Current approaches to robotic and mechatronic devices that support and enhance human movement in health and following neurologic injuries like stroke and spinal cord injury.

allCourses.title: Micro/Nano Robotics
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the emerging field of robotics at small scale (micro/nano robotics). Understanding different physical phenomena at small scales, the differences between nano and micro robotics, common fabrication, and different mechanisms of locomotion and environmental interaction.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Microfabrication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces Engineering and Science students to the science of miniaturization. Different options to make very small machines (micro and nano size) are reviewed, materials choices are discussed, scaling laws are analyzed, and many practical applications are listed.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Microfabrication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces engineering and science students to the science of miniaturization. Different options to make very small machines (micro and nano size) are reviewed, materials choices are discussed, scaling laws are analyzed, and many practical applications are listed.

allCourses.title: Advanced BIOMEMS Manufacturing Techniques
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to BIOMEMS. Advanced biotechnology/biomedicine equipment based on MEMS and NEMS. Fundamentals of MEMS/NEMS sensing techniques and the biological and physics principles involved and the preferred MEMS and NEMS manufacturing techniques.

allCourses.title: Mechanics of Solids and Structures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Finite deformation kinematics; stress and strain measures; invariance in solid mechanics; objective rates; constitutive theory of elastic and inelastic solids; rate formulations; computational approaches; theories of plates and shells; applications to aerospace vehicles.

prerequisite_for.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Continuum Theories

allCourses.title: Mechanics of Solids and Structures
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Finite deformation kinematics; stress and strain measures; invariance in solid mechanics; objective rates; constitutive theory of elastic and inelastic solids; rate formulations; computational approaches; theories of plates and shells; applications to aerospace vehicles.

allCourses.title: Composite Materials and Structures
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Motivation for composite materials. Different classifications according to the nature of the matrix (PMC, MMC, CMC) and the reinforcement topology (fibers, whiskers, particulates). Mechanical properties. Failure mechanisms. Designing with composite materials. Advantages and limitations of homogenization techniques for numerical modeling.

allCourses.title: Nanomechanics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Nanoscale materials and the experimental and computational techniques used to measure their properties.  Mechanical behavior is the main focus, but other material properties such as diffusion and electron transport are discussed.

allCourses.title: Materials Failure and Fracture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces materials failure and fracture behaviors under mechanical, thermal, and environmental conditions. It aims to provide a solid foundation and basic understanding of classic fatigue and fracture problems, and their underlying physical mechanisms.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: A foundational knowledge of mechanical behavior and mechanics of materials, or completion of ENGRMAE 156.

allCourses.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Nanomaterials
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to nanoscale materials and experimental and computational techniques. Topics materials synthesis techniques, thin film deposition, nanoparticle and nanowire growth, characterization with electrons and X-rays, forces and surface interactions at the nanoscale, structure-property scaling laws, and atomistic/multiscale computer modeling.

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Continuum Theories
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents a continuum, macroscopic view of deformation and failure of solids. Covers elasticity, plasticity, visco-elasticity, visco-plasticity, fracture and fatigue. Topics include discussions of physical behavior, mathematical formalism and measurement techniques.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 254. ENGRMAE 254 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Atomistic Theories
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents atomistic mechanisms that control mechanical behavior of materials. Covers plasticity, dislocation theory, strengthening mechanisms, high-temperature diffusion and gain boundary sliding, shear localization, void formation, ductile rupture, brittle fracture and fatigue.

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Solids - Atomistic Theories
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents atomistic mechanisms that control mechanical behavior of materials. Covers plasticity, dislocation theory, strengthening mechanisms, high-temperature diffusion and gain boundary sliding, shear localization, void formation, ductile rupture, brittle fracture, and fatigue.

allCourses.title: Current Issues Related to Air Quality, Climate, and Energy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current issues related to the atmosphere, climate, and air quality in the context of energy conversion and sustainability. Topics include transportation systems; building design; impacts on humans and ecosystems; modeling and meteorology; economics; and application to public policies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 261 or CHEM 245 or EARTHSS 240. ENGRMAE 261 with a grade of B- or better. CHEM 245 with a grade of B- or better. EARTHSS 240 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Air Quality Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles necessary to understand the dynamics of air pollutants. Derivation and description of mathematical techniques for the numerical solution of the atmospheric equation. Formulation and development of air quality models. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 230A and ENGRMAE 230B

allCourses.title: Aviation Systems and the Environment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Methods for analyzing aviation systems, flight and engine performance, operations, and associated modern environmental challenges, including fuel burn, emissions, and noise are introduced. Analysis methods and technological and policy approaches for environmental impact mitigation examined.

allCourses.title: Linear Systems I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Input-output and state-space representations of continuous-time linear systems. State transition matrices,  Controllability and observability. Irreducible realizations.  State feedback and observer design.

allCourses.title: Linear Systems II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in linear systems: bases, linear operator representations, and Jordan forms. Review of dynamical systems, and stability. Time-varying systems, discrete-time representations, and multi-input/multi-output systems. Introduction to continuous and discrete time linear regulator (LQR) problems. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 270A. ENGRMAE 270A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Network Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides foundations on graph-theoretic, probabilistic and analytic techniques that have proven instrumental for studying networked dynamical systems. Applications are presented in diverse areas of science and engineering that include the coordination of vehicles and distribution of energy and resources.

allCourses.title: Robust Control Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Methods for control design of systems with uncertainty. Feedback stability and small gain theorem. Multivariable stability margins and multiplier theory. H-infinity-optimal control, linear matrix inequalities. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 270A. ENGRMAE 270A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Stochastic Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the tools stochastic differential equations and stochastic control. Focus on optimal control of dynamical systems in the presence of stochastic noise. Basic concepts are also central in various branches of theoretical physics and mathematical finance; examples are discussed.

allCourses.title: Optimal Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles and methods of optimal control. Topics include objectives and issues in controlling nonlinear systems; linear variational and adjoint equations; optimality conditions via variational calculus, maximum principle, and dynamic programming; solution methods; applications to control robots and aerospace vehicles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 200A and ENGRMAE 270A. ENGRMAE 200A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 270A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Nonlinear Feedback Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced tools for feedback control system analysis and synthesis. Norms, operators, Lp spaces, contraction mapping theorem, Lyapunov techniques along with their extensions. Circle criterion positivity and passivity. Applications to nonlinear control methods, such as sliding mode or adaptive techniques.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 270B. ENGRMAE 270B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Geometric Nonlinear Control
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Using the mathematics of differential geometry, a number of the concepts and results of linear systems theory have been extended to nonlinear systems. Describes these extensions and illustrate their use in nonlinear system analysis and design. Not offered every year.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 200A and ENGRMAE 270A. ENGRMAE 200A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 270A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Learning Control Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Supervised learning for classification and regression: perceptrons, support vector machines, feed-forward neural networks, Gaussian processes. Generalization and model selection: cross-validation, regularization, and Bayesian methods. Unsupervised learning: clustering and dimensionality reduction. Learning control systems. Introduction to reinforcement learning.

allCourses.title: Parameter and State Estimation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Bayesian and frequentist approaches to parameter and state estimation. Properties of estimators. Linear Gaussian systems and the Kalman Filter. Nonlinear state estimation, extended and unscented Kalman Filters. Introduction to Monte Carlo methods and particle filtering. Application to tracking and navigation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 200A and ENGRMAE 270A. ENGRMAE 200A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 270A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Selected topics of current interest in mechanical systems. Topics include robotics, kinematics, control, dynamics, and geometric modeling.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMAE 270A and ENGRMAE 241. ENGRMAE 270A with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMAE 241 with a grade of B- or better
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Design of Computer-Controlled Robots
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The basic aspects of mechatronic design are covered, including motor and sensor selection, control strategies, finite state machines, inertial measurement units, and implementation of advanced feedback control laws. Students work in groups to create their own mechatronic device. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Experimental Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals and principles of statistical experimental design and analysis. Emphasis addresses understanding and use of designed experiments, response surfaces, linear regression modeling, process optimization, and development of links between empirical and theoretical models.

allCourses.title: Engineering Design Under Uncertainty
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to statistical and ML methods used in engineering design under uncertainty. Students learn how to probabilistically formulate a design problem, translate the formulations into a computer, and systematically find the solution.

allCourses.title: Design for Human Movement
allCourses.restriction: Master of Engineering students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces techniques for analysis and modeling of human locomotion, with a focus on lower-limb rehabilitating and robotic assistive devices. Discusses background and current research, with assignments covering independent reading, computer simulations, and a final project.

allCourses.title: Research Communication in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Guides students along research communication milestones by completion of a conference/journal publication, research proposal, MS thesis, or other significant publication. Peer review, response to reviewers, and a presentation are used to build skill and confidence.

allCourses.title: Master of Science Thesis Project
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Tutorial in which masters-level students taking the comprehensive examination option undertake a masters-level research project.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
allCourses.description: Special topics by individual faculty in major fields of interest.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Engineering students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Master of Science Thesis Research
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the thesis required for the M.S. in Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the dissertation required for the Ph.D. in Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Seminars in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
allCourses.description: Presentation of advanced topics and reports of current research efforts in mechanical engineering. Required of all graduate students in mechanical engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Individual Research
allCourses.restriction: Consent of instructor to enroll
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Statics
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addition and resolution of forces, distributed forces, equivalent system of forces centroids, first moments, moments and products on inertia, equilibrium of rigid bodies, trusses, beams, cables.  Course may be offered online.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D and PHYSICS 7C

allCourses.title: Computer-Aided Design
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Develops skills for interpretation and presentation of mechanical design drawings and the use of CAD in engineering design. An integrated approach to drafting based on sketching, manual drawing, and three-dimensional CAD techniques is presented. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Manufacturing Processes in Engineering
allCourses.restriction: School of Engineering students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: With laboratory. Machines and processes of mechanical manufacturing. Safety and professional procedures emphasized.  Use of measuring instruments, hand tools, lathe, mill, drill press, bandsaw, grinder, welding equipment.

allCourses.title: Electric Circuits
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Design and analysis of analog circuits based on lumped circuit elements with emphasis on the use of operational amplifiers. Sinusoidal and transient response. Constructional and laboratory testing of analog circuits, and introduction to data acquisition. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7D and PHYSICS 7LD

allCourses.title: Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D and PHYSICS 7C

allCourses.title: Introduction to Thermodynamics
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Civil Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Thermodynamic principles; open and closed systems representative of engineering problems. First and second law of thermodynamics with applications to engineering systems and design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7C and MATH 2D

allCourses.title: Topics in Design Project
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Early-stage design/hands-on experience for students, and allows them to participate alongside seniors in the design project.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Nano-Scale Materials and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview of the chemistry, physics, and applications of nanometer-scale materials. Explore the effects of composition, bonding, and confinement on physical properties of nanomaterials, their chemical syntheses, and their device physics in electronic, optoelectronic, and energy technologies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A or CHEM H2A) and ENGR 54 and ENGRMSE 169

allCourses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to physical aspects of polymers, including configuration and conformation of polymer chains and characterization techniques; crystallinity, viscoelasticity, mechanical properties, polymer alloys, processing, and application.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and (CBE 110 or ENGRMSE 165)

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior and Design Principles
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles governing structure and mechanical behavior of materials, relationship relating microstructure and mechanical response with application to elasticity, plasticity, yielding, necking, creep, and fracture of materials. Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize the properties of materials. Design parameters.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize mechanical properties of materials. Emphasis on correlations between property and microstructure. Experiments include: plastic stability in tension, effect of grain size on flow stress, microstructural engineering.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Ceramic Materials for Sustainable Energy
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A technical elective for students interested in materials. Topics covered include structure and properties of ceramic materials, and design for sustainable energy applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Advanced Lab in Synthesis of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Synthesis and characterization of organic and inorganic materials including polymers and oxides. Techniques include electron and scanning probe microscopy, gel permeation chromatography, X-ray diffraction, porosimetry, and thermal analysis. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Computer Techniques in Experimental Research
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles and practical guidelines of automated materials testing. Computer fundamentals, programming languages, data acquisition and control hardware, interfacint techniques, programming strategies, data analysis, data storage, safeguard procedures.

allCourses.title: X-ray Diffraction, Electron Microscopy, and Microanalysis
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Material characterization using X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Topics include X-ray diffraction and analysis; SEM imaging and microanalysis. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: X-ray Diffraction, Electron Microscopy, and Microanalysis Lab
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Material characterization using X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Topics include X-ray diffraction and analysis; SEM imaging and microanalysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Materials Kinetics and Phase Transformations
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Treatment of the kinetics of solid-state reactions and reactions at interfaces. Thermodynamics and kinetics of phase transformations, including solidification processes, diffusional and diffusionless phase transformations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and ENGRMSE 65B. ENGRMSE 65B with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.title: Electronic and Optical Properties in Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers the electronic, optical, and dielectric properties of crystalline and amorphous materials to provide a foundation of the underlying physical principles governing the properties of existing and emerging electronic and photonic materials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSICS 7D and PHYSICS 7E and (MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N) and MATH 3D

allCourses.title: Green Engineering: Theory and Practice
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Methods and impacts of selecting alternative technologies, processes, materials, chemicals, to reduce pollution, waste, and use of toxic substances, thereby creating “green,” environmentally responsible, sustainable solutions. Topics include environmental regulations, recycling, life-cycle assessment, economic analysis, design, green chemistry, and toxicology.

allCourses.title: Composite Materials Design
allCourses.description: Introduction to fiber-reinforced composites for mechanical applications. Properties of reinforcing fibers. Manufacture of fibers and composites. Micromechanics of fiber composites. Strength criteria and failure modes. Macromechanics in design of laminated composite structures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and ENGR 150

allCourses.title: Design Failure Investigation
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Survey of mechanisms by which devices fail, including overload, fatigue, corrosion, and wear. Use of fractography and other evidence to interpret failure modes and specify design/manufacturing changes. Students redesign failed parts or structures based on actual parts and/or case histories.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Surface and Adhesion Science
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Structure, thermodynamics of, kinetics, and reactions on surfaces. Surface electronic and mechanical properties and characterization of all classes of materials including metals, semiconductors, ceramics, polymers, and soft materials. Adhesion between different materials is also addressed.

allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Meaning and phases of design; design considerations; properties of engineering materials; materials property charts; materials selection; process selection; multi-constraint and multi-objective design. Selection of shape in mechanical components. Designing with hybrid materials: challenges and opportunities. Environmental considerations; case studies.

allCourses.description: Demonstrates major concepts in Materials Science and Engineering. Concepts of materials engineering covered include deformation in crystalline solids, effects of heat treatment on mechanical properties, thermal barrier materials, composites design, mechanical behavior of polymers, superconductivity in ceramics.

allCourses.title: Dislocation Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theory of elasticity and symmetry of crystals, plasticity and slip systems, stress field of dislocation, dislocation reaction, theories of yielding and strengthening, application of reaction-rate kinetics to thermally activated dislocation motion.

allCourses.title: Theory of Diffusion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Solid-state diffusion, analysis of diffusion in solids, thermodynamics of diffusion, application of diffusion theory to phase transformation and deformation problems.

allCourses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to physical aspects of polymers, including configuration and conformation of polymer chains and characterization techniques; crystallinity visoelasticity, rheology, and processing.

allCourses.title: Design with Ceramic Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Dependence of ceramic properties on bonding, crystal structure, defects, and microstructure. Ceramic manufacturing technology. Survey of physical properties. Strength, deformation, and fracture of ceramics. Mechanical design with brittle, environment-sensitive materials exhibiting time-dependent strengths.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Engineering Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles governing structure and mechanical behavior of materials, relationship relating microstructure and mechanical response with application to elasticity, plasticity, creep, and fatigue, study of rate-controlling mechanisms and failure modes, fracture of materials.

allCourses.title: Fracture of Engineering Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fracture mechanics and its application to engineering materials. Elastic properties of cracks, the stress intensity factor, the crack tip plastic zone, the J integral approach, fracture toughness testing, the crack tip opening displacement, fracture at high temperatures, fatigue crack growth.

allCourses.title: Transmission Electron Microscopy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The theory and operation of the transmission electron microscope (TEM), including the basic construction, electron optics, electron diffraction and reciprocal space, formation of image and electron diffraction information, microanalysis, and specimen preparation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200

allCourses.title: High Temperature Deformation of Engineering Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical and practical aspects of creep and superplasticity in metallic and non-metallic systems are presented. Topics include: creep testing methods, diffusional creep, deformation mechanism maps, and superplasticity in non-metallics.

allCourses.title: Grain Boundaries & Interfaces in Nanocrystalline Materials
allCourses.description: Structure and character of grain boundaries and interfaces in solids including nanocrystalline materials. Role of grain boundaries in chemical segregation, fracture, deformation, creep, conductivity, diffusion, and grain growth.  Experimental techniques and computational methods used to characterize and model grain boundaries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200

allCourses.title: Scanning Electron Microscopy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The theory and operation of the scanning electron microscope (SEM) and X-ray microanalysis. Topics covered include the basic design and electron optics, electron beam - specimen interactions, image formation and interpretation, X-ray spectrometry, and other related topics and techniques.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200

allCourses.title: Seminar in Systems Microbiology Research
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A research and journal club seminar that covers topics on bacteria and phage using approaches and principles from biology, engineering, and physics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Principles of Coatings, Thin Films, and Multi-layers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles and concepts underlying the engineering of coating systems, thin films, and multilayers. Microstructure control, processing approaches, mechanical behavior, and thermomechanical characteristics and characterization. Interfacial stability, cracking, delamination, and thermal stress issues. Control of functional properties.

allCourses.description: Theory, underlying principles, experimental techniques, and applications of electroceramics and solid-state electrochemical systems.
