allCourses.description: Introduction to the experimental techniques to characterize the properties of engineering materials. Emphasis on understanding the influence of microstructure on elastic, plastic, and fracture behavior. Topics include microstructure characterization, heat treatment, grain size effect, precipitation hardening, and impact loading. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Treatment of the laws of thermodynamics and their application in understanding properties and equilibrium states of engineering materials. Develops relationships pertaining to multiphase equilibrium and presents graphical constructions for interpretation of phase diagrams. Statistical thermodynamics in relation to materials phenomena.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A or CHEM H2A) and PHYSICS 7C

allCourses.title: Diffusion in Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Mass transfer in solids. Models of diffusion and the treatment of steady-state and non-steady state diffusion phenomena and ion-migration. Mechanisms controlling kinetics of diffusion and the role of material structure and point defects. Diffusion in binary systems and Kirkendall effect.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 65A. ENGRMSE 65A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Undergraduate Research in Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides disciplinary research participation. Original or existing research options provide undergraduates the opportunity for faculty/mentor interactions including access to appropriate facilities. Medical Epidemiology research areas: Cancer, Genetic/Molecular, Environmental, Occupational, Biostatistics, and Infectious Disease.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Principles of Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles of epidemiology, biostatistics, and epidemiological research. Topics include research methods of measuring health problems in populations, disease control and prevention in populations, how epidemiology contributes to knowledge of disease etiology, and biostatistical analysis and interpretation of epidemiologic data.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Principles of Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles of epidemiology, biostatistics, and epidemiological research. Topics include research methods of measuring health problems in populations, disease control and prevention in populations, how epidemiology contributes to knowledge of disease etiology, and biostatistical analysis and interpretation of epidemiologic data.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Intermediate Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Epidemiology Majors only. College of Health Sciences students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Program in Public Health students only.
allCourses.description: Explores conceptual aspects of epidemiology, focusing on strengths and limitations of observational designs. Learn to identify, quantify, and correct bias (e.g. selection, confounding), and evaluate causal identical conditions. Gain skills to evaluate study designs systematically.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 206A. PUBHLTH 206A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in the design and statistical analysis of epidemiologic studies. Topics include simulation methods, counter-matching and multiphase study designs, missing data, and Bayesian analysis. Published simulation studies are discussed and replicated using the R software package.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200A and EPIDEM 200B. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B or better. EPIDEM 200B with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods and Causal Inference I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Research design, questions, and analysis tasks, emphasizing theory, methods, and approaches for estimating causal effects in health/social sciences from observational data. Toolset for asking and answering research questions and interpreting evidence. Part one of a two-quarter advanced causal inference course.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200C. EPIDEM 200C with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods and Causal Inference II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explore causal inference methods in epidemiology and public health. From general theory covered in the first quarter, delve into specific methods for estimating causal effects from observational data. Gain an in-depth understanding of these techniques and their applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200D. EPIDEM 200D with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Cancer Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concentrates on understanding how epidemiology plays a role in the search for cancer etiology, prevention, control, and treatment; gives an overview of cancer research with an appreciation of the multidisciplinary nature of the field.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200A or PUBHLTH 206A. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B- or better. PUBHLTH 206A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Genetic Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Genetic epidemiologic research principles, covering diverse study designs and methods. Integrates literature examples, lectures, demonstrations, and software applications for varied study designs, ranging from unrelated individuals to large extended kindreds. Includes in-class discussions, group projects, and exercises for concept reinforcement.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 203 or EPIDEM 203 or PUBH 206. PUBHLTH 203 with a grade of B- or better. EPIDEM 203 with a grade of B- or better. PUBH 206 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents descriptive and experimental approaches to the recognition of the causal association of disease in the general population, as these approaches apply to populations using different student designs and models free from the literature.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to help students develop an appreciation for statistician's view of the research process, emphasizing biomedical research. Instills an understanding of how statistical models are used to yield insights about data that form evidence-based understanding of the world around us.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the basic statistical techniques commonly used in public health research. Topics include descriptive statistics, basic probability, inferential statistics (estimation, confidence intervals, and hypothesis testing), and contingency tables. SAS software is introduced.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics II: Intermediate Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores advanced statistical analysis methods for biological and medical applications. Topics include linear, logistic, and generalized linear regression models like Poisson regression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204A. EPIDEM 204A with a grade of B or better

prerequisite_list.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics III: Advanced Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields.  Introduces statistical methods for analyzing survival and longitudinal/clustered data, and techniques to resolve missing data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204B. EPIDEM 204B with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics IV: Survival Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced statistical analysis for epidemiologic studies, focusing on time-to-event data. Modern approaches, covering survival analysis, missing data, and statistical power analysis. SAS procedures PHREG, LIFEREG, and LIFETEST for intricate dataset analysis. Emphasis on model selection and proper interpretation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204C. EPIDEM 204C with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concentrates on epidemiological approaches to the assessment of community environmental hazards; issues involved in environmental exposure estimation; interdisciplinary approaches to environmental epidemiology, including the use of biomarkers of exposures and susceptibility; epidemiological studies within the context of risk assessment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200 and EPIDEM 204. EPIDEM 200 with a grade of B- or better. EPIDEM 204 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Methods for Design and Implementation of Epidemiologic Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields, and covers topics in subject recruitment, data collection, quality assessment and control, and sample-size estimation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200A and EPIDEM 204A. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B or better. EPIDEM 204A with a grade of B or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Statistical Genetics
allCourses.description: Provides students with knowledge of the basic principles, concepts, and methods used in statistical genetic research. Topics include principles of population genetics, and statistical methods for family- and population-based studies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Two quarters of upper-division or graduate training in statistical methods.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in the design and statistical analysis of epidemiologic studies. Topics include simulation methods, counter-matching and multiphase study designs, missing data, and Bayesian analysis. Published simulation studies are discussed and replicated using the R software package.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 101B or STATS 111 or STATS 211

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Data Management I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Program in Public Health students only.
allCourses.description: Learn SAS basics, Base SAS, DATA step essentials, and PROCs for data exploration and analysis. Topics include data reading, variable creation, sorting, merging, and common functions. Priority for MS/PhD Epidemiology, MPH Epidemiology/Biostatistics students concurrently enrolled.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Data Management II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Program in Public Health students only.
allCourses.description: Develop SAS proficiency in epidemiology/public health research. Goals include expanding SAS knowledge, enhancing self-sufficiency via online resources, and understanding program outcomes. Reinforce study design and data analysis basics while emphasizing SAS as a tool for data management.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 220A and EPIDEM 200A and EPIDEM 204A. EPIDEM 220A with a grade of B or better. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B or better. EPIDEM 204A with a grade of B or better

prerequisite_list.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Cardiovascular Disease Epidemiology and Prevention
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Epidemiological aspects of chronic human diseases. Topics include methodologies for quantifying aspects of prevalent chronic diseases including risk factors, identification of susceptible groups, societal burdens, promising future research; and the intervention, prevention, and control of diseases in populations.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and clinical research fields. Covers common regression-modeling techniques frequently used in biologic and medical applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204. EPIDEM 204 with a grade of B or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Toxic Chemicals in Environment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Industrial ecology of toxicants and their impacts on environmental quality and human health. Explores theoretical basis of toxicity thresholds and regulatory issues. Uses classic and contemporary research articles to understand the legacy of traditional toxicants, and to identify emerging threats.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics III Survival Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields. Covers common techniques for analyzing survival or other time-to-event data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 242. EPIDEM 242 with a grade of B or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environ Health Sci and Policy Majors only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. Studies human-environment interaction, focusing on chemical, physical, and biological agents in community and occupational settings. Covers climate change, environmental justice, children’s health, exposure assessment, and policy for public health improvement.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the complex relationships among exposure processes and adverse health effects of environmental toxins focusing on specific chemicals, sources, transport media, exposure pathways, and human behaviors. Techniques of environmental sampling for exposure assessment are discussed.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
allCourses.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Human Exposure to Environmental Contaminants
allCourses.description: Introduces founders of conceptual thought that environmental contaminants can impact health. Theory and principles of exposure assessment, the continuum from emissions of a contaminant into the environment to evidence of health effects in a population.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents various topics and the latest research in the broad field of epidemiology.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Epidemiology Research Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Research journal club is a group discussion of recent publications in epidemiology and related fields.  Students rotate as lead discussants, guided by faculty.  All attendees are expected to be familiar with the papers at the start of class.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Epidemiology Department Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A forum for the presentation of recent research to epidemiology students, faculty, and other interested parties. The atmosphere is informal, yet rigorous. Speakers range from graduate students through distinguished visitors from other institutions.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Biostatistics and Epidemiology for Medical Fellows
allCourses.description: Prepares medical fellows and other physicians for rotations in research programs. Understanding of basic biostatistics and study design, and interdependencies between the two. Application of principles in evaluation of medical literature for guidance on patient care and public health policy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Medical degree.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: M.S. Thesis Research and Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research and study necessary for a graduate student to prepare and complete the thesis required for the Master of Science (M.S.) degree.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Advancement to candidacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: PhD Degree Dissertation Research & Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research and study necessary for a graduate student to prepare and complete the dissertation required for the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Advancement to candidacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Directed Study in Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed study with Epidemiology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Independent Study in Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Epidemiology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: University Supervised Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to students with active Teaching Assistant (T.A.) appointments.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in Historical Foundations (1500-1800)
allCourses.description: Offers an overview of the European experience from its social, political, and cultural foundations to modern European issues and institutions in a globalized world. Topics include social, political, and cultural history up to the French Revolution.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in European Literatures and Visual Cultures
allCourses.description: Explores developments in literature and/or the visual culture (art, film, media) within the broader context of Europe by comparing different traditions.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in European Identities: Race, Nation, Religion, Migration
allCourses.description: Introduces Europe not as a geographical location but as a site of constant evolution and change. Its “identity” has been negotiated and is being negotiated in the face of significant social, cultural, and political developments, also in a global context.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in European Thought, Culture, and Society
allCourses.description: Introduces multidisciplinary approaches to important themes in European society, culture, art, literature, philosophy, and politics.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: European Studies Core I - Early Europe (Pre-1789)
allCourses.description: Introduction to multidisciplinary approaches to important themes in European society, culture, art, literature, and politics; encourages students to explore intersections among disciplines. Possible themes: Concept of Europe in Renaissance, Self and Other: Europe and Islam, Hybrid Cultures in Medieval Europe.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: European Studies Core II: Modern Europe (Post-1789)
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary approaches to important themes in modern European society, culture, art, literature, and politics, encouraging students to see points of intersection among disciplines. Possible themes: Subjects, Citizens, and Representation; Europe in the World; European Revolutions in Art and Society.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Early European History and Culture: Pre-1789
allCourses.description: Addresses historical and cultural events, issues, and texts (art, literature, music, political theory) from the pre-1789 period in more than one European country.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Modern European History and Culture: Post-1789
allCourses.description: Addresses historical and cultural events, issues, and texts (art, literature, music, political theory) from 1789 to present in more than one European country.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Issues and Institutions in Modern Europe (1789-1945)
allCourses.description: Offers an overview of modern European societies in social, political, and cultural terms. Topics include shifting geopolitical borders, social movements, and various forms of cultural expression (film, art, literature) as they intersect with and shape issues and events after 1800.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: What is the Origin of Language?
allCourses.description: Teaches symbol-based logic and universal grammar in human language as tools to investigate the origin of language. Does language originate with reason? Is language inherently universal or diverse? Does it begin as something literal or figurative.

allCourses.title: Topics in Contemporary Europe (1945 – Today)
allCourses.description: Offers a perspective on contemporary politics and social and cultural life of today’s Europe. Introduces students to literature, film, and social theory crises of the contemporary world as they emanated from World War II, such as nationalism and populism.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in European Culture and Society
allCourses.description: Students engage in rigorous, in-depth, interdisciplinary exploration of specific topics, periods, or themes, investigating and analyzing the intersection of history and culture in different periods and geographical locations in Europe.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 1 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in European Culture and Society
allCourses.description: Addresses historical and cultural events, issues, and texts from an interdisciplinary perspective (art, literature, music, political theory). The historical focus could be from the Middle Ages to the present.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Senior Seminar in European Studies
allCourses.restriction: School of Humanities students only.
allCourses.description: Capstone research seminar. Students engage in rigorous, in-depth, interdisciplinary exploration of specific topics, periods, or themes, investigating and analyzing the intersection of material and discursive culture in different historical periods and geographical locations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty advisor.  Substantial written work required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Core Seminar I: Foundations of European Thought and Culture
allCourses.description: Provides a historical, geographical, and methodological overview of foundational texts and issues in European thought and culture. Covering several historical periods between the Middle Ages and the present, students will see how ideas and institutions change over time.

allCourses.title: Core Seminar II: Theorizing Periods and Movements in European Thought and Culture
allCourses.description: Periods and movements still form basic units for organizing European thought and theory, even as such categories are problematized. This course will allow for greater focus on a specific time period or constellation of issues around a period or movement.

allCourses.title: Core Seminar III: European Thought and Culture Beyond Europe
allCourses.description: Studies the intersection and afterlives of European thought and culture with and in non-European contexts, the way European thought and culture has been translated and transformed, taken up and challenged, in colonial, postcolonial, and other global situations.

allCourses.title: Topics in European Studies
allCourses.description: Seminars on various topics related to European Studies.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Reading and Conference
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. School of Humanities students only.
allCourses.description: For students to do independent research with advisors on their master's thesis or master's examination reading lists.

allCourses.title: Topics in Europe in the Middle Ages
allCourses.description: Explores the literature, history, and thought of the European Middle Ages. Topics may include understandings of self and community, aristocratic power and courtly life, colonialism, crusading, religious beliefs and persecution, monasticism and reform, university culture, epic literature, and Arthurian romance.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Historical Foundations: Europe and the Foundations of the Modern World
allCourses.description: Encompasses a variety of perspectives in the social sciences and the humanities involving crucial developments coming out of Europe from roughly 1500 to 1800, (the Protestant Reformation through the French Revolution), that helped shape the modern (western) world.

allCourses.title: Europe's Futures: 1755-Present
allCourses.description: Introduces students to competing approaches from humanities and social sciences to conceptualizing the future in politics, art, and literature. From the enlightenment to today, investigates the cultural and political context of moments when new ideas emerged to secure Europe's futures.

allCourses.title: Financial Reporting for Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Financial reporting is concerned with the preparation and public dissemination of financial reports designed to reflect corporate performance and financial condition. Provides a base level of knowledge needed by corporate executives to understand and discuss corporate financial statements.

allCourses.title: Investments Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to how securities are traded and how their prices are determined. Discussion of different market organizations, including some recently developed online financial markets. Study of pricing models, including Capital Asset, factor models, and Arbitrage Pricing Theory.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Finance
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines foundations of finance. Teaches tools such as time value of money, capital budgeting techniques, cash flow analysis. Examines foundations of investment management and theory/empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, asset pricing models, factor models, option pricing theory.

allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students in the Merage School Master of Finance program with information and practical skills for success in the program and for business career planning.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Financial Research Methodology
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction into the computational research methods necessary in modern finance, such as optimization, simulation methods, and finite difference and finite element methods. Some applications include quadratic programming for portfolio selection and option pricing.

allCourses.title: Risk Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines modern techniques for managing financial risks, including market, credit, liquidity, and operational risks. Covers measurement techniques for different financial risks and instruments. Discusses how risk measurement tools can be used for management of the risk/return profile of financial institutions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FIN 249. FIN 249 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Portfolio Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a working understanding of the themes and concepts of portfolio management. Covers several disciplines, such as investment valuation, investment decision-making, investing styles, asset allocation, monitoring and re-balancing portfolios, risk management strategies, performance evaluation, and attribution analysis.

allCourses.title: Bonds and Fixed Income
allCourses.description: Addresses concepts covering a broad spectrum of debt securities with emphasis on qualitative and quantitative analysis of fixed income securities in many areas, including corporate (credit) debt, MBS/ABS, structured debt, and credit derivatives.

allCourses.title: Multinational Finance
allCourses.description: Examines the history of the world’s foreign exchange markets, the macroeconomics of foreign exchange, major parity conditions, hedging of currency exposure and international investment. Gives students a basic understanding of foreign exchange market.

allCourses.title: FinTech
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides working knowledge of the role of IT-enabled innovation in financial markets to help students acquire an understanding of broad economic issues that are of wide applicability in many areas of FinTech. Both qualitative analysis and quantitative applications are explored.

allCourses.title: The Real Estate Development Process
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Nature and composition of development community and development process. Emphasis on role of conflicting interests, values and goals, and market uncertainty. Special attention paid to deal structuring and risk management. Lectures, guest lecturers, team projects evaluating actual development project.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Management of the Real Estate Enterprise
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Capstone seminar. Looks beyond “The Deal” to management of the real estate enterprise itself. Explores aspects of decision-making focused upon strategic objectives: goal setting, legal/tax structures, public vs. closely-held entities, corporate ethics, capital structure, managing growth, diversification, technology. Guest professionals.

allCourses.title: Applied Real Estate Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an understanding of the public real estate investment trust (REIT) market and its place in modern investment strategies, presents methods for analyzing and valuing companies, and introduces basic concepts for constructing and managing a real estate investment portfolio.

allCourses.title: Real Estate Transactions
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: For real estate professionals engaged in purchasing, selling, appraising, evaluating, analyzing and lending on, and developing real property with the basic tools needed to understand the primary elements of a commercial real estate transaction in California.

allCourses.title: Corporate Real Estate Management (CREM)
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to Corporate Real Estate Management (CREM) and its many facets. Appreciate the role of CREM, its impact on global society, and its importance to both the real estate community and corporations that it supports.

allCourses.title: Cases in Corporate Financial Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Case-based course in corporate finance. Introduces advanced analytical tools and techniques for value-based financial management in a broad range of corporate settings, including financial forecasting, mergers and acquisitions, leveraged buyouts, ownership and control, corporate restructuring, and financial distress.

allCourses.title: Corporate Valuation
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Expands on concepts covered in introductory finance. Combines lectures and cases designed to confront students with real-world problems to enhance their understanding of the value and limitations of finance theory. Focuses on the value of firms/projects in diverse settings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FIN 210. FIN 210 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Derivatives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Covers major derivative instruments that are widely used for hedging, including forward, futures, swaps and options, speculation, and arbitrage. Focuses on understanding the instruments, how to use and price them, basic risk management principles, and how to implement investment strategies.

allCourses.title: Mergers and Acquisitions
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on mastering mergers and acquisitions concepts and techniques that will enable participants to practically apply them in related fields such as investment banking, consulting, and corporate development. Studies drivers of success in M&A with heavy attention on transactional review.

allCourses.title: Behavioral Finance
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Describes the scientific evidence about where misvaluation comes from, how investors can trade profitably to exploit market inefficiency, how corporate managers should make financing and investment decisions in an inefficient market, and how managers can correct biases to avoid mistakes.

allCourses.title: Wealth Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides overview of considerations needed to connect singular functional areas that comprise personal and business wealth management, including basic and advanced estate planning, investment management, tax management, life/liability and property/casualty insurance, medical and long‐term care coverage, retirement and philanthropy considerations.

allCourses.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of venture capital and private equity, which constitute the “alternative” asset class (as opposed to conventional investments). Many start-up and entrepreneurial firms require substantial capital, and venture capital and private equity organizations finance these high-risk but potentially high-reward companies.

allCourses.title: Advanced Derivatives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Describes the scientific evidence about where misvaluation come from, how investors can trade profitably to exploit market inefficiency, how corporate managers should make financing and investment decisions in an inefficient market, and how managers can correct their own biases.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: FIN 249. FIN 249 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Finance Internship
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with opportunities to apply knowledge obtained from classroom theory through actual practical work experiences. Also provides knowledge of career opportunities, understanding of finance in business environments, and preparation for the finance profession.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Finance
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of finance. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Master of Finance Capstone
allCourses.restriction: Master of Finance Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Students work in teams on an applied finance project associated with their area of focus to demonstrate knowledge and expertise. The project can involve experiential learning, collaboration with a faculty member, or association with an internship.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a select faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: History of Film I: The Silent Era
allCourses.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from its invention to the adoption of synchronous sound. Includes early exhibition, developments in narrative and editing, the formation of the studio system, and avant-garde film movements. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_list.title: Introduction to Film and Visual Analysis

prerequisite_for.title: Film and Media Theory and Practice

allCourses.title: History of Film II: The Studio Era
allCourses.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from the 1930s through the 1960s. Includes the Hollywood studio system, propaganda films, Italian neorealism, post-war Japanese cinema, and the French New Wave. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_list.title: Introduction to Film and Visual Analysis

prerequisite_for.title: Film and Media Theory and Practice

allCourses.title: History of Film III: The Contemporary Era
allCourses.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical developments of cinema in the U.S. and internationally from the late 1960s to the present. Includes New Hollywood and independent U.S. films, ethnic cinemas, postcolonial cinemas, East-Asian new waves, and digital filmmaking. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

prerequisite_for.title: Film and Media Theory and Practice

allCourses.title: History of Radio and Television
allCourses.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical development of radio and television. Includes rise of broadcasting, transition to cable, and emergence of streaming.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: History of Digital Media
allCourses.description: The aesthetic, industrial, and socio-historical development of digital media. May include history of video games, computing, and social media. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Film and Media Theory
allCourses.description: Survey of major directions in film and media theory. Various theories of mass culture, realism, auteurism, semiotics, feminism, cultural studies, and theories of other media, with an emphasis on developing the student’s ability to analyze and articulate a theoretical argument. Materials fee.

allCourses.description: Examination of subjects relevant to the culture of Israel and Judaism in their historical and modern day contexts through the study of film, literature, religious texts, artistic representations, etc.

allCourses.title: The Holocaust
allCourses.description: Introduction to the history of European Jewish communities before the Holocaust; the origins of Nazi antisemitism; the implementation of the "Final Solution"; Jewish resistance to the Nazis; and attempts in film and literature to represent the Holocaust since 1945.
