allCourses.title: Topics in Environmental History
allCourses.description: Explores the many historical interfaces between climate change, modes of production, and culture. Topics include the environmental history of warfare, imperialism, and famine in the nineteenth century and the history of environmental thought.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in International Conflicts
allCourses.description: A study of international conflicts from military, social, economic perspectives with a focus on the preparation for and conduct of war and the consequences. Formerly History 100A.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in History and Journalism
allCourses.restriction: Recommended: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: A series of lectures on, and discussions of, announced topics in history and journalism and the literature of facts. Examples: "Early Modern Women in the Public Sphere," "Victorian Cultural Critics," and "Writing about War.".
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Later Roman Empire
allCourses.description: Creation of a bureaucratic empire; rule by gentry and officers; official culture and rise of Christianity; social conflict and political disintegration.

allCourses.title: Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity Since WWII
allCourses.description: Investigates instances of genocide since 1945 (including Cambodia, Bosnia, Rwanda, and others); explores the history behind these mass murders; considers why people kill, how victims survive, and questions whether international agreements are enough to prevent crimes against humanity.

allCourses.title: Europe in the Early Middle Ages
allCourses.description: Survey of Europe between 300 A.D. and 900 A.D. Topics include the breakup of the Roman Empire, barbarian invasions, spread of Christianity, rise of Islam, the Carolingian Empire, and the Vikings.

allCourses.title: Europe in the Central Middle Ages
allCourses.description: Survey of European history from ca. 900 to ca. 1300. Topics discussed include the growth of the economy, feudalism, the crusades, the rise of towns, the development of the church, popular heresy, and the rise of large-scale polities.

allCourses.title: Europe in the Later Middle Ages
allCourses.description: Survey of European history from ca. 1300 to ca. 1500. Topics include the Black Death, the crisis of the economy, the Hundred Years' War, peasant and urban uprisings, and the Great Schism.

allCourses.title: Topics in Medieval Europe
allCourses.description: Theme-based approach to the main social, political, religious, and cultural developments in Europe between the 4th and 15th centuries. Topics include the Crusades, medieval towns, medieval visionaries, and the deadly sins.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Early Modern Europe
allCourses.description: Theme-based approach to the main social, political, and cultural developments in Europe between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries.  Topics included Renaissance humanism, Reformation and Counter-Reformation, scientific revolution, court culture and nation building, interactions with non-European peoples, cities and commerce.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Modern European History
allCourses.description: Course content changes with instructor. Topics include the Inquisition; science and religion in modern Europe; sex and society in modern Europe; French revolutions; culture in interwar Europe; the Holocaust; the fall of communism in Eastern Europe.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Europe: Twentieth Century
allCourses.description: World War I and its impact on the modern world; rise of an international Communist movement; regimes created by Mussolini, Hitler, Stalin; World War II; the killing of Europe's Jews; Cold War and collapse of communism.

allCourses.title: England in the Early Middle Ages
allCourses.description: Survey of English history from ca. 400 to ca. 1200. Topics include the Anglo-Saxons, the Viking settlement, the Norman Conquest, the Angevin Empire, and the development of royal, legal, and administrative mechanisms.

allCourses.title: Later Medieval England
allCourses.description: Survey of English history between ca. 1200 and ca. 1500. Topics include the Magna Carta, the Barons' War, the Welsh and Scottish wars, the development of Parliament, the Hundred Years' War, and the War of the Roses.

allCourses.title: Modern Britain: 1700 to 1850
allCourses.description: Examines the major developments in British politics, socioeconomic structure, and culture from 1700-1850. The development of the British nation-state and the fashioning of a national identity. Explores basic questions about British national identity.

allCourses.title: Modern Britain: 1850 to 1930
allCourses.description: Examines the social, economic, and political history of Britain from 1850-1930. Post-industrialism, urbanization, population and economic change, increased political participation by working classes and women, consolidation of the empire and the breakup of the United Kingdom.

allCourses.title: Modern Britain: 1930 to Present
allCourses.description: Explores Britain from the Second World War to resignation of Margaret Thatcher. Examines Britain's devolution from world power to member of the European Community; transition from a manufacturing to service-based economy; changing demographic and racial composition in light of decolonization.

allCourses.title: Introductory Topics in History
allCourses.description: Introduces methods and premises of historical study. Topics include introductions to cultural, political, economic, social, and religious history.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: The French Revolution: 1774-1815
allCourses.description: Emphasis on social, economic, and cultural history of the French Revolution.

allCourses.title: Revolution, Nation, and Modernity: France, 1789-1900
allCourses.description: After 1789, France struggled to build a republic based on ideas of nationhood and citizenship with universal aspirations that could be exported to the rest of the world. Topics include empire, secularism vs. religion, gender relationships, birth of cinema.

allCourses.title: War and Empire: France and the World in the 20th Century
allCourses.description: Examines French experience of World War I, the defeat and occupation by Germany in World War II, the violent struggles that came with the loss of the French empire in the 1950s and 1960s, immigration, French responses to globalization.

allCourses.title: History of Paris
allCourses.description: The development of Paris from the beginnings through the present, with emphasis on the last three centuries. The city is examined from the political, social, ecological, and architectural points of view as well as through the perspective of urban planning.

allCourses.title: Hitler and the Germans
allCourses.description: Focuses on Hitler's rise to power and Nazi society. Examines Germany's defeat in World War I; the political and cultural experimentation of the 1920s; the causes of Hitler's success; and life in Germany under the Nazis.

allCourses.title: Topics in Spanish History
allCourses.description: Topics include Spain in the nineteenth century, the Spanish Civil War, and dictatorship and democracy in modern Spain.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Imperial Russia: 1689-1905
allCourses.description: Political and social developments in Russia from 1689-1905.

allCourses.title: Twentieth-Century Russia
allCourses.description: Political and social developments in Twentieth-Century Russia.

allCourses.title: The Era of World War I: 1900-1939
allCourses.description: The era of World War I and its political, social and economic history.

allCourses.title: The Era of World War II: 1933-45
allCourses.description: The era of World War II and its political, social and economic history.

allCourses.title: Women and Gender in Early Modern Europe: 1400-1700
allCourses.description: Explores what it meant to be a woman in early modern Europe. Examines women's lives in early modern Europe while developing skills of historical interpretation. Topics include: notions of masculinity and femininity; "proto-feminism"; marriage and sexuality; female piety and witchcraft.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Women in Europe
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of history of European women. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Jewish History, Ancient to Early Modern Times
allCourses.description: The history of the Jewish people from their origins in the ancient world to the 1700s. Social, religious, and intellectual life of Jewish communities in the Middle East, North Africa, and Europe.

allCourses.title: Modern Jewish History
allCourses.description: History of the Jews in Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, and the United States from the early-eighteenth century to recent times. Emancipation, assimilation, religious reform, antisemitism, Zionism, socialism, the Holocaust, and modern Israel are the major themes.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Jewish History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Jewish history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Antisemitism
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of antisemitism, ancient to modern. Topics include medieval religious anti-Judaism, persecution of Jews and Judaism during the Crusades and the Inquisition, the rise of modern racial antisemitism, Nazi antisemitism, and the persistence of antisemitism since 1945.

allCourses.title: Jews and Power
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority.

allCourses.title: History of Zoroastrianism
allCourses.description: Reviews major trends in the history of Zoroastrianism.

allCourses.title: Ancient Persia
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of Persia in antiquity.

allCourses.title: Medieval Persia
allCourses.description: A survey of Persian history in the context of Late Antique and Medieval Islamic history.

allCourses.title: Modern Iran
allCourses.description: The history of Iran from the end of the Safavid Empire in the eighteenth century to the present.

allCourses.title: Topics in Iranian History
allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, intellectual, social, and/or economic histories of Iran.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Israel and Palestine
allCourses.description: Origins of Zionism in the nineteenth century, Arab-Jewish conflicts in Palestine, emergence of Palestinian nationalism, formation of the Israeli nation after 1948, and the development of the Palestinian movement. Focus on Palestinian and Israeli society and culture. Formerly History 132.

allCourses.title: The Emergence of the Modern Middle East
allCourses.description: Offers a survey of the history of the Middle East from the 19th century to the present time. Formerly History 133A.

allCourses.title: Women and Gender in the Middle East
allCourses.description: Focuses on women and gender in the Middle East from the pre-modern to the contemporary.

allCourses.title: Armenians and Armenia in Ancient to Early Modern World History
allCourses.description: A history of Armenia and Armenians from ethnogenesis to the early modern period at the end of the 1700s within a regional and global context. Takes into account interactions and encounters with the empires, and peoples that encompassed their orbit.

allCourses.title: Armenians and Armenia in Modern World History
allCourses.description: Covers the most important themes in the history of Armenians and Armenia in the 19th, 20th, and 21st centuries within a regional (i.e., Middle East and Caucasus) and global context.

allCourses.title: Topics in Islamic History
allCourses.description: The evolution of Islam as a religion within the social, political, and economic histories of various Muslim societies throughout its 14 centuries. Introduces major concepts, practices, and texts of Islam, and key historical events associated with them. Formerly History 131.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Middle Eastern History
allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, intellectual, social, and/or economic histories of one or many regions of the Middle East.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Africa: Societies and Cultures
allCourses.description: Introduction to the variety of cultures, political organizations, social structures, and artistic expressions created by Africans over a broad time span. Indigenous development of African societies in distinct regions of the continent. Issues, themes, processes for understanding history of Africa.

allCourses.title: Modern Africa
allCourses.description: Explores the last 200 years of history in Africa, from the end of the Atlantic slave trade through colonization to independence.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Africa
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of African history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in South African History
allCourses.description: Introduction to important historical events and processes in Southern Africa. Focuses on particular themes and explores how those themes change over time. Topics include: changing ideas about race, the development of class structures, identity formation, the role of gender.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of the African Diaspora
allCourses.description: Examines the causes and consequences of the multiple diasporas of African peoples since the sixteenth century in the Atlantic world, especially the Americas and Europe.

allCourses.title: The Scientific Revolution
allCourses.description: An examination of early modern European science from 1500-1700. Includes primary readings from central figures (Copernicus, Harvey, Bacon, Descartes, et al.); themes include the impact of printing, humanism, patronage, technology, and discussion of the term "revolution" in this context.

allCourses.title: Crossing the World's Oceans: From Sail to Steam
allCourses.description: Explores the basics of oceanography, the evolution of ships and sailing in the ancient Mediterranean world, the North Atlantic, Polynesia, the South China Sea, the Arab Indian Ocean, the global oceanic world, and the discovery of celestial and terrestrial navigation.

allCourses.title: Maps from Prehistory to the Present
allCourses.description: Examines how technology has assisted in creating visual representations of place, space, and time beginning in ancient Babylonia to the present day.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Science and Technology
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of science and technological history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Language Origins: Evolution, Genetics, and the Brain
allCourses.description: Examines how human language(s) may have originated. Studies pertinent techniques (reconstruction) and addresses related questions, including is our language faculty inborn (i.e., genetically encoded)? Can brain imaging and population genetics research help to unlock this mystery of human evolution?.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Medicine and Health Care
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Medicine and Health Care history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Epidemics and Infectious Disease
allCourses.description: Examines how epidemics tax political, economic, and spiritual resources and challenge prevailing medical theories and practices. Looks at how society has responded to epidemics and disease throughout history, beginning in antiquity and ending in the present.

allCourses.title: Surviving Epidemics
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sophomores only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes diverse social and cultural responses to epidemics from mid-nineteenth century to the present, including incarceration, caregiving, and disability rights. Using interdisciplinary materials and collaborative activities, students interpret strategies and outcomes of Indigenous, racialized, and marginalized communities surviving great illness.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Topics in U.S. History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of U.S. history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Colonial America
allCourses.description: Examines the interactions of various African, European, and Native American societies in North America, including social structures, politics, economics, and cultures.

allCourses.title: Revolutionary America:  1740-1790
allCourses.description: An exploration of why 13 continental colonies, whose commercial and cultural connections with Britain far exceed their interaction with one another, resisted imperial reform after 1763 to the point of war in 1775 and independence the following year.

allCourses.title: The United States in the 1890s
allCourses.description: A social, cultural, political history of U.S. in 1890s. Topics: racial politics of Jim Crow; Spanish-American War and conquest of the Philippines; "New Women" and gendering of modern culture; rise of cities, urban reform, labor resistance to new capitalist order.

allCourses.title: California Dreaming: Conquest, Conflict, and Globalization in the Golden State
allCourses.description: California as a case study of national trends and as a unique setting: its specific problems and culture. Major themes include: colonization, immigration, race relations, agricultural development, industrialization, urbanization, working class movements, social conflict, and political reform.

allCourses.title: Topics in American Social and Economic History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of American social and economic history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in American Cultural and Intellectual History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of American cultural and intellectual history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Sex in the U.S. to 1860
allCourses.description: Perspectives on sexual behavior in colonial and U.S. history to c. 1860. Mainstream and non-mainstream sexual practices, beliefs, identities. Asks why various ideas of sexual behavior developed and how they related to religious, racial, ethnic, political, cultural belief systems.

allCourses.title: Gender in Nineteenth-Century America
allCourses.description: A social and cultural history of women's lives in nineteenth-century America, examining how racial, sexual, class identities were constructed by women themselves and by their surrounding culture. Topics include slavery, anti-slavery movement, domesticity, experience of the Civil War.

allCourses.title: Topics in Women and Gender Relations in the United States
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of women and gender relations in the United States. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Education and the American Dream: Historical Perspectives on Democracy and Education
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between public schooling and the promotion of democratic ideals in American society over the past two centuries.

allCourses.title: Topics in Multicultural U.S. History
allCourses.description: Examines the variety of cultural expressions through which the people who came to inhabit the United States historically signify their collective identities.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Veterans in History and Society
allCourses.description: Explores key concepts, issues, and trends in the interdisciplinary field of veterans studies. Students gain a deep understanding of the ways that social scientists and historians have analyzed the identities, experiences, and worldviews of U.S. military veterans.

allCourses.title: Topics in African American History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of African American history.  Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Chicana/Chicano History: Pre-Colonial to 1900
allCourses.description: Examines social history of the southwest region from antiquity to 1900. Discusses major questions, theory and research methods pertinent to Chicanas/Chicanos. Themes include: indigenous empires, conquest, colonialism, social stratification, ideology, marriage, sexuality, industrial capitalism, accommodation and resistance.

allCourses.title: Chicana/Chicano History: Twentieth Century
allCourses.description: Examines social history of the Southwest with emphasis on Mexican-origin people. Discusses major questions, theory and research methods pertinent to Chicana/Chicano history. Themes explored include: immigration, xenophobia, class struggle, leadership, generational cohorts, unionization, education, barrioization, ethnicity, patriarchy, sexuality.

allCourses.title: Latinas in the Twentieth Century U.S.
allCourses.description: Latinas in the U.S. from 1900 to present, offering a diversity of their cultures, regional histories, sexualities, generations, and classes.

allCourses.title: Latina/Latino Pop:  Latina/Latino Popular Culture
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. History Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: With a focus on the politics of language and space/place, prepares students to critically analyze sites of Latina/Latino popular culture including: music, film, performance, sports, media, and varied subcultures.

allCourses.title: Topics in Asian-American History
allCourses.description: Introduction to important themes in the history of people of Asian ancestry in the United States from the nineteenth century to the present.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Asian American Labor
allCourses.description: Explores history of Asian Americans and work from the nineteenth century to the present. Areas of study include migration, colonialism, family, social organization, and work culture.

allCourses.title: Asian American and African American Relations
allCourses.description: Addresses relationships of Asian American and African American communities in the United States. Topics include race, class, gender, labor, economic systems, political mobilization, community, civil rights, activism, cultural expression.

allCourses.title: American Legal History
allCourses.description: Introduction to American legal case materials, to legal categories and ways of thinking, and to selected topics in U.S. legal history. Does not offer a chronological survey of the development of law in the United States.

allCourses.title: American Urban History
allCourses.description: A study of urban communities in the United States, from colonial times to the present. Traces the impact of industrialization and urbanization on social and cultural life, and investigates the significance of urban life for U.S. democratic culture.

allCourses.title: U.S. as a Global Power
allCourses.description: Examines post-World War II cultural, economic, and strategic patterns that have shaped U.S. relations with the world. Presents diverse perspectives on issues such as nationalism, anticommunism, secrecy and covert action, economic influences, the media's role, and race, gender, and class-related.

allCourses.title: Native American History
allCourses.description: Native American history in North America, emphasizing Indigenous perspectives and creative adaptations to changing historical circumstances. Topics may include sovereignty, settler colonialism, treaties, decolonization, Indigeneity; cultural, economic, religious, environmental practices and experiences; and intersections of U.S. and Native histories.

allCourses.title: Asian American Histories
allCourses.description: Examines and compares diverse experiences of major Asian American groups since the mid-nineteenth century. Topics include origins of emigration; the formation and transformation of community; gender and family life; changing roles of Asian Americans in American society. Formerly ASIANAM 60A.

allCourses.title: History of Sexuality in the US
allCourses.description: Explores intertwined histories of sexuality, race, and gender in the US. By examining how different cultures and times viewed sexuality, race, and gender, it analyzes relationships between regulation of bodies/behaviors and construction of cultural, economic, and political norms.

allCourses.title: Memory and Migration: American Families on the Move
allCourses.description: Examines family migration stories as a tool for understanding the intertwined histories of international and domestic migration that have shaped the lives of the diverse peoples of the United States.

allCourses.title: What to Eat? Immigrants and the Development of American Cuisines
allCourses.description: Relationship between immigration and changing American foodways; impact of several major culinary traditions of immigrants and racial minorities, such as African Americans, Asian Americans, Mexican Americans, Italian Americans, Irish Americans, and Jewish Americans, on America’s gastronomical and socioeconomic landscape.

allCourses.title: Racial Segregation in Modern U.S.
allCourses.description: Explores the history of racial segregation in the United States from the late 19th century to the present.

allCourses.title: Sex and Conquest in Latin America
allCourses.description: Competing ideas of masculinity and femininity, sexual violence, sexual identities, and gendered hierarchies informed how the Spanish engaged in military and religious domination of Mexican and Andean communities, as well as the forms of native resistance throughout colonial Latin America.

allCourses.title: Indian and Colonial Societies in Mexico
allCourses.description: Examines the history of Colonial Mexico from prehistoric times to the eighteenth century. Focuses on the social, economic, and political evolution of the new Mexican society which resulted from the "meeting" of two cultures.

allCourses.title: Twentieth-Century Mexico
allCourses.description: Examines the history of contemporary Mexico beginning with the Mexican Revolution and concluding with the present administration. Social, economic, and political effects of the Revolution; formation of a "one-party democracy"; economic transformation of the nation; the present crisis.

allCourses.title: Topics in Brazilian History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Brazilian history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: World of Coffee
allCourses.description: History of consumption and production of coffee over the centuries, and coffee's cultural, economic, social, political consequences. Coffee's social life as a drug, symbol of hospitality, religious rite, sociability and bourgeois lifestyle, commodity, source of livelihoods, imperial revenues, corporate profits.

allCourses.title: Caribbean History: Colonization to Emancipation
allCourses.description: Exploration of the history of the archipelago from pre-Columbian times to the end of slavery; examining the impact of European colonization, decimation of the indigenous populations, African slavery, resistance, and emancipation; the unity and diversity of experience in region.

allCourses.title: Caribbean History: Emancipation to Independence
allCourses.description: Post-emancipation and anti-colonial struggles ending with political independence for most of the region. Examines social, political, economic, cultural dimensions of post-emancipation period, including large-scale migration to Central America, the U.S., and Britain; the region's global cultural and political contribution.

allCourses.title: Race and Empire in Colonial Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores how native people of Latin America with enslaved and free African incorporated and defied Spanish and Portuguese colonization. Focuses on religious adaptions, resistance movements, legal systems, and the emergence of multicultural communities to explain how race shaped European empires.

allCourses.title: Revolution and Memory in Latin America
allCourses.description: Comparison of how Andeans resurrected the leaders of the Inca, a defeated indigenous empire, to contest the Spanish empire with how enslaved Africans, with their descendants and others, defeated Spanish colonial rule in what would become the Cuban nation.

allCourses.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

allCourses.title: Gender, Race, and Nation in Latin America
allCourses.description: Addresses the importance of gender and race to nation-making in Latin America during the 19th and 20th centuries (1810-1945). Considers how hierarchies between men and women shaped ideas about family, the state, and modernity.

allCourses.title: Revolution and Reaction in Cold War Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores Latin American experiences of revolutionary change and military dictatorship during the Cold War (1945-1990). Pays particular attention to the lives of women, peasants, workers, and the urban middle classes. Case studies include Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, Argentina, Nicaragua, and Mexico.

allCourses.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
allCourses.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

allCourses.title: Revolution in Latin America
allCourses.description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada.  Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

allCourses.title: Topics in Latin American History
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Latin American history.  Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: World Religions I
allCourses.description: An introduction to the history, doctrine, culture, and writing of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

allCourses.title: World Religions II
allCourses.description: An introduction to various religious traditions in selected areas of the world—including India and South Asia, East Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

allCourses.title: Religious Dialogue
allCourses.description: Lectures and discussion on controversial topics in religion: sexual morality; religious violence; science; treatment of women and girls; religious truth, American Constitutional matters; secularization; the future of religion, and other topics.

allCourses.title: Ancient India
allCourses.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan.  Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

allCourses.title: Medieval India
allCourses.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

allCourses.title: Premodern East Asia
allCourses.description: Introduction to histories of China, Korea, and Japan from the earliest states to about 1600. Topics include: state formation and dissolution; the role of ideology and how it changes; religious beliefs and values; agriculture, commerce, and industry; changing family values.

allCourses.title: East Asia: 1600-1895
allCourses.description: Introduction to China, Korea, and Japan from about 1600 to 1895. Establishment of Qing Chinese, late Choson Korean, and Tokugawa Japanese sociopolitical orders and their characteristics, plus major cultural developments. Responses to Western impact and the rise of Meiji Japan.

allCourses.title: East Asia Since 1895
allCourses.description: Introduction to the turbulent modern histories of China, Korea, and Japan since 1895. An overarching concern is to understand the evolution of modern East Asia and its place for humankind's future.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Asia
allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of Asia.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Chinese History to 1800
allCourses.description: A survey of the history of China to 1800.

allCourses.title: Chinese History: 1800-1949
allCourses.description: An examination of Chinese society and thought from the late-eighteenth century to the 1949 revolution. Focuses on the role of intellectuals; popular culture; women in Chinese society; developments in commerce and urban life; rebellion; foreign imperialism.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of China
allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of China.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Age of the Samurai
allCourses.description: Topics include the simultaneous elaboration of a civilian aristocratic tradition and the military ethos, the conflict between martial and economic values in the context of an expanding economy, and the development of Japan's indigenous religions, art, and literature.

allCourses.title: Imperial Japan
allCourses.description: Topics in the rise of modern Japan include the relationship between centralization and imperialism, democracy and fascism, industrialization and feminism in the context of the complex and competing forces that shaped Japan's experience in the modern world.

allCourses.title: Postwar Japan
allCourses.description: From the ashes of defeat to economic superpower, from poverty to material consumerism, from the ethic of diligence and fortitude to hedonism. Addresses what these changes have meant for ordinary people, as well as government policy and Japan's international position.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Japan
allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual and religious history of Japan.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Korean History to 1800
allCourses.description: A general survey of the history of Korea to 1800. Focuses on internal sociopolitical development, major cultural trends, and foreign relations. Students are introduced to various interpretive approaches in the historiography.

allCourses.title: Korean History: 1800-1945
allCourses.description: An examination of Korean society and culture in tumultuous transition, focusing on some new challenges for the Choson Dynasty and its abortive reform effort, external imperialist pressures, and the Japanese colonial rule.

allCourses.title: Korean History Since 1945
allCourses.description: Topics include the national liberation, origins of conflict between two rival regimes, South Korea's emergence as a major player in the international political economy, some salient characteristics of the North Korean Marxist state, triumph of democracy, and prospect for reunification.

allCourses.title: Topics in the History of Korea
allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of Korea.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of South Asia.

allCourses.description: Topics include the cultural, political, economic, social, intellectual, and religious history of Southeast Asia.

allCourses.title: The Viet Nam War Seen through Oral History
allCourses.description: Offers an overview of the Viet Nam War; explores the art of doing oral history and the use of oral testimony in research and writing the history of war through conducting oral history interviews with individuals of the war generation.

allCourses.description: Introduction to the diversity of Jewish cultures from ancient to modern times. Surveys the Jewish experience in various societies and civilizations: ancient Mediterranean, Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.

allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.

Topics include organizational theory, group behavior, project management skills, case studies, personal and group productivity tools, management of distributed work, stakeholders, consultants, and knowledge management. Students do a project exercise.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 43 or GDIM 61

allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces concepts and principles of collaborative systems. Topics may include shared workspaces, group interaction, workflow, architectures, interaction between social and technical features of group work, and examples of collaborative systems used in real-world settings. Students develop a simple collaborative application.

allCourses.description: Students undertake projects intended to gather and analyze data from situations in which computers are used, organize and conduct experiments intended to test hypotheses about impacts, and explore the application of concepts learned in previous courses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 162W

allCourses.restriction: Education Sciences Majors only. Informatics Majors only. Informatics Minors only.
allCourses.description: Examines how popular media may impact how young people learn, develop, and communicate by looking at research related to the impacts of a wide range of popular media including television, video games, digital environments, mobile devices, and other multimedia.

allCourses.description: Broad overview of medical informatics for students with varied backgrounds. Electronic medical records, online resources, mobile technologies, patient safety, and computational design. Legal, ethical, and public policy issues. Health systems management. Evaluation and fieldwork for health systems.

allCourses.description: Consumer health informatics is a subfield of health informatics aimed to empower healthcare consumers through a variety of consumer-facing technologies. Covers health behavior change, health literacy, social support, and the design, evaluation, and implementation of major technological applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 171 or PUBHLTH 105. IN4MATX 171 with a grade of C or better. PUBHLTH 105 with a grade of C or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Health Data Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The increasing availability of electronic heath data provides an unprecedented opportunity to use data-driven approaches to improve human health. Equips students with essential skills in curating, managing, and analyzing health data, focusing on electronic health records.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 171 or PUBHLTH 105. IN4MATX 171 with a grade of C or better. PUBHLTH 105 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of informatics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.
allCourses.corequisite: I&C SCI 192 and M&MG 298 and Advisory coreq text.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Methodology for Informatics
allCourses.description: Introduction to strategies and idioms of research in Informatics. Includes examination of issues in scientific inquiry, qualitative and quantitative methods, and research design. Both classic texts and contemporary research literature are read and analyzed.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Information Systems
allCourses.description: Introduction to qualitative research methods used to study computerization and information systems, such as open-ended interviewing, participant observation, and ethnography. Studies of the methods in practice through examination of research literature.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 261 or IN4MATX 251. IN4MATX 261 with a grade of B- or better. IN4MATX 251 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Quantitative Research Methods in Information Systems
allCourses.description: Quantitative research methods used to study computerization and information systems. Design of instruments, sampling, sample sizes, and data analysis. Validity and reliability. Longitudinal versus cross-sectional designs. Analysis of secondary data. Studies of the methods through examination of research literature.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 251 or IN4MATX 261. IN4MATX 251 with a grade of B- or better. IN4MATX 261 with a grade of B- or better. Basic knowledge of elementary statistics is also required.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Doctoral Seminar on Research and Writing
allCourses.description: Doctoral seminar centered on original research and writing. Provides a chance for doctoral students at all levels to present original work, brainstorm ongoing issues, and learn to provide and receive critical feedback from peers.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Informatics
allCourses.description: Current research and research trends in informatics. Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Engineering
allCourses.description: Study of the concepts, methods, and tools for the analysis, design, construction, and measurement of complex software-intensive systems. Underlying principles emphasized. State-of-the-art software engineering and promising research areas covered, including project management.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Analysis of Programming Languages
allCourses.description: Concepts in modern programming languages, their interaction, and the relationship between programming languages and methods for large-scale, extensible software development. Empirical analysis of programming language usage.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Requirements Engineering and Specification
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of rigorous techniques in requirements engineering - requirements definition phase of software development - with focus on modeling and specification. Topics include notations and models for requirements specification; and methods, tools and processes for software requirements elicitation, representation, analysis.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Requirements Engineering and Specification
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Study of rigorous techniques in requirements engineering – requirements definition phase of software development – with focus on modeling and specification. Topics include notations and models for requirements specification; and methods, tools and processes for software requirements elicitation, representation, analysis.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Analysis and Testing
allCourses.description: Studies techniques for developing confidence in software from traditional testing schemes to integrated, multitechnique analytic approaches. Considers strengths and weaknesses and explores opportunities for synergistic technique application. Emphasis is on approaches integrated into the software process.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Processes
allCourses.description: Explores vehicles for modeling, coding, and analyzing software processes. Considers integration of software process programming approaches with traditional management issues. Explores the use of software process execution as a vehicle for effective integration of tools into environments.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Environments
allCourses.description: Study of the requirements, concepts, and architectures of comprehensive, integrated, software development and maintenance environments. Major topics include process support, object management, communication, interoperability, measurement, analysis, and user interfaces in the environment context.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Software Architecture
allCourses.description: Study of the concepts, representation techniques, development methods, and tools for architecture-centric software engineering. Topics include domain-specific software architectures, architectural styles, architecture description languages, software connectors, and dynamism in architectures.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Software Design Techniques
allCourses.description: Study of concepts, representations, techniques, and case studies in structuring software systems, with an emphasis on design considerations. Topics include static and dynamic system structure, data models, abstractions, naming, protocols and application programmer interfaces.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Retrieval, Filtering, and Classification
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Algorithms for the storage, retrieval, filtering, and classification of textual and multimedia data. The vector space model, Boolean and probabilistic queries, and relevance feedback. Latent semantic indexing; collaborative filtering; and relationship to machine learning methods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 161 and COMPSCI 171 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G)

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: User Interface Design and Evaluation
allCourses.description: Introduction to the design and evaluation of user interfaces, with an emphasis on methodology. Cognitive principles, design life cycle, on-line and off-line prototyping techniques. Toolkits and architectures for interactive systems. Evaluation techniques, including heuristic and laboratory methods.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Research in Human-Centered Computing
allCourses.description: Introduction to contemporary topics in human-computer interaction, including methods, technologies, design, and evaluation. Emerging application domains and their challenges to traditional research methods. Advanced architectures and technologies. Critical issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Some familiarity with HCI principles.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Intelligent User Interfaces
allCourses.description: Explores example software systems and their underlying concepts that leverage computing to empower and augment human individuals in their activities. Topics span the fields of user interface design, human-computer interaction, software engineering, and cognitive computing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: COMPSCI 171

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced User Interface Architecture
allCourses.description: Architectural concerns in advanced interactive systems. The design of current and emerging platforms for novel interactive systems. Paradigms such as constraint-based programming, multimodal interaction, and perceptual user interfaces for individual, distributed, and ubiquitous applications.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Usable Security and Privacy
allCourses.restriction: Informatics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Undergraduate degree in Compsci or Informatics is strongly recommended.
allCourses.description: Introduces usability problems in security and privacy methods, tools, and software. Overviews prominent examples of both failures and successes in usable security and privacy. Surveys state-of- the-art techniques and evaluation methodologies.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Ubiquitous Computing
allCourses.description: The "disappearing computer" paradigm. Differences to the desktop computing model: applications, interaction in augmented environments, security, alternate media, small operating systems, sensors, and embedded systems design. Evaluation by project work and class participation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Ubiquitous Computing and Interaction
allCourses.description: Principles and design techniques for ubiquitous computing applications. Conceptual basis for tangible and embodied interaction. Interaction in virtual and augmented environments. Design methods and techniques. Design case studies. Examination by project work.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 231 and IN4MATX 241. IN4MATX 231 with a grade of B- or better. IN4MATX 241 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Embedded and Ubiquitous Systems
allCourses.description: Embedded and ubiquitous system technologies including processors, DSP, memory, and software. System interfacing basics; communication strategies; sensors and actuators, mobile and wireless technology. Using pre-designed hardware and software components. Design case studies in wireless, multimedia, and/or networking domains.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: I&C SCI 51 and COMPSCI 152 and COMPSCI 161 and (I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G or I&C SCI 6D). B.S. degree in Computer Science is also accepted.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer-Supported Cooperative Work
allCourses.description: The role of information systems in supporting work in groups and organizations. Examines various technologies designed to support communication, information sharing, and coordination. Focuses on behavioral and social aspects of designing and using group support technologies.

prerequisite_for.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Information Systems
Quantitative Research Methods in Information Systems

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Social Analysis of Computing
allCourses.description: The social and economic impacts of computing and information technologies on groups, organizations, and society. Topics include computerization and changes in the character of work, social control and privacy, electronic communities, and risks of safety-critical systems to people.

prerequisite_for.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Information Systems
Quantitative Research Methods in Information Systems

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computerization, Work, and Organizations
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the influence of computerization and information systems in transforming work and organizations. Theories of organization and organizational change. Processes by which diverse information technologies influence changes in work and organizations over short and long time periods.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 251 or IN4MATX 261. IN4MATX 251 with a grade of B- or better. IN4MATX 261 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Theories of Information Society
allCourses.description: Social and economic conceptions of information technology. Macrosocial and economic conditions that foster changes in information technologies. Social construction of information and computer technology in professional worlds. Theories of information technology and large-scale social change.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 251 or IN4MATX 261. IN4MATX 251 with a grade of B- or better. IN4MATX 261 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Digital Media and Society
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the technological and social aspects of online interactions, and policy including online games, social media, electronic activism, e-commerce, and digital libraries. Media-theoretic approaches to digital technology. Architectures, infrastructure considerations, and their consequences.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 251 or IN4MATX 261

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The American legal system and its provisions affecting computer systems, computer networks, and information processing. Intellectual property, contracts, privacy, liability for malfunction, computer crime, constitutional issues, transborder data flow, computer-based evidence, and litigation.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Technology in Global Sustainability
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the relationship between recent developments in information technology and the global transition to sustainability. Topics include the role of IT systems in the provision of human needs and wants (e.g., smart grids, food systems, and other IT-enabled infrastructure).

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Overview of Human-Computer Interaction and Design
allCourses.restriction: Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to human-computer interaction and user-centered design. The material is focused on laying the groundwork for understanding the history, importance, and methods of human-computer interaction and design.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: User Needs Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Understanding the user's context, needs, and preferences. Topics include interviews and observations, modeling the context, flow, culture, space, and artifacts involved in an endeavor, ways of aggregating what is found, and presenting these findings to others.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 280. IN4MATX 280 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Overview of Human-Computer Interaction and Design

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Design and Prototyping
allCourses.description: Introduction to user-centered design and prototyping. Focused on practical methods for interaction design. Topics include the nature of design and the challenges to creating and evaluating good designs, as well specific skills for designing interactive systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 280. IN4MATX 280 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Overview of Human-Computer Interaction and Design

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: User Experience Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Evaluating prototypes and completed systems. Topics include comparative analysis, laboratory experiments, heuristic evaluation, cognitive walkthroughs, surveys, clickstreams, and help-desk.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 280. IN4MATX 280 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Overview of Human-Computer Interaction and Design

prerequisite_for.title: Capstone Project in HCI and Design

allCourses.title: Advanced Design and Prototyping
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Develop and communicate interactive technology design prototypes. Moving concepts from brainstorming and paper prototypes to wireframe and limited functionality mock-ups.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 282. IN4MATX 282 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_for.title: Capstone Project in HCI and Design

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Interactive Technology Studio
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Hum Com Interact Des Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Technologies, languages, and skills required for creating prototypes to communicate interactive technology concepts. Topics include HTTP, CSS, CSS scripting, AJAX, Design Patterns, Javascript, Javascript libraries such as jQuery, SQL, MVC, and cloud architectures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 280. IN4MATX 280 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Overview of Human-Computer Interaction and Design

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Innovations in HCI and Design
allCourses.description: Recent social and technological developments in human-computer interaction and design. Topics will vary as the field progresses but include novel input techniques, novel platforms, and innovations in theory and methods of design.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 280. IN4MATX 280 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Project in HCI and Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Human Comp Interact and Design Majors only.
allCourses.description: Group project that reinforces all concepts learned in this program, including knowing where user experience work is most appropriate and essential, and executing the appropriate steps.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 283 and IN4MATX 284. IN4MATX 283 with a grade of B- or better. IN4MATX 284 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Capstone Project and Portfolio
allCourses.description: Completion of capstone projects and development of portfolios. Ideation, critique, development, and critique.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 287. IN4MATX 287 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Applying Human-Computer Interaction and Design in Industry
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students only. Graduate students only. Human Comp Interact and Design Majors only.
allCourses.description: Selected topics related to understanding and applying human-computer interaction and design concepts and practices within the User Experience industry. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress. Presentation of problem areas and related work. Specific goals and progress of research.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Literature Survey in Software Engineering
allCourses.description: Reading and analysis of relevant literature in Software Engineering under the direction of a faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of informatics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Thesis Supervision
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Informatics Core Course I
allCourses.restriction: IN4MATX 41 may not be taken for credit if taken after I&C SCI 22 or CSE 22.
allCourses.description: Fundamental concepts of computer software design and construction. Data, algorithms, functions, and abstractions. Overview of computer systems: data representation, architectural components, operating systems, networks. Introduction to information systems: parties involved, architectural alternatives, usability, organizational and social concerns.

prerequisite_for.title: Mathematics and Computation in the Digital Age: Introduction to Image Processing

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Informatics Core Course II
allCourses.description: Alternative data structure implementations; analysis of time and space efficiency. Object-oriented programming concepts and techniques: classes, objects, inheritance, interfaces. Formal languages and automata. Problem modeling and design tradeoffs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 41. IN4MATX 41 with a grade of C or better.

prerequisite_for.title: Honors Introduction to Computer Science III

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Software Engineering
allCourses.restriction: School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment. Computer Science Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Concepts, methods, and current practice of software engineering. Large-scale software production, software life cycle models, principles and techniques for each stage of development.

allCourses.description: Introduction to current research topics in Informatics. Various faculty members present current research and relate it to the course content of the Informatics degree program.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Patterns of Software Construction
allCourses.description: Building software applications; reusing and integrating components; designing for reuse. Effective use of libraries and APIs, file and network I/O, creation of user interfaces.
