allCourses.title: Health, Wellness, and Conception of the Body
allCourses.description: Asks what is health and who gets to have it? What is considered a “healthy” or “sick” body? We analyze historical and contemporary experiences of illness, medicine, and caregiving, including how patients represent their bodies and healing.

allCourses.title: Surviving Epidemics
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sophomores only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes diverse social and cultural responses to epidemics from mid-nineteenth century to the present, including incarceration, caregiving, and disability rights. Using interdisciplinary materials and collaborative activities, students interpret strategies and outcomes of Indigenous, racialized, and marginalized communities surviving great illness.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Capstone Seminar: The Clinical Moral Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of the clinical encounter, and the importance of meaning making in these “moral laboratories.” Students enter the clinical space as participant observers, and reflect on how the clinical site informs and challenges reading practices.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MED HUM 1 or MED HUM 3 or GEN&SEX 60A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Critical Perspectives in Medical Humanities
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes social and cultural understandings of the body, health, illness, medicine, and disease. Themes include critical histories of the body; non-compliant subjects interacting with medicine; racial-sexual hierarchies of health; and theories and expressions of pain and suffering.

allCourses.title: Art and Medicine
allCourses.description: Analyzes the relationship between medicine and the visual arts from the late medieval to modern periods, covering topics such as anatomy, optical medical technologies, gender and race in medicine, and popular representations of disease and doctors.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Business and Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Rigorous overview of major business functions and management topics. Addresses the global and fast-changing environment in which modern business enterprises operate as well as the challenges posed by concerns about sustainable growth, ethics, and social responsibility.

allCourses.title: Business Management in the World Today
allCourses.description: Accounting scandals, e-commerce, and globalization are only a few examples that show the profound impact of business practices on individuals and on society at large. Provides students with a broad overview of business functions and management practices.

allCourses.title: Management Science
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Concepts and methods of management science, which applies mathematical modeling and analysis to management problems. Topics include linear and integer programming, project scheduling, inventory management, queuing analysis, decision analysis, and simulation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 7

prerequisite_list.title: Probability and Statistics in Economics I
Probability and Statistics in Economics II

allCourses.title: Managing Organizational Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic theory and concepts which provide the manager with tools for understanding behavior of people in organizations. Areas such as individual, group, and organizational determinants of attitudes, turnover, and job performance.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Marketing
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic marketing concepts; discussion of the role marketing plays in modern society. Topics include industrial and consumer marketing, promotion, distribution, and pricing theory.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Management Information Systems
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Information Technology (IT) continues to drive rapid productivity growth and structural changes in the economy. Topics include what IT is, and how companies can use IT to improve business processes, enhance customer services, and gain competitive advantage over rivals.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Managerial Finance
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basics of financial administration. Capital budgeting, cost of capital, cash budgeting, working capital management, and long-term sources of funds. Provides a basic understanding of issues and techniques involved in financial decision making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B and MGMT 30A

allCourses.title: Strategic Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses management of the entire business.  Role of the general manager in organizations, industry analysis, core competencies, growth through vertical integration, innovation, acquisition and diversification, globalization, strategy implementation, and the ethical and moral responsibility of a manager.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 102 and MGMT 105 and MGMT 109

allCourses.title: China and the Global Order
allCourses.description: Introduces students to China's economic and military relations with the world, assessment of likelihood for conflict, and how to strategically manage business risk from regional conflict. Includes an original documentary series and engaging discussion.

allCourses.title: New Ventures: A Course in Entrepreneurship
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the survival and growth of new ventures. Methods include analysis of live cases, guest speakers, discussion, and field projects with contemporary new ventures to learn about new venture management and surviving the liabilities of newness.

allCourses.title: Lean Startup
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Based on the well-known Lean Launchpad course currently used by a growing segment of the startup world. Students work in teams to ideate, develop a Business Model Canvas, and gather customer/market feedback.

allCourses.title: Global Strategies
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the phenomena of technology and globalization and the impact on global business strategy.  Macro approach considers implications for development of flexible yet focused business strategy and creative and agile execution of policies. Class discussions are stimulated by case analyses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 102.

allCourses.title: Managing Organizational Change
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the implementation of change. Identifies the features of successful changes in organizations of varying sizes and configurations, with an emphasis on the reasons why individuals resist or embrace change.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 1

allCourses.title: Human Resources Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Using hands-on projects, case discussions, and video demonstrations, students learn how to use HR analytics to make strategic decisions. These skills benefit students who plan to enter management, consulting, or HR Analytics. No prior analytical training is necessary.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 102

allCourses.title: Communication in Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addressing communication at three levels - interpersonal, group or meeting, and organizational. Focuses on dealing with conflict, interpersonal problems, being effective in meetings, and getting your message heard. Experiential course.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 102.

allCourses.title: Creativity and Leadership in Entrepreneurial Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Uses activities, experiments, readings, and reflections to develop the skills, self-awareness, and confidence to be more creative. Then uses examples, case studies, and a group project to put creativity into practice—i.e., to innovate—to solve worthwhile problems.

allCourses.title: Human Resources Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theory and practice of managing human resources. Students identify and analyze HR dilemmas, apply labor law, and design systems and processes to develop the human resources needed to help organizations achieve their goals.

allCourses.title: Negotiations
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The objective is to assist students in developing an understanding of different theoretical perspectives and develop their skills in negotiating. Exploration of feelings and beliefs about negotiation, negotiation skills, and putting theory into action by practicing new negotiation skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 102

allCourses.title: Foundations of Teams
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Social and psychological processes that detract from effective teamwork and collaboration. Tools to understand how to be a better team member are introduced. Provides the foundation for students to become effective team leaders and to manage difficult team situations.

allCourses.title: Business Ethics
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Comprehensive introduction to ethical considerations in business with a focus on awareness to the complexity of ethical decision-making and how to make choices from a standpoint of ethical consciousness.

allCourses.title: International Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Impact of different cultures and political/economic systems on assumptions, expectations, and organizational practices relevant to conducting business in different national settings. Understanding of the challenges of cross-national management and resources utilized to work and conduct business outside the United States.

allCourses.title: Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Case analyses, free-form discussion, and written assignments designed to develop critical thinking skills, as well as knowledge of approaches to differing leadership challenges. Experiential exercises encourage students to develop their ability to innovate, foster collaboration, manage conflict, and value diversity.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 102

allCourses.title: Intermediate Accounting I
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: First course in a series of two intermediate-level courses in financial accounting theory and practice. Concepts include the measurement, valuation, and reporting of current and long-term assets, current liabilities, and revenue recognition issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 30A or ECON 25

allCourses.title: Intermediate Accounting II
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Second course in a series of two intermediate-level courses in financial accounting theory and practice. Concepts include the measurement, valuation, and reporting of long-term liabilities and contingencies, accounting for stockholders' equity, and the Statement of Cash Flows.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 131A

allCourses.title: Intermediate Accounting III
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Third in a three-part series (A, B, and C). Focuses on developing knowledge related to investments, debt/equity issues, accounting for income taxes, pensions, leases, and revenue recognition.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 131B

allCourses.title: Individual Taxation
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of federal income taxation pertaining to individuals. Topics include income, deductions, credits, property transactions, and the impact of taxes on business and investment decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 30B

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Taxation
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Taxation topics of particular interest to undergraduate students.  Course content may vary each term depending on the interests of the instructors and the students.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 132A.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Corporate and Partnership Taxation
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of federal income taxation pertaining to partnerships and corporations, including subchapter S corporations. Emphasis on the tax issues associated with formation, operation, and termination of these entities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 132A

allCourses.title: Data Analytics in Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with an understanding of data types and sources and how to apply and leverage analytical techniques in making financial and managerial accounting decisions.  Business and ethical issues surrounding the collection and use of Big Data are also discussed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 30B

allCourses.title: Accounting Information Systems & Spreadsheets
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of accounting information systems including internal controls and transaction processing cycles. Development of efficient spreadsheets as applied to financial and managerial accounting concepts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 30B

allCourses.title: Advanced Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers advanced concepts in accounting theory and practice. Topics include business combinations, consolidated financial statements, foreign exchange transactions, international, and governmental/nonprofit accounting standards.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 131B

allCourses.title: Auditing
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to auditing practice with emphasis on the verification of financial statements and related information. Topics include professional ethics, assessment of audit risk, study and evaluation of internal control, gathering and evaluating audit evidence, and audit reporting.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 131B

allCourses.title: Investments
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Foundations of investment management.  Theory and empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, asset pricing models, factor models, and option pricing theory. Students are expected to combine market research results and electronic information sources to create optimal investment strategies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 109

allCourses.title: Bonds and Fixed Income
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides coverage of topics in fixed income securities. Examines bond pricing and yield calculation, duration and convexity, term structure of interest rates, treasure bond market and corporate debt market. Helps students understand and manage risks of fixed income securities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 109

allCourses.title: Multinational Finance
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on financial issues facing multinational corporations, the most important of which is the management of foreign exchange risk. Introduction to investments and financing decisions in international capital markets.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 109 and (ECON 20A or MGMT 4A) and (ECON 20B or MGMT 4B)

allCourses.title: FinTech
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides working knowledge of economic mechanisms in areas of FinTech. Identifying and analyzing important issues through a balance of qualitative analysis and quantitative applications. Topics covered include Bitcoin, Blockchain, Crowdfunding, peer-to-peer lending, robo-advisor, and their economic and social impacts.

allCourses.title: Introduction to the Real Estate Process
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introductory survey course providing a working knowledge of the real estate market, both residential and commercial. Topics include real estate economics, appraisal, feasibility, investment, tax considerations, financing, and development. Lectures and cases, with supplemental presentations by real estate professionals.

allCourses.title: Cases in Corporate Financial Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Case study course designed to confront students with real-world corporate finance problems and provide an active learning experience. Introduces advanced analytical tools/techniques and provides an integrated framework for value-based financial management in a broad range of corporate settings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 109 and MGMT 141

allCourses.title: Derivatives
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to financial derivatives. Covers forward contracts, futures, swaps, and options. Applications of these instruments, including pricing and risk management, are emphasized.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 109 and MGMT 141

allCourses.title: Consumer Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Application of the behavioral sciences to understanding buyer behavior.  Topics include perception, memory, affect, learning, persuasion, motivation, behavioral decision theory, social and culture influences, and managerial implications.

allCourses.title: Marketing Research
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Research to aid managerial decisions for products and services; problem formulation, research design, data collection, sampling, statistical analyses, managerial recommendations, and implementation in several real-world settings.

allCourses.title: New Product Development
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Identifying markets, developing product ideas, measuring consumer preferences, positioning and designing products, and forecasting their sales.  Hands-on experience with software to conduct various analyses useful in new product development, such as cluster analysis, factor analysis, and conjoint analysis.

allCourses.title: Sales Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed for students interested in learning about sales force management and personal selling by firms engaged in business-to-business and consumer goods/services marketing. Covers advantages of personal selling, how to perform sales calls, challenges of sales managers, roles of buying centers.

allCourses.title: Global Marketing
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students are exposed to the challenges and opportunities facing marketers in the international marketplace. Special attention is given to the management of cultural differences in product development, distribution systems, pricing, and promotion.

allCourses.title: Brand Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to issues in planning, implementing, and evaluating brand strategies, relevant theories, models, and tools for the making of brand decisions; application of these principles.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 105

allCourses.title: Pricing Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides a framework for designing and analyzing pricing strategies. Emphasizes role of pricing in the marketing-mix decisions and broader marketing strategy of a firm. Incorporates study of various economic, psychological, competitive, and organizational foundations that enter into effective pricing decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 105

allCourses.title: Marketing on the Internet
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Recent developments in interactive technologies indicate that marketing on the internet is becoming a serious business activity, with exponential growth. How to do marketing on the Internet and identify the key issues pertaining to the marketing process.

allCourses.title: Digital Media Marketing Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Entails developing digital marketing strategy across numerous digital marketing platforms; understanding digital native consumers and newer consumer.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 105

allCourses.title: Analysis of Marketing Data
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides opportunity to learn and apply analytical skills to marketing datasets to unveil hidden patterns and truths, to measure and quantify the performance differences between different initiatives, and to inform decision-making in an increasingly digital world.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 105

allCourses.title: Leadership Opportunities in Global Sustainability
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Seeks to address critical issues and reviews how leaders and stakeholders deal with those issues; including the concept of sustainability, “the ability to endure,” and climate change. Addresses “sustainable development.” Explores critical views; pro-business views, skepticism and global warming denial.

allCourses.title: U.S. Healthcare Systems
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Providers, suppliers, payers, consumers, and the unique market dynamics among these players. Structure, organization, and financing of health care. The health care industry's relationship to the overall economy will be explored.

allCourses.title: Business of Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: In order to improve the quality and efficiency of health care delivery one must understand the design and management of health care operations. Opportunities for innovation and changes needed to design a simple, accessible, fair, and effective health care system.

allCourses.title: Business of Science
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Business acumen and strategic planning are determining success. Billions spent on advertising, and the lack of effectiveness of drugs are generally ignored. Considering this is a matter of life and death for many, should there be a "Business" of Science.

allCourses.title: Economics of Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Applies key concepts of game theory to the analysis of the strategic behavior of profit-maximizing firms.  Simultaneous move games, sequential games, credibility and commitment, repeated games, pure and mixed strategies, signaling, and screening.  Lecture and problem sets.  Group projects.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ECON 20A and ECON 20B

allCourses.title: Applied Econometrics for Business
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Bridge between an introductory statistics course and a course in econometrics.  Oriented toward the ways in which economists use data to motivate and test economic theories.  How to locate economics data, analyze, and appropriately interpret these data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ECON 20A and ECON 20B.

allCourses.title: Technologies for Business
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introductory course that include hands-on exposure to powerful, high-level tools for using computers in business situations more effectively. Next-generation graphical user interfaces, Internet applications, client/server technology, information security, and wireless.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 107.

allCourses.title: Social Media
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Business Information Mgmt Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers theoretical aspects and business applications of social media tools including blogs, wikis, social networking platforms, immersive environments, and other social computing technologies. Also covers business value of social-media-enabled processes.

allCourses.title: Data and Programming for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Challenges and teaches students how to handle data that come in a variety of forms and sizes. Guides students through the whole data management process, from initial data acquisition to final data analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Previous experience with programming languages (preferably Python).

allCourses.title: Business Intelligence for Analytical Decisions
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: BI from both managerial and technical perspectives. Learn to apply a variety of data mining techniques to learn business intelligence embedded in data, and apply that intelligence to run your business more efficiently. These techniques are useful in different areas.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 107

allCourses.title: Business Data Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Query, manipulate, and understand data and learn about leading edge applications for databases.  Database fundamentals including entity relationship design, creating database tables, normalization, and data querying.  Contemporary applications of database using case studies.  Applications include data warehousing, data mining.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 107

allCourses.title: Information Technology (IT) and Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Strategic and competitive uses of IT and the Internet. Globalization and firm competition; alignment of IT with business strategy; business value of IT; business transformations with IT; implications of offshoring and outsourcing; strategy and IT in the Internet era.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 107.

allCourses.title: Digital Strategies
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Covers business strategies for firms that make technology products. Insights are applicable not only to industries that make information and technology goods but also to industries that leverage digitization and network effects for their products.

allCourses.title: Management of Information Technology
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Strategic use and impact of information technology (IT) in organizations. Covers what IT is, and how it works, business value of IT, and IT strategies that organizations can employ to create value.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 107

allCourses.title: Business Data Communications and Security
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis, technology integration, and technology choices involved with deploying, managing, and securing effective data communications systems, local area networks, Internet, intranet, and wide area networks.  Fundamental concepts, as well as enabling technologies that can provide a strategic advantage to firms.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 107.

allCourses.title: Business Forecasting
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Forecasts are critical inputs into the wide range of business decision making.  Users include accountants, financial experts, human resource managers, production managers, and marketing people.  Methodologies used to support business decision making.  Computer-oriented approach.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 101

allCourses.title: Supply Chain Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Flows of materials and information among all of the firms that contribute to a product or service. Forecasting, demand management, logistical networks, inventory management, supplier contracting, sourcing, information technology, flexibility, globalization, and performance management.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 101

allCourses.title: Optimization in Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Firms attempt to maximize profit or minimize cost.  Linear, integer, and nonlinear programming models in functional areas of business such as finance, marketing, and operations. Solutions via computer and interpretation of output in a managerially significant way.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 101.

allCourses.title: Operations Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Managing the productive resources, from which raw materials as inputs are being transformed into useful outputs of final products and services. Explanation of issues pertaining to both manufacturing and services-oriented systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 101

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Management
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of management. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Business Communication
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with a solid foundation in business communication. Emphasis is placed on improving students' written and oral communication skills to help them succeed in (1) upper-division Business Administration courses, (2) graduate school, and (3) work and career activities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Business Law
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A study of the legal environment of business.  Topics include contracts, agency, partnerships, corporations, and other basic principles of law as they relate to business transactions.

allCourses.title: The Ethical Environment of Business
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The political, social, and ethical environment of business. Topics include the historical development of American business, competitiveness problems, corporate social responsibility, corporate governance, and government regulation of business.

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Study of financial statements and their related footnotes; tools and procedures common to financial statement analysis; relationships among business transactions, environmental forces (political, economic, social), and reported financial statement information; how financial statement information can help solve certain business problems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 30A and MGMT 30B

allCourses.title: Experiential Development of a Global Business Perspective
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Opportunity for students to consider historical and modern global businesses, governmental, and non-profit operations in Switzerland. Effectively provides live case studies for analysis of global interrelatedness.

allCourses.title: Decision Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Use of decision analysis digital technologies for multiple objective decisions under certainty; decision-making under risk using decision trees; fitting probability distributions to judgments or data; and Monte Carlo simulation, applied to business, government, not-for-profit, and personal decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 101

allCourses.title: Predictive Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses prediction and classification problems in the management context via statistical learning. Provides an overview of modern methodologies in forecasting and data mining including multiple regression, decision trees, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor, support vector machines, and neural nets.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 101

allCourses.title: Administrative Internship
allCourses.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Administrative Internship
allCourses.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Administrative Internship
allCourses.description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Management of Innovative Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Using concepts from organization studies and strategy, students examine different frameworks for analyzing and designing innovative organizations, the foundations of strategy and competitive analysis, alliances and networks as a source of innovation, and key issues in managing innovation effectiveness.

allCourses.title: Statistics for Management
allCourses.description: Methods of statistical inference, emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems.  Topics: classical estimation and hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, decision analysis, and forecasting.

allCourses.title: Management Science
allCourses.description: Introduction to management science tools for aiding managerial decision making with emphasis on model applicability, formulation, and interpretation. Use of computer laboratory’s management science software packages. Topics: mathematical programming, stochastic processes, queueing systems, simulation.

allCourses.title: Organizational Analysis for Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Develops a better understanding of the causes and consequences of individual and group behavior, and the frameworks by which to analyze and understand complex organizations; and enhances the skills required to manage and lead an organization.

allCourses.title: Financial Accounting for Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Examines issues related to measuring and communicating an entity's economic activities and financial position and introduces financial statement analysis. The aim of financial accounting is to provide financial information that is useful in making economic decisions.

allCourses.title: Microeconomics for Management
allCourses.restriction: Executive M.B.A. students only.
allCourses.description: Provides basic tools for analyzing economic decisions of consumers and firms, the determinants and consequences of market structure and market failure.  Topics include demand and supply analysis, production and cost theory, perfect competition, monopoly, and introductory game theory.

allCourses.title: Macroeconomics for Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the use of macroeconomic analysis to manage the business cycle for competitive advantage. Such "business cycle-sensitive" management is explored within the context of marketing, operations management, HRM, merger and acquisition activity, and capital financing and expenditures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 204A.

allCourses.title: Marketing Management
allCourses.restriction: Fully Employed M.B.A. Program students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the field of marketing.  Objectives include developing familiarity with fundamental concepts, theories, and techniques in marketing and acquainting students with the type of decisions made by marketing managers including customer targeting, product, pricing, distribution, promotion, and research.

allCourses.title: Business and Government
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the many non-market issues that affect today's managers, such as:  environmental protection, health and safety, intellectual property protection, antitrust, and lobbying.  An interdisciplinary approach using economics, political science, public policy and law.

allCourses.title: Operations Management
allCourses.description: Introduction to strategic and tactical issues in production and operations management.  A blend of quantitative and qualitative considerations.  Topics: product planning, process design, capacity management, production planning, inventory control, distribution management, just-in-time manufacturing, quality management.

allCourses.title: Business Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the functions and responsibilities of senior management and the decisions that determine the direction of the organization and shape its future. Introduces students to concepts, frameworks, and analytical techniques firms use to analyze strategic issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 202 and MGMT 205 and MGMT 209A.

allCourses.title: Individual Directed Study
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.

allCourses.title: Principles of Accounting I
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: First in a two course introductory series. Emphasis on financial accounting concepts and practices essential to the administration of business enterprises; including recording and valuation of financial transactions, and preparation, analysis, and interpretation of financial statements.

allCourses.title: Principles of Accounting II
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Second in a two-course introductory series. Emphasis is on the introduction of managerial accounting concepts and techniques as tools to aid management in carrying out the primary internal functions of planning, control, and decision-making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 30A

allCourses.title: Basic Economics for Managers I
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4A may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20A.
allCourses.description: Microeconomic principles for managers. Useful applications of basic economic principles to situations in business as well as in various professions.

allCourses.title: Basic Economics for Managers II
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment. For School of Social Sciences majors, MGMT 4B may not be used as a substitute for ECON 20B.
allCourses.description: Macroeconomic principles for managers. Useful applications of basic economic principles to situations in business as well as in various professions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT 4A or ECON 20A

allCourses.title: Management of Contemporary Organizations
allCourses.description: Equips students with working knowledge of several major subject areas within the context of business and society studies. Topics include:  role of management in organizations, corporate social responsibility and responsiveness, ethics and values in business, government regulation, and international business.

allCourses.title: Statistics for Business Decision Making
allCourses.restriction: Business Administration Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basics of data analysis and the fundamental notion of statistical inference emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Classical estimation and hypotheses testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, nonparametric methods, and statistical probability.

allCourses.description: Focuses on the strategic and organizational challenges that a rapidly changing environment poses to the firm’s management and frames them according to Merage’s strategic emphasis on analytical decision making, innovation, and information technology.

allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches the graduating MBA how the best managers actually manage. Students develop a toolkit of proven concepts and practices that will help them succeed as managers at any level.

allCourses.title: Negotiations For Executives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Using a combination of theory and practice via negotiation simulations, students expand their repertoire of negotiating skills and develop their ability to analyze different negotiation situations and contexts. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Leadership Strategies
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Provides insights/perspectives about the study and development of leadership.  Helps students answer three questions: Where am I currently as a leader? What tools can I use to improve my leadership? What is my plan for the future as a leader?.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 200 and MGMT EP 202.

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 203A.

allCourses.title: Corporate Valuation
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Studies cases that expand concepts covered in the introductory corporate finance course and focuses on estimating the value of firms and projects in diverse settings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 209A

allCourses.title: Strategic Brand Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Brand management will increase student understanding of important issues in planning, implementing, and evaluating brand strategies; provides relevant theories, models, and tools for making brand decisions; enable students to apply these principles in a computer simulation of brand management.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT EP 205.

allCourses.title: Decision Analysis for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Models of preferences and uncertainty; exercises in creative problem solving. Assessment and use of preference models for private, public, and not-for-profit decision making. Assessment and use of subjective probabilities in decision making. Every other weekend course format.
