allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of business. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Special Topic ITM Seminars
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Each quarter a number of special topic ITM seminars are offered in the 294 series.  Examples of possible topics include Business Intelligence, Technologies for Ecommerce.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Global Business
allCourses.description: Emphasizes and reinforces international perspectives contained in the MBA curriculum by providing a week-long intensive seminar abroad in the second year.  Scholars and business people from the host country instruct EMBA students in designed class sessions and company visits.

allCourses.title: Global Business I for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of global strategy, economics, and financial issues. Topics include global manager’s environment, global strategy, impact of national culture on business systems, strategies and practices, foreign direct investment, corporate governance, human resources, and international marketing. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Global Business II for Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes and reinforces international perspectives contained in the M.B.A. curriculum by providing a week-long intensive seminar abroad in the second year. Scholars and business people from the host country instruct Executive M.B.A. students in designed class sessions and company visits.

allCourses.title: Executive Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Executive Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the conceptual, practical, and personal dimensions of executive leadership. Past and current leadership theories are addressed. Individual personal assessment and diagnosis. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Individual Study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Thinking Strategically in the Digital Age for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the strategic and organizational challenges that a rapidly changing environment poses to the firm’s management and frames them according to Merage’s strategic emphasis on analytical decision making, innovation, and information technology.

prerequisite_for.title: Strategy for Managers: Foundations and Dynamics

allCourses.title: Business Analytics: Decision-Making for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Methods of statistical inference, emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Topics include classical estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, decision analysis, and forecasting. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Management Science for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Uses both prescriptive analysis and risk analysis to explore linear programming models, network problems, and simulation. The goal is to introduce and help students acquire some skills of logical thinking with formal models and improve students’ decision making capability.

allCourses.title: Organizational Leadership for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Develops a better understanding of individual and group behavior in and across organizations; the frameworks by which to analyze and understand behavior in complex organizations; and enhances the skills required to manage collaboration and lead. Evening or weekend course format.

prerequisite_for.title: Strategy for Managers: Foundations and Dynamics
Organizational Change in a Digital World for Managers

allCourses.title: Financial Reporting for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Involves the development, analysis, and interpretation of financial accounting information for external reporting purposes. Emphasis on measurement and valuation issues in decision-making problems and cases. Evening or weekend course format.

prerequisite_for.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation for Managers I
Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation for Managers II
Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation I

allCourses.title: Driving Profitability Through Managerial Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches skills for making vital strategic and tactical decisions (e.g., outsourcing; adding/dropping product lines), to maximize profitability while managing risk. Also covers managerial tools (e.g., budgeting, cost-volume-profit analysis) to drive strategy implementation and incentivize employees. Taught in an evening/weekend format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 203A or MGMTMBA 203A. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of B- or better. MGMTMBA 203A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Microeconomics for Managers in the Digital Age
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides basic tools for analyzing economic decisions, the determinants and consequences of market structure and market failure. Topics include demand and supply analysis, production and cost theory, perfect competition, monopoly, and introductory game theory. Evening and weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Macroeconomics for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Business Administration Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces use of macroeconomic analysis to manage the business cycle for competitive advantage. "Business cycle-sensitive" management is explored within the context of marketing, operations management, HRM, merger and acquisition activity, and capital financing and expenditures. Evening and weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 204A or MGMTMBA 204A. MGMT FE 204A with a grade of B- or better. MGMTMBA 204A with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Microeconomics for Managers in the Digital Age
Microeconomics for Management in the Digital Age

allCourses.title: Marketing Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to marketing. Develops familiarity with fundamental concepts, theories, and techniques in marketing and acquaints students with the type of decisions made by marketing managers including customer targeting, product, pricing, placement, promotion, and research. Evening or weekend course format.

prerequisite_for.title: Strategy for Managers: Foundations and Dynamics

allCourses.title: Business and Government for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the many non-market issues that affect today's managers, such as environment protection, health and safety, intellectual property protection, antitrust, and lobbying. Takes an interdisciplinary approach using economics, political science, public policy, and law. Evening and weekend course.

allCourses.title: Competing with Digital
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the technological and managerial issues surrounding the development and use of IT in organizations. Examines how technology can be used to execute an organization's business strategy and to enable new, innovative business strategies. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Operational Excellence: Processes, Principles, and Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to strategic and tactical issues in production and operations management. Blend of quantitative and qualitative considerations. Topics include product planning, process design, capacity management, production planning, inventory control, distribution management, just-in-time manufacturing, quality management. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Finance for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to financial theory and concepts. Topics include time value of money, valuation of stocks and bonds, capital budgeting, portfolio theory, and capital structure choice. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MGMT FE 201A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MGMT FE 203A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MGMT FE 204A"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 201A and MGMT FE 203A and MGMT FE 204A. MGMT FE 201A with a grade of B- or better. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of B- or better. MGMT FE 204A with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Microeconomics for Managers in the Digital Age

prerequisite_for.title: Strategy for Managers: Foundations and Dynamics

allCourses.title: Investments for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Foundations of investment management. Theory and empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, and valuation models for equities, bonds, and options. Emphasis on practical applications, including optimal investment strategies. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Strategy for Managers: Foundations and Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides conceptual frameworks and techniques to analyze and develop firm strategies. Through case analysis and discussion, helps improve strategic thinking by developing frameworks by which to assess, evaluate, and respond to different business situations. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MGMT FE 200"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MGMT FE 202"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MGMT FE 205"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "MGMT FE 209A"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 200 and MGMT FE 202 and MGMT FE 205 and MGMT FE 209A. MGMT FE 200 with a grade of B- or better. MGMT FE 202 with a grade of B- or better. MGMT FE 205 with a grade of B- or better. MGMT FE 209A with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Thinking Strategically in the Digital Age for Managers

allCourses.title: Networks, Platforms, and Ecosystems
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on unique strategic issues raised by multi-sided platform businesses that facilitate interaction among different parties. Combining economic theory and case examples to unpack subtle factors making multi-sided businesses different. From value propositions to pricing strategies to design decisions.

allCourses.title: Corporate Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how firms should assemble resources in-house, ally with partners, or acquire firms to grow and thrive. Learn the tools necessary to develop and evaluate a corporate strategy and to become an effective strategist, consultant, or analyst.

allCourses.title: New Venture Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches students how to launch and manage new businesses. Provides an overview of the start-up process, including how to identify new business opportunities and develop sound operating models, value new ventures, and understand capital financing. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Entrepreneurship
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: A project course in which student teams develop a business plan to launch a new venture. Drafts of sections of the plan are due throughout the course. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Strategy in a Digital Age
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on applying unchanging basic principles of strategy, economics, and organization to digital technologies. Studies historical and contemporary competitive situations to work out key underlying digital mechanisms that shape competition over time.

allCourses.title: Strategic Innovation for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how innovations are created inside and outside the firm and are diffused to the market. Focuses on competition in technology-based industries, but also considers how innovation can transform established industries, for better or for worse.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 210 or MGMTMBA 210. MGMT FE 210 with a grade of C or better. MGMTMBA 210 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Competitive Intelligence for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how to design a competitive intelligence program, which is a core foundation upon which competitive strategies and execution tactics are developed, assessed, and modified. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Business Dynamics for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Masters of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Business Dynamics enhance analytical skills by analyzing complex challenges that businesses face and to quickly implement a winning response. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 210.

prerequisite_list.title: Strategy for Managers: Foundations and Dynamics

allCourses.title: Practice of General Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to teach the graduating M.B.A. students how the best managers actually manage. Students will develop a toolkit of proven concepts and practices that will help them succeed as managers at any level.

allCourses.title: Organizational Change in a Digital World for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the implementation of change. Identifies the features of successful changes in organizations of varying sizes and configurations, with an emphasis on the reasons why individuals resist or embrace change. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 202 or MGMTMBA 202. MGMT FE 202 with a grade of B- or better. MGMTMBA 202 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Performance Management in 21st Century Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The key to sustained competitive advantage in a 21st century organization. Performance management is all about aligning employee attitudes and behaviors with firm goals and performance.

allCourses.title: The Future of Work: Analyzing Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Analyzing the work that organizations do, looking for the "knowns" and “unknowns” then using variables that are clearest to draw firmer conclusions, while drawing weaker best possible guesses for those that are less clear, understanding the boundaries they represent.

allCourses.title: Negotiations For Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Using a combination of theory and practice via negotiation simulations, students expand their repertoire of negotiating skills and develop their ability to analyze different negotiation situations and contexts. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Global Negotiations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes economic, political, social, and cultural environments of international business negotiations. Topics include self-assessment/analysis, environmental analysis, international team building, negotiation processes and strategies, resources, skills, pre-negotiation preparations, agreements, and post-contract negotiations. Specific emphasis will be placed on cross-cultural problem-solving.

allCourses.title: International Management for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the effects of different national cultures, and political and economic systems on the assumptions, expectations, organizational practices, and organizational forms needed to conduct cross-national organizational work. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 202

allCourses.title: Building Your Leadership Toolkit
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides insights/perspectives about the study and development of leadership. Helps students answer three questions: Where am I currently as a leader? What tools can I use to improve my leadership? What is my plan for the future as a leader.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 202 or MGMTMBA 202. MGMT FE 202 with a grade of C or better. MGMTMBA 202 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation for Managers I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Develops skills essential to using financial statements for business analysis by examining financial information quality, profitability and risk analysis, earnings management, revenue recognition, asset recognition and valuation, and how financial reporting is related to the business environment and managerial incentives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 203A or MGMTMBA 203A. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of B- or better. MGMTMBA 203A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation for Managers II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the financial statement analysis of liabilities and stockholders' equity. Topics include forecasting financial statements, earnings-based valuation models, accounting analysis of mergers and acquisitions, leases, bankruptcy prediction, and derivatives. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 203A or MGMTMBA 203A. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of B- or better. MGMTMBA 203A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Wealth Management for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Aims to integrate behavioral finance, psychology, personal financial planning, risk management, and asset management to provide students with the theoretical and practical knowledge to effectively build and manage wealth.

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Fully Employed M.B.A. Program students only.
allCourses.description: Develops an initial set of skills essential to using financial statements for business analysis. Topics include financial information "quality," earnings management, revenue recognition, forecasting financial information, and equity valuation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 203A.

allCourses.title: Portfolio Management for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Masters of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced portfolio decision making. Topics include index models, portfolio performance measures, bond portfolio management and interest immunization, stock market anomalies, and market efficiency.  Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 209A and MGMT FE 209B.

allCourses.title: Bonds and Fixed Income
allCourses.restriction: Fully Employed M.B.A. Program students only.
allCourses.description: During the past decade, there has been a tremendous amount of innovation in the design and use of debt securities.  Focuses on techniques and methodologies for valuing different types of debt as well as their uses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 201A and MGMT FE 203A and MGMT FE 204A and MGMT FE 209A and MGMT FE 209B.

allCourses.title: FinTech and the Digital Economy
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides working knowledge of the role of IT-enabled innovation in financial markets to help students acquire an understanding of broad economic issues that are of wide applicability in many areas of FinTech. Both qualitative analysis and quantitative applications are explored.

allCourses.title: Real Estate Investment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a survey of basic real estate valuation and investment, including institutions that govern the operation of the market, decisions to purchase, rehabilitate, develop, and dispose of real estate projects. Lectures, discussion, case studies, and presentations by outside speakers included.

allCourses.title: International Real Estate
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of international real estate investment opportunities. Topics include size and breadth; opportunities and challenges (tax treatment, currency/political/market risks, transaction costs, lack of local knowledge); ownership vehicles (REITs, joint ventures, equity funds, etc.). Global cast of guest lecturers supplements lectures.

allCourses.title: Real Estate Capital Markets
allCourses.description: Understanding the four sectors of real estate capital markets: pubic debt, private debt, public equity, private equity; estate investment, key players, investment types drive capital solutions, underwriting strategies, and vehicle structuring, debt versus equity source characteristics and implications for returns.

allCourses.title: The Real Estate Development Process
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Nature and composition of development community and development process. Emphasis on role of conflicting interests, values and goals, and market uncertainty. Special attention paid to deal structuring and risk management. Lectures, guest lecturers, team projects evaluating actual development project.

allCourses.title: Mortgage-Backed Securities and Structured Debt
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theory and operation of the mortgage-backed security market. Historical introduction, technical analysis, examination of operations of residential/commercial mortgage-backed securities markets (RMBS, CMBS), evaluations of the "buy side," mezzanine financing, CDOs, related vehicles. Guest lecturers from industry supplement lectures.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Management of the Real Estate Enterprise
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Beyond "The Deal" to management of the real estate enterprise itself. Explores aspects of decision-making focused upon strategic objectives: goal setting, legal/tax structures, family-owned firms, going public, corporate ethics, capital structure, diversification, core competencies, technology. Guest professionals.

allCourses.title: Applied Real Estate Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an understanding of the public real estate investment trust (REIT) market and its place in modern investment strategies, presents methods for analyzing and valuing companies, and introduces basic concepts for constructing and managing a real estate investment portfolio.

allCourses.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Geared to students who are seeking a career in finance and/or in working with venture capital firms, private equity/buyout firms, investment banks, commercial lenders, mezzanine fund investors, corporate finance, and entrepreneurial firms.

allCourses.title: Corporate Valuation for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Studies cases that expand concepts covered in the introductory corporate finance course and focuses on estimating the value of firms and projects in diverse settings. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MGMT FE 209A or MGMTMBA 209A) and (MGMT FE 209B or MGMTMBA 209B)

allCourses.title: Derivatives for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies financial derivatives instruments, including forward contracts, futures, swaps, and options. Advanced applications of these instruments, including pricing and risk management, are emphasized. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 209A or MGMTMBA 209A

allCourses.title: Consumer Behavior for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines consumer decision-making processes with emphasis on application of concepts and research findings from behavioral sciences for solution of marketing problems. Includes models of consumer decision-making, information processing theories, and sociological influences on consumer decision-making. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Marketing Research for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Qualitative and quantitative marketing techniques that generate customer insights. Discusses problem formulation, data collection, statistical analyses, formulating managerial recommendations, implementation, and how research is used by companies. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Managing Advertising and Communications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Integrated marketing communications, including advertising, sale promotions, public relations, and direct mail. Exposure to elements of a communications plan; marketing research, including copy testing and tracking; creating brand value; media strategies; metrics. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: New Product Development for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to introduce the new product development process and techniques to identify markets, develop new product ideas, measure consumer preferences, position and design new products as well as test them prior to launch. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Micromarketing with Digital Footprints
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: How businesses use digital footprints from household data and point-of-purchase data to customize product offerings and delivery, store locations, advertising, and promotions to households and neighborhoods with the highest market potential. Hands-on experience with Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping software.

allCourses.title: Social Media Marketing
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Surveys the social media landscape to understand developments and examine application areas based on the concepts and contextual formulations. Students investigate topics of their choice based on their research interests.

allCourses.title: Business to Business Selling and Sales Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Sales is the interpersonal process where the needs of the buyer are uncovered and satisfied, to the long-term benefit of both parties. Students explore sales force management and personal selling in a dynamic, digital environment.

allCourses.title: Managing Design and Innovation
allCourses.restriction: Masters of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Presents a design-driven approach, from design as organizational vision to strategic innovation to managing the design process. Students are exposed to design fundamentals and work in teams that involve creativity workshops and real-world projects. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Marketing on the Internet for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the Internet's impact on traditional methods of marketing. Discusses how to capitalize on and increase the Internet's utility as a tool that can increase marketing effectiveness, efficiency, and competitiveness. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Marketing Strategies for High Technology for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Framework and tools for managing technology-intensive businesses.  Product and pricing policies; network externalities; compatibility concerns; systems competitions; technological and market uncertainty; technology licensing strategies; contracting in high-tech markets; product line design; product bundling strategies; usage-based pricing; pricing of networks; auctions.

allCourses.title: Strategic Brand Management for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Addresses important branding decisions faced by organizations. A computer simulation allows students hands-on experience in making decisions about their brand and seeing the results of those decisions. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 205 or MGMTMBA 205. MGMT FE 205 with a grade of B- or better. MGMTMBA 205 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Critical IT Decisions for Business Managers
allCourses.restriction: Masters of Business Administration graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Develops frameworks to help business executives make critical IT decisions. Examples include how much to invest in IT, how to maximize return on IT investment, sourcing and business process outsourcing, strategies for digital environments. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 207.

allCourses.title: Machine Learning Analytics for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces methods to mine data repositories for business intelligence to facilitate analytical decision-making. Topics include clustering for market segmentation; association rules to discover relationships between different purchase decisions; Naive-Bayes classification techniques for decision-making using decision-trees. Evening or weekend format.

allCourses.title: Managing Database and Strategic Applications
allCourses.restriction: Masters of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Examines contemporary business applications of databases including CRM, knowledge management, data-warehousing, and data-mining. Also provides overview of the database design process and data retrieval (querying) to enable analytics and business decision making. Evening or weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 207.

allCourses.title: Data and Programming for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Challenges and teaches students to handle data that come in a variety of forms and sizes. Guides students through the whole data management process, from initial data acquisition to final data analysis.

allCourses.title: Digital Strategies and Markets
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how online social media are impacting organizations and markets. Topics include collective intelligence, online social influence, social networks, and social media monetization. The target audience consists of students interested in IT consulting, competitive strategy, marketing, and entrepreneurship.

allCourses.title: Forecasting for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Basic theory and techniques used to forecast future activities in technological, economic, social, and political arenas. Impact of forecasting on managerial decision making. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Analytical Decision Models for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction of analytics tools for decision making. Topics include linear and non-linear optimization and simulation models. Excel Solver is used as the optimization tool and Risk Solver Platform is used as the simulation tool. Evening or weekend.

allCourses.title: Revenue Management for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Students learn to apply advanced analytics to earn incremental revenue through the efficient use of resources and science-based pricing methods. Statistics and optimization (using Excel and Excel Solver). Industry-specific implementation issues.

allCourses.title: Decision Analysis for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Models of preferences and uncertainty; exercises in creative problem solving. Assessment and use of preference models for private, public, and not-for-profit decision making. Assessment and use of subjective probabilities in decision making. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Supply Chain Analytics for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to fundamental analytics tools to manage business uncertainties, meet customer needs, and drive business disruptions through supply chain innovations. Example topics include forecasting, inventory management, capacity planning, profit analysis, supply chain coordination, risk management, simulation-based performance analysis.

allCourses.title: Project Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the fundamental components of project management and its role in the modern corporation. Emphasis is on how to initiate, implement, control, and terminate a project. Use of computer package for project management.  Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Predictive Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Deals with predicting entities, such as demand for a product or service (forecasting) and predicting membership of known groups (classification). Blends methodologies of forecasting and data mining and focuses on the application of these methods to managerial problems and decision-making.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Business
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Business. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Business Law for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Detailed study from a business viewpoint of contract theories, assignments, delegation of duties, third-party beneficiary contracts, defenses to consensual contracts, types of conditions, methods of excusing conditions, remedies, and types of damages. Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Information, Communication, and Coordination: Practicum for Analyzing Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Use of contextual inquiry and ethnographic methods to assess real world contexts.  Exploring culture, power, physical layout, and the role of artifacts in information flow, communication practices, and coordination through qualitative fieldwork in an organization.

allCourses.title: Edge for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the crucial roles of external forces: globalization, technology, shifting demographics - as transformative catalysts for change - opening markets, erasing boundaries, and transforming industries. Prepares future business leaders to innovate and successfully compete.

allCourses.title: Global Business
allCourses.restriction: Fully Employed M.B.A. Program students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes and reinforces international perspectives contained in the EMBA curriculm by providing a week-long intensive seminar abroad in the second year.  Scholars and business people from the host country instruct FEMBA students in specially designed class sessions and company visits.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of global strategy, economics, and financial issues. Topics include global manager’s environment, global strategy, impact of national culture on business systems, strategies and practices, foreign direct investment, corporate governance, human resources, and international marketing. Evening and weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Global Business for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Admin - Fully Employed Majors only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes and reinforces international perspectives contained in the FEMBA curriculum by providing a week-long intensive seminar abroad in the second year.  Scholars and business people from the host country instruct FEMBA students in specially designed class sessions and company visits. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT FE 295A. MGMT FE 295A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.title: Executive Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides perspectives on leadership. Helps students answer three questions: Where am I currently as a leader? What tools can I use to improve my leadership? What is my plan for the future as a leader? Evening or weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Merage Consulting Projects for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students the opportunity to put into practice concepts, skills, and tools acquired in other parts of the MBA program. Seminars augment internship experiences with analyses of relevant administrative issues.

allCourses.title: Individual Directed Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.

allCourses.title: Responding to Dynamic Times: Thinking Strategically for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the strategic and organizational challenges that a rapidly changing environment poses to the firm’s management and frames them according to Merage’s strategic emphasis on analytical decision making, innovation, and information technology.

allCourses.title: Statistics for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Methods of statistical inference, emphasizing applications to administrative and management decision problems. Topics include classical estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, analysis of variance, decision analysis, and forecasting.

allCourses.title: Operations Analytics for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to computer-based models for decision making. Topics include optimization (linear programming, integer programming, network flow models) and computer simulation. Uses spreadsheets extensively, including Excel built-in and add-in packages. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Organizational Behavior for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Develops a better understanding of individual and group behavior in and across organizations, the frameworks by which to analyze and understand behavior in complex organizations; enhances the skills required to manage collaboration and lead. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Financial Reporting for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Involves the development, analysis, and interpretation of financial accounting information for external reporting purposes. Emphasis on measurement and valuation issues in decision-making problems and cases.  Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Managerial Accounting for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Involves developing and using internal financial and non-financial information to help organizations make planning, budgeting, control, operating, and performance evaluation decisions.  Once a month weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 203A

allCourses.title: Microeconomics for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides basic tools for analyzing economic decisions of consumers and firms. Topics include demand and supply analysis, production and cost theory, perfect competition, monopoly, market failures, and introductory game theory. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Macroeconomics for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Health Care Executive M.B.A. students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces use of macroeconomic analysis to manage the business cycle for competitive advantage. "Business cycle-sensitive" management is explored within the context of marketing, operations management, HRM, merger and acquisitions, and capital financing and expenditures.  Once a month weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 204A.

allCourses.title: Marketing for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to marketing. Develops familiarity with fundamental marketing concepts, theories, and techniques, and acquainting students with the type of decisions made by marketing managers, including customer targeting, product, pricing, place, promotion, and research. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Business and Government for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the many non-market issues that affect today's managers: environment protection, health and safety, intellectual property protection, antitrust, and lobbying. Takes an interdisciplinary approach using economics, political science, public policy, and law. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Competing with Digital in Healthcare: Analytics, Platforms, and Business Models
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on how information technology is used to create value in healthcare-related organizations through product, process, and strategy innovation. Aims to help managers and healthcare professionals understand the strategic role of technology. Every other weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Managerial Finance for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to financial theory and concepts. Topics include time value of money, valuation of stocks and bonds, capital budgeting, portfolio theory, capital structure choice. Once a month weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 201A and MGMT HC 203A and MGMT HC 204A

allCourses.title: Investments for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Foundations of investment management. Theory and empirical evidence related to portfolio theory, market efficiency, and valuation models for equities, bonds, and options.  Emphasis on practical applications, including optimal investment strategies. Once a month weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 209A

allCourses.title: Strategic Management for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides conceptual frameworks and techniques to analyze and develop firm strategies. Through case analysis and discussion, helps students improve analytical and strategic thinking by which to assess, evaluate, and respond to different business situations. Once a month weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 200 and MGMT HC 202 and MGMT HC 205 and MGMT HC 209A

allCourses.title: New Venture Management for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches how to launch and manage new businesses. Provides an overview of the start-up process, including how to identify new business opportunities and develop sound operating models, value new ventures, and understand capital financing. Once a month weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 200 and MGMT HC 202 and MGMT HC 205 and MGMT HC 210.

allCourses.title: Entrepreneurship for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: A project course in which student teams develop a business plan to launch a new venture. Drafts of sections of the plan are due throughout the course. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Global Competitive Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Health Care Executive M.B.A. students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the challenges and opportunities for international business focusing on how and why companies go global, global industry structure and competition, international market development and market entry, and the management of international business risks.  Extensive use of case and discussions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 202 and MGMT 205 and MGMT 210.

allCourses.title: Negotiations For Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Using a combination of theory and practice via negotiation simulations, students expand their repertoire of negotiating skills and develop their ability to analyze different negotiation situations and contexts. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis for Healthcare
allCourses.restriction: Masters of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Develops an initial set of skills essential to using financial statements for business analysis. Topics include financial information "quality," earnings management, revenue recognition, forecasting financial information, and equity valuation. Once a month weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 203A.

allCourses.title: Corporate Valuation for Healthcare  Executives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Studies cases that expand concepts covered in the introductory corporate finance course and focuses on estimating the value of firms and projects in diverse settings. Once a month weekend course format.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMT HC 209A.

allCourses.title: Understanding Managed Care
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: This course is designed to increase understanding of the various concepts of managed health care with an emphasis on the organizational processes required to make it work, and explore the economics and financial pressures these organizations face.

allCourses.title: Decision Analysis for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Masters of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Models of preferences and uncertainty; exercises in creative problem solving. Assessment and use of preference models for private, public, and not-for-profit decision making. Assessment and use of subjective probabilities in decision making. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Project Management
allCourses.restriction: Masters of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the fundamental components of project management and its role in the modern corporation. Emphasis is on how to initiate, implement, control, and terminate a project. Use of computer package for project management.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Business
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of business. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Business Law for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Detailed study from a business viewpoint of contract theories, assignments, delegation of duties, third-party beneficiary contracts, defenses to consensual contracts, types of conditions, methods of excusing conditions, remedies, and types of damages.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Federal Policy in Health Care
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: National/international one-week residential course exploring political analysis as related to management of health care organizations.  Topics include political environment of management, concepts, and processes central to political analysis, bureaucratic politics, politics, and the manager.

allCourses.title: Leadership for Healthcare Executives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Administration - Health Care Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the conceptual, practical, and personal dimensions of executive leadership. Past and current leadership theories are addressed. Individual personal assessment and diagnosis. Once a month weekend course format.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Global Competitive Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Explores advanced topics in managing the geographic scope of the firm: locating activities in the right places, which markets to penetrate, horizontal integration across countries, and multinational partnering.

allCourses.title: Competitive Intelligence
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: The course focuses on how to design a competitive intelligence program which is a core foundation upon which competitive strategies and execution tactics are developed, assessed, and modified.

allCourses.title: Business Dynamics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Enhances students' analytical skills by analyzing complex challenges that businesses face and to quickly implement a winning response.

allCourses.title: Organizational Change
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the implementation of change, including identifying the features of successful change in organizations of varying sizes and configurations, with an emphasis on the reasons why individuals resist or embrace change.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 202 or MGMT FE 202

allCourses.title: Negotiations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Using a combination of theory and practice via negotiation simulations, students expand their repertoire of negotiating skills and develop their ability to analyze different negotiation situations and contexts.

allCourses.title: International Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the effects of different national cultures, political and economic systems on the assumptions, expectations, organizational practices, and organizational forms needed  to conduct cross-national organizational work.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 202 or MGMT FE 202. MGMTMBA 202 with a grade of B- or better. MGMT FE 202 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Leadership Strategies
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides insight/perspectives about the study and development of leadership. Helps students answer three questions: Where am I currently as a leader? What tools can I use to improve my leadership? What is my plan for the future as a leader. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 202 or MGMT FE 202. MGMTMBA 202 with a grade of C or better. MGMT FE 202 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Develops skills essential to using financial statements for business analysis by examining financial information quality, profitability and risk analysis, earnings management, revenue recognition, asset recognition and valuation, and how financial reporting is related to the business environment and managerial incentives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 203A or MGMT FE 203A. MGMTMBA 203A with a grade of B- or better. MGMT FE 203A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation II
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the financial statement analysis of liabilities and stockholders' equity. Covers topics such as forecasting financial statements, earnings-based valuation models, accounting analysis of mergers and acquisitions, leases, bankruptcy prediction, and derivatives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 203A

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Develops an initial set of skills essential to using financial statements for business analysis. Topics include financial information "quality," earnings management, revenue recognition, forecasting financial information, and equity valuation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 203A.

allCourses.title: Accounting Control and Corporate Governance
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Equips MBA students with skills to deal with the challenges and opportunities organizations face in dealing with the separation of ownership and control.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 203A and MGMTMBA 203B.

allCourses.title: Portfolio Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced portfolio decision-making. Topics include index models, portfolio performance measures, bond portfolio management and interest immunization, stock market anomalies, and market efficiency.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MGMTMBA 209A or MGMT FE 209A) and (MGMTMBA 209B or MGMT FE 209B)

allCourses.title: Bonds and Fixed Income
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Fixed-income markets include treasury bonds, corporate bonds, and asset-backed securities.  Focuses on techniques and methodologies for valuing different types of debt as well as their uses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (MGMTMBA 209A or MGMT FE 209A) and (MGMTMBA 209B or MGMT FE 209B)

allCourses.title: Multinational Finance
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on financial issues facing multinational corporations, the most important of which is the management of foreign exchange risk. Other topics include investments and financing decisions in international capital markets.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 209A or MGMT FE 209A. MGMTMBA 209A with a grade of B- or better. MGMT FE 209A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: FinTech and the Digital Economy for Business
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides working knowledge of the role of IT-enabled innovation in financial markets to help students acquire an understanding of broad economic issues that are of wide applicability in many areas of FinTech. Both qualitative analysis and quantitative applications are explored.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Real Estate Process
allCourses.description: Introductory survey course providing a working knowledge of the real estate market. Topics include real estate economics, valuation, feasibility, investment, tax considerations, financing, development, and corporate real estate asset management. Lectures and cases, with supplemental presentations by real estate professionals.

allCourses.title: International Real Estate
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of international real estate investment opportunities. Topics include size and breadth; opportunities and challenges (tax treatment, currency/political/market risks, transaction costs, lack of local knowledge); ownership vehicles (REITs, joint ventures, equity funds, etc.). Global cast of guest lecturers supplements lectures.

allCourses.title: Real Estate Capital Markets
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Understanding the four sectors of real estate capital markets: public debt, private debt, public equity, private equity; fundamental drivers of real estate investment; key players; investment types; underwriting strategies; debt vs. equity source characteristics and implications for returns.

allCourses.title: The Real Estate Development Process
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Nature and composition of development community and development process. Emphasis on role of conflicting interests, values and goals, and market uncertainty. Special attention paid to deal structuring and risk management. Lectures, guest lecturers, team projects evaluating actual development project.

allCourses.title: Mortgage-Backed Securities and Structured Finance
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Theory and operation of the residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities markets. Historical introduction, pricing and technical analysis, the securitization process and roles of individual players, investment characteristics, structured finance and derivatives, recent policy issues. Guest lecturers from industry supplement lectures.

allCourses.title: Seminar in Management of the Real Estate Enterprise
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Capstone seminar. Looks beyond "The Deal" to management of the real estate enterprise itself. Explores aspects of decision-making focused upon strategic objectives: goal setting, legal/tax structures, public vs. closely-held entities, corporate ethics, capital structure, managing growth, diversification, technology. Guest professionals.

allCourses.title: Applied Real Estate Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an understanding of the public real estate investment trust (REIT) market and its place in modern investment strategies, presents methods for analyzing and valuing companies, and introduces basic concepts for constructing and managing a real estate investment portfolio.

allCourses.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Geared to students who are seeking a career in finance and/or in working with venture capital firms, private equity/buyout firms, investment banks, commercial lenders, mezzanine fund investors, corporate finance, and entrepreneurial firms.

allCourses.title: Corporate Valuation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Studies cases that expand concepts covered in the introductory corporate finance course and focuses on estimating the value of firms and projects in diverse settings.
