allCourses.title: Derivatives
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Studies financial derivatives instruments, including forward contracts, futures, swaps, and options. Advanced applications of these instruments, including pricing and risk management, are emphasized.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 209A or MGMT FE 209A

allCourses.title: Consumer Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the consumer decision-making process with an emphasis on application of concepts and research findings from behavioral sciences for solution of marketing problems. Includes models of consumer decision-making, information processing theories, and sociological influences on consumer decision-making.

allCourses.title: Marketing Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Covers conducting marketing research to generate consumer insights that will drive sales, market share, and profitability and/or realize other quantitative objectives. Discusses problem formulation, data collection, statistical analyses, formulating managerial recommendations, implementation, and how research is used by companies.

allCourses.title: Advertising and Communications Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Covers integrated marketing communications which includes advertising, sale promotions, public relations, and direct mail. Topics include elements of a communications plan, marketing research including copy testing and tracking, creating brand value, media strategies, and measuring return on investment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 205.

allCourses.title: New Product Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to introduce the new product development process and techniques to identify markets, develop new product ideas, measure consumer preferences, position and design new products, as well as test them prior to launch. Analytical thinking and techniques are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Global Consumer Insights
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an understanding of the problems and perspectives of marketing across national boundaries, and develops analytical abilities for structuring and controlling marketing programs related to overseas business. Financial, legal, and cultural barriers to international marketing are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Design Management and Innovation
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents a design-driven approach, from design as organizational vision to strategic innovation to managing the design process. Students are exposed to design fundamentals and work in teams that involve creativity workshops and real-world projects.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 205 or MGMT FE 205. MGMTMBA 205 with a grade of C or better. MGMT FE 205 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.title: Marketing on the Internet
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the impact of the Internet on traditional methods of doing marketing, and explores its existing and future uses. Discusses how to capitalize on and increase the Internet's utility as a tool that can increase marketing effectiveness, efficiency, and competitiveness.

allCourses.title: Marketing Strategies
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Prepares students to identify and address strategic marketing problems in today’s business environment. Major foci is on the strategic marketing process, the digital transformation of business, situation analyses, and STP. Integrates marketing knowledge with practice.

allCourses.title: Strategic Brand Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Addresses important branding decisions faced by organizations. A computer simulation allows students hands-on experience in making decisions about their brand and seeing the results of those decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 205 or MGMT FE 205

allCourses.title: Physicians, Executives, and Healthcare Law
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Elective course offered alternating years, for UCI MBA students. Designed to bring major healthcare law issues to the classroom.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 201A.

allCourses.title: Physicians, Executives, and Health Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Elective course offered alternating years, for the UCI M.B.A. students. Designed to bring to the classroom major healthcare leadership and management issues from both the executive and physician perspective.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 201A or MGMT FE 201A

allCourses.title: Managing Nonprofits
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the similarities and differences between for-profit and nonprofit organizations, with emphasis on the management of nonprofits.  Topics include: marketing, fundraising, staffing, management/director relationships, use of volunteers, and emerging career opportunities.

allCourses.title: Economics of Information
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with an understanding of fundamental economic principles governing information technology industries. Particularly, implications for optimal pricing strategies, determinants/consequences of market structure, and the role and rationale for government intervention and the implications for business strategy.

allCourses.title: US Health Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of US health policy with a particular emphasis on current policy developments and debates.  Students will be introduced to the basic tools of policy analysis and will apply them to health policy issues.

allCourses.title: Data Camp for Managers
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of R for basic data analytics and visualization with hands-on training using Data Camp. This project is meant to foreshadow the analysis that students will be doing in their electives.

allCourses.title: Critical IT Decisions for Business Executives
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Develops frameworks to help business executives make critical IT decisions.  Examples include how much to invest in IT, determining management practices to maximize return on IT investment, sourcing strategies for IT and business process outsourcing, strategies for digital environments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MGMTMBA 207.

prerequisite_list.title: Competing with Digital: Technology, Analytics, and Platforms

allCourses.title: Machine Learning Analytics for Business
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces methods to mine data repositories for business intelligence to facilitate analytical decision-making. Topics include clustering for market segmentation; association rules to discover relationships between different purchase decisions; Naive-Bayes classification techniques for decision-making using decision-trees.

allCourses.title: Data and Programming for Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Challenges and teaches students to handle data that come in a variety of forms and sizes. Guides students through the whole data management process, from initial data acquisition to final data analysis.

allCourses.title: Analytics and Technology Consulting
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on elements of analytics and personalized engagement. Students work on a project using a real-life business problem and data to get hands-on understanding.

allCourses.title: Blockchain and Cryptocurrency
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with an introduction to and an architectural understanding of "why" and "how" Blockchain was created, an overview of altcoins, and provide an understanding of the challenges and risks involved with this new Blockchain technology and cryptocurrency landscape.

allCourses.title: Digital Strategies and Markets
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines how online social media are impacting organizations and markets. Topics include collective intelligence, online social influence, social networks, and social media monetization. The target audience consists of students interested in IT consulting, competitive strategy, marketing, and entrepreneurship.

allCourses.title: Forecasting
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic theory and techniques used to forecast future activities in technological, economic, social, and political arenas. Impact of forecasting on managerial decision making.

allCourses.title: Revenue Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students learn to apply advanced analytics to earn incremental revenue through the efficient use of resources and science-based pricing methods. Statistics and optimization (using Excel and Excel Solver). Industry-specific implementation issues.

allCourses.title: Decision Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Models of preferences and uncertainty; exercises in creative problem solving.  Assessment and use of preference models (von Neumann-Morgenstern expected utility and measurable value functions) for private, public, and not-for-profit decision making. Assessment and use of subjective probabilities in decision making.

allCourses.title: Supply Chain Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the use of advanced analytics and data-driven methods to successfully manage uncertainty in supply chains, meeting customer needs in the most timely and cost effective manner, and driving business disruptions through innovations.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Business Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the business understanding, on the process of business analytics, and teaching a framework to understand the key drivers that could be fed into a mathematical model. Emphasizes how to make use of information to drive digital change.

allCourses.title: Project Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the fundamental components of project management and its role in the modern corporation. Emphasis on how to initiate, implement, control, and terminate a project. Use of computer package for project management.

allCourses.title: Predictive Analytics for Business
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Deals with predicting entities, such as demand for a product or service (forecasting) and predicting membership of known groups (classification). Blends methodologies of forecasting and data mining and focuses on the application of these methods to managerial problems and decision-making.

allCourses.title: Field Studies in Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Each quarter a number of special topic seminars are offered in the 290 series.  Examples of possible topics include Communication in Organizations, Power and Authority in Organizations, International Management, Health Care Administration, Real Estate Development.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Business Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Detailed study from a business viewpoint of contract theories, assignments, delegation of duties, third-party beneficiary contracts, defenses to consensual contracts, types of conditions, methods of excusing conditions, remedies, and types of damages.

allCourses.title: Biotech Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Taught jointly by Bio Sci and Merage School faculty, the course addresses fundamental aspects within, and associated with, the biotechnology industry. Curriculum is focused largely on management issues, including finance, product development, pharmaceuticals, project management, regulatory affairs, and ethics.

allCourses.title: Edge
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Master of Business Admin Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Edge explores the crucial roles of external forces - globalization, technology, shifting demographics - as transformative catalysts for change - opening markets, erasing boundaries, and transforming industries. This course prepares future business leaders to innovate and compete successfully.

allCourses.title: Miicromarketing with Digital Footprints
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Admin Degree students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: How businesses use digital footprints from household data and point-of-purchase data to customize product offerings and delivery, store locations, advertising, and promotions to households and neighborhoods with the highest market potential. Hands-on experience with Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping software.

allCourses.title: Operations Management Lab
allCourses.restriction: Master of Business Administration students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to some basic skills of modeling and analyzing business processes using commercial process modeling software. Through class projects, provides students with hands-on experience in building simulation models for improving operational performance of business processes.

allCourses.title: Merage Consulting Projects
allCourses.restriction: Second-year MBA students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students the opportunity to put into practice concepts, skills, and tools acquired in other parts of the M.B.A. program. Seminars augment internship experiences with analyses of relevant administrative issues.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of the selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Ph.D. Special Topics Seminar
allCourses.description: Each quarter a number of special topic seminars are offered in the 291 series for Ph.D. students. Examples include topics such as methods seminar, experimental design, qualitative research, structural equation modeling.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Pre-Colloquium Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Management Majors only.
allCourses.description: Seeks to facilitate discussion of upcoming Colloquium research papers increasing the likelihood that Ph.D. students are active participants in all of the Colloquia. Active participation enhances exposure of Ph.D. students to visiting scholars.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Doctoral Proseminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analysis of the central theories and theoretical controversies in the field of management. Examination of the formal education for managerial careers and exploration of issues relating to professional careers in research and scholarship in the field of management.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to prepare students for teaching career; incorporates seminars addressing topics of classroom dynamics, syllabus preparation, teaching techniques; establishes mentor relationship with faculty member in student’s teaching area, provides classroom experience and includes option of videotape analysis of teaching style.

allCourses.title: Philosophy of Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides exposure to fundamental issues regarding how knowledge is created, defended, and replaced both in the natural and social sciences. Covers current debates on the meaning of the term “scientific” and the validity of the scientific method.

allCourses.title: Doctoral Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Management Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the fundamentals of social science research: theory development, research design, methods, data management, and writing for scholarly publications; for doctoral students intending scholarly research careers. Involves hands-on practice in formulating hypotheses, designing research, and conducting journal reviews.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on qualitative research techniques for management. A hands-on course that includes in-depth/long interviews, visual research methods, participant/non-participant observation, verbal protocols, constructing field notes, multi-media approaches for data gathering and analyses.

allCourses.title: Analysis of Experimental Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced course provides experience in analyzing data from experiments and quasi-experiments in SPSS, including presenting the results and manuscript preparation.  Data analysis topics include ANOVA, ANCOVA, repeated measures, logistic regression, chi-square, and tests of mediation.

allCourses.title: Applied Multivariate Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the most common techniques for multivariate analysis: principal component analysis, factor analysis, cluster analysis, MANOVA, regression with continuous variables, and regression with discrete variables.

allCourses.title: Applied Econometrics and Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Helps students to be more knowledgeable consumers and producers of empirical research. Reviews econometric techniques and research designs used by applied microeconomists. Attention to practical issues that arise when analyzing data.

allCourses.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Students must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and must have qualitative data they can analyze.

allCourses.title: Writing for Scholarly Publication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces methods for planning and carrying out scholarly writing.

allCourses.title: SAS Boot Camp
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches basics of SAS programming for empirical research. No prior knowledge of SAS or other computer programming language is required. Provides knowledge and tools to replicate an empirical study and learn how to perform very advanced data procedures.

allCourses.title: Game-Theoretic Models for Management Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces some classic game-theoretic models for management research. It is about modeling strategic interactions between business competitors and/or partners in an analytical framework.  Various applications will be discussed, e.g., pricing strategies, business alliances, e-commerce, negotiations, and contracts, etc.

allCourses.title: Theories of Power and Empowerment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies different ways of thinking about power and its uses. Explores theories of power that inform various notions of empowerment, including resistance, participatory democracy, and workplace empowerment.

allCourses.title: Business Economics Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Teaches mathematical and conceptual basics of microeconomics and application. Covers basics of consumer/firm behavior, static and dynamic imperfect competition. Building of simple mathematical models to gain economic insights into business practices and decisions.

allCourses.title: Decision Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Decision theories and preference models: How models are elicited or theories are experimentally tested, relevance to different management research areas, alternative theories, applications in management practice, and interpretations for the general public.

allCourses.title: Foundational Theories of Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers major economic and sociological perspectives guiding the study of organizations (i.e., transaction cost economics, agency theory, institutional theories, organizational ecology, network and diffusion theories, behavioral theories, resource dependence), and examines how different theoretical perspectives are tested.

allCourses.title: Information, Psychology, and Social Processes
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: In the marketplace for ideas, which succeed and which fail? How do ideas and information spread between individuals, and how do populations of ideas evolve? This course reviews recent research on these issues and applications to business.

allCourses.title: Establishing Your Academic Career
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of the best practices for succeeding in an academic career. Presenting oneself in conversation, in written documents, in research talks, and in teaching.

allCourses.title: Individual Directed Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to teaching assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 4 units.

allCourses.title: Basic Immunology Core Lectures
allCourses.description: Basic concepts in human immunology including development of the immune system, innate immunity, immunoglobulin structure and genetics, antigen-antibody reactions, the major histocompatibility complex and antigen presentation, T cell and B cell development, initiation of the immune response, effector mechanisms.

allCourses.title: Regulation of Gene Expression
allCourses.description: Aspects of gene expression including the organization of the eukaryotic nucleus in terms of protein-nucleic acid interaction (i.e., chromatin and chromosome structure); the enzymology and regulation of RNA transcription and pre-mRNA processing in eukaryotes; mechanisms of RNAi and translation.

allCourses.title: Medical Microbiology
allCourses.description: Biology of microbial pathogens (viruses, bacteria, fungi, parasites) as foundation for subsequent study of infectious diseases. Topics: molecular basis of microbial pathogenesis; clinical presentation and epidemiology; diagnostic testing; antimicrobial therapy; prevention strategies. Format: lectures, laboratory, clinical cases, liveclasstech interactive questions.

allCourses.title: Medical Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only.
allCourses.description: Cellular and molecular basis of immune response and roles of the immune system in both maintaining health and contributing to disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: M&MG 210A

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. The main goal is to achieve a basic understanding of the cellular and molecular basis of innate and adaptive immunity, and how immune function is coordinated at a systems level.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. Focuses on advanced topics and cutting edge technologies in modern immunology.  Combination of didactic lectures and student-led journal article discussion.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSIO 215. PHYSIO 215 with a grade of B+ or better

allCourses.title: Pathogenic Microbiology
allCourses.description: Biochemical and genetic properties of infectious agents; identification and behavior of pathogens; activities of toxins; the chemotherapy, biochemistry, and genetics of drug resistance; and epidemiology of infectious diseases.

allCourses.title: Medical Virology
allCourses.description: Animal viruses as disease causing agents, including mechanisms of infection at both the cellular and organismic levels. Topics include comparative studies of different groups of viruses, viral transformation, and mechanisms of viral gene expression.

allCourses.title: Immunopathogenic Mechanisms of Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Campus Honors Collegium students and juniors and seniors may audit.
allCourses.description: Examination of the mechanisms underlying disease states mediated by immune dysregulation including mechanisms of immune evasion by cancer, diseases mediated by cytokine dysregulation, role of the microbiome of the GI tract and of other disease sites, and adoptive T-cell (CAR-T-cells).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: M&MG 215. Recommended: M&MG 215.

allCourses.title: Molecular Pathogenesis of Microbial Infections
allCourses.description: Features lectures by faculty on the molecular aspects of microbial pathogenesis, highlighting both microbe and cellular functions. In addition to lectures, students review papers and discuss them. There will be two written exams, one on viruses and one on microbes.

allCourses.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Human Disease
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the molecular mechanisms of human diseases, including neurologic, hematologic, neoplastic, and infectious diseases. Students gain an understanding of these mechanisms, as well as models of human diseases.

allCourses.title: Immunology Journal Club
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in immunology as related to an understanding of human disease.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Topics in Stem Cells
allCourses.description: One-hour seminar presentation by participating faculty or guest lecturer and open to the science community, followed by one-hour discussion of the lecture topic or related topic. Students are responsible for presentations and readings.

allCourses.title: M.D./PH.D. Tutorial
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores a variety of topics that impact careers of medical scientists (M.D./Ph.D students). Topics range from scientific, such as recent advances in particular research areas, to ethical problems brought on by increased technology and intervention in the disease process.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Responsible Conduct of Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Each session includes a formal presentation by faculty/invited speaker followed by a discussion of case studies related to the topic under consideration.

allCourses.title: Career Development
allCourses.description: Topics include preparation of papers, grants and fellowships, scientific presentations, and curriculum vitae, and career opportunities.

allCourses.description: Tutorial in Microbiology and Molecular Genetics. Presented by the department faculty; relates current laboratory research to the literature.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Nucleic Acid Structure and Function
allCourses.description: Structure and chemistry of nucleic acids. Relationship between these properties and the mechanisms of fundamental processes such as replication and repair, RNA-mediated catalysis, formation and regulation of higher order chromatin structure and recombination.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Protein Structure and Function
allCourses.description: The structure and properties of proteins, enzymes, and their kinetic properties.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51C

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Virology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Primary research data on the major DNA and RNA viruses emphasizing strategies of regulation of gene expression. Utilization of viruses as molecular biological tools. Graduate-level knowledge of the biochemistry and molecular biology of macromolecules is required.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 203 and MOL BIO 204. MOL BIO 203 with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 204 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Structural Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Basic principles of magnetic resonance, Xray crystallography, and CryoEM toward the determination of high-resolution biomolecular structures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Literature in Nucleic Acid Structure and Function
allCourses.description: Exploration and critical analysis of recent primary scientific literature in structure, properties, and biological mechanisms involving nucleic acids.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Literature in Protein Structure and Function
allCourses.description: Exploration and critical analysis of recent primary scientific literature in structure and properties of proteins, enzymes, and their kinetic properties.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. The main goal is to achieve a basic understanding of the cellular and molecular basis of innate and adaptive immunity, and how immune function is coordinated at a systems level.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. Focuses on advanced topics and cutting edge technologies in modern immunology.  Combination of didactic lectures and student-led journal article discussion.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSIO 215. PHYSIO 215 with a grade of B+ or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Cancer Biology I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes are studied from molecular viewpoints. Also studies their role in cancer; viral carcinogenesis. Designed for graduate students interested in cancer research. Format includes lectures and student-led discussions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 203 and MOL BIO 204. MOL BIO 203 with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 204 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Cancer Biology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics include cancer cell growth and metastasis, chemical carcinogenesis, and cancer genetics and epidemiology. Designed for graduate students interested in cancer research. Format includes lectures and student-led discussions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 203 and MOL BIO 204. MOL BIO 203 with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 204 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Clinical Cancer
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to acquaint students in basic life science with clinical cancer.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Structure & Synthesis of Biological Macromolecules Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in macromolecular struture and synthesis as related to biological problems.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Literature-based, interactive discussions focused on review of seminal historic and recent immunology literature. Student responsibilities include reading, critical evaluation, and discussion of manuscripts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: M&MG 215. M&MG 215 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Immunology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An advanced course in immunology for graduate students enrolled in the Biotechnology master's program. Emphasis is placed on learning modern techniques in immunology such as ELISAs, western blotting, immunofluorescent staining assays.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Computational Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.
allCourses.concurrent: BIO SCI M123 and COMPSCI 183 and BME 132.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Virus Engineering Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An advanced laboratory for graduate students enrolled in the Biotechnology master's program. Students learn to engineer recombinant eukuryotic viruses and express genes in mouse tissue.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Immunlology Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in immunology as related to an understanding of human disease.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 15 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Virology and Immunology Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introductory laboratory course in virology and immunology designed for Biological Sciences graduate students. Curriculum includes plasmid preparation, plasmid characterization, microscopy, cell culture, transfection and infection of cells, cell counting, plaque assays, ELISA, Western blot, mixed lymphocyte reactions.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An advanced course in genetic engineering and biotechnology for graduates enrolled in the Biotechnology Master's Program. Emphasis will be placed on learning advanced methods in assembling the gene for expression in bacteria, yeast and human cells.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Research-in-Progress Seminars
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Two half-hour presentations by graduate students and postdoctorals to the department on their current research projects.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 15 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Literature in Chemical and Structural Biology
allCourses.description: Exploration and critical analysis of recent primary scientific literature in chemical and structural biology.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Stem Cells
allCourses.description: Presentation by participating faculty or guest lecturer that is open to the science community, followed by discussion of the lecture topic or a related topic. Students are responsible for presentations and readings.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Genomics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A survey course of the principal subfields of genomics and their applications to biological and health sciences that will cover genome assembly and annotation, genome structure, comparative genomics, population genomics, functional genomics, and medical genomics.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Metallobiochemistry
allCourses.description: A review of the biochemistry of metallic elements emphasizing: methods for studying metals in biological systems; the chemical basis for nature's exploitation of specific elements; structures of active sites; mechanisms; solid-state structures and devices; metals in medicine.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Biotechnology - Nucleic Acids
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Supplements laboratory curriculum with scientific background behind experimental methods. Format consists of lectures and the presentation and analysis of relevant papers from the scientific literature.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biotechnology Laboratory - Nucleic Acids
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Nucleic acid techniques and recombinant DNA technology. Extraction and purification of nucleic acids, cloning and subcloning, PCR, site-directed mutagenesis, nucleic acid hybridization, additional associated procedures. Students must demonstrate accurate documentation of data (laboratory notebook) detailing experience and results.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Biotechnology - Protein Purification and Characterization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Supplements laboratory curriculum with scientific background behind experimental methods. Format consists of lectures and the presentation and analysis of relevant papers from the scientific literature.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 250L and MOL BIO 250. MOL BIO 250L with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 250 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biotechnology Laboratory - Protein Purification and Characterization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Major techniques of handling proteins and antibodies. Protein engineering, expression and large-scale purification of recombinant proteins from bacteria, HPLC, antibody purification, western blotting, additional associated procedures. Students must demonstrate accurate documentation of data (laboratory notebook) detailing experience and results.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 250L and MOL BIO 250. MOL BIO 250L with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 250 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biotechnology Management Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Overview of current methods in biotechnology, designed specifically for biotechnology graduate students. Organized into four distinct sections (nucleic acids, proteins, virology, and immunology). Students must demonstrate accurate documentation of data (laboratory notebooks) detailing experience and results.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biotech Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Taught jointly by Bio Sci and Merage School faculty, the course addresses fundamental aspects within, and associated with, the biotechnology industry. Curriculum is focused largely on management issues, including finance, product development, pharmaceuticals, project management, regulatory affairs, and ethics.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Stem Cell Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Biotechnology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to prepare M.S. Biotechnology program students for a career in stem cell research. Laboratory training utilizes tissue culture, mouse and human embryonic stem cells, and is enhanced with didactic material and discussion.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 250L and MOL BIO 251L

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Structure-Function Relationships of Integral Membrane Proteins
allCourses.description: Integral membrane proteins such as voltage and ligand-gated ion channels, water channels, pumps, cotransporters, and receptors (e.g., GPCRs). The emphasis is on the relationship between atomic structure and the functional properties of these proteins.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99. BIO SCI 98 with a grade of B or better. BIO SCI 99 with a grade of B or better.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar in Systems Microbiology Research
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A research and journal club seminar that covers topics on bacteria and phage using approaches and principles from biology, engineering, and physics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Science Communication Skills
allCourses.description: Development of effective communication skills, oral and written presentations. Topics range from the art of creating keynote slides to strategically crafting a personal story, culminating in a live presentation to an invited audience.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Selected topics in specified areas of concentration, e.g., nucleic acids, protein biochemistry, genetic expression, biochemical genetics. Specific topics announced in advance.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Graduate School Fundamentals
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cellular and Molecular Biosci Majors only.
allCourses.description: Lectures and discussions providing basic skills needed for success in Ph.D. graduate studies. Topics include formulating a hypothesis, experimental design, literature review, grant writing, oral communication, biostatistics, time management, and professional development.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cancer Biology Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on molecular mechanisms that underlie the development and progression of cancers. Covers a variety of cancer-related research areas, such as cell cycle control, apoptosis, DNA repair, metastasis, angiogenesis, and others.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cancer Biology Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on molecular mechanisms that underlie the development and progression of cancers. Covers a variety of cancer-related research areas, such as cell cycle control, apoptosis, DNA repair, metastasis, angiogenesis, and others.

allCourses.title: Cancer Biology Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on molecular mechanisms that underlie the development and progression of cancers. Covers a variety of cancer-related research areas, such as cell cycle control, apoptosis, DNA repair, metastasis, angiogenesis, and others.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Biomedical Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Cellular and Molecular Biosci Majors only.
allCourses.description: Lectures and interactive discussions of research methods in modern biomedical science. Each week will focus on a different class of techniques, including molecular, biochemical, immunological, genomic, bioinformatics, microscopy, cancer biology, genome editing. One hour per week, grading based on attendance.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Accounting Intensive I
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to provide students with technical U.S. accounting theory and principles background necessary for graduate work in accounting. Current international accounting convergence issues and standards will be discussed on emerging topics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Taxation Intensive
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with the basic concepts of federal income taxation applicable to all taxpayers. Specifically, principles of taxation for individuals, corporations, and partnerships are discussed.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Accounting Intensive II and Special Topics
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to provide students with the technical U.S. accounting theory and principles background necessary for graduate work in accounting. Current international accounting convergence issues and standards will be discussed on emerging topics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Auditing Intensive
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to provide students with an understanding of the fundamental principles, processes, and ethical considerations involved in the performance of a financial statement audit under U.S. auditing standards.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Emerging Topics in Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with information and practical skills for success in the program and for professional accounting and business career planning, and with discussions of current issues confronting the accounting profession.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Forecasting
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Develops skills to analyze corporate financial reports. Topics include profitability, risk analysis, cash flow analysis, revenue and asset recognition, and forecasting. The skills are useful for students to evaluate financial reporting quality, detect earnings management, and predict firms' financial performance.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Intermediate accounting.

allCourses.title: Advanced Financial Statement Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Develops skills to analyze corporate financial reports with a focus on liabilities, stockholders' equity, and valuation. Topics include forecasting financial statements, cash flows- and earnings-based equity, and valuation models, accounting analysis of mergers and acquisitions, lease pensions, and derivatives.

allCourses.title: Taxes and Business Strategy
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Develops a student's ability to identify, understand, and evaluate tax-planning opportunities. The focus is on tax planning concepts and the effects of taxes on business decisions rather than on detailed tax rules, compliance, or legal research.

allCourses.title: Non-for-Profit Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the accounting and reporting for governmental and non-for-profit entities. Topics include preparation of fund basis financial statements and related reporting and auditing issues. Use of non-financial performance measures for non-for-profit entities is also discussed.

allCourses.title: Accounting Policy and Research
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Considers issues in contemporary accounting standard setting and regulation by examining academic accounting research of the various issues. Enables students to develop their knowledge and better appreciate current debates in accounting.

allCourses.title: Advanced Managerial Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Design of cost information and systems used to plan and control organizational activities; procedures used to account for unit, process, and program costs; cybernetic evaluation of costing procedures; cost estimation, analysis, and accounting via computers.

allCourses.title: Forensic Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Elective course focuses on the principles, and application of forensic accounting.  Topics include the identification, detection, and prevention of fraud, valuations, damage calculations, and litigation support. The role of forensic accountants in the legal system will also be discussed.

allCourses.title: International Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: An online course. A comprehensive study of differences between US GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Intermediate accounting.

allCourses.title: Advanced Auditing and Assurance Services
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to provide advanced coverage of topics and emerging issues in auditing and assurance services. Provides a deeper understanding of the fundamental concepts of auditing, assurance services, and developing hot-topics within the auditing profession.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Intermediate accounting and basic auditing.

allCourses.title: Ethics in Accounting and Business
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to introduce students to the intellectual principles of ethical decision making by emphasizing the theories of ethics and their application in the business, and specifically, accounting professions. MPAC capstone course with a final comprehensive exam for the program.

allCourses.title: Accounting Internship
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with the opportunity to apply accounting knowledge through actual work experiences. The internship experience will provide students with knowledge of career opportunities, an understanding of how accounting plays in today’s business environment, and prepare students for success.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Data Analytics for Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Intended to provide students with an understanding of data analytic thinking and terminology as well as hands-on experience with data analytics tools and techniques. Topics include data reporting, data visualization, and predictive analytics.

allCourses.title: Advanced Analytics for Accounting
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with an understanding of how to synthesize and apply data mining methodologies and advanced data analytic techniques and tools to help solve business and accounting problems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MPAC 242. MPAC 242 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Data Analytics for Audit
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Prepares students to identify opportunities for and apply analytics in the financial audit process. Case studies and project-based learning are used to simulate analytics-based problem solving and business strategy development.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MPAC 242. MPAC 242 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Accounting for Income Tax
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students an understanding of how to master common corporate book-tax differences, compute a corporation’s income tax provision under the ASC 740, recognize advanced topics therein, apply guidance for uncertain tax provisions and assess valuation allowances.

allCourses.title: Advanced Taxation
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to provide students with an understanding of specific current income tax planning strategies for domestic and global businesses. Topics include tax structures, income tax minimization, federal, state, and international income tax deferrals, and income characterization.

allCourses.title: Special Topic Seminars
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected area of Accounting. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Professional Research and Communication
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Combines research of the professional accounting literature on a range of technical topics with a written communication and oral presentations of the findings.

allCourses.title: Corporate Governance
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with an understanding of corporate board governance. Topics include selection of and legal requirements for board members, roles of board committees, managing relations with stockholders and CEOs, and the role of boards in developing corporate strategy.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Accountancy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Individual study under the direction of a selected faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Nano-Scale Materials and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Biomedical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview of the chemistry, physics, and applications of nanometer-scale materials. Explore the effects of composition, bonding, and confinement on physical properties of nanomaterials, their chemical syntheses, and their device physics in electronic, optoelectronic, and energy technologies.

allCourses.title: Synthesis and Properties of Biological, Biomimetic, and Bio-Inspired Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Synthesis of biological materials, including self-assembly and biomineralization, and translational processing to engineered materials via additive manufacturing, freeze casting, and other methods. Subsequent functional properties of these materials are reviewed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and ENGRMSE 165C

allCourses.title: Polymeric Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to physical aspects of polymers, including polymer molecular size and configuration, solution and bulk phase structural properties, mechanical properties including viscoelasticity and rheology, polymer synthesis methods, characterization techniques, processing methods, and examples from existing and emerging polymeric materials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and (ENGRMSE 165A or CBE 40C or ENGRMAE 91)

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior and Design Principles
allCourses.restriction: Mechanical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Aerospace Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles governing structure and mechanical behavior of materials, relationship relating microstructure and mechanical response with application to elasticity, plasticity, yielding, necking, creep, and fracture of materials. Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize the properties of materials. Design parameters.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to experimental techniques to characterize mechanical properties of materials. Emphasis on correlations between property and microstructure. Experiments include: plastic stability in tension, effect of grain size on flow stress, microstructural engineering.  Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

prerequisite_list.title: Principles of Materials Science and Engineering

allCourses.title: Ceramic Materials for Sustainable Energy
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A technical elective for students interested in materials. Topics covered include structure and properties of ceramic materials, and design for sustainable energy applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Computer Techniques in Experimental Research
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles and practical guidelines of automated materials testing. Computer fundamentals, programming languages, data acquisition and control hardware, interfacint techniques, programming strategies, data analysis, data storage, safeguard procedures.

allCourses.title: X-ray Diffraction, Electron Microscopy, and Microanalysis
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Material characterization using X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Topics include X-ray diffraction and analysis; SEM imaging and microanalysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and PHYSICS 7D

allCourses.title: X-ray Diffraction, Electron Microscopy, and Microanalysis Lab
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors only.
allCourses.description: Material characterization using X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Topics include X-ray diffraction and analysis; SEM imaging and microanalysis. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and PHYSICS 7D

allCourses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Treatment of the laws of thermodynamics and their application in understanding properties and equilibrium states of engineering materials. allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.

allCourses.title: Green Engineering: Theory and Practice
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Methods and impacts of selecting alternative technologies, processes, materials, chemicals, to reduce pollution, waste, and use of toxic substances, thereby creating “green,” environmentally responsible, sustainable solutions. Topics include environmental regulations, recycling, life-cycle assessment, economic analysis, design, green chemistry, and toxicology.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Materials Processing: How are Materials Processed to Make Things?
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An in-depth knowledge of manufacturing processes with focus on the fundamentals of materials processing (heat flow, mass flow, fluid flow, etc.). Processing fundamentals that apply to the three main classes of engineering materials: metals, ceramics, and polymers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Composite Materials Design
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fiber-reinforced composites for mechanical applications. Properties of reinforcing fibers. Manufacture of fibers and composites. Micromechanics of fiber composites. Strength criteria and failure modes. Macromechanics in design of laminated composite structures.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and ENGR 150

allCourses.title: Design Failure Investigation
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chemical Engineering majors have second consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Survey of mechanisms by which devices fail, including overload, fatigue, corrosion, and wear. Use of fractography and other evidence to interpret failure modes and specify design/manufacturing changes. Students redesign failed parts or structures based on actual parts and/or case histories.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Surface and Adhesion Science
allCourses.restriction: Chemical Engineering Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Structure, thermodynamics of, kinetics, and reactions on surfaces. Surface electronic and mechanical properties and characterization of all classes of materials including metals, semiconductors, ceramics, polymers, and soft materials. Adhesion between different materials is also addressed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CBE 110 or ENGRMSE 165C) and (ENGRMSE 141 or ENGRMSE 69)

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Materials Processing: How are Materials Processed to Make Things?
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: In-depth knowledge of manufacturing processes (from liquid, solid, and vapor phases) with focus on the fundamentals of materials processing – transport and mechanical forces. Processing fundamentals that apply to the three main classes of engineering materials: metals, ceramics, and polymers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Senior Design Project I
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only. Materials Science and Engr Majors only. MSE 189A, MSE 189B, and MSE 189C must be taken in the same academic year.
allCourses.description: Group supervised senior design projects that deal with materials selection in engineering design and that involve case studies in ethics, safety, design, failure modes, new products, and patents. Activities conclude with a presentation of the projects. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and ENGRMSE 155 and ENGRMSE 60 and ENGRMSE 165C

allCourses.title: Materials Selection and Design
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Meaning and phases of design; design considerations; properties of engineering materials; materials property charts; materials selection; process selection; multi-constraint and multi-objective design. Selection of shape in mechanical components. Designing with hybrid materials: challenges and opportunities. Environmental considerations; case studies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54 and ENGR 150

allCourses.title: Materials Outreach
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Demonstrates major concepts in Materials Science and Engineering. Concepts of materials engineering covered include deformation in crystalline solids, effects of heat treatment on mechanical properties, thermal barrier materials, composites design, mechanical behavior of polymers, superconductivity in ceramics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.description: Students majoring in MSE may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Group Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Group study of selected topics in engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Materials Science and Engr Majors only.
allCourses.description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.title: Individual Study

allCourses.title: Structure of Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Foundations and framework for understanding, quantifying and characterizing structure of crystalline and non-crystalline materials. Focuses on using mathematical and graphical descriptors of structural arrangement, symmetry, short/long-range order, tensors in real space and reciprocal space, fundamentals of diffraction-based materials analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Graduate standing in Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or related educational background (physical sciences or engineering), along with an introductory course in materials science (E54 or equivalent).

allCourses.title: Critical Analysis and Technical Communication I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Develop an understanding of the process to conduct research. Topics include performing analytical analysis of the scientific literature, formation of a hypothesis, defining investigations to validate hypothesis, communicating analysis in written form, writing a research proposal.

allCourses.title: Critical Analysis and Technical Communication II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Develop oral presentation skills and skills to understand significance of published research.  Topics include performing critical and analytical analysis of the scientific literature, connecting core course content with experimental/theoretical methods in the scientific literature, and communicating analysis in oral form.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 201A. ENGRMSE 201A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Materials Physics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the electronic, optical, and dielectric properties of crystalline materials to provide a foundation of the underlying physical principles of governing the properties of existing and emerging electronic and photonic materials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200. ENGRMSE 200 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Nano-Scale Materials and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of the chemistry, physics, and applications of nanometer-scale materials. Explore the effects of composition, bonding, and confinement on physical properties of nanomaterials, their chemical syntheses, and their device physics in electronic, optoelectronic, and energy technologies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200 and ENGRMSE 205. ENGRMSE 200 with a grade of B- or better. ENGRMSE 205 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Materials Science and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.

allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to physical aspects of polymers, including configuration and conformation of polymer chains and characterization techniques; crystallinity visoelasticity, rheology, and processing.

allCourses.title: Design with Ceramic Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Dependence of ceramic properties on bonding, crystal structure, defects, and microstructure. Ceramic manufacturing technology. Survey of physical properties. Strength, deformation, and fracture of ceramics. Mechanical design with brittle, environment-sensitive materials exhibiting time-dependent strengths.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGR 54

allCourses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Engineering Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles governing structure and mechanical behavior of materials, relationship relating microstructure and mechanical response with application to elasticity, plasticity, creep, and fatigue, study of rate-controlling mechanisms and failure modes, fracture of materials.

allCourses.title: Fracture of Engineering Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fracture mechanics and its application to engineering materials. Elastic properties of cracks, the stress intensity factor, the crack tip plastic zone, the J integral approach, fracture toughness testing, the crack tip opening displacement, fracture at high temperatures, fatigue crack growth.

allCourses.title: Transmission Electron Microscopy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The theory and operation of the transmission electron microscope (TEM), including the basic construction, electron optics, electron diffraction and reciprocal space, formation of image and electron diffraction information, microanalysis, and specimen preparation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200. ENGRMSE 200 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Grain Boundaries and Interfaces in Nanocrystalline Materials
allCourses.description: Structure and character of grain boundaries and interfaces in solids including nanocrystalline materials. Role of grain boundaries in chemical segregation, fracture, deformation, creep, conductivity, diffusion, and grain growth. Experimental techniques and computational methods used to characterize and model grain boundaries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200. ENGRMSE 200 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Scanning Electron Microscopy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The theory and operation of the scanning electron microscope (SEM) and X-ray microanalysis. Topics covered include the basic design and electron optics, electron beam - specimen interactions, image formation and interpretation, X-ray spectrometry, and other related topics and techniques.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200. ENGRMSE 200 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Phase Transformations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced thermodynamics and kinetics of phase transformations and phase transitions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MSE 200

allCourses.title: Materials Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics related to classical and statistical thermodynamics applied.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200. ENGRMSE 200 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Phase Transformations and Kinetic Phenomena in Materials
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics related to phase transitions in materials including treatments of diffusion, nucleation and growth, dynamics of diffusional and diffusion-less phase transitions, solidification, and capillarity driven kinetics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 265A. ENGRMSE 265A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Seminar in Systems Microbiology Research
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A research and journal club seminar that covers topics on bacteria and phage using approaches and principles from biology, engineering, and physics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.description: Theory, underlying principles, experimental techniques, and applications of electroceramics and solid-state electrochemical systems. Links solid state physics, atomic structure, thermodynamics, defect chemistry, and transport processes to electrical properties of ceramics - spanning from insulators to fast-ion conductors and HT superconductors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENGRMSE 200. ENGRMSE 200 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.description: Issues focusing on production waste, post-consumer waste, and design and manufacture for recyclability. Students apply those concepts to music from a wide range of historical and cultural origins.

allCourses.description: Introduces students with no musical background to the dramatic and performance conventions of opera, and suggests ways of developing a critical stance vis-a-vis the social, political, gender-related and moral conflicts that are presented by composers and librettists.
