allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Major Composer
allCourses.description: Study of the works of an important composer with emphasis on their significance in historical and social contexts. Composers selected represent a wide variety of historical periods, nationalities, and stylistic orientations.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Music and Gender
allCourses.description: Explores various intersections between music and gender. Examines ways in which gender and sexuality have played a vital role in the creation, dissemination, and consumption of music ranging from medieval Christian mysticism to contemporary hip-hop artists.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Classical Music in Society
allCourses.description: Examines some ways in which classical music has played an integral role in aspects of society. Studies pieces from different cultural, political, and historical contexts in order to understand how musical meaning is created and interpreted.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: History of Film Music
allCourses.description: Course provides an overview of film music history. Special emphasis will be placed on developing an analytic vocabulary for musical elements and cultivating an understanding of how music can function within a film.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Music in Multimedia
allCourses.description: Students explore intersections between music and other media forms through creating multimedia projects, readings, lectures, and discussion. Students produce music, edit video, increase media literacy, and study theories behind how music communicates meaning.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introductory Topics in Music Technology
allCourses.description: Introductory topics in electronic music, digital audio, and other aspects of music technology.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Introductory Topics in Music and Culture
allCourses.description: Examines music and musical practices in different historical periods, societies, and cultural settings.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Asian in Western Music
allCourses.description: Traces and critiques western musical representations of Far East culture and figures, reviewing the reception and significance of these works by present-day Asian consumers of western culture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement recommended.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Popular Music in the United States
allCourses.description: Examines the cultural, social, political, and economic dimensions of popular music in the United States over the last century and a half, with an emphasis on matters related to class, race, ethnicity, and gender.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Music Technology and Computers
allCourses.description: A study of the influence of technology on the musical culture and aesthetics from the 20th century to the present, with particular emphasis on the role of the computer. Work includes lectures, readings, listenings, discussions, demonstrations, writing, and experimentation.

allCourses.description: Development of jazz from African and African American folk origins through blues, early jazz, swing, bebop, "cool" jazz, fusion, free jazz, and contemporary trends.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: The Beatles and the Sixties
allCourses.description: Through a study of the music of the Beatles, students are introduced to selected broader historical and cultural themes (e.g., race and music, gender and music, music and the counterculture) while developing an understanding of the basic elements of music.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: MAHUR-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
allCourses.description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on MAHUR modal system and different instruments of classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: HOMAYUN-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
allCourses.description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on HOMAYUN modal system and famous musicians and performers of classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: SHUR-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
allCourses.description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on the SHUR modal system and different poetic rhythms in classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Rock: The Early Years
allCourses.description: Surveys the social and cultural fabric of the post-World War II United States (from the late 1940s through the early 1970s) as seen through the prism of music - rock and roll music.

allCourses.school: Claire Trevor School of the Arts
allCourses.title: Experiments in Music
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Scientists explain the cognition of music using experimental methodology; artists expand the domain of music by trying previously unknown ways of making it. These two types of experiment deepen our understanding of music, from both scientific and artistic vantage points.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Computer and Communication Networks
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Networking Laboratory
allCourses.description: A laboratory-based introduction to basic networking concepts such as addressing, sub-netting, bridging, ARP, and routing. Network simulation and design. Structured around weekly readings and laboratory assignments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Networks
allCourses.description: Design principles of networked systems, advanced routing and congestion control algorithms, network algorithms, network measurement, management, security, Internet economics, and emerging networks.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NET SYS 201 or COMPSCI 232 or EECS 248A. NET SYS 201 with a grade of B- or better. COMPSCI 232 with a grade of B- or better. EECS 248A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Wireless and Mobile Networking
allCourses.description: Introduction to wireless networking. The focus is on layers 2 and 3 of the OSI reference model, design, performance analysis, and protocols. Topics covered include: an introduction to wireless networking, digital cellular, next generation cellular, wireless LANs, and mobile IP.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network and Distributed Systems Security
allCourses.description: Modern computer and networks security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Group communication and multicast security techniques. Covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Network Coding: Theory and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical frameworks for network coding: linear, algebraic and random network coding; linear programming and combinatorial frameworks. Network code design. Benefits and costs. Practical network coding. Applications to wireless networks, content distribution, security, and other areas.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 248A or NET SYS 201 or COMPSCI 232

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Middleware for Networked and Distributed Systems
allCourses.description: Discusses concepts, techniques, and issues in developing distributed systems middleware that provides high performance and Quality of Service for emerging applications. Also covers existing standards (e.g., CORBA, DCOM, Jini, Espeak) and their relative advantages and shortcomings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: An undergraduate-level course in operating systems and networks.

allCourses.school: Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences
allCourses.title: Distributed Computer Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Design and analysis techniques for decentralized computer architectures, communication protocols, and hardware-software interface. Performance and reliability considerations. Design tools.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EECS 211 and EECS 213.

allCourses.description: Study of Networked concepts.

allCourses.description: Intended to expose students to critical reading and analysis of the primary neuroscience literature. Instructors from departments associated with the Interdepartmental Neuroscience Program participate and discuss topics of current interest.

allCourses.title: Molecular Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Surveys molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in neuronal function, including control of gene expression, post-transcriptional and post-translational processing, RNA and protein targeting, cell death mechanisms, and molecular genetic basis of neurological disorders. Overview of the molecular aspects of developmental neurobiology.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cellular Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Neurophysiological and neurochemical mechanisms of electrical and chemical signaling in neurons. Topics include generation of resting- and action-potentials, voltage- and ligand-gated ion channels, second messenger systems, and synaptic transmission and integration.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cellular Neuroscience Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Intensive hands-on laboratory experience of contemporary techniques for studying ion channels and synaptic function. Experiments include microelectrode recording, patch clamp, quantal analysis of synaptic transmission, heterologous expression of genes for channels and receptors, brain slice, and fluorescence calcium imaging.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Systems Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Study of the mammalian nervous system at the systems level. Anatomy and physiology of sensory, motor, and integrative functions.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences

allCourses.prerequisite_text: NEURBIO 208A
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Overview of fundamental conceptual and experimental issues in the neurobiology of learning and memory. The approach is a cross-level integration of research in molecular-genetic, cellular, circuit, systems, and behavioral analyses.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Foundations in Neuroimmunology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The immune system supports normal brain development as well as controls central nervous system (CNS) infection, and neurodegenerative and neurological diseases. Assesses how the immune system contributes to both host defense and disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Undergraduate- or graduate-level immunology experience is required.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neural Coding, Computation, and Dynamics
allCourses.description: Theoretical principles and biological mechanisms underlying how brains acquire, assimilate, store, and retrieve information, compute adaptive responses to external inputs, and how knowledge is extracted from experience to generate an internal model of the world.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: At least one upper-division course in the field of Neuroscience or one upper-division course in Cognitive Science or Machine Learning.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Scientific Presentation Skills
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: A tutorial seminar on developing skills for presenting research to scientific audiences.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Rigor, Reproducibility, and Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Understanding key concepts in experimental design, execution, and analysis that enhance or detract from scientific rigor.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Bioinformatics and Systems Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students learn the fundamentals of bioinformatics, genomic approaches, and Linux and R program in order to analyze RNA-sequencing data.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Psychophysiological Methods in Clinical Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the principal signals of psychophysiology and outlines how measures calculated from these signals can be applied in clinical research and practice.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: One graduate or undergraduate course in statistics.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Epigenetics in Health and Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the role of chromatin/nuclear structure organization (histone and DNA modification, chromatin remodeling, higher order chromatin structure and nuclear organization) on gene regulation, DNA replication and repair, relevant to development, metabolism, learning and memory, and human disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MOL BIO 203 or MOL BIO 204 or NEURBIO 206. MOL BIO 203 with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 204 with a grade of B- or better. NEURBIO 206 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Clinical and Epidemiological Aspects of Neurodegenerative Diseases
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Clinical and epidemiological aspects of neurodegenerative disorders causing dementia will be reviewed, including AD, PD, FTD, HD and cerebrovascular disease. Seminar format will include student presentations and group discussion.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Regenerative Neurobiology
allCourses.description: Surveys the latest research on regenerative neurobiology. Both basic stem cell discoveries and their potential clinical application to brain disorders will be examined.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neurobiology of Drug Addiction
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of topics in the addiction field, including drug pharmacology, models/approaches to investigate addiction, brain circuits, genetics, epigenetics, and the cellular and molecular biology of drug addiction.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cognitive Neuroepigenetics
allCourses.description: Covers current topics in the emerging field of cognitive neuroepigenetics, focusing on understanding the underlying epigenetic mechanisms of memory formation and persistence. Primary literature will be used to explore these processes.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Balancing Research and Teaching
allCourses.description: The goal of this course is to offer graduate students who have commitments outside of their research program (such as teaching) an opportunity to learn to balance these commitments.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cortex: Structure, Function, and Plasticity
allCourses.description: Structured to include lectures and presentation of papers about cortex with emphasis on sensory-motor cortex. Both historical and current perspectives on cortical structure-function relationship will be critically evaluated.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neurobiology of Aging and Alzheimer's Disease
allCourses.description: Outlines changes occurring in aging and Alzheimer’s disease, and clinical manifestations of those changes. Emphasis on genetic and lifestyle risk factors, molecular mechanisms that are basis for detrimental and protective responses, diagnosis, and developing therapies for aging and Alzheimer's disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NEURBIO 209. NEURBIO 209 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neurobiology of Memory as a Multidisciplinary Science
allCourses.restriction: Majors only
allCourses.description: The study of memory is a highly multidisciplinary science ranging from molecular and cellular studies in reduced studies in reduced preparations to functional imaging studies in humans.  The focus is to integrate across approaches and levels of analysis to better understand how the hippocampus, and its constituent elements, subserves memory.  Emphasis on the challenges of this multidisciplinary field.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Functional Imaging of the Nervous System
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Overview of technical and applied aspects of imaging techniques available for studying the nervous system. The areas emphasized are cellular and subcellular imaging of neural function, systems-level imaging of brain function, and imaging of the human brain.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Analysis of Learning and Memory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Advanced analysis of contemporary research concerning the nature and neurobiological bases of learning and memory. Special emphasis is given to time-dependent processes involved in memory storage.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience of Human Memory
allCourses.description: In-depth treatment of current topics of interest in the cognitive neuroscience of human long-term memory. Topics include methods of investigation of human memory, functional architecture of memory, implicit vs. explicit distinction, and control processes in memory, among others.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NEURBIO 209.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Programming for Neuroscience Research
allCourses.description: A neuroscience-specific introduction to programming and data analysis using either MATLAB or Scientific PYTHON. Students will learn general programming skills and effective use of programming for data management, statistical analysis, and image analysis.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Neurobiology and Behavior
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of Neurobiology and Behavior. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Electronics for Biologists
allCourses.description: Basic principles of electricity; properties and use of discrete components and integrated circuits; circuit analysis and design. Intended for advanced students in the life sciences.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Basal Ganglia and Movement Disorders
allCourses.restriction: Neurobiology and Behavior graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles underlying the organization and functions of the basal ganglia and amygdala are considered. The circuitry, neurotransmitters, and influences on cortex and brainstem motor regions are discussed. Clinical disorders of the basal ganglia, including parkinsonism and ballism, are included.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Neurobiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: The application of genetic and recombinant DNA technology to neurobiology.  Topics include the study of neuronal proteins which play important roles in the formation of synapses and synaptic transmission.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Perspectives in Neuroscience: Past, Present, and Future
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: An overview of the conceptual and technical foundations of contemporary neuroscience from ancient times to the present. The subjects include synapses, neurons, brain organization, sensory, motor and regulatory systems, learning and memory, human brain function and dysfunction.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Statistics and Experimental Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to common methods for statistical analysis used in neurobiology. Topics covered include t-tests, ANOVAs, correlations and regressions, general linear model, power analysis, and non-parametric tests.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Auditory Neuroscience
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary overview of brain mechanisms of hearing. Emphasizes breadth of auditory function and research: single neurons to psychoacoustics, the chochlea to the cortex, and basic science to clinic.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Neurodegeneration
allCourses.description: Neurodegenerative disorders represent one of the most devastating illnesses to afflict humans, and usually occur in an age-dependent fashion. Course reviews the basic mechanisms that underlie cognitive and motor dysfunction in the major disorders of the brain.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: NEURBIO 206.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Developmental Neurobiology—Wiring the Brain
allCourses.description: The development of the nervous system is discussed with particular emphasis on the processes that underlie the appearance of complex and highly ordered neural circuits. Topics include neuronal migration, axon guidance, and formation and maintenance of synaptic connections.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Colloquium in Neurobiology and Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Presentation of contemporary research problems in neurobiology and behavior and related areas by invited speakers.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuroscience Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers emerging topics in addiction neuroscience research in a journal club format. Students discuss recent articles and may present an article of their choosing. Students gain skills in critical thinking and scientific communication.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 6 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: Scientific Proposals for Neuroscience Trainees
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Neurobiology and Behavior Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students learn how to effectively communicate scientific ideas and results. Activities include learning how to effectively write a scientific proposal, how to perform a coherent, persuasive slide presentation, and how to give meaningful, constructive review critiques.

allCourses.school: Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Human Anatomy
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science majors only.
allCourses.description: Human microscopic and gross anatomy emphasizing anatomical structure and basic structure-function relationship.

allCourses.school: Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Human Anatomy Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science majors only.
allCourses.description: Human microscopic and gross anatomy laboratory that combines virtual internet-based anatomy software with classroom in-person traditional instruction emphasizing anatomical structure and basic structure-function relationships.  Course may be offered online.

allCourses.school: Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing
allCourses.title: Introduction to Nursing Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Nursing Science Majors only.
allCourses.description: Covers topics relevant to evidence-based practice; nursing informatics as a specialty; electronic health records and clinical informatics; clinical decision support and decision analysis; using informatics to promote community/population health; telenursing and remote access telehealth; and ethical issues in nursing informatics.

allCourses.description: Conceptual frameworks for professional practice. Scope of professional nursing, jurisprudence and ethics, professional interpersonal relationships, and health care delivery systems in the context of the social, political, and economic environments. Socialization of the student for professional roles in nursing.

allCourses.title: Signal Transduction and Growth Control
allCourses.description: Covers various eukaryotic signaling pathways (tyrosine kinase, ras-raf-MAPK, TGF-ß, wnt, JAK-STAT, and FAS) with an emphasis on the experimental underpinnings. The material is covered in lectures and discussions of pertinent papers.

allCourses.title: Immunopathogenic Mechanisms of Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Campus Honors Collegium students and juniors and seniors may audit.
allCourses.description: Examination of the mechanisms underlying disease states mediated by immune dysregulation including mechanisms of immune evasion by cancer, diseases mediated by cytokine dysregulation, role of the microbiome of the GI tract and of other disease sites, and adoptive T-cell (CAR-T-cells).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: M&MG 215. Recommended: M&MG 215.

allCourses.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Human Disease
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the molecular mechanisms of human diseases, including neurologic, hematologic, neoplastic, and infectious diseases. Students gain an understanding of these mechanisms, as well as models of human diseases.

allCourses.title: Topics in Experimental Pathology
allCourses.description: Select topics related to principles of experimental pathology including normal host responses to disease are presented. Animal models of human disease are emphasized. Material includes both lectures and critical review of the primary literature.

allCourses.title: Experimental Pathology Journal Club
allCourses.description: Graduate-level course, which is open to all years, will involve the reading and discussion of papers, preferably written by the invited seminar speaker. Discussions will cover advanced topics in experimental pathology as related to an understanding of human disease.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Principles of Experimental Pathology
allCourses.description: Introduces graduate students to the general pathologic processes that mediate disease. Topics include cell injury and repair, inflammation, immunopathology, neoplasia, and genetic diseases. Combines lecture, small group discussion, and oral presentations.

allCourses.title: Pathology of Cardiovascular Diseases
allCourses.description: For graduate students interested in human cardiovascular disease. Students receive training in physiology, anatomy, and pathologic processes of the heart and blood vessels. Experimental approaches to study such processes are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Pathology of Pulmonary Diseases
allCourses.description: For graduate students interested in pulmonary disease. Students receive training in physiology, anatomy, and pathologic processes of the lungs and airways. Experimental approaches to study such processes are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Pathology of Renal Diseases
allCourses.description: For graduate students interested in renal disease. Students receive training in physiology, anatomy, and pathologic processes of the kidneys. Experimental approaches to study such processes are emphasized.

For graduate students interested in grastrointestinal disease. Students receive training in physiology, anatomy, and pathologic processes of the gastrointestinal tract. Experimental approaches to study such processes are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Pathology of Gastrointestinal Diseases
allCourses.description: For graduate students interested in grastrointestinal disease. Students receive training in physiology, anatomy, and pathologic processes of the gastrointestinal tract. Experimental approaches to study such processes are emphasized.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PATH 234A

allCourses.description: For graduate students interested in genitourinary tract or breast disease. Students receive training in physiology, anatomy, and pathologic processes of the breast and genitourinary tract. Experimental approaches to study such processes are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Pathology of Genitourinary Tract Disease
allCourses.description: For graduate students interested in genitourinary tract or breast disease. Students receive training in physiology, anatomy, and pathologic processes of the breast and genitourinary tract. Experimental approaches to study such processes are emphasized.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PATH 235A

allCourses.title: Graduate Neuropathology
allCourses.description: For graduate students interested in diseases of the nervous system. Students receive training in physiology, anatomy, and pathologic processes of the central and peripheral nervous system. Experimental approaches to study such processes are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Neuropathology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers genetic and molecular mechanisms of neurological diseases. A grounding in neuroanatomy and prior or simultaneous enrollment in Anatomy 210A or the equivalent is strongly recommended. Resident physicians and clinical fellows can audit the course.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.description: Provided for the preparation and completion of the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Medical Genetics and Genomics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers current concepts regarding mitosis, meiosis, the cell cycle, and chromosome ultrastructure and function. Clinical disorders caused by chromosomal aneuploidy, duplication, and deletion, and principles of Mendelian, chromosomal, and multifactorial and nontraditional inheritance are presented and illustrated.

allCourses.title: Genetic Screening, Prenatal Development, and Human Teratology
allCourses.restriction: Genetic Counseling Majors only. Medical students only.
allCourses.description: Principles and techniques of prenatal, neonatal, and carrier screening. Infertility, pregnancy, and delivery. Normal and abnormal prenatal growth and development. Reproductive and fetal effects of drugs, radiation, infections, and other environmental factors.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PED GEN 200A. PED GEN 200A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Human Genetic Disorders
allCourses.restriction: Genetic Counseling Majors only. Medical students only.
allCourses.description: Inheritance, diagnosis, natural history, management, and counseling considerations for commonly encountered genetic diseases, birth defects, and dysmorphic syndromes.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PED GEN 200B. PED GEN 200B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Disorders due to Inborn Errors of Metabolism
allCourses.description: Aspects of biochemistry and metabolism are reviewed with special emphasis on genetic abnormalities which lead to inborn errors of metabolism. Diagnostic procedures, heterozygote detection, treatment, counseling issues, and prenatal diagnosis are reviewed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PED GEN 200A. PED GEN 200A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Molecular Genetics, Gene Mapping, and Genetic Linkage
allCourses.description: Derivation of different types of DNA probes and DNA libraries, restriction endonuclease polymorphisms, assignment of genes to chromosomes, and genetic linkage.  Emphasis on the use of recombinant DNA technologies and genetic analysis for diagnosis of human genetic disease.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PED GEN 200A and PED GEN 200D. PED GEN 200A with a grade of B- or better. PED GEN 200D with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Quantitative Genetics
allCourses.description: Quantitative aspects of human genetics, including population studies, segregation analysis, linkage, mapping, and genetic risk determination.

allCourses.title: Hereditary Cancer Counseling
allCourses.restriction: Genetic Counseling Majors only. Medical students only.
allCourses.description: Issues in genetic counseling for cancer. Cancer biology; genetic mechanisms and environmental influences in carcinogenesis; tumor pathology; cancer gene mapping; epidemiology. Features natural history, diagnosis, prevention, surveillance, and management of heredity cancers. Psychosocial, ethical, legal aspects of cancer risk assessment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PED GEN 200B. PED GEN 200B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Genetic Counselin Research Design
allCourses.description: Quantitative and qualitative methods for genetic counseling research. Reference management; statistics: sample size, power, and data analysis; reliability and validity; surveys, questionnaires, interviews, focus groups; quality of life and genetic epidemiology research; designing a research protocol; IRB issues; grant writing.

allCourses.title: Cytogenetics Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Practicum introducing methods of specimen collection, short-term lymphocyte and bone marrow culture, long-term fibroblast and amniocyte culture, harvesting and slide preparation, chromosome staining, microphotography, and darkroom techniques. Microscopic chromosome analysis, photographic karyotyping, and appropriate use of cytogenetic nomenclature are emphasized.

allCourses.title: Embryology for Medical Genetics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to normal and abnormal prenatal growth and development of the major systems of the body from an embryological point of view. Intended for first-year genetic counseling students in preparation for clinical rotations.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Genetic Counseling
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Through directed readings, observing patient evaluations, role-playing, and conducting intake interviews, students are introduced to the process of diagnosis, management, and counseling for genetic disease. Psychosocial issues, interviewing techniques, pedigree construction, clinical photography, and various other skills are addressed.

allCourses.title: Clinical Rotation I
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides extensive supervised experience in history taking, interviewing, and psychosocial assessment in the clinical genetics setting. Students independently perform telephone, office, and home-visit intake interviews, participate in counseling, and present cases at patient management conferences.

allCourses.title: Clinical Rotation II
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides further supervised experience in genetic counseling, case management, clinic administration and organization, and the use of community resources. Emphasis is on sharpening counseling skills and on developing a professional identity and code of ethics.

allCourses.title: Prenatal Diagnosis Counseling
allCourses.restriction: Genetic Counseling Majors only. Medical students only.
allCourses.description: A practicum with extensive supervised experience in prenatal diagnosis counseling which provides the student with the opportunity to conduct genetic counseling sessions semi-independently and to further develop clinical skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PED GEN 200A and PED GEN 200B and PED GEN 200C. PED GEN 200A with a grade of B- or better. PED GEN 200B with a grade of B- or better. PED GEN 200C with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Counseling in Human Genetics: Theory and Methods
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical approaches, counseling models and methods, and bio-psychosocial assessment strategies are examined in the context of genetic counseling. Contract-setting, working alliance, the use of self and evaluation methods. Beginning counseling and peer supervision skills are practiced in class.

allCourses.title: Community Resources
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Lectures, guest speakers, and community visits acquaint genetic counselors with public and private health care and funding agencies, parent support and advocacy groups, and other resources to assist individuals and families confronted with genetic disorders, developmental disabilities, and birth defects.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Ethical Issues in Human Genetics
allCourses.restriction: Medical students only. Genetic Counseling Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores major social, legal, and ethical issues in genetic counseling including those arising in genetic screening, prenatal diagnosis, informed consent, privacy and confidentiality, rights of the disabled, new genetic and reproductive technologies, treatment, and access to services.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Counseling in Human Genetics: Putting Thought to Practice
allCourses.restriction: Genetic Counseling Majors only. Medical students only.
allCourses.description: Builds upon the skills learned in previous courses emphasizing advanced counseling methods such as listening, empathy, and collaboration. The counselor's own self-awareness, ethical behaviors, and limits are explored. Individual, team, and group exercises are performed.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PED GEN 202A. PED GEN 202A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Professional Skills Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Hones and augments existing competencies in genetic counseling through ongoing clinical experiences. Develops skills using computers for genetics applications, provision of community and professional education, and clinic administration. Further experience in genetics laboratories or specialty clinics may be elected.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 4 times.

allCourses.description: Exploring modern Iran through film, literature, photography, travel writing, and philosophy and social science texts that introduce students to important concepts in post-colonial studies, social thought, war culture, religion, and media as experienced through the paradigm of a non-Western modernity.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Chemical Neuroanatomy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Organization of the nervous system, especially with respect to chemical identity of elements, for students of pharmacology. Major cell types, methods of study, ultrastructure, synaptic organization of functionally defined systems, localization of chemically defined cells and receptors, and brain development.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Pharmacology
allCourses.description: Application of pharmacological principles in disease therapy.  Advanced pharmacological mechanisms and in-depth study of drug action.  Discussion of several major drug classes/therapeutic strategies:  molecular mechanisms of action, physiological consequences of administration, and clinical use.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Graduate Pharmacology
allCourses.description: Principles of pharmacology and in-depth study of drug action. Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics: absorption, distribution and metabolism, general principles of action and receptor concepts. Discussion of major drug classes: molecular mechanism of action, physiological consequences of administration, and clinical use.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSIO 206A and PHYSIO 206B and BIOCHEM 210A.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Pharmacology
allCourses.description: Introduction to the concepts and techniques used in pharmacological science. Molecular biology, quantitative and biochemical pharmacology, fluorescent probes, behavior, genetics, animal handling, anatomical and receptor binding analysis, methods for ion channel study, the absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination of drugs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neurotransmitter and Drug Receptors
allCourses.description: Ligand gated ion channels, G protein linked receptors, receptor tyrosine kinases, ligand regulated transcription factors, their signaling mechanisms, trafficking and physiological responses. Analysis of receptor properties by pharmacological methods, radioligand binding, and molecular biology.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Pharmacology
allCourses.description: Ligand-gated ion channels, G protein-coupled receptors, receptor tyrosine kinases, ligand-regulated transcription factors, their signaling mechanisms, trafficking, macromolecular complexes, and physiological responses.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the brain and periphery. Molecular biology, signal transduction, transmitter synthesis, and inactivation of major neurotransmitter systems. Drugs that act on these major neurotransmitters.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Design for Pharmacologists
allCourses.description: Population and sample statistics, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, experimental design, power, and the use of statistical computer software.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHARM 251

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethics in Research
allCourses.description: Ethical conduct in research including data handling, authorship, conflict of interest, animal rights, handling of misconduct.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHARM 299
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Applied Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to pharmacological techniques and current research problems; includes laboratory demonstrations and research seminars.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Principles of pharmacology: pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, pharmacogenetics, drug interactions, and toxicity.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Receptors and Drug Targets
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Molecular basis of drug-receptor interaction. Receptor properties including gene and protein structure, signaling mechanisms, trafficking and physiological effects: G-protein linked receptors, ligand-gated ion channels, receptor tyrosine kinases, nuclear receptors, and ligand regulated transcription factors.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Techniques in Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Experimental techniques and model systems used in pharmacological research. Receptor analysis, bioassay, molecular biology, in vitro pharmacology, biochemical pharmacology, imaging, electrophysiology, in vivo pharmacology, disease models.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Design and Data Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. Population and sample statistics, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, and power calculations.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethics in Scientific Research
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Ethical conduct in research including data handling, authorship, conflict of interest, animal rights, and handling of misconduct.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Concepts in Drug Discovery
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Critical steps involved in discovery and optimization of a new drug. Target selection, relationship of molecular structure to pharmacological activities, screening methods, strategies to identify lead compounds, and preclinical characterization necessary for development of the drug for clinical trials.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Topics of current interest in pharmacology; discussion of recent research publications.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Pharmacology I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Topics of current interest in pharmacology; discussion of recent research publications.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 1 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Pharmacology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Topics of current interest in pharmacology; discussion of recent research publications.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 1 times as topics vary.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Master's Project in Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Capstone research paper on topic of interest in pharmacology.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Autonomic and central nervous system pharmacology, including major drug classes and therapeutic uses. Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the brain and peripheral nervous system, including neurotransmitter synthesis, inactivation, and receptor action.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Behavioral Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Pharmacology of integrative function and behavior. Drug treatment of pain. Mechanisms of reward, addiction, and drugs of abuse.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Cardiovascular Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Basic understanding of drugs used in the prevention and treatment of cardiovascular disease. Mechanisms of action, clinical and adverse effects.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Endocrine, Respiratory, and Gastrointestinal Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Pharmacology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Basic understanding of drugs used in endocrine, respiratory, and gastrointestinal conditions, including hormone replacement, contraceptives, and drugs for diabetes, asthma, obesity, ulcer, and gastric reflux. Mechanisms of drug action, clinical and adverse effects.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presentation and discussion of current problems and methods in teaching and research in pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Pharmacology and Toxicology faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
allCourses.description: A selection of philosophical problems, concepts, and methods, e.g., free will, cause and substance, personal identity, the nature of philosophy itself.

allCourses.title: History of Ancient Philosophy
allCourses.description: Examination of the central philosophical themes developed by the pre-Socratics, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, the Stoics, the Epicureans, and the Skeptics.

allCourses.title: Writing Philosophy
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of the aspects of writing that have special importance in philosophy; special philosophical terminology, techniques for evaluating arguments, philosophical definitions and philosophical theories. Requires at least 4,000 words of assigned composition based upon philosophical readings More detail, see file.

allCourses.title: Writing Philosophy
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Discussion of those aspects of writing of special importance in philosophy, e.g., philosophical terminology, techniques for evaluating arguments, philosophical definitions and theories. At least 4,000 words of assigned composition based on philosophical readings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Metaphysics
allCourses.description: A study of one or more of the problems of "first philosophy," e.g., substance, free will, causation, abstract entities, identity.

allCourses.title: Introduction to the Theory of Knowledge
allCourses.description: A study of one or more of the basic issues in epistemology, e.g., the role of perception in the acquisition of knowledge, the nature of evidence, the distinction between belief and knowledge, and the nature of truth and certainty.

allCourses.title: Introduction to the Theory of Knowledge
allCourses.description: A study of one or more of the basic issues in epistemology, e.g., the role of perception in the acquisition of knowledge, the nature of evidence, the distinction between belief and knowledge, and the nature of truth and certainty.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Moral Philosophy
allCourses.description: A study of one or more of the problems of contemporary moral philosophy, e.g., the nature of justice, liberalism versus conservatism, happiness and its relation to virtue and right conduct, the objectivity of moral standards.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Logic
allCourses.description: Introduction to sentence logic, including truth tables and natural deduction; and to predicate logic, including semantics and natural deduction.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Set Theory and Mathematical Reasoning
allCourses.description: An introduction to the basic working vocabulary of mathematical reasoning and proof. Topics include sets, Boolean operations, ordered n-tuples, relations, functions, induction, and their applications to mathematical philosophy.

allCourses.title: Metalogic
allCourses.description: Introduction to formal syntax (proof theory) and semantics (model theory) for first-order logic, including the deduction, completeness, compactness, and Löewenheim-Skolem theorems.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: LSCI 145A or LPS 105A or PHILOS 105A

allCourses.title: Undecidability and Incompleteness
allCourses.description: Introduction to the formal theory of effective processes, including recursive functions, Turing machines, Church's thesis, and proofs of Göedel's incompleteness theorem for arithmetic, and Church's undecidability theorem for first-order logic.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: LSCI 145B or LPS 105B or PHILOS 105B

allCourses.title: Topics in Logic
allCourses.description: Selected topics in mathematical or philosophical logic.

allCourses.title: History of Medieval Philosophy
allCourses.description: A study of some of the major theological and philosophical texts from the Medieval period.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PHILOS 10.

allCourses.title: Topics in Ancient Philosophy
allCourses.description: Selected topics from the writings of Plato and Aristotle, e.g., Aristotle's criticisms of Plato's metaphysics, ethics, or politics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Medieval Philosophy
allCourses.description: Studies of some of the major issues of concern to Medieval philosophers, e.g., universals, the nature and existence of God, faith, and reason.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Renaissance Philosophy
allCourses.description: Studies of such authors as Bruno and Montaigne.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Modern Philosophy
allCourses.description: Focuses on the works of central philosophical figures of modern Philosophy (e.g., Descartes, Leibniz, Hobbes, Locke, Hume, Kant) or on the treatment of one or more central philosophical problems by a number of these figures.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Nineteenth-Century Philosophy
allCourses.description: Studies of some of the major figures after Kant (e.g., Hegel, Nietzsche, Marx, Kierkegaard), especially in German idealism and social thought.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in History of Analytic Philosophy
allCourses.description: Review of central theories or figures in the history of analytic philosophy. Emphasis on writings of Frege, Russell, Schlick, Carnap, and Quine. Topics include the nature of meaning and truth, the synthetic/analytic distinction, and scientific knowledge.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Continental Philosophy
allCourses.description: Studies of some of the major figures (e.g., Husserl), movements (e.g., phenomenology, existentialism) in early twentieth-century continental European thought.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Asian Philosophy
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophies of Asia, e.g. Jainism, Buddhism, Yoga, Vedanta, Confucianism, Taoism, and Shinto.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Modern Philosophy
allCourses.description: A study of major developments in western philosophy from Descartes to Kant with readings from Descartes, Leibniz, Locke, Berkeley, Hume, and Kant.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PHILOS 10 or PHILOS 11.

allCourses.title: Topics in Metaphysics
allCourses.description: Examines central philosophical questions concerning our own fundamental nature and that of the world around us (e.g., causation and necessity, determination, free will, personal identity, the mind-body problem).
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Theory of Knowledge
allCourses.description: One or more topics in the theory of knowledge, e.g., the nature of rational justification, of perceptual knowledge, of a priori knowledge.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Medical Epistemology
allCourses.description: Analysis of epistemological issues concerning medical research and health care. Topics may include medical evidence, transmission of medical knowledge, medical expertise, the epistemology of medical disagreement, classification of illnesses, well-being, philosophy of pain, and medical decision making.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Mind
allCourses.description: Selected topics involving the concept of mind, e.g., the relation between mind and body, the self, personal identity, consciousness, the unconscious.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Religion
allCourses.description: Critical examination of concepts involved in the theological literature, e.g., the nature and existence of God, miracles, the problem of evil, divine command theories in ethics.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Feminist Epistemology
allCourses.description: Investigates the nature of knowledge from a feminist standpoint. Emphasizes the relevance of the knower’s gender and social situatedness in knowledge practices against a traditional account of knowledge as a detached activity of an independent, neutral subject.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Contemporary Philosophy
allCourses.description: A study of recent philosophical developments in Anglo-American and Continental philosophy with readings from such figures as Russell, Moore, Wittgenstein, Quine, Heidegger, and Sartre.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PHILOS 12.

allCourses.title: Topics in Moral Philosophy
allCourses.description: Selected topics in ethics.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Applied Ethics
allCourses.description: Topics may include capital punishment, world hunger, obligations to future generations, environmental ethics, animal rights, economic justice, sexual morality, affirmative action, racism and sexism, or legalization of drugs.

allCourses.title: Medical Ethics
allCourses.description: Analysis of moral issues concerning health care. Topics may include just allocation of scarce medical resources, the doctor/patient relationship, genetic engineering, surrogate motherhood, abortion, euthanasia, or social policy concerning AIDS.

allCourses.title: Topics in Political and Social Philosophy
allCourses.description: Selected topics in social and political philosophy, e.g., the functions of government, the justification of political authority, the nature of democracy, the varieties of liberty, and social justice. Readings from classical and contemporary sources.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Law
allCourses.description: Selected topics concerning legal systems and the concept of law, e.g., the nature and purpose of law, the nature of authority, the relationship between law and morality, law and political-economic systems.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Gender and Race
allCourses.description: Controversies about race and racism, and sex and sexism, continue to play an important role in the public domain. Explores philosophical questions relating to gender and race.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: The Scientific Revolution
allCourses.description: An examination of early modern European science from 1500-1700. Includes primary readings from central figures (Copernicus, Harvey, Bacon, Descartes, et al.); themes include the impact of printing, humanism, patronage, technology, and discussion of the term "revolution" in this context.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Science
allCourses.description: Selected topics in contemporary philosophy of science, e.g., the status of theoretical entities, the confirmation of theories, the nature of scientific explanation.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Physics
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of physics, e.g., the interpretation of quantum mechanics, the nature of spacetime, the problem of quantum field theories.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Geometry and Spacetime
allCourses.description: An examination of the foundations of the special theory of relativity, with emphasis on the geometry of Minkowski spacetime, and its relation to both Euclidean and non-Euclidean (hyperbolic) plane geometries.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D and (MATH 3A or MATH 6G)

allCourses.title: Philosophy of Quantum Mechanics
allCourses.description: An examination of the standard von Neumann-Dirac formulation of quantum mechanics. The quantum measurement problem is discussed along with several proposed solutions, including GRW, many-worlds, man-minds, and Bohm's theory.

allCourses.title: Probability and Determinism
allCourses.description: An examination of a cluster of interrelated issues concerning probability, determinism, logic, and the foundations of quantum mechanics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2D and (MATH 3A or MATH 6G)

allCourses.title: Writing/Philosophy of Biology
allCourses.restriction: Juniors only.
allCourses.description: Philosophy of biology, e.g., scientific method in biology, the structure of evolutionary theory, teleology, ethics, and evolution. Course work includes one 4,000-word and four 1,000-word papers.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Philosophy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of psychology, e.g., the nature of psychological explanation, reductionism, issues in cognitive, behavioral, and neuroscience.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Social Science
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of the social sciences, e.g.: Is their goal to understand behavior or to predict and control it? Are they normative and the natural sciences not? Do they incorporate philosophical doctrines about language and mind?.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Language
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of language, e.g., the nature of meaning, mechanisms of reference, speech acts.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Logic
allCourses.description: Selected topics in the philosophy of logic, e.g., the nature of logical truth and our knowledge of it, the status of propositions, definite descriptions, and existential presuppositions.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Philosophy of Mathematics
allCourses.description: Selected historical and contemporary topics in the philosophy of mathematics, e.g., mathematical truth and ontology, mathematical knowledge, the nature and role of proof, the workings of mathematics in application.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Phenomenology
allCourses.description: A study of the foundations of phenomenology in Husserl and its background in Bolzano, Frege, Brentano, Meinong, Kant, and Descartes.

allCourses.title: Existentialism
allCourses.description: A study of such central existentialist thinkers as Heidegger and Sartre.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PHILOS 7 or PHILOS 150.

allCourses.title: Topics in Feminism
allCourses.description: A study of selected topics in feminist theory and/or gender studies.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Social Ontology
allCourses.description: Examines how things in one’s social environment exist. Such things are compared and contrasted to others in what might be regarded as the given, natural environment. Topics discussed include natural kinds; artifacts; essentialism; constructivism; intentionality; agency.

allCourses.title: Social Epistemology
allCourses.description: Social epistemology is specifically concerned with questions concerning knowledge and justification that arise in a social context. Topics discussed include testimony, experts, disagreement, group knowledge, feminist epistemology, legal epistemology, and epistemology of education.

allCourses.title: Well-Being
allCourses.description: Examines what it is that makes a life good (or bad) for the person who lives it. Topics include hedonism, desire-satisfaction theories of well-being (as well as other such theories), the notion of harm, the possibility of posthumous harm.

allCourses.title: Philosophy of Action
allCourses.description: Philosophy of action is specifically concerned with questions concerning the nature of acting, and related phenomena such as intending, willing, trying, and trusting. It deals both with individual and group action and their moral and epistemological  underpinnings.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Philosophy
allCourses.description: Lectures on selected topics to be given by regular faculty and visiting faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Directed Special Studies
allCourses.description: Independent study on a research topic supervised by a faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Honors Directed Special Studies

allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHILOS 205A or LPS 205A. PHILOS 205A with a grade of B- or better. LPS 205A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Undecidability and Incompleteness

allCourses.description: Formal theory of effective processes, including recursive function, Turing machines, Church's thesis, proofs of Goedel's incompleteness theorem for arithmetics, and Church's undecidability for first-order logic.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHILOS 205B or LPS 205B. PHILOS 205B with a grade of B- or better. LPS 205B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.description: An introduction to the symbolism and methods of the logic of statements, including evaluation of arguments by truth tables, the techniques of natural deduction, and semantic tableaux.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Inductive Logic
allCourses.description: Philosophical questions concerning the foundations of scientific inference, e.g., the traditional problem of induction, the Goodman paradox, the concept of cause, Mill's method of inductive reasoning, probability calculus, different interpretations of probability, and their interaction in inductive reasoning.

allCourses.title: The Nature of Scientific Inquiry
allCourses.description: Investigates the nature, scope, and status of scientific knowledge and the methods used to acquire it. Uses concrete historical examples from a variety of scientific fields to identify distinctive features of the scientific enterprise and explore their significance.

allCourses.title: Contemporary Moral Problems
allCourses.description: Selected moral issues of current interest, e.g., abortion, sexual morality, euthanasia, capital punishment, reverse discrimination, civil disobedience, or violence.

allCourses.title: Philosophy and Psychoanalysis
allCourses.description: An analysis of Freudian psychoanalytic theory and therapy, and its significance for such classical philosophical problems such as the mind-body problem, self-identity and self-deception, psyche and consciousness, innatism, and the origins of moral behavior.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Existentialism
allCourses.description: An analysis of themes in phenomenology and existentialism and their philosophical origins, e.g., consciousness, self and other, freedom and individuality.

allCourses.title: Feminist Moral and Political Philosophy
allCourses.description: Selected topics in moral and political philosophy analyzed from feminist perspectives, e.g., gender-based differences in moral attitudes and virtues, hidden in traditional accounts of political obligation, and feminism and sexual orientation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PHILOS 4.

allCourses.title: The Philosophy of Sex
allCourses.description: Discusses the origins of biological sex, dynamics of sexual selection, sex differences in humans, and the construction of gender in human societies. Seeks to understand the role social values play in the creation of science.

allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Educates pharmacy students about healthy lifestyle choices, the importance of mental and physical health, and self-care. Provides students with methods and techniques for dealing with the stressors of a professional educational environment and life challenges.

allCourses.description: The study of nonprescription products, complementary/alternative medicine, and non-pharmacological interventions for select self-treatable medical conditions commonly encountered by the pharmacist. Emphasis on the pharmacist's consultant role in product selection and non-pharmacological recommendations.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Self Care III: Conventional and Complementary
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Relates to patients' ability to care for themselves with emphasis on the pharmacist's consultant role and continues to explore self-treatable medical conditions commonly encountered by pharmacists, including non-pharmacologic interventions, nonprescription medications, and complementary/alternative products to treat them.

allCourses.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease. Topics include clinical chemistry, clinical toxicology, interprofessional health care, and public health. Covers the cardiovascular and respiratory system.
