allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Analytics and Numeracy I: Biostatistics
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Exposure to basic statistics and techniques that are commonly found in the medical and pharmacy literature, covering descriptive and inferential statistics. Students learn to choose the most appropriate statistical parametric and non-parametric tests and interpret findings from the literature.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Analytics and Numeracy II: Drug Information, Research Methods, and Literature Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses development of knowledge, skills, and attitudes required for biomedical inquiry and discovery, including methods for data retrieval, analysis, interpretation, and synthesis.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Information Analytics and Numeracy III: Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers distribution of disease and health in groups of people and the factors that influence the distribution, including evaluation of therapeutic and diagnostic treatments and delivery of health care services.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Basis of Health and Disease I: Microbiology and Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of medical microbiology, immunology, virology, and parasitology.  Introduction to classification, morphology, and physiology of microorganisms, particularly those that cause human pathology - bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans, parasite, and worms - and the body's immune response.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Basis of Health and Disease II: Microbiology and Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Principles of medical microbiology, immunology, virology, and parasitology. Introduction to classification, morphology, and physiology of microorganisms, particularly those that cause human pathology - bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans, parasite, and worms - and the body's immune response.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Basis of Health and Disease III: Clinical Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Emphasis on normal human physiology and pathology as it related to clinical chemistry and assessment of disease states with the context of the Pharmacist Patient Care Process. Alterations of clinical chemistry results due to drug therapy are covered.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the basic principles of pharmacology, covering pharmacodynamics - effects of drugs on the body - and pharmacokinetics - the process by which a drug is absorbed, distributed, metabolized, and excreted by the body.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers the framework, principles, and core responsibilities of public health research and practice from multidisciplinary perspectives. It also provides the necessary foundation for further studies using crosscutting approaches essential for public health practice.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Principles of Pharmacogenomics
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Walks students through the basics of genetics and genomics. Particular emphasis is placed on the use of genetics or genetic testing to assist in patient treatment regimens and evaluation of disease.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmaceutical Biochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Topics include the biological, chemical and cellular roles of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, hormones, enzymes and vitamins. In addition, the chemical and cellular basis of digestion, intermediary metabolism, biological oxidation and metabolic antagonism are discussed.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmacy Law and Ethics
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to California and federal legal requirements that impact pharmacy practice, emphasizing the legal and ethical principles applied by pharmacists in their decision-making. Explores approaches for resolving ethical dilemmas in patient care.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Health Policy and Pharmacoeconomics
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the organization, financing, and delivery of health care services in the U.S. The relationship of providers, patients, payers, etc., are analyzed. Management and research principles utilized to manage drug therapy are introduced.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Clinical Toxicology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of pharmacology and mechanisms of action are reinforced and applied to learn the clinical effects of acute/chronic exposure derived from environmental, dietary, occupational and pharmaceutical sources. Students focus on information literacy skills and clinical management of poisonings.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medical Physiology with Anatomic Correlates
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concepts of physiology and mechanisms of body function at various levels of organization from cellular to organ systems. Emphasis on quantitative understanding of various body processes. Human anatomy is integrated with physiological concepts. Anatomic-physiologic relationships facilitated through virtual labs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Cannabis Pharmacology and Therapeutics
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students only.
allCourses.description: Provide knowledge about the cannabis plant and the derivative constituents. Introduce the scientific basis for development of cannabis-derived medicinal drug products. Provide evidence-based information to navigate the mass of cannabis information and counsel patients in its use and safety.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Anti-Aging Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses why we age and what we can do about it.  Introduces the five models of aging. Covers the major pathways of aging and drugs that have been demonstrated to extend lifespan in model systems.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmacotherapy Principle to Practice: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation and Cellular Therapy
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Integrates principles of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences with evidence-based traditional and non-traditional therapies for management and prevention of disease in patients receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and cellular therapies.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Mental Health, Medications, and the Media
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the portrayal of psychiatric disease states and psychoactive drugs through the lens of the media. Critically evaluate documentaries, movies, and television series that portray topics such as drug misuse, psychedelic use, and disease states.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Travel Health
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Learn to provide effective pre-travel itinerary-based assessment, planning, and consultation related to vaccine-preventable diseases, prevention of other infectious and non-infectious travel-related diseases, and self-treatable conditions not requiring a diagnosis. Topics include yellow fever, malaria, altitude sickness, and emerging tropical diseases.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Cardiology Pharmacotherapy
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on cardiology specialty topics such as arrhythmias, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic shock, sudden cardiac arrest, advanced cardiovascular life support, and the pharmacist's role in Code Blue situations, medical devices for hemodynamic monitoring and cardiac support, and heart transplantation.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Managed Care Pharmacy I
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the principles and practice of managed care pharmacy, including collection and synthesis of clinical data, assessment of economic data, and decision-making for a Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Leadership and Management
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students only.
allCourses.description: Provide an introduction to various leadership roles in the field of pharmacy, as well as management techniques to engage and inspire team building, cultivate a productive work environment, and develop future leaders in the industry.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Health Coaching and Wellness for Pharmacists
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Trains student pharmacists to use health coaching techniques to care for those with different clinical conditions and goals. Reviews adult learning theories and skills, such as motivational interviewing, as they apply to health coaching. Reviews elements of clinician wellness.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Overcoming Healthcare Disparities in Pharmacy Practice
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Providing an understanding of the causes for healthcare disparities and then  proposing pharmacy practice-based solutions for overcoming them. Engaging with community partners and healthcare professionals for real-world experiences.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmaceutics I
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: The first in a foundational series designed to develop an understanding of the science behind drug formulation, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics and interconnections with the Pharmacist Patient Care Process.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmaceutics II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The second course in a foundational series designed to develop an understanding of the science behind drug formulation, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics, and interconnections with the pharmacist patient care process. Topics include drug substances, dosage forms, and therapeutic effects. Includes laboratory.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmaceutics III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The final course in a foundational series designed to develop an understanding of the science behind drug formulation, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics,and interconnections with the Pharmacist Patient Care Process.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry I
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Application of organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, physical chemistry, pharmacology, and physiology to understand the theory and mechanics of modern day medicinal chemistry. Topics include receptor-protein structure, dynamics, and interactions; drug development and design; and pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Walks students through medicinal chemistry, broadly defined. Students utilize the knowledge gained in organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, physical chemistry, pharmacology and physiology in an integrated fashion as applied to modern medicinal chemistry. Continuation of Medicinal Chemistry I.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Scholarly Project I
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students an opportunity to develop independent thinking, with particular focus on maturing analytical skills. Students are encouraged to develop an independent project, with a mentor, to study pharmacy-related aspects of multiple areas. First phase identifies project focus.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Scholarly Project II
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students an opportunity to develop independent thinking, with particular focus on maturing analytical skills. Students develop an independent project, with a mentor, to study pharmacy-related aspects of multiple areas. Phase 2 focuses on final evaluation of project.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Clinical Trial Design
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students only.
allCourses.description: Provide the basic principles for design of randomized clinical trials; provide a foundation in clinical trial phases and design; and recognize key stakeholders in clinical trials.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Doctor of Pharmacy Epilogue
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reinforces and assesses student pharmacist’s performance on cumulative learning outcomes; pre-APPE and APPE knowledge, skills, and attitudes; entrustable professional activities; team- and practice-readiness; and to demonstrate that student pharmacists are achieving outcomes required by the ACPE.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to engage students and expose them to seminar speakers that come to discuss research or case studies in pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Independent Research
allCourses.restriction: Doctor of Pharmacy students only.
allCourses.description: Supervised investigation and study of topics relevant to the practice of pharmacy not covered in other courses. Intended to facilitate a small number of students performing a deeper dive into topics of particular interest to them.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: New Student Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors only. New students only.
allCourses.description: Weekly meetings consisting of presentations by faculty, professional staff, and Peer Academic Advisors provide information about the Pharmaceutical Sciences major, campus resources, learning skills, and special programs and opportunities.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Physiology
allCourses.description: Covers the function of the human body. All major organ systems are discussed. Designed to prepare students for healthcare careers, such as medicine, pharmacy, dentistry, and for research careers which require basic knowledge of how the human body functions.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 99", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": true, "courseId": "PHRMSCI 120L"}, {"NOT": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Physiology Lab
allCourses.description: Designed to complement PHRMSCI 120. Computer-based lab simulations are used to study the function of the human body. Class physically meet for review sessions and exams.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"NOT": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E112L"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI E109

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Human Anatomy with Pathological Correlates
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers the forms of, and relationships between, the many anatomical components of the human body, including discussion of several pathological conditions of the body as they relate to anatomy.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 97", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 98", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 99", "minGrade": "D-"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 97 and BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99. Recommended: Organic Chemistry series is highly encouraged.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medical Microbiology Laboratory
allCourses.description: An introduction to the structure, metabolism, cultivation, isolation, classification, and identification of the major groups of bacteria. Additional focus on identification of infection and use of antibiotics in diseased patients.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51C. CHEM 51C with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Healthspan Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the complex and multi-factorial process of aging and increases the understanding of factors that contribute to enhanced lifespan, including basic principles of health and wellness and scientifically proven interventions, both pharmacological and non-pharmacological.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and PHRMSCI 120

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropsychopharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the nervous system. Fundamental knowledge for understanding the cellular and molecular actions of drugs and their mechanisms of action on synaptic transmission. Applied neuropsychopharmacology including major drug classes and therapeutic uses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHRMSCI 170A. PHRMSCI 170A with a grade of C- or better

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmacogenomics and Epigenetics
allCourses.description: Survey of the genetic and epigenetic basis of inter-subject variability in response to drugs. Covers drug efficacy, safety, and need for their optimization in pharmacotherapy. Emphasizes genetic mechanisms of polymorphisms in the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of representative therapeutic drugs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Pharmacology I
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Molecular basis of drug-receptor action at the molecular and cellular levels. Structure-function of drug targets emphasizing enzymes, ion channels, and membrane transport proteins. Understanding how the drugs' mechanisms of action contribute to the development of more efficacious and safer drugs.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "CHEM 51C", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "CHEM H52C", "minGrade": "D-"}]}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PHRMSCI 120", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI E109", "minGrade": "D-"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C) and (PHRMSCI 120 or BIO SCI E109)

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Molecular Pharmacology II
allCourses.description: Introductory survey covering the molecular mechanisms of drugs that target the nervous system, such as anxiolytics, antidepressants, antipsychotics, hypnotics, muscle relaxants, and recreational drugs; drugs related to the immune system, including antibiotics, antihistamines, and immunosuppressants; drugs used to treat cancer.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHRMSCI 170A

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Physical Biochemistry
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Thermodynamics and kinetic fundamentals as applied to problems relevant to pharmaceutical sciences such as receptor/enzyme-ligand interactions. Fundamentals of biophysical methods used in the pharmaceutical sciences including structure determination and biomolecular spectroscopy.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PHYSICS 3C", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PHYSICS 7E", "minGrade": "D-"}]}, {"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "CHEM 1C", "minGrade": "D-"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "CHEM H2C", "minGrade": "D-"}]}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "BIO SCI 99", "minGrade": "D-"}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2B and PHYSICS 3C and (CHEM 1C or CHEM H2C) and BIO SCI 99

prerequisite_for.title: Advanced Laboratory in Chemistry and Synthesis of Materials

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.description: Presents information about various fields of research, study, careers, and graduate school opportunities in pharmaceutical sciences. Taught by guest lecturers from various disciplines including 199 research course faculty. Helps Pharmaceutical Sciences students select electives appropriate to their future goals.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI 99 and (CHEM 51C or CHEM H52C)

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmacotherapy
allCourses.description: An exploration of the clinical application of medications to selected disease states. Focus is on an understanding of underlying principles of pharmacology and how this knowledge can be applied to treatment of diseases.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Biopharmaceutics and Nanomedicine
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces theories and tools of new drug formulations. Particularly new novel therapeutics based on biological materials, pathological characteristics utilized to achieve the maximum efficacy and specificity, and drug delivery systems based on emerging nanotechnology are extensively discussed.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Biopharmaceutics and Nanomedicine Lab
allCourses.description: Introduction to cancer drug screening using cellular models, and confirmation of comprehensive therapeutic efficacy using a live animal model. Includes basic cell culture, cytotoxicity assays, cell analysis, drug circulation test, and tumor eradication and imaging experiments. Materials fee.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHRMSCI 170B and BIO SCI 100

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Biopharmaceutics Laboratory
allCourses.description: Introduction to cancer drug screening using cellular models and confirmation of comprehensive therapeutic efficacy using a live animal model.  Includes basic cell culture, cytotoxicity assays, cell analysis, drug circulation test, and tumor eradication and imaging experiments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHRMSCI 170B. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Drug Discovery Computing Techniques
allCourses.description: Techniques used in computer-aided drug discovery, including theory behind these techniques and practical applications. Topics include scientific computing; python; classical force fields and simulations; visualization and movie-making; quantum mechanics in drug discovery; molecular dynamics; solvation models; and several others.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CSE 41 or I&C SCI 31. CSE 42 or I&C SCI 32 is recommended.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethics Conduct of Research
allCourses.description: Covers the ethical responsibilities of biomedical scientists. Topics include, as discussions and case studies, the high standards of science, the responsible conduct of research, animal experimentation, and clinical trials as they relate to the pharmaceutical sciences.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction of the basics of drug activity and mechanisms. Strategies used to identify lead compounds such as natural product chemistry, combinatorial chemistry, molecular modeling, and high-through put screening.  Relationship of molecular structure to pharmacological activity.

Relationship of molecular structure to pharmacological activity. Materials fee.

allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry Lab
allCourses.description: An introduction of the basics of drug activity and mechanisms. Strategies used to identify lead compounds such as natural product chemistry, combinatorial chemistry, molecular modeling, and high-through put screening.  Relationship of molecular structure to pharmacological activity.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C and (BIO SCI 98 or CHEM 128) and BIO SCI 100.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Stem Cell Therapy
allCourses.description: Introduces new paradigms in regenerative medicine involving stem cells, and emerging molecular, nano- and micro-engineered tools for in vivo imaging that is critical for studying and monitoring regeneration. Selected topics include stem cell biology and in vivo imaging modalities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI D103

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Emerging Technologies in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Medicine
allCourses.description: Introduces emerging, ground-breaking technologies in pharmaceutical sciences and medicine, including pharmacogenomics, genome editing, and stem cell and engineered T cell therapies. Explores these novel technologies with both their underlying theories and forward-thinking applications.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Tutoring in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Peer Tutoring Program students only.
allCourses.description: Tutoring program with Pharmaceutical Sciences student peers.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 6 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Professional Internship
allCourses.restriction: Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with opportunity to develop leadership and professional skills necessary for competitive placement in their chosen industry. Students gain new and field-specific skills outside the classroom environment while participating in a supervised internship for a total of 100 hours.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Independent Study in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.description: Students interested in independent study should arrange with a faculty member to sponsor and supervise such work. A time commitment of three hours per week per unit is expected. A written report is required at the end of each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 4 units.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Undergraduate Research
allCourses.description: Original research in the laboratory of Pharmaceutical Sciences faculty. Attendance at regular research group meetings is also generally expected, and a quarterly written report is required. Strongly recommended for students considering research careers and/or graduate degree programs.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Biological Macromolecules
allCourses.description: Introduction to nucleic acid and protein structure, dynamics, and function. Topics include analytical methods, molecular evolution, folding, and catalysis.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Topics in Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Application of pharmacological principles in disease therapy.  Advanced pharmacological mechanisms and in-depth study of drug action.  Discussion of several major drug classes/therapeutic strategies:  molecular mechanisms of action, physiological consequences of administration, and clinical use.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Healthspan Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers the complex and multi-factorial process of aging and increases the understanding of factors that contribute to enhanced lifespan, including basic principles of health and wellness and scientifically proven interventions, both pharmacological and non-pharmacological.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: Undergraduate courses in biochemistry, molecular biology, and basic physiology.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Current Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Math and Computational Biology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Intended to expose students to the primary literature and current research in the field of Pharmaceutical Sciences. Students analyze and present information for discussion. Guest speakers from academia and industry may participate throughout the quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Math and Computational Biology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Intended to expose students to the primary literature and current research in the field of Pharmaceutical Sciences. Students analyze and present information for discussion. Guest speakers from academia and industry may participate throughout the quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHRMSCI 250A. PHRMSCI 250A with a grade of B- or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the concepts and techniques used in pharmacological science. Molecular biology, quantitative and biochemical pharmacology, fluorescent probes, behavior, genetics, animal handling, anatomical and receptor binding analysis, methods for ion channel study, the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination of drugs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Introduction to Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Ligand-gated ion channels, G protein-coupled receptors, receptor tyrosine kinases, ligand-regulated transcription factors, their signaling mechanisms, trafficking, macromolecular complexes, and physiological responses.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Neuropharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Mechanisms underlying chemical signaling processes in the brain and periphery. Molecular biology, signal transduction, transmitter synthesis, and inactivation of major neurotransmitter systems. Drugs that act on these major neurotransmitters.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Experimental Design for Pharmacologists
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Population and sample statistics, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, experimental design, power, and the use of statistical computer software.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHARM 251. PHARM 251 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethics in Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Ethical conduct in research including data handling, authorship, conflict of interest, animal rights, handling of misconduct.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHARM 299. PHARM 299 with a grade of B- or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Pharmacogenomics and Epigenetics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Survey of the genetic and epigenetic basis of inter-subject variability in response to drugs. Covers drug efficacy, safety, and the need for their optimization in pharmacotherapy.Emphasizes genetic mechanisms of polymorphisms in the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of representative therapeutic drugs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: The RNA World: From Discovery to Mechanism
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a comprehensive understanding of RNA in biology. Use of knowledge gained in organic chemistry, biochemistry, genomics, and molecular biology to understand how RNA is integrated into contemporary biology.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: New Frontiers in Chemical and Synthetic Biology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores new developments in chemical and synthetic biology that span the areas of chemistry, molecular biology, genetics, bioengineering, systems biology, and computational genomics.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Advanced Pharmacology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a mechanism-based overview of pharmacology with strong emphasis on clinical application of pharmacology. Students learn the most recent advances in pharmacology as they relate to drug discovery, development, and clinical application.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reserved for current topics of particular interest in areas of pharmaceutical sciences that are not covered by other courses. The subject will vary from year to year, highlighting, for example, significant emerging fields or highly specialized but vital research areas.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Nanomedicine
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students will learn the current challenges in administering drugs to treat highly challenging diseases, the background theories of drug and gene delivery systems, and apply their knowledge in designing innovative forms of therapeutics formulations.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Drug Discovery Computing Techniques

Topics include scientific computing; python; classical force fields and simulations; visualization and movie-making; quantum mechanics in drug discovery; molecular dynamics; solvation models; and several others.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Medicinal Chemistry
allCourses.description: Fundamentals of medicinal chemistry covering diverse aspects of drug design, discovery, synthesis, and development. Molecular basis of drug action with an emphasis on the structure-to-function continuum.

allCourses.title: Stem Cell Therapy

allCourses.title: Graduate Research
allCourses.description: Supervised original research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Research Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presentation and discussion of current problems and methods in teaching and research in pharmaceutical sciences.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Graduate Research
allCourses.description: Supervised original research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Professional Development and Careers in the Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Designed to help Pharmaceutical Science majors select a career track and prepare for graduate program applications and careers in industry.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.description: Limited to Teaching Assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Life 101
allCourses.description: Covers the latest scientific work on the impact of nutrition, exercise, and lifestyle choices on mental and physical health. Motivates students to make positive changes by fostering personal growth.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Gateway to Drugs
allCourses.description: Introduces students to human physiology, how drugs work, and where they come from, common health issues and the drugs used to treat them, and well-known recreational drugs.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Ethical Conduct of Research
allCourses.description: Covers the ethical responsibilities of biomedical scientists. Topics include, as discussions and case studies, the high standards of science, the responsible conduct of research, animal experimentation, and clinical trials as they relate to the pharmaceutical sciences.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: The Art of Public Speaking
allCourses.restriction: Pharmaceutical Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students learn to effectively prepare and present public speeches and slide presentations. Included are storytelling, informative, commemorative, and persuasive speeches, and scientific presentation. Evaluating speeches and strategies to reduce speaker apprehension is also covered.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Honors Research in Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.description: Undergraduate honors research in Pharmaceutical Sciences. A student time commitment of 10-15 hours per week is required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
allCourses.title: Drugs and Society
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Where drugs come from, how drugs work, how and why people abuse drugs, the costs of drug abuse on society, which drugs are commonly abused, and how drug abuse can be prevented and treated. Course intended for non-science majors.

Course may be offered online.

allCourses.description: An introduction to modern cosmology set within the context of general relativity.  Topics include the expansion history of the Universe, inflation, the cosmic microwave background, density fluctuations, structure formation, dark matter, dark energy, and gravitational lensing.

allCourses.description: A series of fundamental and applied scientific problems of social relevance. Possible topics include Newton's Law, calculus, earthquake physics, and radiation.

allCourses.title: Research in Physiology and Biophysics
allCourses.description: Individual research directed toward doctoral dissertation and supervised by a particular professor.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Research in Physiology and Biophysics for First-Year Students
allCourses.description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in the Department of Physiology and Biophysics for first-year Ph.D. students.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Physiology Research
allCourses.description: Introduction to research in physiology and related sciences. Concentrates on techniques emphasized in the various laboratories of the Department of Physiology and Biophysics.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Concepts of Biophysics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Principles of crystallography; introduction to time-resolved absorption and fluorescence spectroscopy; the concepts of kinetic order and kinetic rate theory.

allCourses.title: Electronics for Biologists
allCourses.description: Basic principles of electricity; properties and use of discrete components and integrated circuits; circuit analysis and design. Intended for advanced students in the life sciences.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Medical Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Vertebrate physiology with emphasis on humans and on the relationship between the function of normal tissues and the processes of disease. Fundamental principles of physiology and the interrelationships which control organ function.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: A biochemistry course.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Medical Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Vertebrate physiology with emphasis on humans and on the relationship between the function of normal tissues and the processes of disease. Fundamental principles of physiology and the interrelationships which control organ function.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSIO 206A. PHYSIO 206A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Approaches in Circuit Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces modern methods in circuit neuroscience and how they are used to explore questions relating to the neurological basis of animal behavior. Emphasis is on rodent models but other model systems are incorporated where relevant.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Medical Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: One of the cornerstones of the MS1 Molecular Basis of Medicine block. Includes temporal coordination of lecture material, regular course director meetings, and combined exams with PHYSIO 544: Medical Immunology.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to immunology, but focuses on providing in-depth analysis of selected topics within the broader field of immunology, including relevant research techniques, while improving critical thinking skills.

allCourses.title: Integrative Immunology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. Focuses on advanced topics and cutting edge technologies in modern immunology.  Combination of didactic lectures and student-led journal article discussion.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PHYSIO 215. PHYSIO 215 with a grade of B+ or better

allCourses.title: Immunology Journal Club
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in immunology as related to an understanding of human disease.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 15 times.

allCourses.title: The Physiology of Ion Channels
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses how ion channels work (molecular/structural biophysics) and what ion channels do in diverse cell types (cell physiology). Also discusses the role of ion channels in disease, mechanisms of drug targeting ion channels, and techniques used in ion channel research.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Proteomics
allCourses.description: Introduces students to concepts and methods of proteomics including protein identification, expression proteomics, and protein-protein interactions.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Eye: Health and Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the anatomic and physiological basis of vertebrate vision and disease states in which the structure and function of the eye is disrupted with emphasis on current and developing research areas.

allCourses.title: Practical Structural Biology: How to Use High-Resolution Structures to Guide Research
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Seniors only.
allCourses.description: Geared toward students who want to gain a better understanding of how to use the vast quantity of structural biology information available in publicly accessible databases to help guide their research.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIOCHEM 210A or BIO SCI 98 or BIO SCI M114 or BIO SCI M133 or MOL BIO 211 or MOL BIO 204. BIOCHEM 210A with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 211 with a grade of B- or better. MOL BIO 204 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.title: Topics in Physiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Contemporary research problems in physiology. Students review research articles in current literature and present ideas contained therein, focusing on groundbreaking discoveries and methodologies. Students present results of their own research and attend presentations given by other students and departmental researchers.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Scientific Communication
allCourses.description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Dissertation in Physiology and Biophysics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Preparation and completion of the dissertation required for the Ph.D.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Political Science I
allCourses.restriction: Lower-division students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the variety of statistical applications in the social sciences.  Descriptive statistics.  Measures of central tendency and dispersion.  Percentile ranks.  Standardization and normal approximation.  Basic probability theory focuses on application to statistical inference and binomial distribution.  Laboratory required.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOC SCI 3A
allCourses.overlap: ANTHRO 10A, ECON 15A, PSYCH 10A, SOCECOL 13, SOC SCI 9A, SOCIOL 10A.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Political Science II
allCourses.description: Introduction to statistical inference, sampling distribution, standard error.  Hypothesis tests for proportions and means. Inferential techniques for nominal variables including chi-square, study measures of strengths, significance of relationships between variables, assumptions, data requirements, and types of error in significance tests.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 10A
allCourses.overlap: ANTHRO 10B, ECON 15B, PSYCH 10B, SOCECOL 13, SOC SCI 9B, SOC SCI 10B.

allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Political Science III
allCourses.description: Focus on correlation, regression, and control for effects of variables.  One-way and two-way factorial analysis of variance.  A priori and a posteriori comparisons.  Introduction to repeated measures design and non-parametric statistics. Discusses use of statistics in newspapers and popular magazines.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 10B
allCourses.overlap: ANTHRO 10C, PSYCH 10C, SOCECOL 13, SOC SCI 9C, SOC SCI 10C, SOCIOL 10C.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Science: Political Analysis
allCourses.description: Presents various modes of understanding politics. Emphasis on basic approaches to political analysis, their uses in constructing theories, and their application to particular national political systems.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Science: Macropolitics
allCourses.description: An overview of macro-political inquiry, emphasizing the various determinants of political life in a political community. Explores the origins and challenges of democratic governance focusing on the tension between liberty and equality in a democratizing nation.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Science: Micropolitics
allCourses.description: Introduction to political behavior of individuals and groups within national systems. Three questions addressed: How do individuals come to understand the political world? How do individuals behave within this world? How do groups and individuals engage in the political process.

allCourses.title: Public Opinion
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theories concerning sources of public opinion, processes by which it is altered, organization of citizens’ belief systems, and role of public opinion in government policy. Students analyze survey data as a research project.

allCourses.title: Public Opinion
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theories concerning sources of public opinion, processes by which it is altered, organization of citizens’ belief systems, and role of public opinion in government policy. Students analyze survey data as a research project.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: The American Presidency
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Presents a comprehensive survey of the American presidency and considers the question of political power.

allCourses.title: U.S. Elections and Voting Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines how voters evaluate political parties, candidates, and issues in electoral campaigns to reach their decisions. Numerous controversies concerning the degree of issue voting, sophistication of candidate evaluations, and the decline of political parties are discussed.

allCourses.title: Public Policy Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines different approaches to the analysis of public policy, what constitutes good policy, the role of government, and citizen participation in policy-making. Suggests a policy-design perspective which builds upon other frameworks but concentrates on goals, implementation structures, tools, and rationales.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL E8 and (UPPP 4 or UPPP 166)

allCourses.title: Presidents Since World War II
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Reviews the actions and character of presidents from Harry Truman through Bill Clinton.  Each week a different president is examined from a variety of perspectives.  Students are expected to write a substantial original research paper.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 21A

allCourses.title: American Public Policy
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

allCourses.title: Writing for the President of the United States
allCourses.description: Imagines how White House staffers can help presidents with clear, focused, and effective writing. Through a variety of formats, students study, hone, and practice writing skills that will prove useful in and out of the White House.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 21A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: American Metropolitan Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the politics of urban and suburban America, including the policy making process; the exercise of political power; local politics, federalism and the problems of metropolitanism; and major policy problems facing urban areas.

allCourses.title: California Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the structure and function of California government, traces historical development of political power, with constantly changing casts of power-brokers and seekers. Explores California exceptionalism and the roles played by the electorate, legislature, executive, and organized interests in policy making.

allCourses.title: California Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the structure and function of California government, traces historical development of political power, with constantly changing casts of power-brokers and seekers. Explores California exceptionalism and the roles played by the electorate, legislature, executive, and organized interests in policy making.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division writing requirement.

allCourses.title: The American Electorate
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of how polls are conducted, and how they can be manipulated by question wording, sampling techniques, interviewing procedures, and context. Public attitudes toward Congress are examined. Students analyze survey data on their own as a research project.

allCourses.title: Parties and Political Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A consideration of the role that parties and other political organizations play in the American political process.  Also looks at the development and significance of PACs, interest groups, and social movements as vehicles for democratic participation.

allCourses.title: Representation
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Deals with classical theories of representation: issues of racial and political representation in U.S. legislatures and city councils; proportional representation models; and comparative election systems.

allCourses.title: The Politics of Protest
allCourses.description: Examines the Civil Rights, Black Power, and women’s movements in relationship to the Asian American movement. Uses social movement theories to illuminate the cases, and the cases to critique and revise the theories.

allCourses.title: Latinos in U.S. Politics
allCourses.description: Comparing the political issues facing Latino groups by examining their migration histories, voting behavior, nonelectoral participation, and policy issues.  Latino issues are examined on the national, state, and local levels, including formal representation, immigration, affirmative action, and language policy.

allCourses.title: Comparative Minority Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the political experiences of Blacks, Latinos, and Asian Americans in the United States from roughly 1950 to the present. Focuses on how each group has pursued political empowerment via both conventional political channels and social movements.

allCourses.title: African American Politics
allCourses.description: Examines politics of African Americans in order to gain a broader perspective of the American political process. Major developments in African American politics (including the civil rights movement, Black presidential bids), continuing problem of racism, responsiveness of key governing institutions.

allCourses.title: The United States Congress
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Does the Congress do a good job of representing the American citizenry? Is it the most appropriate mechanism for the creation, resolution, and implementation of public policy.

allCourses.title: The United States Congress
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Does the Congress do a good job of representing the American citizenry? Is it the most appropriate mechanism for the creation, resolution, and implementation of public policy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Congress:The New Institutionalist Approach
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Study of the U.S. Congress emphasizing how rules and institutions (filibuster, veto, the committee system, party caucuses) structure how the Congressional game is played. Combines theoretical study of procedures with the practical study of actual bills.

allCourses.title: Constitutional Convention
allCourses.description: Analyzes the Constitution, its amendments, and periods of Constitutional reform as a foundation for a critical evaluation of the Constitution with an eye both to necessary reforms and to elements of the Constitution that should be maintained.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 21A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: U.S. Immigration Policy
allCourses.description: Examines selected immigration policy debates since the nineteenth century, rationale and consequences of immigration law since 1965, problems of administration, implementation and enforcement, impact of immigration policy on foreign relations, and contemporary debate regarding the future of U.S. policy.

allCourses.title: Urban Politics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines economic limits of cities and welfare policy. Addresses such issues as why are the poor concentrated in the central cities? Which anti-poverty programs will work best in cities? Which level of government can best combat poverty in the U.S.

allCourses.title: Politics of Animal Rights
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Asian American Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines animal rights/welfare movement’s efforts to transform moral, practical, and legal standing of nonhuman animals in contemporary U.S. Explores intersection of racism, sexism, and speciesism informed by theories of race and ethnicity, including Asian American Studies.

allCourses.title: Sex, Drugs, and Rock and Roll: The Politics of Prohibition
allCourses.description: Why and how does the U.S. government prohibit, regulate, or try to control sex, drugs, and rock and roll? Reveals the motivations and politically strategic decisions that underpin these governmental efforts.

allCourses.title: Political Ideologies: The Way We View Our World
allCourses.description: Politics has become divisive and ideological. But ideologies are poorly understood and have become mere labels for identifying friends and enemies. Course analyzes the nature of ideology, focusing on liberalism, conservatism, fascism, socialism, and contemporary "liberation" ideologies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Political Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Majors only. POL SCI 128C may not be taken for credit if taken after POL SCI 137C.
allCourses.description: Examination of how psychological theory and research may be used to better understand political thought and behavior. Drawing on theories of learning, cognition, and personality, discusses such topics as the formation of political attitudes, and the process of political decision-making.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in American Politics and Society
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of American politics and society. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Game Theory and Politics I
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.

allCourses.title: Game Theory and Politics II
allCourses.restriction: Social Policy/Public Service Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: More advanced game theory and its political applications, beginning where Game Theory and Politics I ends.  Examples of topics covered include revolutions; arms race; spatial models of party competition; political manipulation; political coalitions and their power.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 130A or ECON 116A

allCourses.title: Modern Political Theory
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines major thinkers and intellectual movements in the political thought of the 17th and 18th centuries.

allCourses.title: 20th Century Political Theory
allCourses.description: Examines major thinkers and intellectual movements in the political thought of the 20th century.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 31A

allCourses.title: Critical Political Theory
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology and Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Acquaints students with current political theories, critical of conventional thinking, which attempt to join political, economic, social, historical, linguistic, and philosophical concerns to questions involving the relationships between and among individuals, groups, and institutions in the society, economy, and polity.

allCourses.title: Critical Political Theory
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology and Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Acquaints students with current political theories, critical of conventional thinking, which attempt to join political, economic, social, historical, linguistic, and philosophical concerns to questions involving the relationships between and among individuals, groups, and institutions in the society, economy, and polity.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Social and Political Theory
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focus is on recent major work in social and political theory. An in-depth analysis of a relatively small body of writing. Authors discussed include Jurgen Habermas, Anthony Giddens, and Richard Rorty.

allCourses.title: Language and Power
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Seminar to study a theory of how reality/meaning/knowledge is created in language as a consequence of structures of power. 3.5 GPA and/or background in modern language analysis strongly recommended.

allCourses.title: Language and Power
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Seminar to study a theory of how reality/meaning/knowledge is created in language as a consequence of structures of power. 3.5 GPA and/or background in modern language analysis strongly recommended.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Sexism and Power
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology and Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sexism seen as a socially constructed power which creates and maintains gender differences as relations and practices of structured inequalities. Males and females are objects constructed in a powered language dominated and controlled by males to their positional/distributional advantage.

allCourses.title: Sexism and Power
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology and Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sexism seen as a socially constructed power which creates and maintains gender differences as relations and practices of structured inequalities. Males and females are objects constructed in a powered language dominated and controlled by males to their positional/distributional advantage.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Origins of Liberalism
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the ideals, social forces, and historical events that gave rise to liberal political theory. Topics include patriarchal authority, the divine right of kings, religious toleration, slavery, colonialism, political economy, the evolution of law, and tensions between liberty and equality.

allCourses.title: Just War Revisited
allCourses.description: Examines the evolution of the doctrine of the just war across the history of Western political thought, the importance of changes in the doctrine and whether it applies today; examines international relations case studies to determine today's relevancy.

allCourses.title: Logical Models in Social Sciences
allCourses.description: Science asks two questions. "How things are?" leads to measurement and statistical analysis. But we see only what we look for. "How things should be, on logical grounds?" leads to quantitative logical models which tell us what to look for.

allCourses.title: Cannibals and Conquistadores: The Philosophy of the Other
allCourses.description: Examines critically the notion of the "other" by looking at the philosophical challenges difference poses in the context of the European discovery of the New World. Seeks to understand the naissance of the concept of human rights and tolerance.

allCourses.title: Cannibals and Conquistadores: The Philosophy of the Other
allCourses.description: Examines critically the notion of the "other" by looking at the philosophical challenges difference poses in the context of the European discovery of the New World. Seeks to understand the naissance of the concept of human rights and tolerance.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Middle East Narratives
allCourses.description: Explores various narratives of peoples living in the Middle East: Bedouins, Jews, Muslims, Christians, Druze, Baha’i; looks at how their identities were formed and altered over time through empire, religion, exodus, war, democracy, diasporas; focus is philosophical and historical.

allCourses.title: France and You: Trans-Atlantic Problems and Partnerships - Past, Present, Future
allCourses.description: Co-taught by professors from UC and Sciences Po, French and UCI students are brought together in a virtual classroom. Students engage in joint projects on issues of global import: democratic fragility, race relations, international security, and climate change.

allCourses.title: Types of Political Representation
allCourses.restriction: Recommended: Upper-Division students. Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Political representation plays an important role in democratic systems, but is elusive once examined closely.  Students delve into the concept and relate different views to political life. Half of the course is spent on writing instruction.

allCourses.title: Types of Political Representation
allCourses.restriction: Recommended: Upper-Division students. Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.

allCourses.restriction: Psychology and Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
