Drawing on theories of learning, cognition, and personality, discusses the formation of political attitudes, the process of political decision-making, the nature of political leadership.

allCourses.title: The Moral of the Story: Introductory Seminar in Ethics
allCourses.description: Introduces major theories and classic texts in ethics, from Plato and Aristotelian virtue ethics to utilitarianism and Kant and contemporary moral psychology.

allCourses.title: Moral of the Story: Introduction to Ethics
allCourses.description: Focuses on how we learn about ethics from stories, in the form of fables, bedtime stories, religious stories, soap operas, television, and movies as adults. Students bring in stories that informed their own ethical development.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Ethics of Difference
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines differences traditionally judged politically salient—race, ethnicity, religion, gender. Personal interviews with an elderly person encourage students to understand the social construction of difference and to reexamine their own attitudes by putting themselves in the place of another.

allCourses.title: Ethics of Difference
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines differences traditionally judged politically salient—race, ethnicity, religion, gender. Personal interviews with an elderly person encourage students to understand the social construction of difference and to reexamine their own attitudes by putting themselves in the place of another.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: The Moral Life During War
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Can people keep their humanity during war? What does the term humanity signify when simply surviving requires faith, courage, and desperation? When facing wartime brutality, must we abrogate morality? What does it mean to compose a moral life during war?.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Political Theory and Methods
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of political theory and methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: International Political Economy
allCourses.description: Examination of problems in global political-economic relations through competing conceptual lenses or grand theories: mercantilism, liberalism, and Marxism. Surveys North-North and North-South issues relating power and wealth.

allCourses.title: International Political Economy of East Asia
allCourses.description: Integration of theoretical perspectives in international political economy with the study of economic development in East Asia, with special emphasis on regional integration.

allCourses.title: Immigration Politics in Western Europe
allCourses.description: Examines the politics of immigration in Western Europe. Considers historical, economic, political, and social dimensions of immigration as well as the nature of ensuing conflict. Students investigate a variety of immigrant-related policies, including asylum, citizenship, and integration.

allCourses.title: US Foreign Policy Toward Asia
allCourses.description: U.S. policy toward the countries of East Asia: bilateral and regional security relationships, U.S. economic relations with the major Asian countries, the development of regional institutions, and human rights.

allCourses.title: The International Relations of East Asia
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Surveys various aspects of relations between the nations of East Asia. Topics include the historical development of the region; current political and security relations, including the impact of the American military presence.

allCourses.title: U.S. Foreign Policy I: Globalism and Cold War
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Looks at changing international perspectives, policy responses, and military strategies of presidential administrations from Truman to Reagan. In assessing the motives and objectives of U.S. foreign policy leaders during the “Cold War” era, the concept of “national interest” is examined.

allCourses.title: U.S. Foreign Policy II: Cold War Decline & After
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Deals with U.S. foreign policy from the post-Vietnam War era through the collapse of the Cold War and into the emergence of the post-Cold War era, roughly from 1972 to the present.

allCourses.title: U.S. Foreign Policy III: National Security Decision-Making
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors and International Studies majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Concept of "national security" from 1947-1990s is reviewed. Organizational and psychological factors that influence decision-making, the dangers of "groupthink," and the issue of accountability are analyzed. National security agenda (military, economic, environmental, and social) for the 1990s is discussed.

allCourses.title: US Coercive Diplomacy
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the theory of compellence and the U.S. practice of coercive diplomacy - the power to change behavior of other governments. Specific case examples: the Cuban missile crisis, bombing of North Vietnam, the Nicaraguan Contras, Desert Shield/Desert Storm, and Libya.

allCourses.title: Human Rights and Foreign Policy
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analyzes theories, patterns, and cases of human rights foreign policy. How do countries pursue the values and standards of human rights in their foreign relations. How does the U.S. fit into worldwide trends? Examines historical and contemporary cases.

allCourses.title: U.S. Intervention in Latin America
allCourses.description: Explores political, economic, social, and cultural ties that bind Latin America to the United States. Focuses on U.S. intervention and Latin American response from early nineteenth century to present day. Case studies include Mexico, Guatemala, Cuba, Chile, and Central America.

allCourses.title: East Asian Security
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of issues in East Asian security including U.S.-China relations, economic interdependence, global supply chains, South China Sea, environmental cooperation, COVID-19, and others. Includes Oxford-style debates.

allCourses.title: Globalization and Its Discontents
allCourses.description: Reviews current literature on globalization and its impact on global, regional, and domestic politics. Explores how different states, nations, and cultures respond to common global predicaments and opportunities emanating from the international economy and the global institutions associated with it.

allCourses.title: Intelligence in International Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science and International Studies majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Intelligence agencies, activities, and functions—their impact on international politics; how governments and societies seek to control intelligence agencies and activities; and how intelligence agencies work—their techniques, resources, technology, problems, successes, and failures.

allCourses.title: Homeland Security
allCourses.description: Examines the 9/11 origins of the concept of homeland security; assess the evolution, structure, and operations of the Department of Homeland Security; critically examines the evolution of threat assessment to the U.S. and the utilization of risk management methodologies.

allCourses.title: Approaches to International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Reviews theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of international relations using contending perspectives to analyze power and influence, capabilities, interdependence, reciprocity, international regimes, anarchy, cooperation, imperialism, and hegemony.

allCourses.title: Ethics in an Age of Terror and Genocide
allCourses.description: Original sources document personal impact of wars on genocides, from World War II to the Bosnian and Rwandan genocides and current wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. Students train for and conduct personal interviews with someone who lived through a war.

allCourses.title: Ethics and International Relations
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the dynamic field of ethics and international relations. A variety of traditional and emerging perspectives are examined, skeptical views are discussed in detail, and arguments are illustrated with current cases.

allCourses.title: Religion and World Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between religion and world politics historically and today, focusing on connections with peace/war, democracy, human rights, secularism(s), and globalization. Covers major debates, scholarship, concepts, and theories through class exercises, exams, and essays.

allCourses.title: International Humanitarianism
allCourses.description: Examines, analyzes, and evaluates the humanitarian phenomenon, the actors involved in it (including states, international organizations (IOs), and nongovernmental organizations (NGOs)), the rise of a body of international humanitarian law, and the problems and debates associated with international humanitarianism today.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: International Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Active learning course that examines origins, decision-making processes, activities, and evolution of leading international organizations (e.g. U.N., NATO, EU, AU, WTO, World Bank, IMF). Activities include drafting reforms, applying theory, assessing dysfunctions, and participating in U.N. negotiation simulations.

allCourses.title: Critical Investigations into Humanitarianism in Africa
allCourses.description: Explores the complex phenomenon of aid to Africa (emergency and development aid), and the representational, cultural, historical, and other reasons why some participants and many observers critique it. Students occasionally engage with peers and faculty in African institutions.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of international relations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Seminar on Regime Change in East Asia
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines nine factors relevant to regime change, studying one factor each week in class.  Students write four short (two-page) analytic papers, and one eight-ten-page research paper on one country.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 6A and POL SCI 6B and POL SCI 6C.

allCourses.title: Seminar on Regime Change in East Asia
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines nine factors relevant to regime change, studying one factor each week in class.  Students write four short (two-page) analytic papers, and one eight-ten-page research paper on one country.

allCourses.title: East Asian Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the recent history and political systems of China, Japan, and Korea, comparing the three countries with each other and with occasional reference to the United States, British, and French systems.

allCourses.title: Political Power in Contemporary China
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analyzes the sources of political power in contemporary China, including historical legitimacy, political institutions, and Chinese Communist Party power. Identifies challenges to the CCP’s rule and rising socio-political issues such as mass protest, censorship, and the environment.

allCourses.title: Chinese Politics: Policy, Leadership, and Change
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines major policies from 1949 to the present, and considers the changing role of the Communist Party and its shifting treatment of various social groups; the era of Mao Zedong, reforms under Deng, and post-Deng politics.

allCourses.title: Are Chinese Politics Changing?
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: There’s been speculation about whether the Chinese political system is fundamentally changing. This upper-division writing seminar reviews new books on this topic and considers the question from a range of angles. Four two-page papers and one 8–10-page paper required.

allCourses.title: Are Chinese Politics Changing?
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: There’s been speculation about whether the Chinese political system is fundamentally changing. This upper-division writing seminar reviews new books on this topic and considers the question from a range of angles. Four two-page papers and one 8–10-page paper required.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Korean Politics and Society
allCourses.description: Examination of contemporary political/social structures and process of Korea (South and North). Historical and cultural influences on current political systems and policies. Also included are economic development, national security, unification issues, and foreign relations.

allCourses.title: Electoral Systems
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Worldwide overview of electoral laws by which votes are converted into assembly seats. Systematic analysis of these laws and their effect on political process/stability. Single-, two-, and multi-party systems. Proportional representation versus plurality rule. Majoritarian and consensus patterns of government.

allCourses.title: Voting and Political Manipulation
allCourses.restriction: Business Economics Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to social choice and cooperative games. Topics include majority rule, types of voting methods, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.

allCourses.title: German Politics and Society
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Concentrates on twentieth-century German politics and society, focusing on the contemporary political system of democratic West Germany. Study of the historical legacies of Weimar and the Nazi period, the postwar division between the two states and their reunification.

allCourses.title: West European Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores four main themes: (1) thinking scientifically about politics; (2) understanding the linkages between different political structures and spheres of activity; (3) evaluating some theories about politics; (4) learning about three countries: Britain, France, and Germany.

allCourses.title: European Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the politics of Europe including the smaller countries and the former Warsaw Pact. Includes case study of three or four countries, as well as contemporary issues such as globalization, immigration, population decline, and European integration.

allCourses.title: Political Economy of Development
allCourses.description: Why are some countries rich and some countries poor? In Political Economy of Development, students assess and evaluate competing hypotheses on what drives social, economic, and political development around the world.

allCourses.title: Immigration Politics in Western Europe
allCourses.description: Examines immigration politics in Western Europe, analyzing trends and policy from the postwar period through to today. Topics include citizenship, immigrant integration, asylum, the far-right, and a rotating focus on contemporary issues, e.g., terrorism, Islamophobia.

allCourses.title: Latin American Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the main concepts and theoretical approaches underlying the study of Latin American politics, examines recent political dynamics, and explores the challenges the region faces in the twenty-first century and how countries will attempt to address them.

allCourses.title: Canadian Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses the basic structures and processes of contemporary Canadian government and politics. Additional topics may include regionalism, federalism, western alienation and oil, Canadian solutions to social welfare policy questions, developments in Quebec, and other issues associated with French-English relations.

allCourses.title: Human Rights
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the causes and consequences of human rights violations with a focus on Latin America. What are human rights? When and where are they violated? What political mechanisms are available to deal with human rights problems? How effective are they.

allCourses.title: Cuban Society and Revolution
allCourses.description: Explores the causes, development, and legacy of the 1959 Revolution. Themes include economic dependency, democracy, race, gender, culture, and the always volatile relations between Cuba and the United States.

allCourses.title: Comparative Politics: Four Nations, Three Continents
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies four countries in a comparative fashion: their respective political histories and cultural traditions; actual differences among their superficially similar party, parliamentary, and executive institutions; contemporary economic policy. The countries represent three continents and varying levels of economic development.

allCourses.title: Peoples and Cultures of Post-Soviet Eurasia
allCourses.description: Examines the cultures and political conflicts of the more than 130 indigenous ethnic groups in the European and Asian territories of the former U.S.S.R. Emphasis is on the theoretical issues of ethnicity, nationalism, and conflict management.

allCourses.title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
allCourses.description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

allCourses.title: Jews and Power
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority.

allCourses.title: Antisemitism
allCourses.description: Covers the key concepts, sources, and dynamics of historical and contemporary antisemitism. Topics covered include the politics of anti-Jewish hatred, conspiracy theories, and the Holocaust.

allCourses.title: US Government in Comparative Perspective
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the United States in comparative perspective, covering general features of the United States and other countries, such as institutional design and policy choices. Addresses the debates about American exceptionalism and American decline.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: New Democracies
allCourses.description: Examines what democracy is; considers competing theories about its causes; explores multiple democratic institutions; discusses several types of democracy; and analyzes various aspects of democratic quality and stability, focusing on Eastern Europe, Latin America, and sub-Saharan Africa.

allCourses.title: Organizations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: How bureaucracies, formal organizations, and voluntary associations work, how/why they grow, and where they are going. History and structure of organizational rationality; dynamics of organized groups; behavior in organizations; limits of bureaucratization and attempts to overcome these limits through decentralization.

allCourses.title: Political Economy of Japan
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Surveys postwar developments in the politics and political economy of Japan. Topics include the political and institutional context of policy making; pressures for change which Japan's political economy has faced in the last decade; Japan's past and present foreign policies.

allCourses.title: Political Participation
allCourses.description: The ways in which people in various political systems take part in politics, especially in activities directed toward affecting outcomes.  Who is active, what they do, why they do it, and what difference it makes.

allCourses.title: Participation and Representation
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the concepts "political participation" and "political representation" and the interconnection between these concepts. Addresses both the theoretical issues and debates raised by these concepts and considers how they are studied empirically.

allCourses.title: Citizen Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Study of the role of public opinion in the political process. Reviews some key research approaches and findings on which our current understanding of public opinion is based. Provides an opportunity to conduct research and to analyze public opinion surveys.

allCourses.title: Citizen Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Study of the role of public opinion in the political process. Reviews some key research approaches and findings on which our current understanding of public opinion is based. Provides an opportunity to conduct research and to analyze public opinion surveys.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Protests, Movements, and Revolutions
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of models of collective action drawn from sociology, economics, psychology, and political science. Focus on areas such as social movements, strikes, crowd psychology, cults, fads, fashions, public opinion, and symbolic and mythical elements in collective culture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCIOL 1 or POL SCI 11A or ECON 1

prerequisite_list.title: Introduction to Political Science: Political Analysis

allCourses.title: Nationalism
allCourses.description: Nationalism, one of the most potent social and political forces of the twentieth century, is explored. Seeks to understand the sources and nature of various forms of nationalism.

allCourses.title: Nationalism
allCourses.description: Nationalism, one of the most potent social and political forces of the twentieth century, is explored. Seeks to understand the sources and nature of various forms of nationalism.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: International Divided Cities
allCourses.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

allCourses.title: Afghanistan
allCourses.description: Provides an examination of Afghanistan's traditional social organization, economy, political organization, and relationship among ethnic groups as a basis for discussing the consequences of domestic political turmoil and foreign interventions over the last 20 years. Current situation and future addressed.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Contemporary Middle East Politics
allCourses.description: An overview of basic issues that shape the politics of the Middle East and North Africa. Themes include implication of the colonization era, nation-state formation, inter-Arab relations, nationalism, Arab-Israel conflict, Islamic resurgence, and more.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Comparative Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of comparative politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
allCourses.description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Race and Ethnicity Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of race and ethnicity. Topics vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Law and its various roles in society. The nature and meaning of law; legality and power in the American system; law as a mechanism for social change; the role of law in dispute processing, social control, compliance with judicial decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A

allCourses.title: Law and Society
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Law and its various roles in society. The nature and meaning of law; legality and power in the American system; law as a mechanism for social change; the role of law in dispute processing, social control, compliance with judicial decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Jurisprudence
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of legal philosophies.  Explores jurisprudence from the ancient Greeks to the present, including natural law philosophy; legal positivism and realism; sociological jurisprudence; and liberal, radical, and conservative thought.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A

allCourses.title: Comparative Constitutional Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the impact of constitutional courts on politics and policy-making in Canada, France, Germany, and the United States. Cases may focus on the constitutional politics of free speech, abortion, rights to property, and the conduct of foreign relations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A.

allCourses.title: Comparative Constitutional Politics
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the impact of constitutional courts on politics and policy-making in Canada, France, Germany, and the United States. Cases may focus on the constitutional politics of free speech, abortion, rights to property, and the conduct of foreign relations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: American Constitutional Law
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: American constitutional interpretation of cases involving separation of powers, federal-state relations, rights of property, free expression, privacy, criminal due process, political participation, and equality. Includes legal research methods, development of judicial review, legal reasoning, and impact of Supreme Court decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A

allCourses.title: Law in the Twenty-First Century
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the complex relationship between law, the social sciences, and modern society.  Lectures explore such issues as the interplay between technology and constitutional rights, the impact of science on law, and the evolving roles of attorneys and judges.

allCourses.title: Legal Implications of the Drug Trade
allCourses.description: Examines United States policy to combat domestic and international narcotics trafficking. Analyzes the national drug policy and program implementation by federal and state agencies. Considers the effects of these policies on our individual constitutional rights and the criminal justice system.

allCourses.title: International Law
allCourses.description: Examination of the origin, changing structure, application of international law, and the role of legal norms in regulating the behavior of states and maintaining international order.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A

prerequisite_for.title: International Law and the U.S. Legal System

allCourses.title: International Law and the U.S. Legal System
allCourses.description: Explores how international law and U.S. law interact, focusing on recent cases and controversies. Topics include: treaty and customary law as U.S. law; international human rights litigation in U.S. courts; war powers; detentions in the war on terror; and torture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A or POL SCI 172A.

allCourses.title: Constitution and Rights
allCourses.description: How are constitutions crafted, maintained, and changed?  Does constitutionalism support or undermine democracy?  What difference do rights and constitutional courts make?  Explores these questions through a comparative examination of the theory and practice of constitutionalism in developing democracies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A

allCourses.title: Courts in New Democracies
allCourses.description: Examines the conceptual, theoretical, and empirical foundations of the study of courts and politics in new democracies, introducing students to a variety of contemporary debates about how political dynamics shape courts, and how courts shape politics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A

allCourses.title: Civil Liberties
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Political analysis of selected Supreme Court cases involving claims under the Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment. Topics include:  race, sex, and other forms of discrimination; criminal justice; privacy; freedom of speech and related claims.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A

allCourses.title: Contemporary Constitutional Rights
allCourses.restriction: Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses the interpretation and application of the United States’ fundamental rules. These rules tell us something about the goals of society, and the means chosen to achieve them by allocating rights, duties, costs, and benefits among its members.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 71A.

allCourses.title: U.S. Supreme Court
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview and analysis of the role played by the U.S. Supreme Court in the American political system. Judicial review, appointment of justices, judicial activism and judicial restraint, process of case selection, court deliberation, land decision-making, impact of Supreme Court decisions.

allCourses.title: U.S. Supreme Court
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview and analysis of the role played by the U.S. Supreme Court in the American political system. Judicial review, appointment of justices, judicial activism and judicial restraint, process of case selection, court deliberation, land decision-making, impact of Supreme Court decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: The Bill of Rights in Film
allCourses.description: Focuses on ways American cinema has portrayed, represented, and analyzed U.S. Bills of Rights. Juxtaposes cinematic presentations on specific Bill of Rights clauses, treating films as cultural texts, with pertinent judicial decisions and more scholarly appraisals of those same provisions.

allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of public law. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

allCourses.description: Supervised internship and study in political, governmental, nonprofit, or related organizations for students participating in the Department’s Public Affairs Internship Program. Enrollment dependent upon availability of intern positions.

allCourses.description: Doctoral training requires more than learning substantive debates and research methods; it also requires students learn professional practices, routines, and expectations.  This year-long workshop offers students a mix of professional development, outside speakers, and casual conversations with departmental faculty.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Doctoral training requires more than learning substantive debates and research methods; it also requires students learn professional practices, routines, and expectations.  This year-long workshop offers students a mix of professional development, outside speakers, and casual conversations with departmental faculty.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 210A

allCourses.title: Colloquium
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Doctoral training requires more than learning substantive debates and research methods; it also requires students learn professional practices, routines, and expectations.  This year-long workshop offers students a mix of professional development, outside speakers, and casual conversations with departmental faculty.
