allCourses.title: Foundations of Modern Political Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to foundational debates and controversies in contemporary political science, exploring these issues through the prism of nineteenth, twentieth and twenty-first century scholars who have profoundly shaped the contours of contemporary political science.

allCourses.title: Micropolitics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with comprehensive introduction to the substance and methods of the study of political behavior. Focuses on the level of individual behavior, but the relation to macrosocial analysis is considered.

allCourses.title: Macropolitics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines some of the major research issues in political science involving macro-level questions: systemic processes, political institutions, or system outputs.

allCourses.title: Public Opinion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the study of U.S. public opinion. Provides an overview of the theories regarding opinion formation, the methodologies employed, and the role of public opinion in democratic governments.

allCourses.title: Ethics Workshop
allCourses.description: Students find an important question in ethics, search literature to assess topic's importance, post question to be researched, propose method of analysis and type of data, analyze data, and note how their works contribute to knowledge in the field.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Politics and Society
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in politics and society.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to American Government
allCourses.description: Introduction to American political processes and institutions. Topics include elections, political participation, parties, interest groups, the Presidency, Congress, the bureaucracy, and the judiciary.

prerequisite_for.title: Writing for the President of the United States

allCourses.title: Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst.  Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.

allCourses.title: Collaborative Governance and Public Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to inclusive management.  To make effective use of public resources, public managers are inventing ways of managing that alter relationships within organizations, between organizations, between sectors, and with the public.  Requires rethinking fundamentals such as leadership and motivation.

allCourses.title: Public Opinion
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the study of U.S. public opinion. Provides an overview of the theories regarding opinion formation, the methodologies employed, and the role of public opinion in democratic governments.

allCourses.title: Theories of Power and Empowerment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies different ways of thinking about power and its uses. Explores theories of power that inform various notions of empowerment, including resistance, participatory democracy, and workplace empowerment.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in American Politics
allCourses.description: Current research in American Politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Political Epistemology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on fundamental issues of knowledge in the study of politics, especially interconnections and tensions between politics and knowledge.  Counts as the Field Seminar in Political Theory.

allCourses.title: Theories of Textual Interpretation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examination of different theories of textual interpretation, including Straussian, hermeneutical, poststructuralist, feminist, postcolonial, and critical race theories. Key questions include: How does one go about the task of interpreting texts? What makes one interpretation better or more insightful than another.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Voting Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to voting modules. Substantive topics include majority rule, voting methods and their properties, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.

allCourses.title: Electoral Systems Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies electoral systems worldwide, analyzes their effect on the number of parties and duration of government cabinets, and applies the results to the present democratizing countries.

allCourses.title: Research Logic and Design in Political Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to standard research techniques in political science. Issues of epistemology, research design, and approaches to empirical analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Upper-division or graduate-level statistics.

allCourses.title: The Moral Life During War
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Can people keep their humanity during war? What does the term humanity signify when simply surviving requires faith, courage, and desperation? When facing wartime brutality must we abrogate morality? What does it mean to compose a moral life during war?.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Political Theory
allCourses.description: Current research in political theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Seminar in International Relations Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of the major theories guiding research and scholarship in international relations.  Focus on major conceptual approaches (realism, neoliberalism, marxism) and levels of analysis (systemic, state, and subnational), as well as on methodological/epistemological debates engulfing the field.

allCourses.title: Norms in International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Evaluates various theoretical and empirical approaches to understanding the emergence, diffusion, and effects of international norms.

allCourses.title: Research Design in International Relations
allCourses.description: Surveys research design primarily through substantive readings in international relations. The purpose is to familiarize students with choices/dilemmas relevant to IR-specific research. Students at various stages in the graduate program and with different methodological orientations are welcome.

allCourses.title: U.S. Ethnic Politics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Assesses theories of ethnic political attitudes and behaviors in U.S. politics and examines methodological approaches to testing theories of ethnic politics. The primary focus is contemporary ethnic politics with attention to ethnic politics in American political development.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in international relations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Voting Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to voting models. Substantive topics include majority rule, voting methods and their properties, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.

allCourses.title: The State in Comparative Perspective
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminar examining the state from theoretical, empirical, comparative perspectives. How the state came into being, the state’s role in the economy, toward society and internationally, and in policy-making in Western Europe, East Asian newly industrialized countries, the Third World.

allCourses.title: Political Culture and Democracy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the political culture literature and its relationship to democratic development. What are the cultural prerequisites of democracy, what aspects of political culture facilitate democratic politics and governmental performance, and what forms and reforms a political culture.

allCourses.title: Theories and Practice of Migration and Citizenship
allCourses.description: Examines theories of migration and citizenship. In examining these themes, the course includes discussion of theory development, multi-method testing, and case study comparison with a focus on Western Europe and other advanced democratic receiving states.

allCourses.title: Regime Change in East Asia
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Regime change from authoritarianism to democracies (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan); gradual political change (China). Uses theories from comparative literature on regime transition; combines theory with historical institutions, political culture, prior regimes, elements in the transition process in the four countries.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Game Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to non-cooperative games.  The prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, sequential games, subgame perfection. Applications include collective action, agenda-setter models, spatial competition of political parties, models of revolution and arms race.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Comparative Politics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in comparative politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Political Participation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines theoretical approaches to the explanation of the pattern of participation and consideration of the results of empirical studies of such activity by mass publics (mainly in Europe and North America).  Addresses issues in both comparative politics and political behavior.

allCourses.title: Political Economy I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Course studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.

allCourses.title: Political Economy II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Course studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 270A

allCourses.title: Political Economy III
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Political Economy lies at the intersection of economics and political science. Course studies effects of politics on the economy and uses tools derived from economics to understand the behavior of governments and of citizens when they deal with politics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 270B

allCourses.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Students must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and must have qualitative data they can analyze.

allCourses.title: Predictive Models in Social Sciences
allCourses.description: Basic numeracy (logarithms, fixed-exponent and exponential formats, graphing). Models based on ignorance and logical constraints. Logical quantitative models (how things should be) to complement and guide statistical analysis (how things are).

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Psychology I
allCourses.description: Reviews theoretical questions regarding the relationship between the analytical and normative and the polity. Considers relationships between the analytical and normative concerns of psychology and political science, addressing empirical literatures on political socialization, ideology and public opinion, identity and nationality.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Psychology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Discusses the complex set of relationships among the three disciplines of politics, psychology, and economics, focusing on human decision-making processes and political choice.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in American Politics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of American politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Dissertation Research
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Political Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.description: Independent research with Political Science faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Theory
allCourses.description: Types of questions:  What is politics?  What are the theoretical and philosophical bases for different types of political arrangements?  How do these perspectives get translated into reality?  Among others, the works of Rousseau, Locke, Mill, and Marx are read.

allCourses.title: Dilemmas of Diversity
allCourses.description: Focuses on racial, ethnic, and gender diversity, multiculturalism, and their impact on our social and political ideals. Traces the sources of ideas about difference, equality, and toleration, and examines tensions that occur when forms of identity conflict with one another.

allCourses.title: Lower-Division Special Topics in Political Theory
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of political theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to International Relations
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Analysis of political relations between and among nations with emphasis on explanations of conflict and cooperation. The role of ideologies and their relation to international problems are also examined.

allCourses.title: Global Security and Cooperation
allCourses.description: Examination of global conflict and cooperation since World War II, and future prospects. The Cold War, nuclear arms race, regional conflicts, arms proliferation and control, deterrence theory, psychology of conflict, governmental and nongovernmental efforts to promote global peace and cooperation.

allCourses.title: Global Issues and Institutions
allCourses.description: Surveys recent developments in the nature of global interdependence.  Examines the major political, economic, and military conflicts of this century and recent problems of population growth, environmental decay, ethnic/national antagonism and violence, and post-Cold War politics.

allCourses.title: Global Political Ideologies
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An overview of the major political ideologies shaping the current world order and global conflict. Topics include liberalism, democracy, nationalism, capitalism, communism, socialism, fascism, neoliberalism, clash of civilizations, sectarian violence, populist nationalism, and de-globalization.

allCourses.title: Human Rights and Global Governance
allCourses.restriction: International Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Historical development of civil, political rights and the rise of human rights in international law. Explores role, and limitations, of the UN, ICJ, and ICC in global governance. Reconceptualizing democracy and political representation in a postnational 21st century.

allCourses.title: Lower-Division Special Topics in International Relations
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of international relations. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Politics Around the World
allCourses.description: Introduces comparative politics. Compares political systems in a variety of countries. Includes elections, parties, parliaments, presidents, protest movements, and other aspects of national politics. Addresses how to make meaningful comparisons across countries.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Race and Ethnicity in Political Science
allCourses.description: Examines major theories that attempt to explain the roles of race and ethnicity in U.S. politics.

allCourses.title: Lower Division Special Topics in Minority Politics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of minority politics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Science: Political Analysis
allCourses.description: Presents various modes of understanding politics. Emphasis on basic approaches to political analysis, their uses in constructing theories, and their application to particular national political systems.

prerequisite_for.title: Seminar on Regime Change in East Asia

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Science: Macropolitics
allCourses.description: An overview of macro-political inquiry, emphasizing the various determinants of political life in a political community.  We also explore the origins and challenges of democratic governance focusing on the tension between liberty and equality in a democratizing nation.

prerequisite_for.title: Seminar on Regime Change in East Asia

allCourses.title: Introduction to Political Science: Micropolitics
allCourses.description: Introduction to political behavior of individuals and groups within national systems. Three questions addressed: How do individuals come to understand the political world? How do individuals behave within this world? How do groups and individuals engage in the political process.

prerequisite_for.title: Seminar on Regime Change in East Asia

allCourses.title: Introduction to Law
allCourses.description: An introduction to the study of judicial politics.  Questions include:  what is law?; what is a court?; who are the judges? Analysis of a wide range of judicial decisions illustrates the political importance of courts in the U.S. and elsewhere.

prerequisite_for.title: International Law and the U.S. Legal System

allCourses.title: Lower-Division Special Topics in Law
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of law. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Honors Seminar in Political Science
allCourses.description: Course for students enrolled in the Honors Program in Political Science.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Only open to students in the Political Science Honors Program.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Honors Thesis Workshop
allCourses.restriction: Open only to students in the Political Science Senior Thesis program.
allCourses.description: A weekly seminar/workshop to facilitate the exchange of ideas and research strategies among students and to review their progress in writing the thesis.

allCourses.title: Globalization and Human Security
allCourses.restriction: Campuswide Honors Collegium students only.
allCourses.description: Emerging issues of human security in the globalized world, including personal human security, physical integrity, human trafficking, global climate change, food. Challenges of these complex human security problems for a multi-scalar system (international, national, local).

allCourses.title: Introduction to Portuguese and Brazilian Literature
allCourses.description: General introduction to selected authors and works in relation to literary currents and to specific historical and cultural contexts. Taught in Portuguese.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PORTUG 2C. PORTUG 2C with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Portuguese and Brazilian Literature
allCourses.description: General introduction to selected authors and works in relation to literary currents and to specific historical and cultural contexts. Taught in Portuguese.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PORTUG 2C. PORTUG 2C with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Portuguese and Brazilian Literature
allCourses.description: General introduction to selected authors and works in relation to literary currents and to specific historical and cultural contexts. Taught in Portuguese.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PORTUG 2C. PORTUG 2C with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.title: Topics in Luso-Brazilian Literature
allCourses.description: In English. Contextualized study of a major author, current, or genre in Brazilian, Portuguese, and/or Lusophone African literature. Examples: Gender, Race, and Sexualities in Postcolonial Lusophone Literatures; Women and Writing in Brazil and Portugal; The Short Story.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.description: Individual study with Portuguese faculty.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Portuguese
allCourses.description: Basic grammar, conversation, and composition with an initial exposure to the varied cultures of the Portuguese-speaking world.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Portuguese
allCourses.description: Basic grammar, conversation, and composition with an initial exposure to the varied cultures of the Portuguese-speaking world.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PORTUG 1A. PORTUG 1A with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Portuguese
allCourses.description: Basic grammar, conversation, and composition with an initial exposure to the varied cultures of the Portuguese-speaking world.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PORTUG 1B. PORTUG 1B with a grade of C or better.
ge_list: GE VI: Language Other Than English

allCourses.title: Studies in Luso-Brazilian Literature and Culture
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Critical analysis of selected literary works from Portugal and/or Brazil. Contextualizes the works within their historical and literary specificity, and discusses pertinent theoretical issues raised by them. Taught in Portuguese.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Reading knowledge of Portuguese.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Individual Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Individual study.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Portuguese
allCourses.description: Conversation, reading, and composition skills are developed using texts of literary and social interest. Emphasis on grammar and review.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PORTUG 1C. PORTUG 1C with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Portuguese
allCourses.description: Conversation, reading, and composition skills are developed using texts of literary and social interest. Emphasis on grammar and review.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PORTUG 2A. PORTUG 2A with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.title: Intermediate Portuguese
allCourses.description: Conversation, reading, and composition skills are developed using texts of literary and social interest. Emphasis on grammar and review.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PORTUG 2B. PORTUG 2B with a grade of C or better.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Urban Studies
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Special topics courses are offered from time to time.  Course content varies with interest of the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Urbanization and Social Change
allCourses.description: Surveys the global and historical co-evolution of cities and social institutions, including religion, the economy, governance, the arts, technology, and family life.

allCourses.title: Urban Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines structural inequality and the influence that urbanization has in affecting race, ethnic, and class relations. Explores how race/ethnicity, class, urban space, housing, economic development, public education and land policy intersect in cities, both historically and today.

allCourses.title: Comparative Urbanization in a Developing World
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only. Urban Studies Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to comparative urbanization in developing countries. The first part of the course introduces students to the geography, history, and theories of urbanization, and then reviews urban planning, public policy, and governance.

allCourses.title: Urban America
allCourses.description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.

allCourses.title: California's Population
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Surveys California's human population (past, present, and future) and its interactions with trends in society, government, the economy, and the environment.

allCourses.title: Technology and Economic Development
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Importance of technology for urban economic and social development. Concepts of technological innovation and diffusion, and their relevance for cities and metropolitan areas. Principles of networks and their importance for diffusion. Relationship of technology to urban infrastructure and metropolitan form.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13

allCourses.title: Urban and Regional Planning
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Important substantive areas, concepts, tools in the field of urban and regional planning. Topics include: forces that have historically guided and are currently guiding U.S. urbanization; land use, economic development, housing and community development, environmental planning; legal, environmental, governmental contexts.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PP&D 4

allCourses.title: Cities and Transportation
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The relationship between urban areas and transportation systems.  Economic analysis of cities, transportation and urban form, highway congestion, environmental impacts of transportation, public transit, land use and transportation, and political influences on transportation planning.

allCourses.title: Housing and Urban Development Policy
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Surveys public policy issues and develops analytic techniques in the areas of housing and urban development.  Examines a range of policy topics including housing assistance to low- and moderate-income families, housing finance system, incentives for economic development and neighborhood preservation.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: previous course work in economics.

allCourses.title: Urban Economic Development Policy
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical and practical perspectives on local economic development policy.  Integrates economic, planning, and political perspectives.  Overview of economic role of cities and metropolitan areas.  Specific development issues include: link between taxes, regulation, job growth; redevelopment planning; evaluation economic development policy.

allCourses.title: Strategies of Health Promotion
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies, Social Ecology, and Public Health Policy majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examination of strategies for promoting physical and mental health at community, organizational, and individual levels. Interventions designed to promote healthier lifestyles, organizational structures, and environmental conditions. Criteria for monitoring cost-effectiveness of these programs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PP&D 4 or ENVIRON E8.

allCourses.title: Foundations of Community Health
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A social ecological framework for understanding community health is presented. Measures of individual and community health are compared, and the influence of personal and environmental factors on individual, group, and population health is examined. Community health promotion strategies are discussed.

allCourses.title: Poverty in Developing Countries
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on poverty in developing countries.  Analyzes the magnitude and changing nature of poverty in the global south. Critically examines poverty conceptualized in terms of economic deprivation, well-being, and social exclusion.

allCourses.title: Engaging Globally
allCourses.description: Introduces students to issues of community engagement and social action in international contexts. Prepares students to understand social and environmental problems in a globalized world. Includes online instruction, on-site service learning in structures projects, critical reflection, and final paper.

allCourses.title: Global Poverty and Inequality in the 21st Century
allCourses.description: Explores a multidisciplinary understanding of poverty and inequality in the 21st century and assesses impact of education, health, technology, and other interventions. Course offered online only.

allCourses.title: American Public Policy
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

allCourses.title: Cities and Food
allCourses.description: Explores the role of cities in transforming global diets: how urbanization has shaped what and how we eat, and what the co-evolution of diets and city life portend for the future.

allCourses.title: Environmental Sustainability I
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to sustainability from different points of view; historical, scientific, political, ethical, and economic.

allCourses.title: Environmental Sustainability II
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Investigates how sustainability can be implemented in a variety of contexts including water, energy, non-renewable resources, biodiversity, and urban policy, and also how it could be measured.

allCourses.title: Environmental Law and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Criminology, Law and Society Majors only. Planning, Policy, and Design Majors only.
allCourses.description: Environmental law as a combination of traditional legal principles and newly created statutes, rules, and decisions applied to environmental protection. Investigates roles of courts, legislature, executive branch and administrative agencies, and private citizens attempting to regulate environmental quality.

allCourses.title: Human Ecology
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the interaction of social choice and physical constraint in shaping the earth's human carrying capacity, including ramifications for local, regional, or global environmental issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PP&D 4

allCourses.title: Global Environmental Issues
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies, Social Ecology, Political Science, and International Studies majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: While many agree that environmental problems threaten humankind, there is much disagreement over the nature of these threats and how to address them.  Examines global environmental issues from various perspectives in order to provide answers to these questions.

allCourses.title: Water Resource Policy
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Earth System Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Environmental Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examination of contemporary water problems worldwide, with particular attention to the competing water demands in the western U.S., and water demand by the poor in developing countries. History and analysis of U.S. water policies at local, state, and federal levels.

allCourses.title: Ethics and International Relations
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the dynamic field of ethics and international relations. A variety of traditional and emerging perspectives are examined, skeptical views are discussed in detail, and arguments are illustrated with current cases.

allCourses.title: Brownfields: Law and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies and Social Ecology majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the legal structure and policy issues of redeveloping contaminated properties known as Brownfields. Federal and state Brownfield programs, liability and risk management, cleanup and future land use, institutional controls, community economic revitalization, legislation and policies to encourage Brownfield redevelopment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL E8.

allCourses.title: Environmental Hazards in an Urbanizing World
allCourses.description: Development patterns, including urbanization, can contribute to environmental hazard severity. Humans can plan, mitigate, and prepare to reduce costly hazard losses. Students learn about environmental hazards and human response to these threats.

allCourses.title: Environmental Governance
allCourses.description: How should the environment be managed and who should be responsible? What is effective environmental management, and for whom? These questions are answered by exploring traditional and emerging theoretical frameworks and applying them to real world environmental challenges.

allCourses.title: Experience Design
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies and Social Ecology majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores functional, experiential, emotional, sensorial, and extra-sensorial aspects of built and modified natural environments. Examines methods for acquiring, evaluating, and presenting information and developing specifications for designers’ information needs and for assuring great designed environments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PP&D 4 and PP&D 152.

allCourses.title: Environmental Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies, Social Ecology, and Psychology and Social Behavior majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Impact of the physical environment on individual and group behavior. Three basic concerns examined: (a) environmental determinants of behavior at the individual and interpersonal level; (b) social planning and urban design; (c) methodological approaches to the study of environmental issues.

allCourses.title: Cultural Ecology and Environmental Design
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to cultural ecology and environmental and architectural design. Addresses the understanding of people’s relationships with their built environments, the basic elements of architecture, architectural analysis, and cultural analysis are covered. Examines values in design and design for multicultural societies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PP&D 4

allCourses.title: Elements of Environmental Design
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic elements of environmental design such as scale, proportion, rhythm, color, sound, lighting, surfaces, texture, architectural definition of spaces, volumes, massing volumetric analysis, solids and voids, and cultural aspects of design.  Excitement and creativity in design, imageability.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PP&D 4 and PP&D 152

allCourses.title: Urban Design Principles
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to principles of urban design and its applications.  Study of contemporary and traditional theories of urban design formulated to improve physical characteristics of built environment to facilitate an enhanced quality of life.  A variety of case studies are discussed.

allCourses.title: Urban Design and Graphics Studio
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introductory course organized around a variety of assignments to encourage learning by design in a studio setting.  Students work on design projects and graphic representation assignments to learn practical aspects of urban design.

allCourses.title: Urban Public Policy
allCourses.description: Examines why and how urban policies are enacted and carried out in contemporary U.S. cities and regions. Topics include evolution and organization of city governments and policymaking over the past century; who directs public policy and controls how cities develop.

allCourses.title: Public Policy and Management
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Exposes students to best management practices that assure effective planning and implementation of policies and programs in government, business, and nonprofit sectors. Includes guest lecturers who are proven leaders in four principal institutions of community: business, education, government, and nonprofit.

allCourses.title: Public Policy Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines different approaches to the analysis of public policy, what constitutes good policy, the role of government, and citizen participation in policy-making. Suggests a policy-design perspective which builds upon other frameworks but concentrates on goals, implementation structures, tools, and rationales.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL E8 and (PP&D 4 or PP&D 166)

allCourses.title: Health Policy
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Considers social and economic aspects of health and disease in the United States.  What are the proper roles of the individual, community, and government in improving health and health care?  International comparisons will be made wherever possible.

allCourses.title: Latino Metropolis
allCourses.description: Explores the processes of Latino urbanization in the United States and the spatialization of Latino identities, particularly in the context of Southern California with selected comparisons drawing from other cities.

allCourses.title: Technology Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies and Social Ecology majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers concepts of interest for policy-making and technology analysis, dealing with invention, innovation, and the socioeconomic impacts of new technologies.  Comparative assessments of new technologies and their national and regional impacts on organizations, sectors, and activities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13.

allCourses.title: Chicano Movement
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the history of Mexicans in the U.S. with particular attention paid to their integration into the U.S. capitalist economy.  Examines this economic history and the Chicano movement, "El Movimiento," within the wide context of socio-economic change.

allCourses.title: International Divided Cities
allCourses.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

allCourses.title: History of Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the historical roots and fundamental perspectives of urban and regional planning.  Exploration of the significant historical phases and personalities which have shaped the profession.  The roles and responsibilities, the limitations and potential, of urban planning.

allCourses.title: Theoretical Foundations of Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intellectual excursion into central themes in policy and planning, including philosophy of the market, institutionalization of space, hypostatizations of policy, constructions of communities, logics of spatial analysis. Objective is engagement of the professional in thoughtful reflections on practice and institutions.

allCourses.title: Plan Development and Communication
allCourses.restriction: Urban and Regional Planning Majors only.
allCourses.description: Graphic representation and communication of physical place characteristics, design and physical planning ideas and concepts using a variety of graphic techniques of free hand drawing, sketching, orthographic representations, scale drawings, 3D representations, maps, photo-documentation, and various media.

allCourses.title: Environmental Economics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a broad introduction to environmental economics and to environmental policy.  Environmental problems facing the United States and Europe are analyzed, and whenever possible, the environmental problems facing developing countries.

allCourses.title: Microeconomic Analysis for Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides students with a working knowledge of basic microeconomic concepts.  Emphasizes applications related to urban planning and policy analysis.  Topics covered include demand analysis, firm behavior, market structure, public goods, externalities, and the role of economics in land markets.

allCourses.title: Land Use Law
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Investigates legal and institutional frameworks for development control. Review of constitutional issues implicated in land-use regulation. Traces development control historically and analyzes contemporary approaches to land-use control which reflect environmental and economic development concerns.

allCourses.title: California's Population
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a non-specialist introduction to social demography through a focus on California population.  Surveys historical and current trends in the State's growth, its industries and occupations, and its ethnic and racial makeup.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Methods: Overview
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of “qualitative” research and non-positivistic inquiry. Formulation of research questions, selection of method, data collection techniques, and analysis (briefly). Overview of selected methods from ethnography, naturalistic field research, phenomenology, ethnoarchaeology, critical approaches, and others.

allCourses.title: Practice Experience
allCourses.restriction: Urban and Regional Planning Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides Master of Urban & Regional Planning Students an opportunity to link classroom knowledge with real Planning situations through a ten-week unpaid practice experience.

allCourses.title: Urban Design and Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Acquaints students with vocabulary, history, theories, process, and trends in urban design, and the relationship of design to human well-being.  The local environment is used as a resource and a laboratory.

allCourses.title: Transportation Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces current topics in transportation planning.  Includes an analysis of the economic role of transportation in urban areas, land-use impacts of transportation projects, traffic congestion, air quality, alternatives to the automobile, and other transportation topics.

allCourses.title: Advanced Qualitative Methods: Analyzing Qualitative Data
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the theory and practice of analyzing qualitative data. Student must have already learned about data collection and research design for qualitative research and they must have qualitative data they can analyze.

allCourses.title: Quantitative Analysis for Planners
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to the basic statistical concepts used to address issues of public concern.  Prepares students to perform, interpret, and evaluate quantitative data analyses commonly used in professional studies.

allCourses.title: Analytical Methods for Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Emphasizes the development of analytical techniques proven useful in the fields of management and administration.  Topics include multiple regression, cost-benefit analysis and discounting, decision trees, and other techniques useful for the purposes of community analysis and planning.

allCourses.title: Advanced Planning Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Readings and discussions aimed at developing a foundation for critical research into theories and epistemologies of planning and policy. Topics include the liberal, communitarian, communicative, and other conceptions of nationality; praxis, hermaneutics, and policy; topologies of justice and social fracture.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Methods: Fieldwork and Data Collection
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers fieldwork, data collections techniques, and related issues for anti-positivistic research.  Data collection techniques include observation, physical traces, participation, in-depth interview.  Data checks include veracity, detail, completeness, rigor.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Graduate standing or consent of instructor

allCourses.title: Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst. Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Regional Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Major concepts and techniques of regional analysis, with applications for urban and regional planning and public policy-making. Definition of regions, processes of economic change, regional structure, location of activities, and analysis of selected policy issues. Emphasis on practical applications.

allCourses.title: Environmental Politics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Reviews and critiques literature on discussion topics including: the nature and effectiveness of environmental movements and policies; the role of science and technology; the use of economic incentives in policy; decentralization of decision making; and creating arenas for public involvement.

allCourses.title: Local Economic Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes the economic development process.  Attention is given to economic theories of local development and practical implications of those theories.  Topics include local economic development and poverty, tax incentives, infrastructure credits, effects of government competition for economic activity.

allCourses.title: Public Health Cost-Effectiveness Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines using cost-effectiveness information to allocate limited resources to maximize health benefits to a population; defining and measuring cost, survival and health-related quality of life; and how to calculate cost-effectiveness using decision trees and Markov simulation models.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Methods: Case Study
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Deals with case study as a qualitative, anti-positivistic research method.  Discussion focuses on the essential nature of case study research, quality of case study, rigor, design, implementation, analysis, data collection techniques, analysis, and writing.

allCourses.title: Demographics for Planning and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides planning and policy practitioners with a condensed, nonspecialist orientation to the sources, applications, and interpretation of population statistics, and conveys the steps used in constructing local-area population forecasts and projections.

allCourses.title: Transportation and Environmental Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Critically evaluates how transportation can promote sustainable, healthy, and equitable cities. Examines the interaction of transportation systems with urban form, land use, community health, and environmental quality.

allCourses.title: Transportation, Transit, and Land-Use Policy and Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Places students into a specific transportation public policy situation to devise real solutions, with the goal of helping students understand factors in land use, travel behavior, politics, and finance that shape transportation planning policy choices.

allCourses.title: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Problem Solving in Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the application of geographic information systems (GIS) in urban planning.  Steps through a GIS-based planning procedure that balances housing, jobs, tax base, utilities, transportation, and the natural environment.

allCourses.title: Community Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the current condition of urban design in the United States.  Topics include the academic environment, the retail environment, multi- and single-family residential environments, the office environment, and new urban design tools.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
allCourses.description: Application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to the field of urban and regional planning.  Emphasizes current issues that occur in actual implementation settings. Lecture/discussion followed by laboratory demonstrating the area of GIS discussed.  Offers "hands-on" student usage of GIS software.

allCourses.title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems
allCourses.description: Extends study of geographic information systems to more advanced issues, including data sources, data conversion, relational database integration, software customization, and spatial and three-dimensional analysis.

allCourses.title: Urban Design Theories and Applications
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to contemporary and traditional theories of urban design and their applications.  Organized around one question:  How might planning and design of built environment contribute to making a good city?  National and international case studies are introduced.

allCourses.title: International Environmental Policy
allCourses.description: Explores causes and effects of environmental problems and the effectiveness of different adaptation or restoration strategies and how they are closely linked to ways in which political, economic, demographic, and cultural systems interact among themselves and ecological systems.

allCourses.title: Health Promotion and Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on health and health care in the United States, but discussion of global health issues and/or international comparisons will be made whenever possible.  Considers both the social and economic aspects of health and disease.

allCourses.title: Regional Development Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Regional economic development concepts and studies, with applications for urban and regional planning, and public policy-making. Roles and performance of economic sectors, technological innovation, and communications in the process of development. Analysis of regional development policies and programs.

allCourses.title: Health Policy and Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary inquiry into theory and practice concerned with delivery, quantity, costs of health care for individuals and populations. Explores managerial and policy concerns regarding structure, process, outcomes of health services including the costs, financing, organization, outcomes, and accessibility of care.

allCourses.title: Land-Use Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examination of the role of public policy in guiding growth and development in urban and suburban environments.  Description of a wide-ranging set of growth policies, the rationales underlying their use, controversies and legal constraints, and evaluation of their effectiveness.

allCourses.title: Urban Security
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines changing urban security landscape facing planners, businesses, policymakers, first responders, and academics. Identifies threats and vulnerabilities andhow they can be reduced . Focus on transnational networks where contemporary cities are enmeshed, and function as sources of threat and opportunity.

allCourses.title: Housing Policy
allCourses.description: Examines theories and practices of housing policy and the relationship of housing to larger neighborhood, community, and regional development issues. Considers the roles of private for-profit and not-for-profit developers, lenders, and all levels of government in the provision of housing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Basic statistics.

allCourses.title: Neighborhood Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on asset-based development and community-building tools.  Public policies and neighborhood-based case studies are explored which provide practical skills for the planner of the future.

allCourses.title: Poverty and Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Critical examines competing conceptualizations, methods of measurement, and poverty alleviation strategies widely used in developing countries. Focuses on poverty conceptualized as economic deprivation, well-being, vulnerability, and social exclusion.

allCourses.title: Issues in Environmental Law and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Treatment of legal and policy strategies for promoting environmental protection and deterring environmental degradation within the context of other societal objectives. Topical approach with a focus on problems of special interest to criminologists and to environmental policy specialists.

allCourses.title: Site Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines site specific, neighborhood, and community site planning from the site designer and local government perspectives.  By reviewing actual discretionary case applications and case studies, students learn how regulatory, environmental, and government constraints influence site planning.

allCourses.title: Grant Writing for Community Planning and Development
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces students to grant writing and processes involved in generating funding for nonprofit programs and community research projects.

allCourses.title: Planning, Policy and Design Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: For first- and second-year doctoral students.  Topics include professional development; journal publication process; academic conference presentations; and the job market for doctoral students in and out of academia.

allCourses.title: Urban and Community Development Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: For first- and second-year doctoral students.  Topics include scholarship related to the urban and community development area.  Discussion of assigned articles and book chapters and how they relate to urban and community development.

allCourses.title: Environmental Ethics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to major themes and debates in environmental ethics, with application to contemporary environmental issues.

allCourses.title: Global Urbanization
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines the spread of cities worldwide in the twentieth century. What are the political and economic causes of this process? What are the social-cultural, political, and economic effects? How is contemporary urbanization linked to global restructuring of other kinds.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Special topics in urban and regional planning are offered from time to time, but not on a regular basis. Course content varies with interest of the instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Culture, Community, and Space
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers how cultures relate to natural and built physical environments.  Ways in which culture influences space; ways space influences culture.  Concepts for understanding the interrelationship, including values, norms, traditions, religion, and place attachment.  Culture and cities, urban form, ethnic communities.

allCourses.title: Theories of Power and Empowerment
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies different ways of thinking about power and its uses. Explores theories of power that inform various notions of empowerment, including resistance, participatory democracy, and workplace empowerment.

allCourses.title: Urban Design Studio for Planners: An Introduction
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introductory urban design for planners.  Organized around a variety of assignments to encourage learning by design in a studio setting. Students work on design projects and drawing assignments to learn practical aspects of urban design.

allCourses.title: Collaborative Governance and Public Management
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to inclusive management. To make effective use of public resources, public managers are inventing ways of managing that alter relationships within organizations, between organizations, between sectors, and with the public. Requires rethinking fundamentals such as leadership and motivation.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Theories of Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on two important theorists with the aim being to study not so much their theory, but their mode of theorizing. Taking them two at a time (e.g., Foucault, Bourdieu) allows us to understand each more deeply through the comparison.

allCourses.title: Environment-Behavior Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of major theoretical and research perspectives within the field of environment-design research/environment-behavior studies (EBS).  Reviews contributions to EBS from architecture, planning, geography, psychology, sociology, and other fields.

allCourses.title: Professional Report
allCourses.description: Workshop designed to assist M.U.R.P. students in conducting their professional reports.  Students select topics, design projects, conduct professional investigations, and write up reports.

allCourses.title: Professional Report Seminar I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to prepare students for writing a professional planning report. Students learn how to diagnose a planning problem; select appropriate analytical methods to assess the problem; pose, evaluate, and recommend alternative approaches to addressing the problem.

allCourses.title: Professional Report Seminar II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Students write and deliver oral presentations in a manner appropriate for professional planning, which includes peer feedback from these presentations. Includes lectures, student assignments, and guest speakers. "Deliverables" and due dates are treated as fixed and contractual professional commitments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PP&D 292A.

allCourses.title: Research Practicum
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Through reading, discussion, and review of existing research proposals, and implementation of preliminary work for dissertation research, students enhance their knowledge of research design and methods, as well as develop skills to write a proposal for dissertation funding.

allCourses.title: Urban Planning Practicum I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engages students in practical planning projects in the community under a central theme within Planning. Students take a problem-solving approach and employ and further develop data gathering, analysis, graphic and oral communication, public engagement, and report writing skills.

allCourses.title: Urban Planning Practicum II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engages students in practical planning projects in the community under a central theme within Planning. Students take a problem-solving approach and employ and further develop data gathering, analysis, graphic and oral communication, public engagement, and report writing skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PP&D 294A

allCourses.title: Master's Thesis Research and Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Planning, Policy, and Design faculty.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Advancement to candidacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Planning, Policy, and Design faculty.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Advancement to candidacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.title: Research Design
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides training in research design and methods. Students learn how to evaluate the strength of research findings based on the methods used by a researcher and learn to use lessons from the course to develop a research proposal.

allCourses.title: Directed Studies in Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed Studies in Urban Planning.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study in Urban Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent Study in Urban Planning.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Urban Studies
allCourses.restriction: Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Social Ecology students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the substantive areas, concepts, and tools in the field of urban studies.  Acquaints students with physical, environmental, social, economic, and political dimensions of cities.  Examines the challenges facing cities, including poverty, sustainability, development, globalization, and others.

allCourses.title: Urban Sociology
allCourses.description: Overview of theoretical, substantive, and policy issues in urban sociology.  History of urbanization, the school of human ecology, and recent trends regarding urbanism.  Time is devoted to understanding the causes and possible solutions to urban problems.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social Behavior
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Course content varies with interest of instructor.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Life Span Developmental Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Addresses the major issues, concepts, and methods of life span developmental psychology. The fundamental theories, distinctive methods, and the physical, perceptual, cognitive, social, motivational, and emotional development for each developmental phase of the life course are considered.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B.

allCourses.title: Abnormal Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Survey of disorders organized by the diagnostic categories of the American Psychiatric Association. Interdisciplinary orientation combines environmental, psychological, and organic perspectives on etiology and treatment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C) and SOCECOL 10.

allCourses.title: Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theory and research are considered as they contribute to an understanding of the role of psychological processes in health and illness. The distinction between prevention and treatment of illness is established, and a variety of psychosocial interventions are elaborated.

allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Social Animal: An Introduction to Social Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theories and research exploring social behavior and social influences on behavior. Topics include methods of social research, attitude formation and change, social perception, the social self, stereotypes and prejudice, conformity, obedience, altruism, aggression, interpersonal relationships and love, and group behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSCI 9"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSY BEH 9"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSCI 11C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSY BEH 11C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSYCH 7A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSYCH 9C"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Infant Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Study of human development from conception through the first two years of life, covering processes and events in the domains of physical, social, and cognitive development.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B.

allCourses.title: Child Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines social, emotional, and intellectual growth and development between the ages of 2 and 12 years.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B.

allCourses.title: Advanced Research Methods
allCourses.description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Adolescent Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines current research on the biological, social, and cultural contexts of adolescent development. Topics include the impacts of puberty, adolescents' decision-making competencies, changes in family and peer relationships, identity development, and psychosocial problems such as depression and problem behavior.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B.

allCourses.title: Adult Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines why and how we change (with attention to gains as well as losses) from ages 18-65 and the nature and sources of continuity over time. Topics include physical and intellectual functioning, personality, coping strategies, and social roles and relationships.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B.

allCourses.title: Gerontology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines stereotypes and myths associated with aging; physiological and psychological changes that accompany old age; distinguishes behavior changes due to aging per se from those due to historical and socioeconomic factors; political, social aspects of old age in contemporary society.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B

allCourses.title: Cognitive Development
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines theories on nature of cognitive development. Discusses behaviorist theories on role of the environment including those of Vygotsky and Piaget, and recent evidence from cognitive psychologists stressing the importance of knowledge and skills within specific domains.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B.

allCourses.title: Human Development and Cross-Cultural Perspectives
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Human development in diverse cultures (e.g., Asian, American, and African). Special emphasis on East-West contrasts and when East meets West (i.e., Asian-American experiences). Topics include parenting, family relations, language and cognition, schooling and academic achievement, and morality.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B) and SOCECOL 10.

allCourses.title: The Psychology of Gender
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Discussion of gender identity development and examination of gender differences and similarities across the life span. Consideration of the biology and psychology of gender in relation to physical, behavioral, personality, and intellectual capabilities.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSCI 9 or PSYC 9B or PSCI 11B or PSYC 7A

allCourses.title: Human Sexuality
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A broad survey of human sexuality encompassing genetic factors, physiological and anatomical development, customary and atypical forms of behavior, reproductive processes, and cultural determinants.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9B.

allCourses.description: Part of a three-course series that provides a comprehensive introduction to psychology. Required for students majoring in Cognitive Sciences, Psychological Science, and Psychology. Topics include the science of psychology, research methods, biology and behavior, consciousness, sensation, and perception.

allCourses.description: Part of a three-course series that provides a comprehensive introduction to psychology. Required for students majoring in Cognitive Sciences, Psychological Science, or Psychology. Topics include learning and memory, thinking, language and intelligence, human development, emotion, and motivation.

allCourses.restriction: Lower-division students only. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
