Topics include personality psychology, social psychology, abnormal and clinical psychology, and health psychology.

prerequisite_for.title: Social Animal: An Introduction to Social Psychology

allCourses.title: Child Development, the Law, and Social Policy
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the rights of children and adolescents in the U.S. and internationally; law and policy with regard to the family, government services, health care, education, juvenile justice and the labor market; and the connection between child development, law and policy.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C. Recommended: PSCI 111D or PSCI 112D.

allCourses.title: Work and Family
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Effects of employment and unemployment on mental health and marital quality; effects of work on parenting and child development; corporate and social policies for "families that work"; young adults' decision-making about work and family.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Development of Motivation Across the Lifespan
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors only. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces major concepts in life-span development of motivation and self-regulation, and discusses exemplar empirical findings pertaining to these concepts during the various phases of life. Students participate in discussion, present findings from research articles, and write a paper.

allCourses.title: Attachment Relationships
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Students learn about the development of attachment-related needs throughout development, as well as the links between attachment and emotion, psychopathology and treatment. Lectures emphasize classic as well as cutting-edge research and are supplemented by primary source readings.

allCourses.title: The Science and Practice of Wellness and Resilience
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors only. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Wellness is a common, but elusive goal. Covers the history, theory, psychology, and behavioral science behind skills for wellness and resilience. Provides opportunities to practice the strategies to help further understanding of the behavioral nature of each of the areas.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYC 7A or PSYC 9C

allCourses.title: Behavioral Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines biobehavioral aspects of health and illness, focusing on how stress contributes to or exacerbates disease processes. Background information on psychosomatic medicine and stress models and detailed examination of specific organ systems emphasizing the reactivity of these systems to stress.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Human Stress
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Stress as a multidisciplinary topic. Biological, psychological, and sociological approaches to adaptation-related disorders. Effects of acute and chronic stress on emotions, physiology, and behavior. Methods of stress assessment, stress reduction, and intervention.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSCI 9"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSY BEH 9"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSCI 11C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSY BEH 11C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSYCH 7A"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "PSYCH 9C"}]}]}

allCourses.title: Child Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Exploration of psychological antecedents, concomitants, and consequences of medical illnesses in children. Children's beliefs about health, illness, and medication; the role of stress; coronary-prone behavior; therapeutic adherence and physician-patient interaction; coping with chronic illness; effects of child's illness on family.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 9C or PSYCH 7A) and SOCECOL 10.

allCourses.title: Clinical Sport Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An interdisciplinary introduction to clinical sport psychology, that includes, among other things, an introduction to psychopathology in sport; plus the use of psychological skills training, including anxiety reduction techniques, visualization, self-efficacy, coping skills, concentration, and goal-setting in sports.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: The Hardiness Approach to Stress Management
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: New development within psychology involving a combination of motivations and skills that extensive research has shown enhances performance, conduct, morale, stamina, and health. Combines study of hardiness research with strategies for improvement of personal hardiness through a series of exercises.

allCourses.title: Clinical Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Behavioral role in etiology, treatment, and prevention of certain diseases. Behavioral intervention including biofeedback, stress-, pain-management, health habit counseling, and other skills to assist patients make cognitive, emotional, and behavioral changes needed to cope with disease or achieve better health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Introduction to Interdisciplinary Salivary Bioscience
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors only. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the integration of salivary analytes into developmental, social, behavioral, and health sciences. Lectures cover theoretical perspectives; oral fluid as a biological specimen; saliva collection and study design; basics of salivary assay methods; and research findings across multiple fields.

allCourses.title: The Science and Practice of Wellness and Resilience
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors only. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Wellness is a common, but elusive goal. Covers the history, theory, psychology, and behavioral science behind skills for wellness and resilience. Provides opportunities to practice the strategies to help further understanding of the behavioral nature of each of the areas.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Health and Social Relationships
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Theoretical and empirical arguments for an association between health and social relationships are highlighted. The complexities of this association based on relationship type and context, attachment, gender, culture, sexuality, age, and other factors is also highlighted.

allCourses.title: Clinical Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overview of theories, assessment techniques, research methodologies, and intervention approaches in clinical psychology. Psychodynamic, behavioral, humanistic, and cognitive perspectives are examined along with ethical and professional issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C) and PSCI 102C.

allCourses.title: Psychological Testing and Assessment
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Laboratory-seminar exploration of diverse methods of assessing, analyzing, and recording behavior. Includes methods of direct behavioral observation, structured (analog) assessments, rating scales, interviewing, and self-monitoring. Development of assessment skills and their application in intervention and research programs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C and (PSCI 102C and PSCI 150C). Recommended: SOCECOL 10.

allCourses.title: Clinical Child Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines research and theory concerning childhood psychopathology behavior disorders. Diagnosis and assessment, early identification of high-risk children, fears and phobias, antisocial behavior, childhood psychoses, autism, depression, attention deficit/hyperactivity disorders, and ethical and policy implications of identifying children who are different.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Developmental Psychopathology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Research and theory of origins, course, and outcomes of disordered behavior. Continuity and change in patterns of behavior; environmental challenges and buffers; stress/competence in children; vulnerable/invincible children; children of mentally ill parents; families at risk; childhood antecedents of adult disorders.

allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Presentation of principles and procedures of therapeutic interventions based on cognitive-behavior methods. Cognitive factors in learning, emotional arousal, psychological disorder, and psychotherapy reviewed. Introduces the application of cognitive behavioral methods to problems of depression, anxiety, anger, pain, and impulsivity.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSYCH 7A or (PSCI 11A and PSCI 11C) or (PSYCH 9A and PSYCH 9C).

allCourses.title: Child Therapies
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines research methodologies, empirical data, and implications of diverse intervention strategies. Primary topics include psychotherapy process and outcome, family therapies, behavioral intervention, cognitive behavior modification, pediatric psychopharmacology, and ethical and social policy implications of intervening in other people's lives.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Forensic Psychology: Advanced Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the psychology of criminal offending, particularly violent behavior. Examines violence, sexual offending, and mental disorder related to crime with regard to clinical assessment and treatment; mental health services within forensic institutions.

allCourses.title: Clinical Neuropsychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors only. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors only. Social Ecology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Introduces key concepts and case studies in clinical neuropsychology. Instruction focuses on neuropsychological concepts underlying brain-behavior relationships and their assessment in clinical case examples; and psychological science as relates to brain injuries/diseases impacting higher mental functions (e.g., memory).

allCourses.title: Clinical Neuroscience
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Biological Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An introduction to the neuroclinical bases of human behavior, including neuropsychological approaches to mental disorders. Also includes case formulations, research articles, therapeutic approaches, and other discussions related to select psychopathology and other neurobehavioral topics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSYCH 7A or PSCI 11A or PSYCH 9A or BIO SCI 99.

allCourses.title: Forensic Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Criminology, Law and Society Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Forensic psychology is the interface between clinical psychology and the law. Emphasizes clinically relevant legal topics (insanity defense; competency to stand trial) and includes critical thinking about issues that arise when psychologists are involved in legal proceedings.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11B or PSCI 11C.

allCourses.title: Psychodynamic Studies
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to contemporary psychodynamic studies. Emphasis on clinical concepts associated with psychodynamic psychotherapy, including unconscious determinants of behavior, typical defenses, life experiences, and techniques. Exploration of links between psychodynamic-oriented psychotherapy and other disciplines (e.g., psychology, music, medicine, neuroscience, film).
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.title: Human  Neuropsychology
allCourses.restriction: School of Biological Sciences students have first consideration for enrollment. Cognitive Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of human brain disorders using a clinical case study approach to illustrate fundamental issues in studying brain and behavior. Topics include sensory deficits, attentional neglect, amnesia, cortical organization, clinical psychopathology, and more.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: BIO SCI N110 or BIO SCI N115A or PSYCH 9A or PSCI 11A

allCourses.title: Addiction
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Designed for those with an interest in the nature and treatment of addiction. Focuses on the etiology and treatment of addiction, but does not prepare students to treat substance abuse disorders.
