allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The distribution of disease and injury across time, space, and populations. Covers basic concepts and methods of descriptive epidemiology including the natural history of disease, data, and indices of health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: STATS 7 or STATS 8 or PUBHLTH 7 or PUBHLTH 7A

prerequisite_for.title: Epidemiology of Drug Use and Misuse

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Social Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Overviews evidence linking environmental factors to mental and physical disorders including such variables as socioeconomic status, income inequality, work stress, job loss, social capital, location, and other demographic characteristics. Measurement and research design issues of both individual and aggregate levels.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: (PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C) and SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Genetic Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the methodological approaches for studying the importance of genetic factors and gene-environment interactions in human diseases. Topics include: genetic and epidemiological concepts, population studies, family studies, and applications in medicine and public health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 101

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Analytic and Applied Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers basic concepts of analytic epidemiology and applications, including experimental and observational designs, prevention, screening, treatment and rehabilitation, infectious disease, and injury prevention.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 101

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Health Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.
allCourses.description: Broad overview of medical informatics for students with varied backgrounds. Electronic medical records, online resources, mobile technologies, patient safety, and computational design. Legal, ethical, and public policy issues. Health systems management. Evaluation and fieldwork for health systems.
allCourses.prerequisite_tree: {"AND": [{"OR": [{"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "WRITING 60", "minGrade": "C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "WRITING 39C", "minGrade": "C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "WRITING 30", "minGrade": "C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "WRITING 31", "minGrade": "C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "HUMAN 1C", "minGrade": "C"}, {"prereqType": "course", "coreq": false, "courseId": "HUMAN H1C", "minGrade": "C"}]}]}
allCourses.prerequisite_text: WRITING 60 or WRITING 30 or WRITING 31 or HUMAN 1C or HUMAN H1C. WRITING 60 with a grade of C or better. WRITING 30 with a grade of C or better. WRITING 31 with a grade of C or better. HUMAN 1C with a grade of C or better. HUMAN H1C with a grade of C or better

prerequisite_list.title: The Art of Writing: Prose Fiction

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Project in Health Informatics
allCourses.description: Students undertake significant quarter-long projects related to health informatics. Topics may include field evaluations of health care technologies, prototypes, iterative design, and system implementations.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 105 or IN4MATX 171

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Epidemiology of Drug Use and Misuse
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Applies epidemiologic concepts to the use and misuse of licit/illicit substances. Emphasizes descriptive aspects of drug use and determinants of progressing from experimental use to misuse. Assesses subgroups of abusers, risk factors, trends, and surveillance techniques for estimating drug prevalence.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 101

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Consumer Health Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Health Informatics Minors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Consumer health informatics is a subfield of health informatics aimed to empower healthcare consumers through a variety of consumer-facing technologies. Covers health behavior change, health literacy, social support, and the design, evaluation, and implementation of major technological applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 171 or PUBHLTH 105. IN4MATX 171 with a grade of C or better. PUBHLTH 105 with a grade of C or better
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Data Analytics
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. School of Info & Computer Sci students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The increasing availability of electronic heath data provides an unprecedented opportunity to use data-driven approaches to improve human health. Equips students with essential skills in curating, managing, and analyzing health data, focusing on electronic health records.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: IN4MATX 171 or PUBHLTH 105. IN4MATX 171 with a grade of C or better. PUBHLTH 105 with a grade of C or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Obesity Epidemiology
allCourses.description: Exploration of the epidemiological evidence of obesity nationally and globally including the etiology of the obesity epidemic, various measurements of obesity, associated comorbidities, prognosis, treatment approaches, and prevention strategies. Emphasize preventing obesity at both individual and societal levels.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Community, Social Justice, and Health Equity Research for Action
allCourses.description: Focuses on community as a unit of identity, community, well-being, and social justice perspectives and initiatives to promote community health. Addresses community change and improvements in community well-being, with a focus on health equity research for action.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 or PUBHLTH 2 or CHC/LAT 61 or CHC/LAT 62 or CHC/LAT 63

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Epidemiology and Genetics
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of epidemiology and genetics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Nutrition and Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Global issues related to nutrition and public health. Evaluation of nutritional risk factors associated with the development of chronic diseases and the role of nutritional medicine in prevention. Topics include food safety, communicable diseases, supplements, and regulatory issues.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Complementary and Alternative Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines health and disease in contemporary American culture/society with definitions, models, and practices of what has come to be known as "orthodox" or "conventional" medicine. Selected "alternative" or "complementary" modes of promoting health and well-being including homeopathy, herbology, and chiropractic.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Policy
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Considers social and economic aspects of health and disease in the United States.  What are the proper roles of the individual, community, and government in improving health and health care?  International comparisons will be made wherever possible.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Issues in Biotechnology
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences and Public Health Policy majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: An assessment of developments in biotechnology potentially affecting various facets of human society, or warranting significant public debate. Covers the implications of genetic engineering and other biotechnological developments for public health, environment, agriculture, legislation, research ethics, public policy, and commerce.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 2.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental and Public Health Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines factors involved in shaping public health and environmental policy. Topics include the role of science in public health policy, the function of governmental regulatory agencies, citizen participation, and economic and sociopolitical aspects of controlling infectious diseases and regulating carcinogens.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Foundations of Community Health
allCourses.restriction: Environmental Science and Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A social ecological framework for understanding community health is presented. Measures of individual and community health are compared, and the influence of personal and environmental factors on individual, group, and population health is examined. Community health promotion strategies are discussed.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Law: Fundamentals in Action
allCourses.description: Addresses the relationship of U.S. public health law to health systems at the individual and population levels. Examines legislative and judicial concepts and how they are applied to disease prevention strategies, health services, management, and policy.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Programs for the Corporate World
allCourses.description: International perspective on workplace health promotion. Strategies for developing programs to improve employee health and to decrease risks of chronic degenerative diseases. Case studies include assessment of employee health, program design, implementation, and evaluation. Emphasis on disease prevention.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Administration
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines historical aspects of public health administration including policies, procedures, trends, and development of organizations. Addresses information and skills necessary to succeed in public health leadership roles. Discusses strategic planning, collaborations, and ethical considerations for successful management in public health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: American Public Policy
allCourses.description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Asian American Community Public Health
allCourses.description: Focuses on major issues and concepts of community health and their application to public health programs for Asian American populations. Analyzes individual, institutional, community, and policy factors that influence a person's health status within a larger environmental context.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Medical Sociology
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Current problems in U.S. health-care system and proposals for reform. Examines  financial barriers to access; problem of patient dumping; underinsurance; prenatal and perinatal care; child services; preventative care and needs of the elderly; minorities; low-income people; undocumented.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Tobacco Control Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Majors only. Public Health Policy Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explore tobacco control's interdisciplinary facets: history, policy, advocacy, and public health science. Analyze industry tactics, litigation, and impact of tobacco control policies. Discuss parallels with emerging industries. Culminates in a group project on tobacco's stakeholders.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Health Policy and Administration
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of health policy and administration. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Beliefs, Attitudes, and Health Behaviors
allCourses.restriction: Psychology and Social Behavior, Social Ecology, Public Health Policy, and Public Health Sciences majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines health-relevant beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors from a social psychological perspective. Topics include: self-control; obesity; sexual behavior; medication errors, stress, perceived control and social support; happiness and well-being; changing health attitudes and behaviors; self-disclosure and health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PSY BEH 9 or PSY BEH 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Clinical Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Psychological Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Psychology and Social Behavior Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Social Ecology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Behavioral role in etiology, treatment, and prevention of certain diseases. Behavioral intervention including biofeedback, stress-, pain-management, health habit counseling, and other skills to assist patients make cognitive, emotional, and behavioral changes needed to cope with disease or achieve better health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Recommended: PSCI 9 or PSCI 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: The Human Pain Experience
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences and Public Health Policy majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the physiological and sociocultural correlates of human pain perception. Emphasis on laboratory and clinical methods of measuring acute and chronic pain; social influences on the experience and communication of pain; biopsychosocial approaches to pain control.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: (PSY BEH 9 or PSY BEH 11C or PSYCH 7A or PSYCH 9C) and any upper-division course from the Health or Pre-clinical Psychology areas.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Social Ecology of Health Promotion
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences, Public Health Policy, and Social Ecology majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Core themes of Social Ecology are examined as they apply to major areas of health promotion research and practice. Students attend lectures and work collaboratively on team projects conducted in university and community settings.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Behavior Theory
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to foundational theories for health behavior change. Explores individual, interpersonal, and community-level theories applied to health interventions. Understand societal challenges and preventable behavioral causes of diseases.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Promotion Programs
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores social ecological perspectives and the role of behavior change theories in health promotion planning. Introduces systematic planning for the development of an intervention program. Emphasizes the cornerstone of planning, implementing, and evaluating a health promotion program.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Drug Abuse and its Prevention
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical and practical underpinnings of drug abuse and its prevention at the individual and population levels. Students practice developing drug abuse prevention schemes for specific populations. Recent developments in pharmacological and biobehavioral theories of drug dependence are explored.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Communication
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Theoretical foundations and practical use of communication sciences in public health, covering effective techniques such as audience segmentation, tailored messaging, and multi-model communication for behavior change campaigns across various settings. Includes crisis communication strategies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 2

prerequisite_list.title: Case Studies in Public Health Practice

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health and Wellness
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Presents information about wellness from both science and policy perspectives in order to demonstrate the role of wellness in public health. Emphasizes the conditions that create wellness in the individual, the community, the nation, and the world.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Psychology
allCourses.description: Impact of the physical environment on individual and group behaviour. Three basic concerns examined: (a) environmental determinants of behaviour at the individual and interpersonal level; (b) social planning and urban design; (c) methodological approaches to the study of environmental issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: ENVIRON E8 and (SOCECOL 10 or PP&D 4)

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Happiness, Wellbeing, and Health
allCourses.description: Explores positive and protective psychological, social, and behavioral factors that influence physical, mental/emotional, and social wellbeing.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Sociology of Mental Health
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Majors only. Sociology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines the social causes, consequences, and patterns of mental health and illness. Students learn a sociological perspective on mental health, mental illness or disorder, and medicine/health care, ranging from social definitions, roles, and interactions to societal stratification and international patterns.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social and Behavioral Health Science
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of social and behavioral health sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Pollution and Remediation
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Public Health Sciences and Public Health Policy majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: The study of pollution—its identification, risks, and remediation. Analysis of sources of natural and anthropogenic environmental pollutants using ecological concepts, chemical fate and transport, engineering technologies, economics, and policy to provide understanding and solutions to these problems.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Geology
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores geologic principles applied to environmental and health issues. Topics include earth systems, earth materials, water pollution, natural hazards, waste disposal, climate change, and geology's impact on human health in UCI and Orange County.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Human Ecology of Health
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences and Public Health Policy majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Many human health problems are directly associated with ethnicity, sex, and age. Integrates the science of these issues with anthropology, geography, economics to understand the relationship, management, treatment. Involves lectures and discussions to probe these factors.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention and human well-being. Topics include air and water quality, food safety, built environment, radiation exposure, climate change, environmental justice, children's health, and policy interventions for public health improvement.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Toxic Chemicals in the Environment
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences and Public Health Policy majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores the sources, transformation, and sinks of toxic chemicals in the environment, and their effects on public health. Covers regulatory issues and design-for-the-environment initiatives to reduce or eliminate the adverse effects of toxic chemicals.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 2.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Toxic Chemicals in the Environment Laboratory
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences and Public Health Policy majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Covers field sampling techniques and laboratory analysis methods for assessing the occurrence and effects of toxic chemicals in environmental compartments, including water, soils, sediments, air, and food resources.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 2. Prerequisite or corequisite: PUBHLTH 164.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Issues in Potable Water Reuse
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences and Public Health Policy majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Provides an in-depth study of the treatment and subsequent reuse of wastewater for drinking. Analyzes existing regulations for both drinking water and reuse situations, microbial and chemical contaminants, health concerns and risk assessment.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCECOL E8.

prerequisite_list.title: Introduction to Environmental Analysis and Design

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Geographic Information Systems
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences, Public Health Policy, and Criminology, Law and Society majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Basic geographic, cartographic, and GIS concepts including computer representation of physical, political, statistical, and social aspects of space using vector and grid-based maps. Experience with extensive geographic base map files and databases through use of GIS software (ArcView 3.x).

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to how air pollutants are emitted into the atmosphere, how people are most exposed to air pollutants in developed and developing areas, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and the influence of air pollutants on global warming.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Nuclear Environments
allCourses.description: Understanding the impact of the nuclear age on the environment and human health through interrelated developments of nuclear power and nuclear weapons. The early years of weapon development, catastrophic environmental pollution, perils of nuclear power in the U.S. and Russia.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Human Exposure Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Indirect methods in estimating human exposure to environmental agents. Topics include air, noise, dermal and ingestion exposure assessment, time-activity and micro-environmental approach, uncertainty and variability analysis, and the use of GIS and remote sensing in exposure assessment.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Global Health
allCourses.description: Provides a foundational interdisciplinary understanding of global health issues and their importance to societal goals, including poverty reduction, sustainable development, and international contexts of wellness and covers major communicable and non-communicable diseases and demographic patterns of disease burden.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Human Exposure to Environmental Contaminants
allCourses.description: Explores origins of environmental health awareness. Covers exposure assessment theory, variability, risk assessment integration, and societal implications. Discusses notable environmental contaminants impacting human health.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Climate Change and Disaster Management
allCourses.description: Examines the social, economic, environmental, and health impacts of anthropogenic climate change through engaged learning that integrates practice and theory.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health and Global Environmental Change
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines global environmental and climate change's impact on human health. Explores metabolic pandemics, infectious diseases, and underlying health conditions. Fosters interdisciplinary collaboration among environmental health, public health, medicine, and policy sciences.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: One upper-division course in environmental science, public health, environmental policy, and/or environmental management.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Global Health Ethics
allCourses.description: Provides a foundation for understanding and application of key issues.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Assessment
allCourses.description: Surveys the general principles, basic mathematical methods, and practices of environmental modeling and human health risk assessment. Topics include advection-dispersion models, risk management, and risk perception. Students conduct an original risk assessment as a final group project.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2A and STATS 7.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: War and Public Health
allCourses.description: Explores how war impacts public health both globally and domestically in the United States. Focus on the link between war and the burden that it ultimately places on physical, mental, environmental, and societal health as well as on health systems.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Global Health Policy and Diplomacy
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles and consequences of global health policy and diplomacy, including governance structure, functions, analysis, advocacy, and outcomes. Emphasizes practical application of multilateral policies for global health security and responses to transnational threats such as pandemics, climate, pollution, and migration.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Environmental and Global Health Science
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of environmental and global health sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Epidemiology of Infectious Disease
allCourses.description: Explores the distribution of infectious disease and disease risks among human populations. Covers concepts and methods of infectious disease epidemiology, including case studies of important infectious diseases such as COVID-19, HIV, and malaria.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Infectious Disease Dynamics
allCourses.description: Learn how the immune system interacts with infectious diseases, in particular with viral infections. An introduction to basic virology and immunology, it concentrates on the way in which the immune system is critical to the prevention of infections.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Evolutionary and Ecological Principles in Medicine
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explore the dynamics of populations on an ecological, epidemiological, and medical level. Considers the dynamics of competition, predation, and parasitism; the spread and control of infectious diseases; and the in vivo dynamics of viral infections and the immune system.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Infectious Diseases
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of infectious diseases. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Geographic Information Systems for Public Health
allCourses.description: Extensive use of GIS software. Lecture topics cover mapping basics, projections, and geocoding. Practical tutorials and lab sessions for hands-on practice with public health data. Assessments focus on synthesizing GIS tools for problem-solving.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice. Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Field Studies in Public Health
allCourses.description: Join faculty on field studies or work at field agencies post-practicum. Gain hands-on experience in real-world settings. Ideal for practical application of theoretical knowledge in diverse environments.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 2
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Directed Studies
allCourses.description: Engage in faculty-guided research activities individually or in small groups. Explore diverse topics, develop critical thinking, and enhance research skills. Ideal for hands-on learning and academic growth.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 1
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Undergraduate Research
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Engage in original research with public health faculty. Attend research group meetings and submit quarterly reports. Ideal for students pursuing research careers or advanced degrees.
