allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Foundations of Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only. College of Health Sciences students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Program in Public Health students only.
allCourses.description: Explores public health research and practices fundamentals from a multidisciplinary view. Gain core skills for crosscutting approaches essential in public health.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents descriptive and experimental approaches to the recognition of the causal association of disease in the general population, as these approaches apply to populations using different student designs and models free from the literature.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Designed to help students develop an appreciation for statistician's view of the research process, emphasizing biomedical research. Instills an understanding of how statistical models are used to yield insights about data that form evidence-based understanding of the world around us.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to the basic statistical techniques commonly used in public health research. Topics include descriptive statistics, basic probability, inferential statistics (estimation, confidence intervals, and hypothesis testing), and contingency tables. SAS software is introduced.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics II: Intermediate Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores advanced statistical analysis methods for biological and medical applications. Topics include linear, logistic, and generalized linear regression models like Poisson regression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204A. EPIDEM 204A with a grade of B or better

prerequisite_list.title: Biostatistics I: Introduction to Statistical Methods

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Biostatistics III: Advanced Statistical Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Intended for graduate students in epidemiology, public health, and related fields.  Introduces statistical methods for analyzing survival and longitudinal/clustered data, and techniques to resolve missing data.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 204B. EPIDEM 204B with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in the design and statistical analysis of epidemiologic studies. Topics include simulation methods, counter-matching and multiphase study designs, missing data, and Bayesian analysis. Published simulation studies are discussed and replicated using the R software package.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 101B or STATS 111 or STATS 211

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Graduate Epidemiology in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Presents descriptive and experimental approaches to the recognition of the causal association of disease in the general populations, as these approaches apply to populations using different student designs and models from the literature.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Principles of Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Fundamental principles of epidemiology, biostatistics, and epidemiological research. Topics include research methods of measuring health problems in populations, disease control and prevention in populations, how epidemiology contributes to knowledge of disease etiology, and biostatistical analysis and interpretation of epidemiologic data.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Intermediate Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Epidemiology Majors only. College of Health Sciences students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Program in Public Health students only.
allCourses.description: Explores conceptual aspects of epidemiology, focusing on strengths and limitations of observational designs. Learn to identify, quantify, and correct bias (e.g. selection, confounding), and evaluate causal identical conditions. Gain skills to evaluate study designs systematically.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 206A. PUBHLTH 206A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods
allCourses.description: Advanced topics in the design and statistical analysis of epidemiologic studies. Topics include simulation methods, counter-matching and multiphase study designs, missing data, and Bayesian analysis. Published simulation studies are discussed and replicated using the R software package.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200A and EPIDEM 200B. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B or better. EPIDEM 200B with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Surveys statistical methods for public health. Topics include descriptive statistics, probability models, likelihood functions, estimation, and hypothesis testing for categorical and continuous date. Student learn to use statistical software to perform epidemiologic data analysis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 203 and MATH 2A.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Probability and Statistics in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Program in Public Health students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: An introduction to probability and statistical methods, using examples in public health. Topics include descriptive statistics, laws of probability, discrete and continuous probability distributions, estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and power calculations for one- and two-sample comparisons.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 206A. PUBHLTH 206A with a grade of B or better

prerequisite_for.title: Analysis of Public Health Data Using Statistical Software

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Analysis of Public Health Data Using Statistical Software
allCourses.restriction: Program in Public Health students only. Master of Public Health Degree students only. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Overview of common statistical methods in public health and how to implement them in R. Topics include linear regression, ANOVA, the Kruskal-Wallis test, logistic regression, missing data and censoring, Kaplan-Meier survival curves, log-rank tests, and Cox regression.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 207A. PUBHLTH 207A with a grade of B or better

prerequisite_list.title: Probability and Statistics in Public Health

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advances in Social Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces major themes in social epidemiology, adopting a topical approach. Weekly topics include theories, debates, methods, policy implications, and empirical examples of specific social factors. Students apply principles to their own health interests.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces basic demographic methods used in social science and public health research. Topics include sources and limitations of demographic data; components of population growth; measures of nuptiality, fertility, mortality, and population mobility projection methods; and demographic models.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Theory-Driven Secondary Data Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Learn how to develop and test theoretically-driven research questions in secondary data sources. Logic of theory building and testing, how to conduct statistical analyses on testable research questions, and interpret results. There is also a lab component.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Genomics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the role of genetic predisposition in the occurence of the human diseases with emphasis on population screening and prevention of disease. Includes interactions between genetic factors and environmental situations, policies, and ethics of population genomics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 203.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Latinos/Latinas and Medical Care: Contemporary Issues
allCourses.description: Introduction to medical anthropological and social science perspectives on Latinos/Latinas in relation to a number of health and medically-related issues, i.e., immigration, gender, reproduction, culture, social structure, political economy, sexuality, utilization of medical services, and health beliefs.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Latinos/Latinas and Medical Care: Contemporary Issues
allCourses.description: Introduction to medical anthropological and social science perspectives on Latinos/Latinas in relation to a number of health and medically-related issues, i.e., immigration, gender, reproduction, culture, social structure, political economy, sexuality, utilization of medical services, and health beliefs.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHC/LAT 211A

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Intermediate Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Learn to design and conduct epidemiologic studies using common designs. Determine why bias and measurement error arise in observational studies, and how they influence effect estimates. Perform and interpret epidemiologic data analyses using statistical software.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 203

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Epidemiology in Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines epidemiology and global health. Topics include global health concepts, research in resource-poor settings, climate change's impact on health, and interventions in low-income settings. Emphasizes literature review, health determinants, and interdisciplinary approaches with a practical focus.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Surveillance Systems
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Surveillance as a fundamental element of the practice of public health is examined in terms of the application and evaluation of monitoring systems. Topics include surveillance of infectious and chronic diseases, environmental constituents, and other indicators of population health.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBH 206

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Cancer Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Concentrates on understanding how epidemiology plays a role in the search for cancer etiology, prevention, control, and treatment; gives an overview of cancer research with an appreciation of the multidisciplinary nature of the field.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: EPIDEM 200A or PUBHLTH 206A. EPIDEM 200A with a grade of B- or better. PUBHLTH 206A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Biostatistics, Epidemiology, and Health Informatics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in biostatistics, epidemiology, and health informatics. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Cost-Effectiveness Analysis
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines using cost-effectiveness information to allocate limited resources to maximize health benefits to a population; defining and measuring cost, survival and health-related quality of life; and how to calculate cost-effectiveness using decision trees and Markov simulation models.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Promotion and Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on health and health care in the United States, but discussion of global health issues and/or international comparisons will be made whenever possible.  Considers both the social and economic aspects of health and disease.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Policy and Management
allCourses.restriction: Master of Public Health Degree students have first consideration for enrollment. Master of Public Policy Degree students have first consideration for enrollment. Graduate students only. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban and Regional Planning Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary inquiry into theory and practice concerned with delivery, quantity, costs of health care for individuals and populations. Explores managerial and policy concerns regarding structure, process, outcomes of health services including the costs, financing, organization, outcomes, and accessibility of care.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Policy and Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Urban and Regional Planning Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Master of Public Health Degree students have first consideration for enrollment. Master of Public Policy Degree students have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Multidisciplinary inquiry into theory and practice concerned with delivery, quantity, costs of health care for individuals and populations. Explores managerial and policy concerns regarding structure, process, outcomes of health services including the costs, financing, organization, outcomes, and accessibility of care.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Care Delivery and Financing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Advances health policy comprehension. Explores healthcare delivery, spending, organizations, quality, insurance programs, payment mechanisms, reforms, and innovation. Special emphasis on incentives for payers, providers, and patients, influencing healthcare decisions.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 222A. PUBHLTH 222A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Risk Communication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines theory and research related to the communication of scientific information in risk communication contexts, risk perceptions, and behavior as related to decision-making under risk.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Leadership
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Integrates theory and practice of public health leadership through lectures on global health leadership, case studies on leadership issues, and course assignments that include assessment of leadership traits, and development of individual career mission, vision, and values statements.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Politics and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explore health policy according to the World Health Organization, focusing on decisions, plans, and actions for societal health goals. Understand political institutions, stakeholders, and interest groups influencing policy. Develop policy analysis skills and advocacy strategies through an interdisciplinary approach.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Economics
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An overview of health economics with a focus on U.S. healthcare and health management. Explore economic aspects such as evaluation, medical care demand, insurance, productivity, and markets for healthcare professionals. Delve into microeconomic theory, government regulation, and health reform.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Health Policy and Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in health policy and management. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Topics in Environmental Health Promotion and Education
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on design of intervention strategies dependent on the environmental agent, exposure to assessment, SES, health effects, stakeholders, and support base. Programmatic design includes media selection, communication/education, and pre/post surveys. Analysis of transborder and local environmental health promotion programs.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Policy and Global Sustainability
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Organized around four transcendent questions: does the world value sustainability, what challenges must be met to move toward it, what are the roots of inequality, and is capitalism compatible with sustainability.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Theories of Health Communication
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Evaluates health communication theory and strategies for diverse settings (healthcare, community, social media). Emphasizes audience segmentation, personalized tailoring, and subgroup targeting in case studies. Explores multimodal communication's role in persuasive messaging.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Behavior Theory
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only. Master of Public Health Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Explores theories of health behavior change, moving from individual to broader contexts, with a focus on applying theory to create population-based theory-driven models delineating behavioral determinants of public health problems.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Promotion Planning
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores strategic planning for public health interventions, emphasizing social and behavioral health science. Develops intervention plans targeting specific health issues and populations.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Social Research Methods
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: An interactive graduate seminar covering topics related to the research process and study design. Begins with conceptualizing research questions, hypotheses, and then turns to topics in measurement and concludes with experimental, quasi-experimental, and observational study designs.

prerequisite_for.title: Models of Practice and Intervention at the Community Level

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Program Evaluation
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Interactive course develops program evaluation plans. Students create plans for health programs in partnership with community organizations. Activities include lectures, discussions, readings, critiques, presentations, and final evaluation plan submission.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Fundamentals of Maternal and Child Health - Programs, Problems, and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores Maternal and Child Health (MCH) through public health and neurobiological perspectives. Study key factors influencing global development. Examine historical foundations, conceptual frameworks, and current issues such as COVID-19's impact. Analyze programs and legislation addressing MCH disparities.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Status and Care Disparities
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Expert health care providers present viewpoints and interdisciplinary strategies for addressing sociocultural, economic, gender, age, and other disparities in population health status and care provision.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Models of Practice and Intervention at the Community Level
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Examines and critiques current models, frameworks, theories for.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: CHC/LAT 200A or PUBHLTH 246. CHC/LAT 200A with a grade of B- or better. PUBHLTH 246 with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Community Health and Health Equity
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores community health roles, applications, and impacts in public health practice. Introduces community  organizing, health advocacy, interventions, and strategies for addressing health inequities.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Social and Behavioral Health Sciences
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in Social and Behavioral Health Sciences. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Human Exposure Modeling
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the basic principles and methods in estimating human exposure to environmental pollutants. Topics include source emissions, spatial/temporal aspects of human exposures, air pollution exposure modeling, time-activity patterns, micro-environmental exposure assessment, the uncertainty/variability analysis.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Hydrology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of the occurrence, distribution, and movement of water in the environment. Quantitative methods are introduced for analyzing hydrologic processes. Human impacts on water distribution and quality are considered.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Earthquakes and Seismic Hazard
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an overview of earthquakes and introduction to seismic hazard. Topics include characteristics and effects of earthquakes, sources of earthquakes, seismic hazard assessment, introduction to earthquake loss estimation and mitigation. California examples are emphasized.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Seminar in Paleoseismology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Provides an introduction to paleoseismology and its applications. Topics include data collection methods, data analysis, earthquakes in different tectonic environments, and applications to seismic hazard assessment and fault characterization.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environ Health Sci and Policy Majors only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. Studies human-environment interaction, focusing on chemical, physical, and biological agents in community and occupational settings. Covers climate change, environmental justice, children’s health, exposure assessment, and policy for public health improvement.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Environmental Health Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explores the complex relationships among exposure processes and adverse health effects of environmental toxins focusing on specific chemicals, sources, transport media, exposure pathways, and human behaviors. Techniques of environmental sampling for exposure assessment are discussed.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
allCourses.description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Human Exposure to Environmental Contaminants
allCourses.description: Introduces founders of conceptual thought that environmental contaminants can impact health. Theory and principles of exposure assessment, the continuum from emissions of a contaminant into the environment to evidence of health effects in a population.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Impacts of Environmental Change
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Seminar on health impacts of environmental change at various scales of analysis. Uses numerical models such as "MIASMA" and "TARGETS" to analyze alternative outcomes of environmental-change scenarios. Presentations from experts are featured.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Health Psychology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Focus on theory and research in health psychology as applied to major acute, chronic, and occupational health problems. Adopting the biopsychosocial model of health, emphasis is on understanding and influencing how biology, behavior, and the environment influence health and illness.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Health, Science, and Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only
allCourses.description: Topics relevant to the field of environmental health, science, and policy are covered in depth.  Included are: hazardous and biological pollutants in soil, water, air; remediation technologies; water conflicts; and regulations pertaining to contaminants.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Management
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Learn general principles and basic mathematical methods for environmental modeling and human health risk assessment, including compartmental and advection-dispersion models for contaminants in air and water, uptake by plants and animals, exposure, assessment, dose-response modeling, risk management, and risk perception.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: MATH 2A and STATS 7

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Toxic Chemicals in Environment
allCourses.restriction: Grad students only or Consent of instructor to enroll
allCourses.description: Industrial ecology of toxicants and their impacts on environmental quality and human health.  Explores theoretical basis of toxicity thresholds and regulatory issues.  Uses classic and contemporary research articles to understand the legacy of traditional toxicants, and to identify emerging threats.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Target Organ Toxicology I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Outlines vulnerability of selected organ systems to environmental and occupational chemicals. Reviews molecular aspects of toxicological damage. Topics include molecular toxicology and the following organ systems: nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, dermal, and skeletal embryology.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Target Organ Toxicology II
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Analyzes mechanistic responses in animals and humans to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation, focusing on organ system physiology. Topics specifically covered include reproductive, endocrine, developmental, kidney, liver, pancreas, vascular, immune toxicology, radiation, and chemical carcinogenesis.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 277A or EHS 206A. PUBHLTH 277A with a grade of B- or better. EHS 206A with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Industrial Toxicology
allCourses.description: Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 277B or EHS 206B. PUBHLTH 277B with a grade of B- or better. EHS 206B with a grade of B- or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Environmental & Occupational Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in environmental and occupational health. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Global Burden of Disease
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces composite measures of disease burden, including Disability Adjusted Life Years and their use in prioritizing disease burden at local, regional, and global levels. Focuses on WHO's landmark assessments and introduces DISMOD software for specific analyses.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Covers concepts and methods of infectious disease epidemiology and case studies of various infectious diseases. Includes surveillance, outbreak investigation, emerging pathogens, ecological and molecular epidemiology.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Climate Change and Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Environmental Health Sciences Majors only. Epidemiology Majors only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Explore major topics in climate change and global health, analyzing micro- and macro-level impacts. Covers infectious and non-communicable diseases, demographic aspects, and interventions. Gain the ability to propose public health solutions for climate-related health challenges.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Geographic Information Systems for Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Engage extensively with GIS software, combining lectures and hands-on tutorials. Cover mapping basics, projections, geocoding, and toolbars. Apply GIS to public health data for practical understanding of its applications.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBH 206. PUBH 206 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_for.title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems and Spatial Epidemiology

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Graduate Field Studies
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Field studies with Public Health faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Global Health Law and Diplomacy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Extends theory and practice of law and diplomacy from the scope of health to trade, intellectual property, national security, human rights, and environmental protection. Focuses on negotiations that shape and manage the global policy environment for health.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems and Spatial Epidemiology
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Explore GIS software extensively, with lectures followed by hands-on tutorials. Topics include rasters, groundwater modeling, spatial statistics, and R programming. Analyze spatial epidemiology using public health data, with weekly assignments and a class project.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 283. PUBHLTH 283 with a grade of B- or better

prerequisite_list.title: Geographic Information Systems for Public Health

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to qualitative research methods. Covers epistemology, the range of qualitative data, developing research questions appropriate for qualitative data analysis, fieldwork, data collection, analysis, and report writing. Students engage in fieldwork.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Research Proposal Writing in Global Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Overview of financial support for research in global health and disease prevention. Collaborative agreements, guidelines for proposal writing, team building, budgeting, peer-review process, and transitioning from proposal to research project implementation.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Global Health and Disease Prevention
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Current research in global health and disease prevention. Topics vary from quarter to quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of public health. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice.  Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice.  Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Seminar: Advances and Challenges in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Forum for exploring recent advances and challenges in all disciplines of public health research and practice.  Features case studies exemplifying the integration of core competencies with cross-cutting interdisciplinary themes of public health.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Ethics and Responsible Conduct of Research in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Ethical dimensions of public health research, practice, and policy: ethical principles and frameworks, moral challenges in public health, research ethics, oversight of public health research, structural racism and health inequities, ethical issues in cross-cultural research, research misconduct, whistleblowing.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Foundations of Clinical and Translational Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduction to clinical research design, implementation, and translational science from lab to community. Foundation of clinical research design, approaches to accelerate therapeutic discoveries into healthcare practices, comparison of necessities and impediments to clinical research with transformative potential of translational science.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Research Communication in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Skills for academic writing: focus on peer-reviewed journal articles, writing strategies, effective dissemination to academic/non-academic audiences, and career-related topics for graduate students in health-related fields.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Graduate Practicum and Culminating Experience in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Provides opportunities for hands-on experience for graduate students at agencies or organizations engaged in public health practice. Students are matched with placement sites based on academic preparation and students' career goals. The practicum report is integrated into the culminating experience.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 200 and PUBHLTH 244 and PUBHLTH 222 and PUBHLTH 264 and PUBHLTH 207A. PUBHLTH 200 with a grade of B or better. PUBHLTH 244 with a grade of B or better. PUBHLTH 222 with a grade of B or better. PUBHLTH 264 with a grade of B or better. PUBHLTH 207A with a grade of B or better

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Doctoral Dissertation Research and Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only.
allCourses.description: Dissertation research with Public Health faculty.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Advancement to candidacy.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 12 units.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Research Design and Proposal Writing
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Majors only. College of Health Sciences students only. Program in Public Health students only. Doctor of Philosophy Degree students only.
allCourses.description: Evaluate strengths of research findings based on methods used by researchers to develop research proposals. Components such as collaborative agreements, guidelines for proposal writing, budgeting, peer-review process, and transitioning from proposal to research project implementation are addressed.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Directed Studies in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Directed study with Public Health faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Independent Study in Public Health
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Independent research with Public Health faculty.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Urban Environmental Health
allCourses.description: Explores urban health disparities, focusing on social determinants and environmental impacts. Examines global urban health challenges, disease burdens, and historical legacies of contamination. Introduces interventions and policies to mitigate urban health inequalities and enhance public health in diverse urban settings.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: University Teaching
allCourses.description: Limited to teaching assistants.
allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Environmental Quality and Health
allCourses.description: Explores the interplay of pollution and human health: population, epidemiology, toxicology, zoonotic diseases, water and air quality, climate change, waste management, contaminants (metals, pesticides, organics, radioactivity), and environmental justice. Delves into risk assessment and public health policy implications.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Introduction to Public Health Statistics
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the development and application of statistical reasoning and methods in addressing, analyzing, and solving problems in public health, health care, and biomedical, clinical, and population-based research and practice.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Statistics I
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Public Health Sciences Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: First of two courses in statistics. Introduces fundamental statistics for health science students, emphasizing quantitative reasoning from a public health perspective. Topics include probability, data analysis, and statistical inference.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Statistics II
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Majors only. Public Health Policy Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Second of two courses in statistics. Focus on regression, probability, and significance testing from a public health perspective. Prepares students to interpret scientific publications and conduct basic statistical analyses.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH 7A

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: AIDS Fundamentals
allCourses.description: Considers the biological and sociological bases of the AIDS epidemic. Topics include the history of AIDS, current medical knowledge, transmission, risk reduction, and how the community can respond.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Natural Disasters
allCourses.description: Examine natural disasters and their impacts on humans. Topics include volcanoes, earthquakes, severe weather, fires, floods, landslides, coastal processes, and risk assessment. Use WebGIS for hazard data and risk analysis in California.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Disparities in Health Care
allCourses.description: Students become agents of social change for equitable health care delivery. Focus on cultural competency, awareness, communication skills, and disparities. Explore clinical, public service, and research opportunities. Engage with guest lecturers to cultivate and empower diverse communities.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit for 8 units.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis I
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only. Public Health Policy Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Advanced research opportunity for Public Health Honors. Students conduct research projects with faculty, attend lectures, and engage in timeline creation. Requirements include upper-division coursework, GPA criteria, and a faculty-approved thesis project.

prerequisite_for.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis II

allCourses.repeatability: May be repeated for credit unlimited times.

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis II
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students initiate and complete data collection for the honors thesis. In addition, students begin data analysis and summarize results at a class symposium at the end of the quarter. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH H192A

prerequisite_list.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis I

prerequisite_for.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis III

allCourses.school: Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health
allCourses.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis III
allCourses.restriction: Public Health Policy Majors only. Public Health Sciences Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students write their honors research project (PUBHLTH H192A-PUBHLTH H192B) and prepare an oral report to be presented at a class symposium at the end of the quarter. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: PUBHLTH H192B

prerequisite_list.title: Public Health Honors Seminar and Thesis II

allCourses.title: Statistics and Methods for Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introductory course with focus on gaining a sound understanding of what constitutes credible evidence in support of policy arguments and  management decisions.

allCourses.title: Information and Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Evaluates strengths and weaknesses of qualitative and quantitative methods and the data used in making public policy claims. Looks at the bases of certain widely accepted measures of poverty, growth, environmental quality, and the like.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explores different approaches to public policy analysis, the diverse conceptions of the goals and objectives that should be served by policy, and the appropriate role of the policy analyst. Policy consequences are traced to indirect and subtle incentives and disincentives.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Qualitative Methods
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Fieldwork, data collections techniques, and related issues for anti-positivistic research. Data collection techniques include observation, physical traces, participation, in-depth interview. Data checks include veracity, detail, completeness, rigor.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Economics of Government
allCourses.description: Prepares students to analyze public policy questions with tools from economics. By the end, students should be able to identify important economic issues in public policy debates and consume and critique economic research on these topics.

allCourses.title: Microeconomics and Public Policy
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of microeconomics that are required for applied policy analysis. Provides students with an intuitive understanding of the microeconomic approach, and familiarizes them with concepts used in applied public policy analysis.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 2 times.

allCourses.title: Policy and Ethics
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors only.
allCourses.description: Examines the challenge of identifying ethical principles that can guide us in formulating and assessing public policy, the public policy process from an ethical perspective, and the ethics of the individual engaged in the public policy arena.

allCourses.title: Collaborative Governance and Public Management
allCourses.restriction: Public Policy Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to inclusive management. To make effective use of public resources, public managers are inventing ways of managing that alter relationships within organizations, between organizations, between sectors, and with the public. Requires rethinking fundamentals such as leadership and motivation.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Study of Religion
allCourses.description: The intersection of religious belief and practices with selected subjects of continuing interest.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in the Philosophy of Religion
allCourses.description: Critical examination of philosophical concepts in religious scripture and theology, e.g., the nature and existence of God, miracles, the problem of evil, and divine command theories in ethics. May include any religious tradition.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Gender and Religion
allCourses.description: Critical examination of how religious beliefs and practices have shaped (and been shaped by) attitudes toward gender and sexuality in modern and/or premodern society.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Thinking about Religion: Theories and Methodologies
allCourses.restriction: Religious Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey and investigation of the major thinkers, theories, and methodologies in the study of religions. Designed to develop the student's ability to analyze and articulate theoretical arguments; includes a paper on relevant Religious Studies topics.

allCourses.title: Thinking about Religion: Theories and Methodologies
allCourses.restriction: Religious Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey and investigation of the major thinkers, theories, and methodologies in the study of religions. Designed to develop the student's ability to analyze and articulate theoretical arguments in writing; includes a paper on relevant Religious Studies topics.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Science and Religion II
allCourses.description: The development of genomics, stem-cell research, robotics, nanotechnology, neuropharmacology raises difficult religious and philosophical questions. Examines interdisciplinary approaches that cut across institutional boundaries, cultural borders, religious traditions. Focuses on relationship between religion and cognitive/affective/social neuroscience.   Course may be offered online.

allCourses.title: Religion and World Politics
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between religion and world politics historically and today, focusing on connections with peace/war, democracy, human rights, secularism(s), and globalization. Covers major debates, scholarship, concepts, and theories through class exercises, exams, and essays.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: POL SCI 41A or INTL ST 11 or INTL ST 12 or REL STD 5A or REL STD 5B or REL STD 5C

allCourses.title: Topics in Asian Religious Traditions
allCourses.description: Studies involving (but not limited to) Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Jainism, Sikhism, Daoism, Shinto or Shamanism, including both elite and doctrinal aspects and forms of more popular religiosity.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Ancient India
allCourses.description: Examines the visual and religious history of the region defined as "India" today, but necessarily encompassing modern Bangladesh and Pakistan.  Culminates with the supposed Golden Age of the Gupta empire and its far-reaching legacies.

allCourses.title: Medieval India
allCourses.description: Begins with the Gupta period's aesthetic legacies in South Asia's architecture, sculpture, and painting. Explores the dispersal of Islam throughout South Asia, including the Muslim communities of southern India.

allCourses.title: Topics in Modern Indian Religion
allCourses.description: Topics in religions of the Indian subcontinent including, but not confined to, Hinduism, Jainism, Sikhism, Islam, and Buddhism from the founding of the Mughal Empire in 1526 to the creation of the several modern states of the Indian subcontinent.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Jain History, Culture, and Ethics
allCourses.description: Introduces history, texts, philosophy, culture, and ethical practices of the Jain tradition as it developed in India and now exists globally, including in Orange County.

allCourses.title: Topics in Jain Studies
allCourses.description: Studies involving aspects of the Jain tradition in relation to philosophy, ethics, culture, ritual, art, or diaspora, and/or analyses of environment, gender, or in relation to other Indian traditions.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Jewish, Islamic, and Middle Eastern Religious Traditions
allCourses.description: Character and evolution of Egyptian, Jewish, Zoroastrian, Muslim, and other religious communities of the region from their formative periods to the present era.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: History of Antisemitism
allCourses.description: Survey of the history of antisemitism, ancient to modern. Topics include medieval religious anti-Judaism, persecution of Jews and Judaism during the Crusades and the Inquisition, the rise of modern racial antisemitism, Nazi antisemitism, and the persistence of antisemitism since 1945.

allCourses.title: Jews and Power
allCourses.description: Examines the relationship between the Jewish people and political power over a 3500 year period. How have Jews preserved their communal interests and personal safety? How have they defined the proper relationship of the people to political authority.

allCourses.title: History of Zoroastrianism
allCourses.description: Reviews major trends in the history of Zoroastrianism.

allCourses.title: Early Western Religious Traditions
allCourses.description: Religious perspectives of the Mediterranean and European regions from the earliest times to approximately 1500 C.E.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Recent Western Religious Traditions
allCourses.description: Studies related to Catholic, Protestant, and Orthodox Christianity as well as alternative belief systems in Europe of the early modern and modern eras.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Religion in the Americas
allCourses.description: Religious belief and social context in North and South America from the earliest human societies to the present.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Race and Religion
allCourses.description: Critical analysis of race and religion as expressed through (1) various structures of socio-political ordering, metaphysics, language, class, colorism, power, biology, nationalism, and culture, and (2) various expressions of moral philosophy, ethics, music, literature, arts, rituals, liberation, and revolution.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Diaspora Religions
allCourses.description: Examination of what happens to belief and practice as religious communities are scattered geographically.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Topics in Religion and Science
allCourses.description: Examinations of the dynamic interplay between religion and science, including historical conflicts, contemporary dialogues, and ethical implications. Classes analyze how these two realms shape our understanding of the universe, humanity, and morality.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: An Economic Approach to Religion
allCourses.description: Introduction to how basic economic concepts such as demand, supply, consumption, production, competition, free-riding, innovation, regulation, and rent-seeking can be applied to understand observed religious behavior.

allCourses.title: Topics in Comparative Studies in Religion
allCourses.description: Literary, historical, or philosophical comparison of selected religious and quasi-religious traditions, their beliefs and practices.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Medical Ethics
allCourses.description: Analysis of moral issues concerning health care. Topics may include just allocation of scarce medical resources, the doctor/patient relationship, genetic engineering, surrogate motherhood, abortion, euthanasia, or social policy concerning AIDS.

allCourses.title: Senior Colloquium
allCourses.restriction: A minimum of two students must enroll.
allCourses.description: Reading and group discussion of selected texts under the direction of an instructor.  Paper required.
allCourses.repeatability: May be taken for credit 3 times as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Independent Study
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Directed reading and research in consultation with a faculty member.  Substantial written work required.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Philosophy and Religion
allCourses.description: Examines the intersection of religion and philosophy from a standpoint that does not presuppose previous academic study of either.  Both Western and Eastern traditions and perspectives may be explored.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.
allCourses.description: Critical analysis of race and religion as expressed through (1) various structures of socio-political ordering, metaphysics, language, class, colorism, power, biology, nationalism, and culture, and (2) various expressions of moral philosophy, ethics, music, literature, arts, rituals, liberation, and revolution.

allCourses.title: Topics in Religion and Science
allCourses.restriction: Graduate students only.

allCourses.title: Gender and Ethnicity: Chicana/Latina Feminisms in the US
allCourses.description: Focuses on the Latina Feminist Group and testimonios to examine the historical development of Chicana/Latinx feminist thought and practice. Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship to survey the diversity of contemporary Chicana/Latinx feminisms through an intersectionality lens.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Sexual Assault
allCourses.restriction: Sociology majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the causes and consequences of sexual assault including rape, incest, and child molestation, and efforts to eliminate sexual assault. Explores the impact of gender, media, and "rape culture." Analyzes the effects of assault on victims and paths to recovery.

allCourses.title: Credit, Debt, and Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines the influence social background has on net worth. Engages sociological texts to understand the causes and consequences of credit and debt for inequality in the U.S.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Aging
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to sociology of age, aging, and the aged. Problems posed by aging population. Life course transitions and how social organizations influence the life course. Addresses work, health, and family in later life.

allCourses.title: Sociology of Aging
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduction to sociology of age, aging, and the aged. Problems posed by aging population. Life course transitions. How social organizations influence the life course. Work, health, family in later life.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Social Inequality: Sociological Perspectives
allCourses.description: Concrete sociological studies from across the world, including the United States, are compared to give perspectives on social status, power, economic differences, race, ethnicity, and gender.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: One course in Anthropology, Economics, Political Science, or Sociology.

allCourses.title: Social Inequality: Sociological Perspectives
allCourses.description: Concrete sociological studies from across the world, including the United States, are compared to give perspectives on social status, power, economic differences, race, ethnicity, and gender.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: One course in Anthropology, Economics, Political Science, or Sociology. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Inequality
allCourses.description: Explores immigration, ethnicity, and inequality as interconnected social forces. International migration, propelled by global inequalities, plays a central role in the formation of multinational societies, shapes inter-group relations and patterns of ethnic inequality, and transforms the immigrants themselves.

allCourses.title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.

allCourses.title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
allCourses.restriction: Chicano/Latino Studies Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Sexism and Power
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only. Sociology and Political Science majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sexism seen as a socially constructed power which creates and maintains gender differences as relations and practices of structured inequalities. Males and females are objects constructed in a powered language dominated and controlled by males to their positional/distributional advantage.

allCourses.title: Neighborhood Inequality and Residential Segregation
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examine how legacies of residential segregation continue to permeate areas of U.S. social life. Engage sociological texts alongside related current events that describe, explain, and predict the causes and consequences of residential segregation for enduring racial inequality in the U.S.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Special Topics in Age, Gender, Race, and Ethnicity
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of age, gender, race, and ethnicity. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Vietnam War
allCourses.description: Examines social structures and social changes in Vietnamese and U.S. societies through the study of the Vietnam War.

allCourses.title: U.S. War on Terrorism
allCourses.description: Analyzes the United States war on terrorism by focusing on terrorism, the U.S. wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and changes in police powers through the Patriot Act, as well as the political leadership which directs the war.

allCourses.title: African American Protest Movements
allCourses.description: Examines the work of major African American Marxist individuals and organizations in the twentieth century. Their theories of racism, capitalism, and their developed practices are covered.

allCourses.title: Environment and Society
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Examines society's changing relationship to the natural world. Delineates different models of "nature" and then explores their institutional roots, the social responses they have generated, and their implications for social inequality.

allCourses.title: Revolution and Social Transformation in China
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Introduces the major political events in Mao’s communist revolution and the social transformations afterward. Helps students understand the historic and political landscape from which China is now departing.

allCourses.title: Chicanx/Latinx Education
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latinx low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

allCourses.title: Social Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Sources, functions, and dynamics of the unequal distribution of wealth, prestige, knowledge, and power in American and other societies.

allCourses.title: Social Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Upper-division students only.
allCourses.description: Sources, functions, and dynamics of the unequal distribution of wealth, prestige, knowledge, and power in American and other societies.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Protests, Movements, and Revolutions
allCourses.restriction: Political Science Majors have first consideration for enrollment. Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: A survey of models of collective action drawn from sociology, economics, psychology, and political science. Focus on areas such as social movements, strikes, crowd psychology, cults, fads, fashions, public opinion, and symbolic and mythical elements in collective culture.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCIOL 1 or POL SCI 11A or ECON 1

prerequisite_list.title: Introduction to Political Science: Political Analysis

allCourses.title: China in the Global Age
allCourses.description: Chinese society from 1949 to present. Social change in the context of political control and ideological considerations. Focus on the power structure, political decision processes, and ideological legitimation, and interplay with the Chinese community and its culture.

allCourses.title: Migration Destinations
allCourses.description: Examines the migration patterns to the three largest nations that receive immigrants (i.e., permanent settlers): Australia, Canada, and the United States.

allCourses.title: International Divided Cities
allCourses.description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Social Policy
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explains how people decide to migrate and how they are incorporated into a host society (both historically and currently), examines the effects of immigration on the U.S., analyzes how the framing of immigration shapes the discourse about the issue.

allCourses.title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
allCourses.description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

allCourses.title: Immigration and Social Policy
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Explains how people decide to migrate and how they are incorporated into a host society (both historically and currently), examines the effects of immigration on the U.S., analyzes how the framing of immigration shapes the discourse about the issue.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Special Topics: Societies and Social Inequality
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Studies in selected areas of societies and social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites vary.
allCourses.repeatability: Unlimited as topics vary.

allCourses.title: Sociology Majors Seminar
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students learn sociology by doing it. A modest-sized research project is planned and implemented by each student.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCIOL 110

allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors only.
allCourses.description: Students learn sociology by doing it. A modest-sized research project is planned and implemented by each student.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCIOL 110. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.title: Honors Research and Thesis
allCourses.restriction: Sociology Honors students only.
allCourses.description: Focuses on the design and implementation of individual research projects undertaken by senior Sociology majors. Writing projects consist of a proposal and paper on some empirical research.
allCourses.prerequisite_text: SOCIOL H188A. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement.

allCourses.restriction: Sociology Majors have first consideration for enrollment.
allCourses.description: Independent honors research with Social Sciences faculty.
